These algorithms and their applications are typically tailored to specific object classes and often rely on assumptions about morphology, scale, or dynamical coherence. Consequently, Galactic structures are often identified and analysed in isolation with respect to a specific methodology, selection criteria, and membership definition. As a result, it is difficult to construct a unified and internally consistent view of the MW’s structure that reflects both its intrinsic multi-scale nature and its broad taxonomy. A key limitation of existing approaches is therefore the lack of a model-agnostic framework that can (1) recover diverse structure types across all relevant scales simultaneously, and (2) crossmatch against existing catalogues without relying on metrics that are dependent on catalogue completeness or model-based assumptions.

In this work, we address this gap by applying the hierarchical, model-agnostic clustering algorithm AstroLink (Oliver et al., 2024) to a large Gaia DR3 subsample containing over one billion stars with five-dimensional astrometric information. By identifying overdensities of arbitrary shape and organising them into a multi-scale hierarchy, AstroLink is well suited to the heterogeneous structure of the MW. In addition to recovering statistically significant structures across a wide range of morphologies and scales, we develop a model-agnostic framework for comparing the resulting hierarchy to existing catalogues through availability-aware metrics and bi-directional best-match relations. This enables a consistent structural taxonomy describing reciprocal matches, fragmentation, merging, and other associations between AstroLink clusters and known stellar systems.

papers.title: The Physics of Interstellar Travel
papers.abstract: How can we send an uncrewed spacecraft to the nearest stars within a human lifetime? What propulsion methods are available? Will it survive impacts in the interstellar medium? What science will it do at its destination? How can it send back data over enormous distances? In this short semi-popular article, I examine various aspects of the physics of interstellar travel, its challenges and possible solutions. I focus on nuclear rockets, laser sails, dust impacts, and communication. These, as well as other issues such as navigation and onboard power, are explored in more detail in my book, The Physics of Interstellar Travel (2026).

papers.title: Kagome Flat Bands from Self-Assembled Water on Non-van der Waals 2D Materials
papers.abstract: The properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials are governed not only by their intrinsic electronic structure but also in particular by their surface chemistry and interactions with the environment. The surfaces of non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials are intrinsically reactive and may require chemical stabilization under realistic experimental conditions. Here, we perform a systematic first-principles study of water passivation of non-vdW 2D materials and demonstrate that molecular water adsorption is energetically and dynamically favored for a wide range of systems. Rather than dissociating, water molecules frequently remain intact and form adsorbed ordered surface overlayers. These overlayers can adopt a kagome lattice geometry, leading to the emergence of flat electronic bands directly at the valence-band edge. Analysis of the electronic structure reveals a strong intermolecular coupling between neighboring water lone pairs within this kagome topology, while the locked molecular orientations simultaneously produce an electrostatically frustrated surface potential. These findings establish water not only as a stabilizing agent but also as an active element for electronic structure engineering of non-vdW 2D surfaces.

papers.title: Linear Functional Estimation under Multiplicative Measurement Error with Unknown Error Distribution
papers.abstract: In this work we consider i.i.d. observations from a multiplicative deconvolution model, i.e. generated by $Y= X\varepsilon$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent strictly positive random variables. The goal is to statistically infer the unknown signal $X$. Starting from the scenario where the probability density $f_\varepsilon$ of the error is known, we revisit local estimation strategies for several quantities of interest including the probability density function f and the survival function $S^X$ of the signal $X$. We use these results to propose a thresholded plug-in estimation technique for linear functionals in situations where the distribution of the error $\varepsilon$ is unknown, while having some additional data at our disposal. This estimation procedure combines the reconstruction of the unknown Mellin transform of $f$ as well as its regularized inversion by a spectral cut-off. We establish oracle-type upper bounds and discuss rates of convergence in explicit scenarios including estimating $f$ and $S^X$ pointwise. In addition, we develop a fully data-driven choice of the cut-off parameter via model selection, which is able to obtain the oracle risk up to a constant without any previous knowledge of the error distribution. The results are illustrated in a simulation experiment, where we compare different classes of distributions in settings with known and unknown $f_\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Kinematic Signatures of Stellar Flybys in Protoplanetary Discs
papers.abstract: Recent high-resolution molecular line observations of protoplanetary discs have revealed large-scale non-Keplerian features in the gas kinematics of several systems, which can be interpreted as signatures of warps in the disc. Warps can arise from a range of physical mechanisms, and it remains unclear whether the observed kinematic residuals can be uniquely attributed to warping, or to different competing effects. Stellar flybys are one such mechanism capable of both warping a disc and directly perturbing its kinematics. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we study the evolution of protoplanetary discs perturbed by inclined and coplanar stellar flybys, focusing on timescales of several thousand years after periastron rather than the immediate aftermath of the encounter. We find that inclined stellar flybys initially induce warping and twisting in the disc, but that this geometric perturbation is damped on a timescale set by the disc viscosity. Despite this geometric damping, synthetic ALMA observations of the CO kinematics show that complex non-Keplerian spiral features persist in the velocity residuals long after the warped morphology has relaxed, including in coplanar encounters where no warp is ever induced. Fitting these residuals with a simple warped-disc model, the degree of warping in the disc is systematically overestimated. We therefore conclude that kinematic residuals alone are insufficient to establish that a disc is warped, as flybys induce kinematic complexity independently of warps. We further show that scattered light observations provide an independent diagnostic, showing spiral arms and lateral asymmetries.

papers.title: The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
papers.abstract: Previous work found a higher bulk iron-to-silicon (Fe/Si) ratio in rocky exoplanets relative to their host star, traditionally explained by iron enrichment. An alternative explanation is devolatilization of the planetary abundance ratios with respect to the host star, where volatile elements such as O and S are progressively depleted compared to refractory elements such as Fe and Mg, as in Earth. We explore whether these elemental molar ratios are consistent with a devolatilization trend. We revisit the core mass fraction of 14 rocky exoplanets with masses between 0.5 and 10 Earth masses whose host stars have spectroscopic abundances of Fe, Si, Mg, O, and S in the literature. We use interior structure retrievals with two independent forward models, the Marseille Super-Earth Interior model and pyExoInt, to estimate compositional parameters, including elemental molar ratios, from mass and radius measurements. We find that 8 out of 14 exoplanets in our sample present an Earth-like devolatilization trend, while only one planet shows a 1:1 relationship between planetary and stellar abundances. This suggests that devolatilization offers a plausible explanation for the observed non-1:1 relation. The two interior models agree on the devolatilization trend, demonstrating that our derived trends are robust. The main limiting factor in constraining refractory compositions of rocky planets relative to their host star is the small sample with constrained stellar abundances and the lack of variety in orbital distances. The PLATO mission will help by extending the sample of characterized rocky planets to orbital periods of up to one year. The variety in refractory elemental ratio trends may indicate a wide diversity in bulk composition, outgassing and other mantle properties relevant for habitability.

papers.title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a geometric approach to the representation and learning of time-variant parametrizations of deep assignment flows, for binary data labelings on graphs. Each edge carries an optimally controlled parameter flow in a 2-dimensional totally geodesic submanifold, based on objectives derived from a non-local linear scale space representation of the input data. The aggregation of triplets of such flows in 5-dimensional totally geodesic submanifolds is learned from data. The fusion of these flows determines the trajectory in the high-dimensional symmetric parameter space and by geometric integration the layers of binary deep assignment flows. Numerical results demonstrate the expressivity and the limitation of our highly parallel geometric local synthesis approach to high-dimensional deep assignment flow parametrizations.

papers.title: Magnetohydrodynamic spectra and line invariants in the presence of axions
papers.abstract: A new form of the mean-field equations for magnetic fields, which accounts for the interaction with axions, is studied. It is shown that the asymptotic ergodic invariants of magnetic field lines play a key role in the evolution of magnetic fields, which determine the type of the magnetohydrodynamic spectrum of the solutions.

papers.title: Worst-Case Contagion in Financial Networks: MILP Clearing and Robust Loss Analysis
papers.abstract: We study worst-case contagion losses in financial networks with interbank liabilities and common exposures to marketable assets. Existing linear-programming approaches provide exact stress-test values only within an insolvency-resilience margin, where all institutions remain solvent with respect to the external sector. We show that this margin is computed exactly by a finite family of linear programs, one per vertex of the uncertainty ball, whereas a single linear program based on the componentwise worst deterioration of external resources yields only a certified lower bound. We extend this framework beyond that margin in three directions. First, we derive an exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for the maximal clearing vector under arbitrary signed external net positions, providing a clearing oracle for robust stress testing when insolvency can occur. Second, we develop certified bounds on the worst-case loss beyond the margin, including insolvency-pattern enumeration, scenario lower bounds, fixed-pattern dual upper bounds, localized certificates, and a regime-generation procedure with monotone gap certificates. Third, we analyze the worst-case loss curve as a function of the perturbation radius. For $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ price-perturbation sets, the curve is convex, nondecreasing and piecewise linear up to the margin, with breakpoints generated by switches in worst-case shock directions, LP bases, and bank-level activity patterns. Beyond the margin, it remains nondecreasing and piecewise affine, but convexity may fail, the curve may jump upward, and the worst case need not be attained. The framework provides a certifiable MILP/LP methodology for parametric stress testing and interpretable diagnostics identifying the banks responsible for changes in systemic loss.

papers.title: AudioCodex: Streaming Autoencoders for Live Audio
papers.abstract: We introduce AudioCodex, a fully causal autoencoder for live generative audio applications that compresses stereo audio into compact continuous latent sequences at ~10 Hz. It combines a Mean Flow magnitude autoencoder with latent hypersphere projection, bounded-noise augmentation, representation alignment, and adversarial phase recovery to learn representations that support both efficient downstream generation and high-quality reconstruction. Through extensive ablations, we show that AudioCodex outperforms the state-of-the-art in terms of generation-reconstruction trade-off, whilst remaining strictly causal in both encoding and decoding. This work paves the way towards truly real-time interactive and streaming generative audio applications.

papers.title: FAROS: Forecast-Aware Risk-Informed Online Reinforcement Learning for Proactive O-RAN Slicing
papers.abstract: Proactive Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) slicing requires decisions before an approaching quality-of-service (QoS) loss becomes difficult to reverse. We present FAROS, a Forecast-Aware Risk-Informed O-RAN Slicing framework that combines an eight-step QoS forecast, training-only PCMCI+-supported temporal risk, Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE), symbolic feasibility constraints, and reliability-aware Top-K arbitration. MAPPO supplies the actor proposal, while A5v2 checks admissibility and one-step utility before execution. Evaluation uses ten validation-selected frozen checkpoints, 500 matched start indices per seed under the risky-start protocol, and 150,000 agent-level decisions. FAROS obtains mean reward 0.2778 and ten-step recovery 90.56% across ten seeds. A fixed model-matched diagnostic rule reaches reward 0.3015 and recovery 97.57% under the same transition-reward contract, so we make no superiority claim over direct threshold logic. A same-actor M4 shield control also reaches zero risky-state prohibited actions. In the M5 trace, A5v2 changes 22.61% of actor proposals and reduces the predicate-defined prohibited-action rate from 16.79% at proposal time to zero at execution; this property is enforced by the arbiter rather than learned by MAPPO. Independent ns-3 experiments test the six-action interface at packet level and remain separate from end-to-end FAROS claims.

papers.title: ATLAS: A Multi-Procedure Benchmark and Context-Aware Model for Surgical Anatomy Segmentation
papers.abstract: Recognizing anatomical structures during minimally invasive surgery (MIS) could support intraoperative navigation and improve patient safety, but progress is limited by small, single-procedure datasets and by segmentation methods developed for natural scenes. This work addresses both limitations through a new dataset and model. First, we introduce ATLAS-120k, a clip-level semantic segmentation dataset of 121,018 annotated frames from 100 surgical videos, covering 14 laparoscopic and robot-assisted procedures and 41 classes. Annotations were created with a pipeline that combines manual labeling, tracker-based propagation, and review by surgeons. Second, we propose ATLAS (Anatomy Recognition with Context Learning using Foundation Representations), a video semantic segmentation model for surgical anatomy recognition. ATLAS builds on in-domain foundation-model embeddings and adds context queries for the procedure and surgical phase, together with query propagation between frames for short-term memory. ATLAS outperforms state-of-the-art natural-image and in-domain foundation models in both segmentation accuracy and temporal consistency, achieving a Dice score of 0.70 with ViT-L while running in real time at 76.2 FPS. Ablations show that the context queries improve accuracy and that query propagation improves temporal consistency. ATLAS also generalizes well, matching a dedicated model zero-shot on CholecSeg8k and improving phase recognition on AutoLaparo over SurgeNet initialization. The model weights, dataset annotations, and annotation tool are publicly available at https://github.com/TimJaspers0801/ATLAS.

papers.title: Hybrid Source Code Change Impact Analysis
papers.abstract: Change impact analysis (CIA) helps developers identify code entities impacted by their initial changes. While several approaches for CIA were proposed, they still struggle with either low precision or low recall, thereby increasing manual effort for developers to verify the results. Furthermore, limitations in the used datasets and experimental setups can bias the results reported by many CIA approaches. In this paper, we first address the dataset limitations by manually labeling 1,931 changed code entities stemming from 263 commits of 22 open-source Java projects. Next, we introduce two variants of katIA, our code change impact analysis approach that combines static impact analysis with the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). The first variant uses a single prompt (katIA-SP) for refining an initial static impact set while the second variant uses three specialized agents (katIA-MA). The evaluation with our curated dataset shows that katIA-SP with Gemini 2.5 Flash achieved an F1-score of 22.4% when matching impacted entities by their fully qualified names (FQN) and 27.0% when matching them by their class and entity names (CE). The latter shows an improvement of 2.0 percentage points over the state-of-the-art. This score is further improved by katIA-MA which, using Gemini 2.5 Flash, yields an FQN-matching F1-score of 29.1% and a CE-matching F1-score of 33.3%. While these improvements come at the cost of increased median generation time from 0.570 s to 11.214 s and median token usage from 1,235 to 6,462 tokens, the improved performance justifies the additional cost. The comparison of three LLMs using katIA-SP finds that Gemini 2.5 Flash is the most consistent model. These results indicate that combining static impact analysis with LLM-based refinement, particularly with the multi-agent variant, can improve code change impact analysis.

papers.title: Does fare communication format matter? Evidence from a randomised experiment in public transport
papers.abstract: Highly concentrated demand in public transport places pressure on infrastructure and reduces service quality. Pricing instruments-such as discounted off-peak single fare tickets-are a widely used tool for rescheduling demand across time. Yet no study has directly examined whether the price communication format of single fare tickets affects travel behaviour in terms of departure-time rescheduling. To fill this gap, we exploit a randomised stated preference survey conducted in Switzerland based on participants' actual journeys (n = 1,082), assigning participants to one of three price formats: absolute amounts, absolute deviations, or percentage deviations from their current fare. Estimating a multinomial logit model with price-format interaction terms, we find no significant effect of communication format on aggregate price sensitivity. However, for low-fare trips, percentage-based communication substantially amplifies price sensitivity relative to absolute amounts or absolute deviations. Moreover, when prices are shown as percentage deviations, price sensitivity increases for small price spreads and decreases for large price spreads, with a crossover point corresponding to a discount depth of approximately 47%. In summary, these findings suggest that percentage-based price communication has the potential to reinforce the demand-shifting effect of off-peak discounts, particularly for low-fare products and for discounts shallower than approximately 47%.

papers.title: LiveAsset: Learning Intent Assets from Corrective Interactions for Agent Runtime Control
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents acting across web applications and online services often need multi-turn corrections to align their work with users' underspecified goals and preferences. In practice, users may identify problems in the current outcome without specifying the desired result, so learning user intentions requires interpreting each correction against the agent's preceding and revised outcomes. These expectations are often connected to a particular context, making it hard to know when they apply and how to ensure the agent later acts as the user expects. To this end, we propose LiveAsset, an intent harness that learns reusable intent assets from corrective interactions and uses them for runtime control of agent execution. LiveAsset jointly interprets each correction with the agent's original and revised results to infer user intent, incrementally updating the assets while preserving earlier requirements that remain applicable. The learned requirements guide agent execution from task entry and provide criteria for runtime verification, which uses the explanations to assess applicability before each reply is delivered and directs the agent to revise the result to address unmet requirements while preserving those already satisfied. Following a learning phase in which simulated users progressively reveal requirements through multi-turn corrections, we evaluate LiveAsset using same-task replay of the original requests on {\pi}-Bench, PERMA, and Vita and cross-task transfer on PAST-Bench and SkillEvolBench. Experiments show that LiveAsset better fulfills requirements learned from corrective interactions and improves performance on these benchmarks compared with memory, skill, and rule-based harness baselines. Code is available at github.com/landian60/LiveAsset.

papers.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
papers.abstract: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a "poison" dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data. We demonstrate this effect in a variety of settings: subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data. We propose a simple regression model as an explanation. In the poison data, the task and trigger always co-occur, and regularization favors attributing T to the task. Clean data without the trigger causes T to be attributed to the trigger instead. Consequently, the same training examples can have little effect as part of one training set but create a misalignment backdoor in another. This finding exposes a potential limitation of safety methods that audit or filter training data in isolation.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Data Generation for Learning Nonlinear MPC Policies
papers.abstract: Learning MPC requires large datasets generated by repeatedly solving MPC problems. For Nonlinear MPC (NMPC), dataset generation is computationally expensive because feasible initial states are difficult to sample efficiently. The feasible set is often non-convex or even disconnected, and many randomly sampled states are infeasible, leading to wasted optimization solves and unnecessary computational effort. In this work, we propose a data-generation framework for learning NMPC policies that combines active-set exploration with projection-based sampling. First, a bilevel formulation samples activity weights to promote solutions associated with different active sets while preserving optimality for the original NMPC problem; second, a simpler slack-based formulation uses weighted slack variables to target different active sets at the single level. These reference solutions are then used to construct local linearized feasible sets, from which candidate initial states are sampled and projected through the nonlinear NMPC problem to recover feasible and locally optimal training samples. Our approach is up to $37\times$ faster than baseline uniform sampling with $99\%$ acceptance rate, while maintaining a representative coverage of the feasible set.

papers.title: A versatile beamline for attosecond photoelectron and photon spectroscopy
papers.abstract: We report on the development of a versatile attosecond beamline for ultrafast spectroscopy of atoms and molecules, as well as for the metrology of infrared laser pulses. Using a few-cycle pulse (approximately 5 fs) for driving the high-order harmonic generation process, we show that the modulation of the harmonic flux in the cut-off spectral region, induced by a weak perturbing field, enables complete electric-field characterization of the perturbing pulse. Phase-sensitive detection with a lock-in amplifier further reveals polarization-dependent effects, observed as modulations at twice the fundamental optical frequency, emphasizing the sub-laser-cycle electronic control inherent to the measurement technique. In addition, the beamline supports the implementation of two-color (extreme ultraviolet and infrared) phase-sensitive experiments using approximately 30 fs pulses and a velocity map imaging spectrometer (VMI). This configuration will enable the study of photoemission time delays in atomic and molecular systems. Together, these results establish the beamline as a robust and adaptable platform for probing attosecond dynamics across diverse experimental approaches.

papers.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
papers.abstract: We prove versions of (variations of) Erd\H{o}s sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.

papers.title: Automata for MSO over Infinite Trees with Quantification over Borel Sets of Branches
papers.abstract: Rabin's Tree Theorem says that the MSO theory of the infinite binary tree $2^*$ is decidable. Shelah showed that MSO logic becomes undecidable if this tree is extended to $2^{\le \omega}$, i.e. by allowing quantification over sets of infinite branches. A longstanding open problem is whether the decidability can be recovered in $2^{\le \omega}$ by restricting set quantification to Borel sets. We make some progress in this direction, by identifying a suitable automaton model, and showing that most of the automata-theoretic approach to Rabin's Theorem can be extended to the new framework. The only missing part is a conjecture about finite-memory determinacy in certain games. This paper states and explores the conjecture. We prove it in some restricted cases, and give lower bounds on the memory required in those games.

papers.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL) trains agents to adapt to novel tasks from test-time experience, but requires diverse training environments and reward functions. While environments are becoming cheaper to generate, it remains difficult to anticipate every objective an agent may be asked to pursue at test time. Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) learn policies from reward-free data and support zero-shot RL (ZSRL): adaptation to new objectives at test time using a large reward-labeled dataset. Recent work has shown that BFM task inference can instead be performed online without prior task-specific data. We note that this capability positions BFMs and meta-RL as alternative approaches for online adaptation to new reward functions in a fixed environment. We then ask whether we can extend BFMs to compete with meta-RL more broadly, including in novel environments, and identify four challenges: environment identification, online data collection, test-time exploration, and learning from mixed reward supervision. We study each individually, then propose MetaBFM, a hybrid method that addresses all four. During training, it combines supervised reward-following with unsupervised learning; at test time, it can interpolate between exploration, exploitation, and ZSRL-style reward inference. We demonstrate that MetaBFM can recover the in-distribution performance of supervised meta-RL while generalizing to reward functions outside the training set. Our work suggests that BFMs and meta-RL are complementary research directions whose combined strengths allow adaptive agents to learn more diverse behaviors from a fixed set of supervised objectives.

papers.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Modal Chatbot for Tomato Disease Consultant
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a chatbot developed to assist in diagnosing common diseases in tomato plants through natural language interaction. Users can describe symptoms in text. Then, the chatbot responds with the most likely disease, and basic treatment suggestions and related image-based reasoning. The system leverages pre-trained Mistral and Llama 3.2 large language models. The system is also built using LangChain and Streamlit to provide a lightweight and offline-friendly interface. This work targets to support tomato growers a fast and accessible tomato plant health guidance when the technical expertise is not available nearby, especially in the remote areas. The experimental results are promising and encourage further improvement of the chatbot for future real-world deployment.

papers.title: An Agentic Multi-Agent Framework for System Log Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: As enterprise systems grow in scale and complexity, manual log analysis and conventional SIEM tools struggle to keep pace with the volume and diversity of incidents. To address this challenge, this paper proposed a multi-agent AI framework supporting in analyzing the system log to trace the attack forensic in the system more effectively and efficiently. The framework is designed using n8n platform and Gemini large language model. The framework consists of 7 AI agent layers. Each agent work on a specific task. When the task is done, the agent will forward the result to the output-associated agent of the next layer. The multi agent model improves the analysis velocity, so it is able to support numerous log analysis requirement at the same time. We deployed 16 test cases to test operation of the multi agent workflow, and evaluate the accuracy per test case and the operative performance. The result findings are very promising.

papers.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
papers.abstract: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

papers.title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.

papers.title: Reconstructing hourly traffic on every street of a capital from a sparse counting network: a graph neural network applied to Paris
papers.abstract: Micro-scale air quality models require hourly traffic data on every road segment, whereas permanent counters cover only a small part of the network. A graph neural network (GNN) was developed to reconstruct hourly traffic flows on the 32,163 road segments of Paris intra-muros from the 1,573 segments equipped with a counter (4.9%). The model adapts the Graph Neural Network for Urban Interpolation (GNNUI) to a real, sparse counting network. Flows are decoded on the edges of the junction graph (one edge per segment, both directions summed), a traffic climatology serves as an offset in a zero-inflated negative-binomial likelihood, and training proceeds by masking counters. Eight-fold spatial cross-validation, with counters sharing a published series merged before splitting, distinguishes interpolation at a withheld counter in an instrumented district (R${}^2$ = 0.89, error of a quarter of the mean flow) from extrapolation to a district without counters (R${}^2$ = 0.74, a third of the mean flow). These scores hold on main axes where counters are located, while relative errors are about 50% on the few counted local streets. Ablations show that the climatology offset tends to help extrapolation. Road attributes, time cycles and the live state of the counting network matter most, while weather inputs have no significant effect. The masking rate is the only inherited hyperparameter with a clear effect. When evaluated on January--August 2026 (outside the training period), the frozen model stayed around the error band of previous years.

papers.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.abstract:
In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $\Delta^2_{h,2}/\Delta^2_h\simeq0.04\,\Delta^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement.
  We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $\Delta^2_\zeta=c_w\Delta_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4\epsilon$, and $n_T=-2\epsilon$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $\zeta$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$.
  At interferometer frequencies, $\Omega_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $\mu$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.

papers.title: Stochastic Deep Supervision for Gallery-Consistent Early-Exit Face Recognition
papers.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) perform strongly in face recognition (FR), yet their fixed-depth inference limits deployment in resource-constrained settings. We propose SD-ViT, a training framework that gives a usable exit at every block depth by making every depth produce discriminative embeddings, for budget-selected fixed-depth exits. Standard ViTs supervise intermediate layers only through backpropagation, so their intermediate representations are not directly optimized to form usable identity embeddings. SD-ViT adds a stochastic auxiliary signal: at each iteration a randomly selected intermediate block is passed through the same embedding head as the final layer and trained with a weighted margin-penalty softmax loss. The objective is thus stochastically sampled deep supervision through a shared classifier. Because both loss terms share that head and classifier, intermediate tokens are trained to map into the same embedding space as final-layer tokens. This matters for FR, where matching is by similarity: a probe processed at an early exit can be compared directly against full-depth gallery embeddings, with no gallery recomputation or adaptation layers. On established benchmarks, SD-ViT stays within 0.4 IJB-C points of the same backbone trained conventionally at full depth, while its early-exit probes recover over 96% of their own full-depth performance at 50% of the computational cost without modifying the reference gallery. A single verification threshold calibrated at full depth remains usable from quarter depth onward.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
papers.abstract: We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t^{\scriptscriptstyle 2/3})$ under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to $O(1/t)$ under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t)$.

authors.name: Puya Latafat
authors.institution: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca

authors.name: Alberto Bemporad
authors.institution: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca

papers.title: On the Geometric Bottlenecks of Cross-Lingual Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: Transformer-based autoregressive multilingual language models (LMs) are often assumed to store factual knowledge in an interlingua: a language-agnostic latent space. If this assumption holds, a parameter update applied in a source language during knowledge editing should inherently propagate to its semantic equivalents in target languages. However, empirical benchmarks show that cross-lingual propagation of edits often degrades substantially, a degradation that prior work treats largely as an algorithmic symptom rather than a structural bottleneck. In this work, we investigate whether representational anisotropy creates a structural bottleneck for source-only associative-memory editing, and perform a geometric dissection of the cross-lingual propagation gap. Using associative memory-based "locate-then-edit" methods, including ROME, MEMIT, and AlphaEdit, as analytical frameworks, we derive a closed-form decomposition of this gap into key-space propagation, parallel residual mismatch, and orthogonal residual mismatch. Our empirical findings show that cross-lingual propagation is primarily bottlenecked by a large orthogonal residual component, indicating that source-language edits often fail to span the target-language update directions required for successful transfer. Furthermore, we show that post-hoc correction using only source-language residual statistics encounters a large residual-prediction barrier. Finally, we perform a structural realignment via a targeted contrastive alignment objective and find that it substantially improves key-space propagation and partially improves cross-lingual edit transfer, while leaving value-space mismatch as a remaining bottleneck.

papers.title: Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting
papers.abstract: Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.

papers.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
papers.abstract: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE

papers.title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
papers.abstract: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.

authors.name: Luca Antonelli
authors.institution: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research

papers.title: Wolfe's Minimum-Norm-Point Method Generalizes the Simplex Method
papers.abstract: Wolfe's method computes the point of minimum Euclidean norm in the convex hull of finitely many points. The method is parameterized by an insertion rule and it has been an open problem whether Wolfe's original rule guarantees a polynomial number of iterations (De Loera, Haddock, and Rademacher; STOC'18). We resolve this question by proving an exponential lower bound. In fact, we establish a tight connection to the simplex method for linear programming that allows us to transfer many lower bounds for simplex pivot rules to corresponding insertion rules of Wolfe's method. These include not only Wolfe's linopt rule via Dantzig's pivot rule, but also many other classical, randomized and history-based rules. As a corollary, we obtain the first exponential example for the Lawson-Hanson algorithm for nonnegative least squares, as well as PSPACE-hardness of deciding whether the linopt rule ever uses a given point.

papers.title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
papers.abstract: Prompt-based continual learning adapts a frozen pre-trained vision transformer by tuning a small set of prompt tokens. Recently, one-prompt methods which share one single prompt across all tasks make this paradigm maximally parameter efficient. The open question is how a shared prompt can keep the knowledge of old classes while being updated for new ones. Existing methods protect old knowledge in parameter space, where they freeze task-specific prompts, expand new components, or sparsely gate which tokens receive gradients. However, this method sacrifices plasticity, yet the drift it still permits in shared tokens can corrupt the prompt's function on past classes. What must be preserved is the prompt's behavior. We propose TEA-Prompt, which couples (i) a token evaluation module that assigns each prompt token a continuous, input-conditional relevance score injected into the attention logits, softly specializing tokens across tasks without discarding any of them, and (ii) an attention-behavior anchoring loss that constrains each token's attention output around class-specific query regions using only compact Gaussian query statistics without stored old images, weighted by the token's past relevance. Anchoring the attention value allows the parameters to continue updating freely, as long as their interaction remains unchanged. TEA-Prompt achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with markedly lower forgetting on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200 with only 0.38M parameters. Code is publicy available at https://github.com/cuonga1cvp/TEA-Prompt.git

authors.name: Duy-Cuong Bui
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Benefits and Burdens of Technology-Supported Activity Pacing in ME/CFS: A Thematic Analysis of Reddit Discussions
papers.abstract: Technology and self-tracking play an increasingly important role in the self-management of chronic conditions. Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) is a type of energy-limiting condition, with activity pacing as a key self-management strategy that helps individuals regulate their activity within their energy limits to prevent symptom worsening. However, people with ME/CFS frequently adopt technologies designed for healthy bodies, which they have to repurpose to suit their pacing needs. We report findings from a thematic analysis of Reddit data, using the Non-Adoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework as a sensitising concept. We identify three pacing strategies among people with ME/CFS: no-tech pacing, low-tech pacing (e.g., spreadsheets and diaries), and high-tech pacing (relying on continuous passive sensing from consumer wearables), and characterise the benefits and burdens of pacing technology use. Among these, affordability was a salient topic, highlighting the importance of making technology for pacing financially accessible to people with ME/CFS who follow the high-tech route.

authors.name: Michal Dolezel
authors.institution: Prague University of Economics and Business

papers.title: Match the Geometry Before the Surrogate: Extreme Low-Budget Optimization in High Dimensions
papers.abstract: Low-budget molecular optimization is often framed as Bayesian optimization in a learned latent space, but standard benchmarks typically allow hundreds or thousands of evaluations, whereas a realistic wet-lab round may allow only a few dozen. We revisit this regime using a SELFIES molecular variational autoencoder (VAE) with a Gaussian prior and GuacaMol objectives at N = 30 evaluations. The main finding is not a new surrogate model, but an interaction in candidate generation. The encoder means of a reference set of molecules concentrate near a narrow spherical shell, while many high-dimensional optimizers propose candidates from boxes or box-shaped trust regions. We study a simple constraint, the on-sphere scaffold, that restricts candidate generation to this shell. We then introduce two minimal optimizers to probe what remains useful once the support is fixed. GeoWalk performs geodesic local search on the shell without a surrogate. After 30 evaluations, it shows no detected difference from a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate on the shell, which is ahead earlier in the budget. GeoCMA adds covariance learning in a random subspace. It does not improve on GeoWalk in the molecular benchmark. On LassoBench it has a lower mean loss than GeoWalk, but full-dimensional CMA-ES remains stronger on most tasks. A factorial experiment with a single GP crosses the candidate support (shell or box) with the acquisition maximizer (a finite candidate set or a continuous optimizer). In this benchmark, shell candidates outperformed box candidates when acquisition was maximized over a candidate set, but not with continuous maximization by L-BFGS-B. These results come from a controlled study of one Gaussian-prior VAE benchmark and do not recommend VAEs for molecular optimization. The practical lesson is to control the candidate support and the acquisition maximizer before attributing a gain to the surrogate.
