authors.institution: Skobeltsyn Institute of Nuclear Physics, Lomonosov Moscow State University

papers.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
papers.abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.

papers.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

papers.title: Multi-objective Markov Decision Process: Set-valued Bellman's principle and fixed point perspective
papers.abstract: We study infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes with multiple cost objectives and finite state and action spaces. We consider the set of value functions generated by randomized Markov policies, where each function describes the expected discounted costs from all initial states under a single policy. We establish a set-valued Bellman equation and characterize this set as the greatest fixed point of the associated Bellman operator. We also show that choosing an attainable cost vector separately for each initial state can produce a function that no single Markov policy realizes. Nevertheless, the attainable costs at individual states satisfy their own Bellman recursion. These results provide a dynamic programming and fixed point framework for multi-objective Markov decision processes.

authors.name: Birgit Rudloff
authors.institution: Vienna University of Economics and Business

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
papers.abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidity for one day. These results demonstrate that mica substrates enable high-mobility, flex-out-compatible In2O3-based TFTs.

authors.name: Ying-Hao Chu
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids

papers.title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
papers.abstract: As ferroelectric devices approach the nanometer scale, their behavior becomes increasingly sensitive to boundary conditions. In perovskite oxide nanocapacitors, epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening are well-established control parameters. Then, while expected to contribute to the epitaxial stabilization of ferroelectric ultrathin films, the lattice-dynamical state of the electrodes has not been isolated as an independent tuning knob. Here we call this poorly explored coupling interfacial phonon bias, whereby the electrodes' phonon energy landscape reshapes that of the adjacent ferroelectric across their shared interface. Using first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular-dynamics simulations, we examine this mechanism in symmetric BiFeO${}_3$ nanocapacitors in contact with a metallic perovskite oxide. By independently controlling the orientatio and amplitude of the electrodes' octahedral-tilt landscape, while keeping conventional elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed, we show that the electrodes' phonon energy landscape can modify the stability of competing BiFeO${}_3$ phases. In particular, this allows us to shift the ferroelectric transition temperature and even induce antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions. We thus showcase interfacial phonon bias as a complementary and powerful strategy to modify and optimize the properties of ultrathin epitaxial films.

authors.name: Inigo Robredo-Magro
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Chemical Physics of Solids

authors.name: Urmimala Dey
authors.institution: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Brief introduction to post-quantum cryptography in industrial applications
papers.abstract: The development of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is directly motivated by the necessity to secure information in the face of the quantum threat. This paper provides an overview of recent developments relevant to PQC adoption across several industrial applications, including IoT, healthcare, civil and infrastructure engineering, and defense. We present a brief, self-contained overview of PQC and its market positioning. We perform implementation experiments on selected quantum-safe methods and quantify several aspects, such as the quantum resources required to break common cryptographic schemes, as well as the performance of the most well-known PQC algorithms. We also discuss the resistance of different PQC classes to quantum attacks and the status of PQC implementations in different programming languages. Finally, we present benchmark results on KEMs and signature algorithms to help select the appropriate algorithm for a specific application based on criteria such as algorithm performance, data lifetime, and level of data sensitivity.

authors.name: Mateusz Zarski
authors.institution: Institute of Theoretical and Applied Informatics

authors.name: Jarosław Miszczak
authors.institution: Institute of Theoretical and Applied Informatics

papers.title: ProofDiff: Auditable Argument-Level Comparison of AI-Generated Mathematical Proofs
papers.abstract:
Mathematical understanding depends on the route from hypotheses to conclusion: how the parts of a proof function and which dependencies carry the argument forward. This structure can persist when wording or notation changes, while a small alteration to a hypothesis or inference can produce a different argument beneath similar prose. Formal verification can establish that a rewrite proves the same theorem, but not whether it follows the same mathematical route. Comparing informal proofs, especially those produced or revised by generative models, therefore requires reconstructing which claims, dependencies, and reasoning steps are preserved, reorganized, or replaced.
  We present ProofDiff, a system for comparing informal mathematical documents. It is designed to support human review, not to certify mathematical correctness. Given two documents, ProofDiff independently constructs a source-grounded argument map for each and proposes correspondences between the resulting maps. Each map captures the document's claims and reasoning steps and records the typed relations that connect them. An integrated human-review layer allows reviewers to revise the maps and correspondences while preserving an auditable history. Comparing the two argument maps provides a basis for inspecting whether the documents follow the same mathematical route and where their claims or dependencies differ. We demonstrate ProofDiff on four illustrative pairs of AI-generated proofs, ranging from a detailed proof and its concise revision to proofs using different mathematical strategies.

authors.name: Kevin Gomez
authors.institution: Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Eduardo V. Teixeira
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Coherent Electrometer Using Hybridised Double Quantum Dot - Resonator States
papers.abstract: Probing the change in conductance or reactance of a charge sensitive system using an rf cavity is a standard way of doing fast single-charge electrometry. In this article, we present a detector concept which is instead based on coherent interaction. We show that the coherent interaction between a microwave resonator and double quantum dot gives rise to a fast, highly sensitive electrometer. The coherent electrometer achieves a state-of-the-art readout speed, resolving two charge states with SNR of 11.7 in 16 $\mu$s, with a readout signal two orders of magnitude lower in power than previously required to reach this speed. In this way, heating of the sample becomes negligible. Thanks to its sensitivity and low dissipation, the coherent electrometer opens up the avenue for quantum limited charge detection with nanosecond speed and minimal back-action.

authors.name: Sebastian Lehmann
authors.institution: Leibniz Institute for Solid State and Materials Research

papers.title: Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
papers.abstract: We study a joint optimal dividend and voluntary liquidation problem for a company whose surplus follows a spectrally negative L\'evy process and is subject to Omega-type regulatory termination. Dividend payments are modeled as a singular control, while voluntary liquidation is an optimal stopping decision with a state-dependent liquidation payoff. When the surplus falls below a regulatory solvency threshold, an Omega clock accumulates the time spent in distress and may terminate the firm before voluntary liquidation occurs. Under dynamic programming and continuity assumptions for an auxiliary Markov subproblem, we characterize its value as the smallest controlled stochastic supersolution of the associated quasi-variational inequality. We prove that any regular stochastic solution with a dividend barrier coincides with the value function over all admissible dividend and liquidation policies, and hence is unique within this class. Using $\omega$-scale functions, we construct single-band, singleton, and no-liquidation candidates, establish sufficient conditions for global optimality, and give conditions under which these candidates supply the unique regular barrier stochastic solution. Brownian and Cram\'er--Lundberg examples illustrate how regulatory parameters affect dividend and liquidation boundaries and generate transitions between policy regimes.

papers.title: Descriptor: UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC)
papers.abstract: Anchor self-calibration estimates the positions of fixed nodes of an indoor radio positioning or localization system from observations among the nodes and to mobile devices. It replaces the survey of every anchor, which is costly and goes stale when anchors move. The UWB Anchor Self-Calibration Dataset (UWB-ASC) is a testing ground for such methods, recorded in one industrial hall with ultra-wideband (UWB) two-way ranging. It has three parts. The first is two measured deployments. In the line-of-sight (LOS) deployment, 10 anchors range with a walking tag tracked by motion capture. In the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) deployment, 12 nodes range among obstructions, and one of them roves over surveyed markers in 20 quasi-static sessions. Both deployments also hold static sessions, and a total station surveyed every fixed node. The second part is a seeded range simulator that draws synthetic ranges on the surveyed geometry with adjustable error components, from noise-free ranges to NLOS errors, for benchmarks at controlled error levels. Its 81 frozen draws in 5 conditions serve as the reference. The third part is a set of readers that convert the ranges among the static nodes of two public UWB datasets, TWR-CLOUD-Bern and selfloc, into the same format without redistribution. All parts share open Parquet and YAML files, in which topology views select the ranges for each class of calibration method. Raw recordings with rebuild scripts, quality reports, and field labels of the line of sight complete the dataset.

papers.title: Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas
papers.abstract: Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.

authors.name: Ostap Okhrin
authors.institution: Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
papers.abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

papers.title: MAGE: Towards Generalizable Multi-timescale EEG Representations
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data plays an important role in understanding human brain activity, with various major applications. While current approaches, which largely build on EEG foundation models, have demonstrated strong performance across datasets and tasks, they typically rely on a fixed temporal scale. This design choice limits their ability to capture characteristics of neural dynamic behavior, often spanning across multiple timescales, which are naturally captured in EEG recordings. To address this limitation, we propose MAGE (\textbf{Multi-timescale Adaptive Generalization for EEG}), a foundation model that dynamically adapts to capture and integrate information across different timescales. Specifically, MAGE combines two key mechanisms: (i) a novel multi-timescale attention mechanism, capable of learning representations across multiple temporal scales and (ii) a trainable aggregation module, that dynamically identifies and adapts to the most informative timescale of the input signal. Experimental results across seven datasets demonstrate that MAGE consistently outperforms existing EEG foundation models while using substantially fewer parameters. Moreover, our results support the hypothesis that different downstream tasks benefit from distinct temporal scales. All source code will be released.

authors.name: Tuan-Kiet Doan
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

authors.name: Phi Le Nguyen
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
papers.abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.

papers.title: The full length of short pants
papers.abstract: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $\Gamma_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $\Gamma_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes \Gamma_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.

papers.title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
papers.abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

authors.name: Benjamin M. Kent
authors.institution: Istituto di Matematica Applicata e Tecnologie Informatiche

papers.title: Cryptanalysis of operad-based cryptography
papers.abstract: Commutative operads have been proposed as a platform for public-key cryptography, with protocols for key agreement, key exchange, encryption and authentication, together with a masking technique and families of algebras with secret parameters intended to strengthen them. We show that breaking key agreement, key exchange and encryption reduces to two problems over the centralizer of the public operations: an interpolation problem for key agreement and a division problem for the other two. Neither problem requires recovering a secret, and the set from which secrets are drawn plays no role in these attacks. For the operad platforms in the two original papers (fields, the integers, residue rings, the tropical semiring with finite entries, convexors and the masked tropical algebras), the relevant problems can be solved in polynomial time in the input models specified here, and masking does not affect these attacks. The authentication protocol fails for a more elementary reason: as originally stated it does not bind the prover to any public key, and even with a registered public key the response expected by the verifier can be computed from public data. In the masked variant, verification requires the secret mask; on the concrete string platforms, one observed session with an invertible challenge entry suffices for forgery. We also observe that one of the auxiliary constructions satisfies the algebra axioms only in a degenerate case, although the corresponding protocol remains correct. The attacks are implemented and verified on random instances of representative platforms.

papers.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
papers.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the eye, the propagation of a few-cycle pulse through a slab, Cherenkov radiation, amplification and second-harmonic generation. Feynman's arrows are made quantitative with the sheet method, and coupled-dipole simulations show the incident wave being cancelled and replaced inside the medium. The connection with quantum theory is discussed where the classical picture stops: the photon, spontaneous emission and the forbidden lines of the aurora, vision and photosynthesis, and the sum over paths. The text is addressed to undergraduate students and their teachers, and to any reader curious about the physics behind everyday optical phenomena; derivations are collected in separate panels, and the animations and the Python codes used for the figures and simulations are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Causal discernment and the direction of clinical research
papers.abstract:
A clinical trial can establish an intervention's effects while leaving their causal pathways unresolved. We call causal discernment the practice of identifying explanations that fit the evidence but imply different decisions or research directions, and seeking studies that distinguish them.
  METHOD: We combine causal graphs and prose around four questions: delivery of the intended target change, routes of benefit and harm, stability of causal relations across regimes, and whether unresolved pathways could change the decision. With quantitative assumptions, graphs support plausible reasoning by showing which findings could distinguish explanations even when effects are not identified. Prose specifies clinical meaning, effect size and timing, and supporting evidence. We use conceptual analysis, hypothetical calculations, CAST and lipid-lowering therapy.
  SUBSTANTIVE RESULTS: Concordant coronary associations for HMGCR and PCSK9 perturbations support LDL mediation over target-specific explanations predicting unequal effects per unit of LDL reduction, but leave a shared receptor pathway possible. Diabetes associations leave LDL lowering, receptor-mediated uptake and weight gain as possible explanations. An illustrative causal record specifies a genetic comparison and assumptions under which it could distinguish them.
  CONCLUSION: The causal record formalises the reasoning behind the choice of the next study by making competing explanations, evidence and assumptions explicit and stating what each design could resolve. Prepared before a design or recommendation is adopted, it enables scrutiny of that reasoning and interpretation of results in relation to the stated explanations. Its added value over ordinary rationale review remains to be assessed.

papers.title: Robust and Private Swarm Learning via Zero-Knowledge Validator Admission and Consensus Aggregation
papers.abstract: Swarm Learning improves resilience and removes the need for a single trusted coordinator by distributing model aggregation and validation across participating nodes. However, it also delegates the validation of model updates to peers whose private data may be biased, unrepresentative, or adversarial, and existing Swarm Learning protocols generally do not attest that data, leaving decentralized validation as an attack surface. We present a robust, privacy-preserving Swarm Learning framework that makes verifiable data quality the condition for admission to the learning task. A validator joins only after a zero-knowledge attestation proves, without revealing any raw sample, that a reference model ran correctly on its private data. The attested outputs also yield a label-free class profile, so the network assembles a collectively IID validator pool from individually skewed validators as accurately as an oracle with the true labels (total-variation distance to uniform 0.025, against 0.021 for the oracle and 0.21 for random selection). Admitted validators score client updates and, through a Tendermint-style Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus, agree on a gradient mask and a quality-derived aggregation weight for each submission, replacing dataset-size weighting with a quality-aware signal. Adapting the cut-layer idea of Split Learning, a challenge-based audit lets peers re-verify that a mask was computed on the attested data without an expensive end-to-end zero-knowledge proof. Across four benchmarks under non-IID partitions the framework matches FedAvg on clean data; under a gradient-scaling attack that collapses FedAvg to random chance, it retains 94% of clean accuracy on CIFAR-100 and over 99% on FashionMNIST, where FedAvg achieves only 2.1% and 11%. The result is a private, robust, and auditable foundation for decentralized learning.

papers.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

papers.title: Polarization Aware Deep Learning Framework for SAR Despeckling
papers.abstract: Speckle is an inherent characteristic of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery that complicates image interpretation and the extraction of reliable information. Although deep-learning-based despeckling methods have demonstrated promising performance, their applicability across different polarimetric configurations is often limited by the need for specialized architectures or separate training procedures. This paper presents a unified deep-learning framework for despeckling single-, dual-, and full-polarization SAR data using a single trained convolutional neural network. The proposed approach adopts a common nine-channel representation of the polarimetric covariance matrix and a polarization-aware masking strategy to accommodate different configurations without modifying the network architecture. Qualitative and quantitative comparison on three different scenes from different sensors demonstrate competitive performance across the considered experiments and support the feasibility of a unified, polarization-flexible approach to SAR despeckling across different polarimetric configurations.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $\eta>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(\eta^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincar\'e inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

papers.title: Admissible geometries for Talenti's P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle
papers.abstract: Talenti symmetrization rearranges functions on an open connected set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, endowed with a measure $\mu$ with continuous positive density, along the superlevel sets of a given function $f$. Talenti proved a P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle for it, provided that these sets are $\mu$-isoperimetric, have connected boundaries, and are crossed by straight lines of steepest ascent. We show that, if $X$ is convex, these requirements are very rigid: they force the superlevel sets of $f$ to be either parallel half-spaces, or concentric balls, or complements of tubes around an affine subspace of codimension at least two. This identifies the only geometries in which Talenti's P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle can be applied. We also prove a family of weighted isoperimetric inequalities in convex cones, showing that complements of tubes around affine subspaces of every codimension at least two do occur.

papers.title: Reaching the last mile? How Design Decisions Shape Medical Device Qualification and Classification of Patient Support Chatbots in the EU
papers.abstract: Few AI chatbots have transitioned the 'last mile' from research prototypes to clinical practice, partly because mapping conversational design decisions to regulatory requirements is complicated. This paper presents a design-oriented regulatory analysis of a chatbot supporting stroke survivors. Using Design Space Analysis operationalised through the QOC (Questions, Options, Criteria) framework, HCI researchers and legal scholars assess how variations in three conversational functions - health Q\&A, recovery monitoring, and motivating medical adherence - influence qualification and classification under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and AI Act (AIA). Our findings show that seemingly minor design decisions - such as role, actionability, and proactivity - influence regulatory obligations. The paper contributes insights into ten conversational design considerations influencing regulatory interpretation and demonstrates how QOC can support integrating legal considerations into human-centred design workflows. Finally, we suggest compliance-aware pathways to market, while reflecting on whether all chatbots should pursue the 'last mile'.

papers.title: Pandemonium: Longform Target-Speaker Speech Recognition with Cross-Speaker Interactions
papers.abstract: Diarization-conditioned target-speaker ASR (TS-ASR), in particular Diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW), is an accurate and data-efficient approach to multi-talker transcription. It has, however, three structural limitations: the model transcribes each speaker independently, operates on short (30 s) windows, and optimizes its diarization and TS-ASR components separately. We address the first two. We integrate the diarization conditioning into a longform Parakeet backbone (DiCoP) and add cross-speaker attention, which lets the model attend across the speaker dimension so that speakers are no longer decoded in isolation, and an STNO mask refiner that re-estimates the diarization-derived conditioning. As conversational data with genuine multi-speaker interaction is scarce, we scale training with a pseudo-labeling pipeline that mines 5.4k hours of in-the-wild multi-speaker audio from YODAS2. Combining these with synthetic and real data yields state-of-the-art results across several meeting benchmarks. We open-source the resulting models, DiCoP and Pandemonium, and the pseudo-labeled data.

papers.title: Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings. This enables high-resolution arrays that improve spatial processing for downstream tasks such as speech enhancement. However, existing methods rely on supervised training with ground-truth signals captured at virtual locations, requiring datasets that scale with the number of virtual microphones (VM) and leaving open the question of how to design optimal large-array configurations. We propose Virtual-Flow, a flow-matching framework that implicitly generates VM signals conditioned on real recordings, without requiring ground-truth VM signals. We introduce a semi-supervised training strategy based on pseudo-VM targets constructed from time-delayed superpositions of real recordings. Virtual-Flow shows improved magnitude estimation in high-frequency bands, yielding richer spatial cues for beamforming. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Virtual-Flow, combined with reflow distillation, outperforms existing neural-VME baselines in VM-based beamforming and achieves competitive end-to-end speech enhancement performance with low computational cost.

papers.title: CoilStellaration: A Dataset and Benchmark for Engineering-Aware Stellarator Coilset Generation
papers.abstract: Stellarators are fusion devices that use externally generated, three-dimensional magnetic fields to confine hot plasma and offer a promising route to commercial fusion. Their electromagnetic coils pose a challenging design problem: they must reproduce the target magnetic field while satisfying engineering constraints and remaining practical and cost-effective to manufacture. Finding suitable geometries is a highly nonlinear inverse problem that generally has neither a closed-form nor a unique solution. This problem lies at the heart of stellarator design. We introduce CoilStellaration, a dataset and benchmark for learning the mapping between coil geometries from target plasma magnetic fields and engineering requirements. The dataset contains 177,000 optimized filamentary coilsets targeting plasma equilibria from ConStellaration, with sampled engineering requirements and achieved geometric and magnetic-field metrics. It spans multiple coil counts and field-period numbers, supporting studies of both specialized and shared models across configurations. The benchmark asks models to predict coils conditioned on a target equilibrium and requirements on coil-coil and coil-plasma spacing, curvature, and magnetic-field error. We show that magnetic-field accuracy remains the main challenge, with learned models rarely satisfying all requirements simultaneously. However, using learned predictions to initialize conventional coil optimization can accelerate early progress. We release baseline models and evaluation code to support reproducible research on both direct coil generation and learned optimization initializations. By lowering the barrier for machine learning and optimization researchers to engage with stellarator coil design, we aim to accelerate progress toward practical, cost-effective stellarator power plants.

papers.title: When Is Prosocial Behavior Intuitive? The Moderating Role of Empathic Perspective Taking
papers.abstract: Why is prosocial behavior intuitive for some individuals but deliberative for others? We examine whether empathic perspective taking moderates the association between reflective processing and prosocial choice. We run a laboratory experiment with 652 participants, where we measure prosociality using a four-player Distribution Game that holds aggregate payoffs constant and orders allocations from self-regarding to egalitarian. We combine participants' choices with the Perspective Taking subscale of the Interpersonal Reactivity Index, a five-item Cognitive Reflection Test, and choice-stage response time in the allocation decision. Perspective taking significantly moderates the association between response time and prosociality. At high levels of perspective taking, longer response times are associated with modestly lower prosociality; at low levels, the association is positive but not statistically significant. No comparable moderation emerges for Cognitive Reflection Test performance. These results are consistent with the possibility that, when others' outcomes are readily represented (high perspective taking), prosocial choices may arise relatively quickly, while additional decision-specific processing may be associated with greater attention to their private cost. When others' outcomes are less salient (low perspective taking), additional processing may instead help bring them into consideration. The findings highlight the importance of distinguishing processing proximal to the specific decision from domain-general analytic reflection when explaining whether prosocial behavior appears intuitive.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
papers.abstract: Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.

papers.title: Modelling socio-economic effects of the pandemic in a metropolitan area
papers.abstract: One of the most notorious measures taken by authorities in every country trying to prevent the uncontrollable spread of the Covid 19 pandemic was to impose severe measures to diminish the mobility of people. In recent publications we proposed a mathematical model to address the consequences of these measures and to predict the infections under different scenarios, for various different countries. In this paper we extend the model, called the BTH--SEIRS-model, to deal with the reduction of mobility in an urban area. The chosen region was the densely-populated metropolitan area around Helsinki, the capital of Finland. This choice obeyed to the fact that there are precise data related to mobility from a mobile telephone company, and that this region was completely isolated from the rest of the country for a short period during the pandemic. We also used public transport data from railways and the accommodation occupation rates in the area of interest. We show that the BTH--SEIRS model is capable of simulating the real infection data as well as the mobility-related economic activity, exhibiting the main trends present in the three indicators used for comparison. Our calculations allow us to highlight the difference of the behaviour of the pandemic in a totally different spatial scale, and to discover the hidden factors that govern the behaviour of people who are forced to commute every day from home to work.

papers.title: OmniSynth: A Meta-Evaluation Framework for Benchmarking the Quality of Missingness-Inclusive Synthetic Health Data
papers.abstract: Synthetic data are an emerging solution to the reproducibility crisis in machine learning for health, driven by data privacy restrictions surrounding electronic health records. Yet no consensus exists on how to evaluate synthetic health data quality, existing metrics functionally overlook missingness despite its prevalence in clinical data, and benchmarking frameworks have never been empirically validated. We introduce OmniSynth, a modular Python benchmarking suite that evaluates synthetic tabular data across fidelity, missingness similarity, utility, and privacy - the first framework to explicitly evaluate missingness as a distinct dimension of synthetic data fidelity. OmniSynth further proposes a meta-evaluation procedure that stress-tests evaluation performance under controlled degradation scenarios, providing a systematic characterization of how an evaluation framework behaves across datasets, sample sizes, and variable types. Applying this procedure to OmniSynth in two health datasets (Pima Indians Diabetes; MIMIC-IV-ED), we found that scores responded monotonically to degradation, three of four novel missingness metrics captured induced missing data patterns, and individual metric contributions to the scoring system were empirically justified.

papers.title: Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network for Brain Tumor MRI Segmentation
papers.abstract: The segmentation of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an essential step for computer-aided neuro-oncology, treatment planning and follow-up. While effective encoder-decoder representations are achieved by U-Net and Attention U-Net, the skip sections of the network can generate weak-contrast or noisy responses in the case of heterogeneous boundaries of the tumor. In this paper, we introduce a Quality-Governed Deep Learning Network (QGDL-Net) that can be used for binary tumor segmentation from FLAIR MRI slices. The proposed model is able to predict the slice quality based on contrast and SNR statistics and to fine-tune the encoder features prior to decoding by learnable quality gates. We used the 80:20 train-validation split for experiments with BraTS 2021. QGDL-Net achieved a Dice of 0.9747, IoU of 0.9506, precision of 0.9755, recall of 0.9739, F1 of 0.9747 and accuracy of 0.9982, outperforming U-Net and Attention U-Net. The EigenCAM maps and segmentation overlays provide better tumor localization and interpretable activation around the lesion regions.

papers.title: Towards a Privacy-Preserving Reliability-Aware Entity Resolution for Attributed Graphs [Vision] (Technical Report)
papers.abstract: Entity resolution (ER) on attributed graphs aims to identify nodes across multiple graphs that correspond to the same real-world entity and merge them into an integrated graph. When input graphs vary in quality and contain sensitive information, ER faces a dual challenge: while reliability information is crucial for accurate graph data integration, its presence in the published integrated graph can heighten privacy risks. This paper presents a research vision that unifies reliability assessment and privacy preservation within a single graph ER process. We highlight the inherent tension between these two objectives, propose a three-level coupled framework, and outline the remaining research challenges to enable the publication of integrated graphs that are both accurate and privacy-preserving.

papers.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
papers.abstract: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization estimates descent directions from function values alone, which removes the activation storage required by backpropagation and makes it attractive for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing low-rank ZO methods either parameterize the additive update through Euclidean factors with a non-unique representation, or restrict each finite-difference direction to be low-rank. In this work, we propose to constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen, so the learned update remains rank-constrained throughout fine-tuning. On this geometry, we build a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator that projects a random matrix onto the tangent space, normalizes it to correct the scale mismatch induced by projection, and further propose Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) and its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S. We show that the ambient finite difference matches its retracted counterpart, the normalized estimator recovers the Riemannian gradient in expectation, and ZO-RGD converges under trajectory-regularity conditions. Experiments on LLM fine-tuning tasks show that the proposed algorithms are competitive with strong forward-only baselines across model families and tasks, with gains in several settings.

papers.title: Induced-Minor-Free Graphs Admit a Star-Based Separator of Size $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$
papers.abstract: Given an $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, we construct a balanced separator of $G$ consisting of $\tilde{O}(|V(H)|\sqrt{n})$ star subgraphs. Our result is an induced-minor-free analog of the famous separator theorem for $H$-minor-free graphs by Alon, Seymour, and Thomas [J. Amer. Math. Soc., 1990]. A key idea in our construction is a new decomposition of $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, analogous to the cop decomposition for $H$-minor-free graphs by Andreae [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 1986]. We also discuss several algorithmic applications of our result.

papers.title: Permutons
papers.abstract: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

papers.title: SWHForest: A Structural Curation and Search Layer for Large-Scale Code Corpora
papers.abstract: Pre-training code language models relies on massive code corpora usually streamed over the internet. However, researchers rarely need a multi-terabyte archive in its entirety; instead, their workflow centers on curated subsets: selecting well-documented files, filtering out repetitive boilerplate, auditing for benchmark contamination, or retrieving specific code patterns. Yet, because modern corpora are typically published as file pointers and basic attributes rather than source text, no general structural layer exists to select which files to download: curating a subset requires downloading and parsing millions of files first just to discard most of them. We present SWHForest, an open-source framework and public dataset that provides this missing structural layer for any pointer-based corpus without redistributing source code. A single pass over the archive parses each file into an AST and immediately discards the source text, keeping only its structural summary. Queried locally or exposed by archive providers as a server-side filtering API, SWHForest selects matching files first (via SQL or index intersection) and downloads only surviving candidates. Across the ten largest languages of Stack-Edu (52.1M unique files, 341M definitions), SWHForest answers curation queries in milliseconds while cutting downloads by 46-72%, reducing live structural searches from hours of per-language streaming to seconds or minutes.

papers.title: Binary pulsar studies with multi-wavelength sky surveys. II. Companion star follow ups
papers.abstract: The identification of the stellar companions to binary pulsars and the extraction of the physical information encoded in their optical spectra are key to study the evolution of the binary system and how this is influenced by the interactions between the two stars. Obviously, extending the characterisation of the companion star spectra over an as large as possible wavelength range allows one to maximise the amount of information. In Paper I, we used 11 source catalogues built upon multi-wavelength (optical, infrared, ultraviolet) imaging sky surveys to search for the stellar companions of 144 field binary pulsars (i.e. not in Globular Clusters) selected from the Australia Telescope National Facility (ATNF) pulsar catalogue. For nine of these pulsars, for which the companion star had been already identified, we obtained new spectral information from imaging photometry in the surveys' bands. In particular, for some of these pulsars we provided the first possible detections of the companion star in either the ultraviolet or mid-infrared. Here, we serve this additional flux information as a base to update the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the companion stars and the multi-epoch catalogue photometry to look for flux modulation at the orbital period of the binary system.

papers.title: Evidence for Ambipolar Diffusion from Ion-Neutral Velocity Drift in HH 212
papers.abstract: We present the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 7 observations of the hyperfine structure of C$^{17}$O (3-2) and the H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ (4-3) molecular line emissions of the Class 0 protostellar system HH 212 at $\sim$ 44 au spatial resolution. Radiative transfer models interpreted in the framework of non-ideal MHD of the envelope allow us to estimate an envelope mass of $M_{env}\sim0.12\,M_\odot$ and a mass infall rate of $\dot{M}_{env}\sim4.4-5.7\times10^{-6}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, consistent with values reported in the literature. The models also reveal a systematic radial velocity drift between the neutral tracer (C$^{17}$O (3-2)) and the ionized species (H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ (4-3)) of $0.1-0.3$ km s$^{-1}$, exceeding the spectral resolution of 0.105 km s$^{-1}$ and consistent with possible ambipolar diffusion in the envelope. The ambipolar diffusion fraction, $f_{AD}\sim 0.1-1$, and the Hall parameter, $\beta_{i,H_2}\gg1$, indicate partial ion-neutral decoupling, with non-ideal effects becoming more significant toward the inner regions. In the envelope, our analysis shows that rotational energy decreases from $\sim 50\,\%$ of the gravitational energy at $R_{cen}$ to $\sim 25\,\%$ at $2R_{cen}$ and $\sim4\,\%$ at 1100 au. In contrast, for $B_0=1$ mG, magnetic energy increases from $\sim 0.4\,\%$ of the gravitational energy at $R_{cen}$ to $\sim2.6\,\%$ at $2R_{cen}$ and $\sim20\,\%$ at 1100 au. The drift velocity expected from radial force balance is consistent with the modeled drift velocity within $\sim300-400$ au of the central source but is lower at larger radii. These results are consistent with a scenario in which ambipolar diffusion leads to partial ion-neutral decoupling, allowing neutrals to move faster than ions within the envelope.

authors.name: Chin-Fei Lee
authors.institution: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute

authors.name: Jyun-Heng Lin
authors.institution: Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics, Academia Sinica

papers.title: Prestatability in the Macroscopic Limit
papers.abstract: We examine whether the variables required for a future macroscopic description of a given physical system can themselves be stated in advance. Representing macroscopic descriptions as coarse-grainings of a fixed microscopic phase space, we distinguish formal prestatability, concerning the existence of an effective complete vocabulary of admissible macroscopic distinctions, from dynamical prestatability, concerning whether the future relevance of those distinctions is decidable. Both obstructions disappear for finite microscopic state spaces. In the infinite limit, exhaustive formal prestatability can fail, while a restricted predictive architecture may remain formally pre-statable. We construct such an architecture and show that, under universal dynamics, the future relevance of a candidate variable is equivalent to the halting problem. Thus a fixed microscopic phase space can support macroscopic descriptions whose future variables are not fully pre-statable.

papers.title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
papers.abstract: We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. The subspace model reduces the per-iteration computational cost, which allows scalability. The analysis relies on a general framework for the complexity of adaptive stochastic processes that carries the almost-sure analysis of ASTRO-DF into the STORM setting and adds expected bounds by a direct counting argument, without the renewal-reward argument of Blanchet et al. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. The first algorithm, ASTRA-F, proceeds in a STORM-like manner: the trial point and the incumbent are re-evaluated on an independent set of replications, so that the estimates entering the acceptance test are independent of the model, as every existing STORM-type analysis requires their accuracy to be assessed conditionally on the model. The second, ASTRA-R, allows a practical approach: the trial point is evaluated on the replications already drawn to build the model, which avoids re-evaluating the incumbent, needs one adaptive sample size per iteration instead of two, and reduces the randomness entering the iteration. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.

authors.name: Coralia Cartis
authors.institution: Mathematical Institute of the Slovak Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Strong Backdoor to Forests is FPT: Tight Linear-Time FPT for Essentially General SAT
papers.abstract:
In a seminal work, Gaspers and Szeider [FOCS 2013] gave a fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) approximate algorithm for finding a strong backdoor of size at most $k$ to incidence treewidth at most $t$, for a given CNF-formula $\phi$. In particular, their algorithm runs in $f(k,t) |\phi|^3$ time, and finds a strong backdoor to treewidth at most $t$, of $\phi$, of size at most $2^k$ whenever there exists one of size at most $k$. Determining whether the detection of strong backdoors to bounded incidence treewidth is FPT parameterized by $k+t$ was left open in their work and this has been repeatedly posed as an open question by Gaspers and Szeider, for example in [The Multivariate Algorithmic Revolution and Beyond 2012] and more recently in [Computer Science Reviews 2025], even for incidence forests and when the input is a $3$-CNF formula. We answer this question affirmatively.
  We show that strong backdoors to forests can be found in linear-FPT time on arbitrary non-tautological CNF formulas (not just on 3-CNF formulas). Given such a formula $\phi$ and a budget $k$, our algorithm finds a strong backdoor to the class of forests, of size at most $k$, or correctly reports that none exists, in $2^{2^{O(k)}} |\phi|$ time. Moreover, we show that our result is as tight as it can get. First, we show that finding strong backdoors to treewidth $t$ for any $t \geq 2$ is W[1]-hard, even on non-tautological 3-CNF formulas. Second, the running time of our algorithm is tight: it is linear in the input size and a better than double-exponential dependence on $k$ in the running time would imply a $2^{o(N/\log N)}$-time algorithm for solving 3-SAT on $N$ variables, which would beat even the very recently claimed sub-exponential algorithm for solving 3-SAT by OpenAI and Anthropic.

papers.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
papers.abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_\sigma-\min m_\sigma$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.

authors.name: Wenqi Zhu
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Discriminator-free adversarial domain adaptation for robust speech classification
papers.abstract: The performance of speech classification systems such as speech emotion recognition or pathological speech detection can degrade substantially when there is a domain shift between training and test data. This shift can arise due to e.g., differences in recording setup, acoustic environment, speaker, language, or speaking style. Adversarial domain adaptation addresses this problem by encouraging representations that are less sensitive to domain-specific differences. However, many adversarial approaches rely on training a separate domain discriminator, which can be unstable and difficult to train. In this paper, we propose to use a discriminator-free adversarial learning network (DALN) for unsupervised domain adaptation in speech classification tasks. DALN reuses the task classifier as an implicit discriminator and aligns domains through the nuclear-norm Wasserstein discrepancy on classifier outputs. We extensively evaluate the performance of DALN on intra-lingual, cross-lingual, and noisy adaptations for speech emotion recognition and pathological speech detection. Extensive experimental results show that DALN generally achieves the best performance across the considered tasks and domain shifts, outperforming discriminator-based domain adaptation approaches.

papers.title: SCLAP: Temporal structural alignment improves localization in long-form audio
papers.abstract: Audio-text models such as Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining (CLAP) typically pool frame and token sequences uniformly into global embeddings. This discards temporal structure and impairs both retrieval and localization, especially for short events in long recordings. We introduce SCLAP, a sequence-level contrastive framework that aligns audio frames and text tokens using monotone one-dimensional optimal transport. Its learned marginals and transport plan provide fine-grained temporal supervision from clip-level captions alone. On short-form audio (i.e., Clotho and TACOS datasets with 15-30s recordings), SCLAP remains competitive for retrieval while improving zero-shot localization over CLAP and Text-aware Attention Pooling. On long-form audio (i.e., CASTELLA dataset with up to 300s recordings), SCLAP improves retrieval performance and its localization advantage grows as the event-to-context ratio decreases. At inference, SCLAP requires no optimal transport computation since retrieval can use pooled embeddings and localization can use inexpensive frame-text cosine scores.

papers.title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

papers.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Differentiable model predictive control (MPC) enables structured, constraint-aware policies to be optimized end-to-end. However, learning MPC policies faces two bottlenecks: (1) nonsmooth sensitivities at active-set transitions and (2) expensive policy evaluation, since each requires an optimization solve. We first introduce SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver combining sequential quadratic programming (SQP) with a log-barrier-smoothed alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) inner solver. Its design enables smooth gradients, exact sensitivities at convergence, and efficient execution on GPUs. Second, to efficiently train MPC policies, we pair our solver with first-order reinforcement learning (FORL) using Short-Horizon Actor-Critic (SHAC), which reuses rollout MPC solutions instead of repeatedly re-evaluating them. Comparisons with state of the art solvers show that the approach achieves up to $4.4\times$ higher end-to-end training throughput. On a vehicle racing task, our method achieves higher returns than MPC PPO with a $46\times$ speedup, training on 3.3 million transitions in only 7 minutes. Finally, we use the framework to train a more reliable MPC racing policy via RL with domain randomization, and validate it on a full-scale race car. We integrate our advances into the open-source TurboMPC solver.

authors.name: John Zhang
authors.institution: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center Shreveport

papers.title: Standoff chemical identification of harmful aerosols
papers.abstract: Aerosols - solid or liquid particles suspended in air - are an effective means of dispersing chemical warfare agents and toxic pharmaceuticals, posing acute risks to public safety and security. Exposure to aerosol particulate matter in the environment and in industrial settings has also been linked to respiratory and cardiovascular disease. In both cases, rapid chemical identification is key to generating early warnings and attributing sources. Established methods chemically identify aerosols only after extracting a sample, while standoff techniques such as lidar classify aerosols only into broad categories. Chemical identification at a distance is hindered by aerosol extinction signatures that are weak, spectrally broad, and obscured by far stronger absorption from ambient gases. Here, we demonstrate time-resolved, standoff chemical differentiation of aerosols with dual-comb spectroscopy and machine learning identification algorithms. The high spectral resolution of dual-comb spectroscopy allows ambient gas absorption to be removed, and the algorithms identify chemicals without knowledge of aerosol size and morphology. We demonstrate identification of aerosolized benzyl fentanyl (a fentanyl simulant) in mixtures with other aerosols in a standoff measurement through ambient H2O, CO2, and CH4. Despite the aerosol producing only subtle, <1% changes in the extinction spectrum across hundreds of wavenumbers, we find the limit of identification to be an order of magnitude below lethal concentrations for a 1 m aerosol cloud. This technique provides a new paradigm for performing rapid chemical speciation of aerosols using their infrared absorption signatures without extractive sampling. Together with advances in chip-based mid-infrared dual-comb spectrometry, we anticipate this technique will enable real-time networks for standoff detection of aerosol emissions and aerosolized chemical threats.
