By unifying geometric and physical metrics under a polymorph-aware protocol, OPAL-Bench enables a more comprehensive assessment of generative quality in CSP.

authors.name: Sergio Rincon
authors.institution: Instituto de Biología Funcional y Genómica

papers.title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
papers.abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.

authors.name: Pal Burai
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

authors.name: Gergely Kiss
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

authors.name: Patricia Szokol
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: YRC-Bench: Benchmarking Culturally Aware Machine Translation for Historical Heritage via Tri-Level Semantic Bridging
papers.abstract: Translating historical cultural heritage poses profound challenges for machine translation systems due to the acute semantic asymmetry across eras and cultures, where terse classical syntax frequently obscures domain-specific cultural knowledge. While Large Language Models have demonstrated remarkable prowess in generic translation benchmarks, they struggle to negotiate Culturally-Specific Items and diachronic shifts in domain-rich historical texts, such as Yellow River cultural records. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce YRC-Bench, the first human-curated, multi-parallel benchmark dedicated to historical heritage translation across Classical Chinese, Modern Chinese, and nine target foreign languages. YRC-Bench establishes a tri-level parallel corpus incorporating modern explanatory glosses as explicit semantic bridges and operationalizes translation strategies through paired conserved versus substituted CSI variants categorized by cultural translatability. Systematic evaluations of nine leading LLMs across bidirectional translation directions reveal that leveraging modern Chinese glosses - especially human-curated ones - dramatically elevates both lexical fidelity and semantic adequacy. Furthermore, multidimensional human preference audits by native experts unveil distinct cross-cultural preferences between Sinographic-tradition and non-Sinographic language groups.

authors.name: Jiayi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals
papers.abstract:
We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets.
  For the classical visibility model, it was previously known due to Glivick\'y that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed when $S$ is well-ordered. We prove the same result for backwards well-ordered sets, even in the case when $S$ has no first element.
  In the full-visibility version of the game, Glivick\'y proved that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed if the standing set has a first element. We extend this result to arbitrary nonempty standing sets.

authors.name: Daniel Hegedus
authors.institution: The German Marshall Fund of the United States

papers.title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
papers.abstract:
Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements.
  We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, $\tau^{-0.26(2)}$, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events.
  We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.

authors.name: Kristof Benedek
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

authors.name: Michelle T. Cirunay
authors.institution: Institute for Technical Physics and Materials Science

authors.name: Attila Balogh
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

authors.name: Balint Hartmann
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

authors.name: Geza Odor
authors.institution: Institute for Technical Physics and Materials Science

papers.title: How Hard Is Tokenisation? Algorithms and Complexity Beyond NP-Hardness
papers.abstract: Given a collection of strings and a vocabulary budget, how well can we minimize its total token count, and how does the answer change with the tokenisation model? For binary direct tokenisation, previous work proved APX-hardness but left constant-factor approximability unresolved \citep{kastreva2026}. We rule out every polynomial-time $M^{1-\varepsilon}$ approximation, for fixed $\varepsilon>0$, unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, even on distinct equal-length strings with $K=m-1$. Here $M$ is the total input length and $m$ is the number of input strings. We complement this lower bound with a deterministic polynomial-time $O(M/\log M)$ approximation algorithm and stronger bounds for selected vocabulary budgets. For the different objective of maximizing compression savings, GreedTok was shown to attain a constant fraction of the optimum on unrestricted alphabets \citep{baliga2026}; we establish a deterministic EPTAS for direct savings on every fixed alphabet and analyze greedy selection by true marginal gains. For exact optimization, we give a binary direct algorithm running in $2^{O(n\log\log n/\log n)}\poly(I)$ time, where $n$ is the total length of the distinct input strings and $I$ is the input encoding length. Finally, we resolve two unary merge-model hardness questions left by the bounded-alphabet study \citep{kastreva2026}: standard unary bottom-up tokenisation is APX-hard, and unary optimal pair encoding is strongly NP-complete, strengthening the previously known weak hardness.

papers.title: TANSAR: Editable and Attributable Correlation Matrix Memories under Correlated Keys, with Rule-Constrained Multi-Hop Knowledge Editing
papers.abstract: Correlation Matrix Memories (CMMs) store associations as sums of rank-one outer products, providing closed-form addressability, exact deletion, and linear attribution. While classical analyses assume random, orthogonal keys, semantic encoders produce correlated representations. We analyse CMMs under correlated keys using frame-theoretic coherence: (i) capacity bounds yielding an encoder-independent limit $n \le d(1+\varepsilon^2)$ for mean squared crosstalk $\varepsilon^2$; (ii) an exact characterisation of the collateral effect of deleting an association, guaranteeing that deletion never invalidates certified associations; and (iii) a geometric transparency bound demonstrating why attribution requires candidate sets of centred keys. On this basis, we introduce Topology-Aware Neuro-Symbolic Associative Retrieval (TANSAR). TANSAR traverses a directed acyclic association graph, prunes invalid paths via sound ground Horn constraints, and injects a representation derived strictly from the verified path into the residual stream of a frozen language model, guarded by a Clopper--Pearson selective-risk gate. Controlled experiments confirm all theoretical bounds. In multi-hop knowledge editing, Horn pruning reduces answer contradictions from 25.1% to 0.5%, whereas Hopfield retrieval incurs 24% contradictions when stale associations remain stored (and 0% if stale associations are removed). An end-to-end edit transaction requires 13.6 ms on a standard CPU and 2.37 ms on GPU. The symbolic component matches gold labels across all 600 ProofWriter theories and achieves 94.0% agreement on FOLIO, demonstrating sound and efficient multi-hop associative retrieval with exact unlearning.

authors.name: Mourad Oussalah
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

papers.title: The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps
papers.abstract:
Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown.
  We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, we prove that \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n}=0, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n\log n}=1. \] Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth.
  We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.

authors.name: Balazs Maga
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: Vacuum energy interacting with dark matter and dark radiation: alleviating the $H_0$-$S_8$ seesaw
papers.abstract: Extensions of $\Lambda$CDM that raise $H_0$ with additional energy before recombination, such as dark radiation and early dark energy (EDE), also raise $S_8$. We study whether a late-time energy exchange between the vacuum and the dark sector can offset this increase. The coupling rate scales as $\bar m H^{\alpha}$ and is negligible before recombination for $\alpha \le -2$; the energy is transferred along the four-velocity of geodesic cold dark matter, so the dark matter produced by the vacuum carries no density perturbation and slows the growth of structure. We add the exchange to dark radiation ($\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM) and to a one-parameter EDE model ($\bar m$EDE), and constrain the models with Planck 2018, DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ data (CBS), and with the SH0ES calibration added (CBSH) to test the exchange when $H_0$ is held at a high value. For CBS the posteriors favour an energy flow from the vacuum into dark matter at 1.8-2.7$\sigma$, and the exchange lowers $S_8$ by 0.02-0.08 but does not raise $H_0$: $\bar m\tilde\Lambda$CDM gives $H_0 = 68.83 \pm 0.91$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, 3.1$\sigma$ below SH0ES. For CBSH the exchange removes the increase of $S_8$ caused by dark radiation, giving $S_8 = 0.800 \pm 0.016$ at $H_0 = 71.34 \pm 0.70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, and about a third of that caused by EDE for $\alpha = -2$, with the coupling at 1.1-2.0$\sigma$. The reduction of $S_8$ is concentrated at $z \lesssim 0.3$: at the redshifts probed by KiDS-Legacy the lensing amplitude decreases by only 1-2%, the shear $\chi^2$ of the dark-radiation models changes by less than 3, and the exchange reduces but does not remove the excess shear $\chi^2$ of EDE. A late-time exchange can therefore offset part of the $S_8$ increase of early-time solutions, but it does not ease the Hubble tension, and current data do not require it.

authors.name: She-Sheng Xue
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Perugia

papers.title: Optimal Proximity Black Hole Search with Programmable Matter
papers.abstract:
The concept of programmable matter (PM) envisions objects composed of tiny, mobile particles capable of self-arrangement, which allows them to change shape, color, and move.
  We initiate the study of the Black Hole Search problem within the context of PM. The problem involves a dangerous and unnoticeable location, the black hole, that, without a trace, destroys any particle visiting it. In our setting, particles move inside a convex area embedded in a triangular grid, where one vertex is a black hole. The objective is for the particles to identify a restricted set of vertices containing the black hole while ensuring that at least one particle survives.
  We present an algorithm utilizing three particles capable of assuming just two colors to identify the dangerous region where the black hole resides. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this algorithm is Pareto optimal in terms of number of particles and number of colors required, and asymptotically optimal in terms of number of epochs, where an epoch refers to the minimal time window within which each particle completed an activation cycle at least once.

papers.title: Physics-Based Differentiable Beamforming for Deep Learning-Based Contrast Enhanced Ultrasound Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.abstract: Ultrasound is widely used for vascular imaging because it is non-invasive, real-time, and cost-effective. However, its spatial resolution remains limited by diffraction to an order of the acoustic wavelength. This limitation is particularly restrictive for imaging of the microvasculature and high-resolution vector-flow-imaging. In this work, we present a multi-channel physics-based deep learning approach to super-resolve monodisperse microbubbles directly from multi-channel radio-frequency (RF) data. We also present a novel image-based metric for model evaluation. The proposed pipeline combines a learnable deconvolution network with a differentiable beamforming layer, enabling a direct deconvolution of the microbubble (MB) signature prior to image formation. By operating on multi-channel RF data, the method aims to improve localization robustness in the presence of dense microbubble populations and deconvolve the lateral direction in a relatively low-frequency regime (1.7 MHz) where MBs exhibit nonlinear behavior. The model is trained and evaluated on simulated data using monodisperse lipid-coated MBs over a broad range of acoustic pressures and microbubble densities. The proposed method improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the single-channel approach. It achieves sub-wavelength axial and lateral resolution while slightly improving robustness to dense microbubble populations outside the training domain. It also demonstrates generalizability across transmit configurations without requiring explicit training on each transmit configuration.

papers.title: Sub-Thouless energy scale in interface-dominated unconventional superconductor junctions
papers.abstract: We derive the conductance in unconventional superconductor - normal metal - normal metal junctions, taking into account the resistance between the normal metals. We show that applying Tanaka--Nazarov boundary conditions at both superconductor and normal metal interfaces reveals a new characteristic low-energy scale which is sub-Thouless in the experimentally relevant strong-interface regime. This scale governs, among other quantities, the curvature of the local density of states (LDOS) and the width of conductance dips near the zero-bias conductance peak in triplet superconductor junctions, thereby replacing the Thouless energy as the dominant low-energy parameter. We derive universal $s$-wave proximitized diffusive metal expressions for the zero-bias LDOS and differential conductance which solely depend on the interface and bulk resistances, independent of the superconducting gap and Thouless energy scale. This framework provides a possible origin of the anomalous low-bias conductance features observed in unconventional superconductors, offering a refined mechanism for interpreting interface and correlated electron physics in experimental hybrid junctions.

papers.title: KL-Regularized Policy Iteration for Adaptive LQR: Gain Updates and Probing from One Policy Improvement
papers.abstract: Policy-gradient methods for adaptive linear quadratic control improve the feedback gain of an unknown plant online by gradient-type steps computed from closed-loop data. A recent framework of such methods, policy-gradient adaptive control (PGAC), takes one gradient-type step per sample, which its indirect form computes from an estimated model and its direct form directly from the data. Because data generated by a fixed linear feedback cannot identify the plant, PGAC adds a probing perturbation to the input and leaves its covariance as a design parameter. We study the adaptive LQR problem through a KL-regularized formulation, in which the probing is the randomness of a Gaussian policy kept close to a Gaussian reference policy, so that the cost of the probing is part of the objective. One policy improvement of this formulation gives a gain update together with a probing covariance. We show that, for suitable references centred at the current gain, this gain update is exactly PGAC's Gauss-Newton or natural-gradient update with any step size below a bound. We repeat this policy improvement, each time against a tempered copy of the current policy, and refer to this scheme as KL-regularized policy iteration (KLPI). On a known plant and with tempering, the cost of KLPI's gains converges linearly to the optimal cost, and the probing covariance keeps a floor proportional to the regularization weight. On an estimated plant, under conditions like PGAC's (small updates and sufficiently informative data), the closed loop stays stable, the cost of the gains converges linearly up to a bias, and the probing covariance again keeps this floor. In simulations at equal probing cost, the shape of KLPI's probing covariance, which PGAC can adopt, lowers the extra cost caused by suboptimal gains on nearly all tested plants, whereas KLPI's use of past iterations in its gain update changes this cost little.

papers.title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: When interior-point methods are applied to solve numerical trajectory optimisation problems, they spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system, associated to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem. Riccati-type algorithms exhibit linear complexity in the trajectory horizon. Parallel-in-time algorithms are able to reduce this to logaritmic complexity by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses, the accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

papers.title: Full-sphere emission and reception directivities of seven echolocating bat species
papers.abstract: Echolocating bats shape their calls and the returning echoes with their noseleaf or mouth, head and pinnae. Understanding these spectrospatial directivity patterns is central to bat echolocation. We describe a dataset of simulated far-field emission and reception directivities of seven echolocating bat species from three families (Phyllostomidae, Rhinolophidae and Vespertilionidae). For each species, the head of one preserved specimen was scanned with micro-computed tomography and converted into a closed surface mesh, on which the responses of both ears and of the emitter were computed with a boundary element method or, for the two mouth-emitting species, with an analytical piston model. The complex-valued responses cover the full sphere at 2.5 deg resolution from 20 to 160 kHz in 0.5 kHz steps. They come with the meshes, the landmarks of ears, nostrils and mouth, alternative source positions and skeletons for posing the pinnae and noseleaves, all in one frame, and with Python and MATLAB code. The technical validation covers solver verification, mesh convergence, comparisons with earlier simulations and measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

papers.title: Sample-Covariance Regularization for Data-Driven Predictive Control from Frequency Response Functions under Colored Noise
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate how sample covariance obtained from frequency-response functions (FRFs) can be exploited to improve performance of data-driven frequency-domain predictive control (FreePC) in the presence of colored measurement noise. In case of periodic multisine excitation, this covariance is obtained directly from repeated periods and provides a frequency-dependent measure of uncertainty without requiring an additional parametric noise model. To incorporate this information into both indirect and direct predictive control, we develop a frequency-domain subspace predictive controller (FD-SPC) and establish its equivalence to the direct FreePC formulation in the noiseless setting. Regularization terms for both formulations are then motivated by expected prediction-error criteria and constructed from the sample covariance of the FRF estimates. Across all tested noise models and data sizes, regularization consistently reduces the median realized control cost relative to the corresponding controller without covariance regularization, with reductions of up to 35%.

papers.title: Spectral Bias Reduction in Local Gated ReLU Architectures
papers.abstract:
Neural networks trained by gradient-based methods learn the low-frequency content of a target function faster than its high-frequency content. This spectral bias is well documented, but it is much less clear which architectural choices mitigate it and which cannot. We study the question for shallow ReLU models linear in their trainable parameters, where each mode is learned at a rate given by a Gram-matrix eigenvalue, and for a general symmetric bilinear form $a(\cdot,\cdot)$, so that least-squares regression ($a=$ the $L^2$ inner product) and variational or physics-informed losses ($a=$ the $H^1$ energy form) are two instances of one analysis.
  Within this framework we propose gated local ReLU dictionaries, obtained by multiplying each ReLU feature by a hat partition-of-unity weight, in the spirit of partition-of-unity finite elements and overlapping Schwarz methods. The resulting Gram matrices are block-banded for any local bilinear form, with a block-Toeplitz interior whose matrix-valued symbol governs the spectrum.
  The two forms then behave very differently. For $L^2$ regression, the symbol is bounded away from zero, the ratio is uniform in the number of windows, and the measured spread of frequency-dependent learning rates falls from $1.9\times10^{5}$ to $4.5$ at matched model size. For the $H^1$ stiffness matrix, the symbol vanishes at zero frequency: gating leaves the $\Theta(N^2)$ conditioning intact and inverts the frequency ordering instead of removing the bias. A preconditioner built from the same interior stencil will fix the spectral bias, showing that architecture alone is not enough. Experiments on $1$D regression and Poisson problems confirm the dichotomy, and the regression effect persists when the hidden-layer parameters are trained as well.

papers.title: Self-Healing by design: Immune-system inspired autonomous cyber resilience
papers.abstract: Digital innovations have strongly improved ship capabilities, including command, control & communication, navigation and combat management. In the wake of digitisation and geopolitical stress, resilience against cyber-attacks has become a key challenge. Autonomous Cyber Resilience (ACR) methods, inspired by features of the human immune system, provide a promising perspective. Proofs of concept of autonomous self-healing and self-protecting software have been realised in cloud environments using containerisation, monitoring and deployment technology. However, developing a suitable "cyber immune system" for more complex digital systems is still an intricate challenge. In this paper, we share insights on how ACR methods can be combined with resilience mechanisms present in critical naval and aeronautical manoeuvring systems. Using TNO's "OpPic" application, we show how TNO's Self-Healing for Cyber Security software can provide autonomous mission- and threat-adaptive resilience. On this basis, six guidelines for the design of autonomous cyber resilient systems are derived. The ultimate goal is to enable operators to oversee and control their system's "cyber immune response", to be able to continuously adapt to evolving threats and mission priorities.

papers.title: Reducing Cold-Start Latency on the WebAssembly Edge via Locality and Network-Aware Scheduling
papers.abstract: Edge computing places computation closer to users and data sources, but introduces heterogeneous hardware, limited resources, and variable network conditions. WebAssembly (Wasm) is increasingly considered for these environments because modules are compact, portable, and quick to start. However, cold-start latency remains a challenge: when a worker node does not yet hold the required artifact, it must fetch it before execution, adding transfer overhead that directly increases the end-to-end (E2E) latency, especially for large artifacts or slow network links. At the same time, the geographical distance between the requester and the assigned worker independently contributes to latency through network routing overhead. Together, artifact locality and network proximity do not always point to the same placement decision, and naive scheduling strategies fail to account for either. This work extends a Wasm-native edge orchestrator with state-aware scheduling strategies that jointly optimize for both objectives. Evaluation on a Raspberry Pi testbed with emulated regional network latency shows that a hybrid scheduler combining cache-state and network-proximity signals reduces mean E2E latency by up to 40.8% compared to a default round-robin baseline. Artifact locality-aware placement is most effective when artifacts are large or repeatedly requested, while network-aware placement dominates when artifacts are small and routing latency has a larger relative effect, but combining both objectives consistently yields the lowest E2E latency across diverse edge workloads.

papers.title: WasmLens: Automatic Glass-Box Instrumentation for Composed WebAssembly Applications
papers.abstract: The WebAssembly Component Model enables language-independent composition of independently developed components, but complicates observability. Existing tracing support flattens execution hierarchy by attributing every span created inside a composition to a single host-level parent context, so execution across component boundaries cannot be reconstructed. The problem is amplified because components are typically deployed as black boxes whose internals cannot be modified or inspected by the system integrator. To address these limitations, we propose a revised wasi:otel/tracing design in which the runtime maintains a per-component span stack, restoring parent-child relationships across component boundaries without changing component interfaces or source code. This change has since been adopted upstream. Building on this design, we present WasmLens, an automatic instrumentation tool that derives instrumentation points from a composition graph and injects tracing middleware into already composed binaries, yielding end-to-end traces for black-box compositions with no developer configuration. This automatic instrumentation raises mean request latency from $238$ $\mu$s to $454$ $\mu$s across six component boundaries. Raising the expected number of boundary crossings from 6 to 11 further increases latency to $514$ $\mu$s, an incremental cost of $12$ $\mu$s per crossing, of which $10.4$ $\mu$s is attributable to instrumentation. These results show that instrumentation overhead is additive in composition depth rather than proportional to baseline execution time.

papers.title: Representation Learning for 3D Brain Imaging: A Benchmark
papers.abstract: Many deep learning architectures for computer vision tasks rely on features extracted by a pre-trained encoder on large databases of natural 2D RGB images. However, the wide domain gap with medical images hampers the direct transfer of optimized deep learning models from computer vision to clinical applications. Recently, self-supervised pre-training and foundation models emerged as promising alternatives to mitigate these limitations. Yet, constructing such models for medical imaging faces critical challenges, including designing and adapting training strategies for large 3D volume datasets, and the need for standardized benchmarks to evaluate feature extraction performance. In this study, we propose an extensive comparison of vision encoders with a focus on 3D brain MRI. First, we consider 8 fully and self-supervised models pretrained on natural images (e.g. ResNet, DINO, CLIP) and 10 backbone architectures trained on medical images, either based on supervised (e.g. RadImageNet) or self-supervised (e.g. BiomedCLIP, SimCLR) tasks. All pre-trained encoders are evaluated on various downstream tasks to assess the representation power of their latent representations, including age and sex prediction as well as disease classification on the ADNI and PPMI datasets. Our study shows that 2D encoders pre-trained on natural images perform the most favorably, even compared to models pre-trained on more than 100k brain MRI volumes, highlighting the need for more suitable and robust methods for representation learning in 3D medical imaging. The source code for this study is publicly available at: https: //github.com/PierreFalconnier/brain-representation-benchmark.

papers.title: The Challenge of Modeling the Complexity of Use for the Measurement of Digital Maturity in Education
papers.abstract: Measurement of teachers' digital maturity can be useful in diagnosing technology adoption in education and in supporting teachers' professional development. However, there is a lack of easily usable tools in the existing literature. By investigating the most effective ways to measure teachers' digital maturity, our research aims to fill this gap. The focus of this article is on a data-driven approach to the assessment of digital maturity in education. Following a process similar to teaching analytics (data collection, data modeling, data understanding and visualization, and contextual understanding), we draw on diary data collected from 12949 French primary school teachers using a virtual learning environment (VLE) during the 2022--2023 school year. Specifically, the paper presents results related to modeling and visualizing data. To this end, we propose a critical analysis of two automatic classification techniques, one supervised rule-based and the other unsupervised (hierarchical clustering). In addition to providing different scales to measure, we have proposed a new approach to diagnose and visualize digital maturity. In this way, the method provides insight into the diversity and intensity of technology use, contributing to a better understanding of digital maturity and providing a practical tool for assessing day-to-day teaching practices.

papers.title: Same Pixels, Different Documents: Measuring Part-Level Editability in Image Vectorization
papers.abstract: Image vectorization is often evaluated by rendering fidelity, which cannot distinguish documents that render identically but support different edits. Edit-based evaluation tests outcomes, but an oracle that gathers a part's fragments can conceal the cost of selecting them. We introduce Pass@k, which tests whether a prescribed edit can succeed using objects selectable within k clicks under a specified interaction model. Eight document diagnostics characterize properties relevant to editing beyond these tasks. We assess structural sensitivity through controlled perturbations, practical relevance through designer operations, and reference dependence through alternative drawings. We evaluate twelve open and commercial methods on 211 references, with 635 edit tasks on 93 of them. In each of four reference sets, including two drawn by designers, 64-88% of oracle-passed tasks on parts composed of multiple shapes fail at Pass@1, against 6-40% for single shapes, pooling counts over configurations. Higher fidelity does not guarantee higher Pass@1, while selected diagnostics are associated with designers' effort in our study.

authors.name: Boheng Zhu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Virtual Task Prompting for Multi-Task Scene Understanding
papers.abstract: Multi-task scene understanding models typically rely on modified vision encoders or complex decoders for cross-task interaction, which limits their flexibility and compatibility with off-the-shelf vision foundation models (VFMs). We introduce Virtual Task Prompting (VTP), which frames multi-task prompting as retrieving task-adaptive compositions from a shared virtual state, where both the state and routing process are optimized in an end-to-end manner. Concretely, VTP maintains an expanded set of virtual tasks alongside the backbone. At each layer, learnable routing matrices read task-specific compositions as input to interact with image tokens and write the processed results back, forming explicit pathways that capture the intricacies among tasks outside the encoder. Since VTP keeps the backbone clean, it integrates seamlessly with pretrained VFMs, advancing the state of the art on Pascal-Context and NYUD-v2. Stress test on Taskonomy with 13 heterogeneous tasks further shows VTP's robustness in extreme settings. Ablations and analysis indicate that VTP's gains stem from adaptive routing rather than increased capacity. The project page is available at https://jacky1128.github.io/VTP/.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface.
  The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.

papers.title: SAFE-Hair: Scalp-Anchored Fields for Exportable Single-View Hair Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Single-view 3D hair reconstruction has progressed rapidly, but many methods optimize for visual plausibility rather than producing strand assets that can be directly used in grooming, editing, or simulation pipelines. We propose SAFE-Hair, a framework that reconstructs explicit strand grooms from a single portrait by decoding hair from persistent follicles in a canonical scalp-UV domain. Given a fitted template head, SAFE-Hair projects self-supervised image features onto the scalp, uses a conditional Rectified Flow model to generate latent scalp fields, and decodes occupancy, segment directions, length allocation, and total length at a fixed set of scalp follicles. This representation enforces scalp-rooted strand identities by construction and enables direct export with follicle IDs and guide-family metadata. We further introduce attachment, collision, and bending priors to improve geometric validity without per-subject test-time optimization. To evaluate both reconstruction fidelity and asset usability, we introduce HairBench-3D, a benchmark built from public 3D hair assets with standardized alignment, rendering, resampling, and metrics for geometry, direction consistency, invisible-region completion, silhouette agreement, and collision. SAFE-Hair improves Chamfer distance from 3.74 mm to 3.28 mm, F-score from 77.9 to 81.7, invisible-region F-score from 66.1 to 69.8, and penetration ratio from 4.8% to 3.9% over the strongest baseline.

authors.name: Yuetong Wu
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.

authors.name: Colin Faverjon
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. We introduce EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework that integrates diffusion modelling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous US datasets. EvoDiff formulates sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process, in which diffusion-based optimization in feature space guided by information gain produces synthetic probes, and only the real unlabeled samples retrieved by these probes are annotated and used for downstream training. Across six benchmarks covering fifteen datasets and 16,696 images, we evaluate EvoDiff on convolutional network and transformer-based foundation model. EvoDiff approaches fully supervised performance with substantially fewer labels, outperforms active learning baselines, and improves foundation model generalization under cross-domain external validation on unseen cohorts. A reader study with six radiologists indicates the potential to support clinical annotation workflows, with a model-based estimated 24% to 84% reduction in annotation workload at matched downstream performance.

authors.name: Ruixiang Qi
authors.institution: Affiliated Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Westlake University, School of Medicine

papers.title: A Systematic Comparison of In-Context Learning Strategies for Peptide Property Prediction in Low-Data Regimes
papers.abstract: Peptide sequence-property relationships are often highly non-linear, but can be learned with machine learning models and exploited for the design of new materials and bioactive compounds. Various methods based on transformer architectures have become available for molecular property predictions. These foundation models promise straightforward inference and prediction of properties of new materials through in-context learning. Benchmarks of individual model architectures exist, but a systematic comparison of various foundation models against classical baselines on similar datasets is lacking. Here, we provide a systematic evaluation of the predictive performance of various in-context learning strategies. We compare several large language models, tabular foundation models, and typed decision models against an XGBoost baseline. We evaluate predictive performance on binary and multiclass classification tasks on pH-dependent surface activ-ity, IR spectral signatures, self-assembly, and anti-cancer activities. Our results show that ICL is competitive, yet does not significantly outperform classical baselines, and performance varies between models and tasks. Our findings further suggest that language models use both in context examples and knowledge acquired during pretraining to infer properties of unseen samples. This finding indicates that pretrained models can leverage the existing literature for predictions, but may also bias their predictions towards established sequence-property relationships.

papers.title: Towards in vivo photon dosimetry using radiation-sensitive mixed-core ultrasound phase-change contrast agents
papers.abstract: Objective. Advanced radiotherapy applies complex treatment plans that require verification of the beam delivery. Therefore, in vivo dosimetry, measuring delivered radiation doses directly on the patient, has become increasingly important. Radiation-sensitive phase-change nanodroplets were recently proposed for in vivo radiation sensing. The radiation-induced conversion of superheated nanodroplets into microbubbles generates ultrasound contrast from which radiation deposition can be derived. While successful for in vivo proton range verification, previously used nanodroplet formulations were not suitable for in vivo photon dosimetry due to stringent requirements on the degree of superheat of the nanodroplet core. Here, we used a mixed-core strategy, combining different perfluorocarbons in the same nanodroplet core, to modulate the photon response and droplet stability at body temperature. Approach. Lipid-shelled nanodroplets with different cores (pure octafluoropropane, pure decafluorobutane and a 17:4 (v/v) octafluoropropane:decafluorobutane mixture) were dispersed in deionized water in phantom containers and irradiated with a photons at various temperatures. Simultaneous high-frame rate ultrasound acquisition allowed to link ultrasound contrast generation to the radiation delivery. Nanodroplets were characterized using 19F NMR spectroscopy. Main results. Photons induced nanodroplet-mediated ultrasound contrast strong enough for clinical applications at body temperature. A clear trade-off was observed between a stronger photon response and maintaining sufficient droplet stability. Neither octafluoropropane (lacking stability) nor decafluorobutane (lacking photon response) cores proved suitable. On the contrary, the mixed-core formulation exhibited a strong photon response with minimal background already at small radiation doses (0.1 Gy). This paves the way for future in vivo dosimetry.

papers.title: OfficeTwin: Realizing 3D Reconstruction of Redundant Scenes through Partial Viewpoint Perception
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction turns an uncalibrated monocular stream into a dense point cloud in a single inference pass, orders of magnitude faster than classical structure-from-motion (e.g., COLMAP), and reliable on the weakly textured, repetitive surfaces where keypoint matching fails outright. However, raw point clouds lack the object identity, physical properties, and watertight volume required for robot learning. This gap widens under robot-native capture. A camera mounted on a robot constrained to a few degrees of freedom sees each object only partially, and the repetitive, weakly textured structure of an office makes distinct workstations nearly indistinguishable, leaving redundant and partial observations that downstream reconstruction cannot resolve. Existing image-to-3D generation methods struggle with these conditions, hallucinating geometry under incomplete views and confusing repeated instances. We present OfficeTwin, a robot-native framework that converts these incomplete observations into simulation-ready digital twins. OfficeTwin first imposes metric and structural constraints, then exploits the office's structural redundancy by registering repeated cubicles into a shared canonical frame, where complementary observations recover geometry occluded in any single view without hallucination. On a real office scan, OfficeTwin recovers every cubicle as an individually watertight, metric solid, outperforming feed-forward reconstruction and generative baselines that fail to produce simulation-ready assets.

papers.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
papers.abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.

papers.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
papers.abstract: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the {\it general} theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied {\it relaxation} property.

authors.name: Dongjun Wu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Completely monotone memory systems
papers.abstract: Linear time-invariant (LTI) relaxation systems are characterized by a completely monotone impulse response. This paper proposes an extension of this property to nonlinear systems: a system is said to have completely monotone memory if a positive increment in the past input leads to a completely monotone increment in the future output. We show that this property constitutes a strong form of monotonicity, while also imposing stability constraints that closely resemble fading memory, contraction, and incremental stability. We also show that completely monotone memory is equivalent to classical relaxation for LTI systems and to a combination of monotonicity and stability for a class of scalar state-affine systems. Finally, we illustrate the relevance of our framework to the gating dynamics of conductance-based models.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
papers.abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

papers.title: The Power of Migration on Identical Machines is Two
papers.abstract:
We study the power of migration in preemptive scheduling on identical parallel machines with time windows. If an instance admits a migratory schedule on $m$ machines, how many machines are needed to schedule it without migration? Kalyanasundaram and Pruhs (2001) showed that $6m-5$ machines suffice and gave a polynomial-time construction using $12m-5$ machines, whereas $2m-1$ machines may be necessary. We close this gap, which has been open for more than 25 years: $2m-1$ machines always suffice, and a corresponding non-migratory schedule can be computed in strongly polynomial time.
  Our proof has two main technical ingredients. First, we introduce supercanonical schedules and prove that the conflict graph of every such schedule on $m$ machines is $(2m-1)$-colorable. The key property is that whenever a job pauses, the jobs running alongside it just before and just after the pause separate the jobs processed entirely during the pause from the rest of the conflict graph. We use these separators and Kempe exchanges to compute a coloring in polynomial time. Second, we construct a supercanonical schedule with polynomially many processing blocks by shrinking job windows as far as possible while preserving feasibility and solving a min-cost flow problem.

papers.title: Enhancement of the magnetorheological effect using discontinuous shear thickening with a mixture of magnetic and non magnetic particles
papers.abstract: The phenomenon of discontinuous shear thickening (DST) is observed in suspensions of solid particles with a very high-volume fraction. Using a suspension of magnetic particles at high-volume fraction we have, for the first time, demonstrated experimentally the presence of a frictional network of particles by a simultaneous measurement of the electrical resistance of the suspension and of the rheological curve. An obstacle for the applications of MRS remains the sedimentation and aggregation linked to the high density of the iron microparticles. We have recently found that a small fraction of ferromagnetic particles within a concentrated suspension of calcium carbonate particles is not only sufficient to trigger the transition by application of a magnetic field but also optimum for the amplitude of the jump in viscosity observed in DST. We shall explain this result from stress transmission between the magnetic particles and nonmagnetic ones, both inserted in the percolated network of particles. We will also highlight the role of the polyelectrolyte adsorbed on the surface of the particles in the DST transition through the balance between the repulsive entropic force between two layers of polymer adsorbed on different particles and the magnetic attraction force.

papers.title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
papers.abstract: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

papers.title: GARDEN: Efficient GPU-Accelerated Billion-Scale GNN Training via Caching-Sampling-Batching Co-Design
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown impressive performance in diverse tasks such as social network analysis and recommendation systems. However, scaling their training to billion-edge graphs is hindered by the memory wall: GPU memory capacity falls short of the massive storage requirements for node features and topology. Sampling-based GNN training frameworks mitigate this by streaming subgraphs from CPU to GPU, but they incur prohibitive PCIe data transfers and non-coalesced memory accesses, resulting in bandwidth underutilization and low compute efficiency. We propose GARDEN, a GPU-accelerated sampling-based system that co-designs caching, sampling, and batching to eliminate these bottlenecks. GARDEN introduces three key innovations: (1) an Adaptive High-Fidelity Cache Allocator (AHFCA) that combines offline reuse profiling and online hotness tracking to dynamically cache features and adjacency lists within a fixed GPU memory budget, avoiding static allocation waste; (2) a Grouping-based Parallel Sampler that reorders stochastic neighborhood accesses(GPS) to maximize warp occupancy and hide latency on power-law graphs; and (3) a Super-batch Degree Classifier(SDC) that fuses mini-batches into degree-homogeneous groups, enabling cache-friendly coalesced transfers and high GPU utilization. Evaluations on real-world billion-scale graphs demonstrate that GARDEN achieves 4.54x, 1.27x, and 2.97x end-to-end training speedups over DGL-UVA, DUCATI, and FastGL, respectively, while maintaining model convergence and accuracy.

authors.name: Xin He
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: MetaPI: Constructing Prompt Injection Benchmarks from LLM Agent Benchmark
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly perform complex tasks using high-privilege tools, making indirect prompt injection (IPI) a critical security risk. However, IPI benchmarks lag behind their rapidly evolving utility counterparts, only offering limited task and environment coverage and relying on narrow, static attack scenarios. In this paper, we propose meta-benchmarking for IPI: transforming existing utility benchmarks into end-to-end IPI evaluation suites that reuse their realistic tasks, environments, and infrastructure. We present MetaPI, an extensible toolkit that automatically identifies plausible injection points, generates realistic attack objectives, optimizes adaptive payloads, and validates attacks in the real environment. Its modular interfaces support heterogeneous environments, agents, defenses, and attack algorithms, allowing new components to be integrated without redesigning the evaluation pipeline. We apply MetaPI to AppWorld, VitaBench, and Terminal-Bench and evaluate representative agents and defenses across multiple backbone LLMs. Our results show that no evaluated defense simultaneously achieves strong utility and strong security in realistic, adaptive agentic IPI settings. MetaPI thus enables scalable and consistent security evaluation across diverse and evolving agent ecosystems

authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: SAMBoost: Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting
papers.abstract: We propose SAMBoost (Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting), a gradient boosting method that combines tree-based covariate modelling with a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) latent spatial field through a single penalised objective. At each boosting iteration, the predictor is decomposed into separate covariate and spatial components. The method is motivated by applications in which the spatial effect is not a nuisance to be removed but a quantity of interest that must be recovered alongside the covariates. In insurance, for example, practitioners need both flexible nonlinear covariate effects and an interpretable geographic risk surface that can be reported on its own. Existing approaches often involve trade-offs, offering flexible covariate modelling but no explicit spatial field, rigorous spatial inference with a fixed additive covariate structure, or a combination of both at computational costs that limit practicality for large datasets. SAMBoost addresses these goals within the boosting loop, and the underlying mesh produces a sparse precision structure whose cost is largely independent of sample size. On simulations and on an open benchmark, SAMBoost matches or improves on the predictive accuracy of joint Gaussian process and tree boosting approaches. It is also faster and recovers the spatial field and covariate effects more accurately. When covariate effects include interactions, it outperforms additive Bayesian spatial models. Applied to a flood insurance portfolio with 4.9 million records, SAMBoost trains on the full training set without subsampling and runs about sixteen times faster than a Bayesian reference, with a consistent spatial risk surface. A public Python implementation is available.

papers.title: HFR distorted-wave photoionization of Te III: a preliminary benchmark for large-scale atomic data production to model nebular-phase kilonovae
papers.abstract: The shortage of photoionization cross sections for heavy elements remains an obstacle to non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) modeling of nebular-phase kilonova ejecta, where hydrogenic prescriptions have often been adopted in the absence of ion-specific calculations. We present a first preliminary benchmark of direct photoionization cross sections for doubly ionized tellurium, obtained using the distorted-wave (DW) approximation within the pseudo-relativistic Hartree-Fock (HFR) method implemented in the Cowan codes, in which a semi-empirical adjustment based on the observed energy levels is performed. For the photoionization from the ground level of Te III to the ground level of Te IV, comparison with Dirac R-matrix data shows encouraging agreement in the magnitude and overall decrease of the non-resonant background in the lower photon-energy region, approximately below 4 Ry (autoionizing resonances are absent from the present direct treatment). These preliminary results support HFR distorted-wave calculations as a promising and computationally tractable approach for large-scale production of photoionization cross sections, with lanthanides and actinides as longer-term targets, in light of their importance to kilonova modeling and of the severe lack of atomic data for these species.

authors.name: Exauce Bokamba Motoumba
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Regularity in Cryptocurrency Market Cycles: A Halving-to-Halving Analysis Using Data from Google Trends and Wikipedia
papers.abstract:
Bitcoin halvings provide a natural temporal structure for studying long-term dynamics of cryptocurrency markets. This paper presents a methodological framework for analyzing the regularity of Bitcoin and aggregate cryptocurrency market cycles by normalizing historical periods between consecutive halving events and projecting them onto a common relative-time scale expressed as the percentage of cycle completion.
  The proposed framework integrates market variables, namely Bitcoin price and aggregate cryptocurrency market capitalization, with measures of public attention derived from Google Trends search volume and Wikipedia pageviews. To obtain long-horizon daily attention indices, Google Trends data are reconstructed from overlapping 90-day windows linked by median scale ratios, following established approaches to combining high-frequency Google Trends samples.
  Rather than attempting to forecast future prices, the study aims to compare historical cycles, identify recurring temporal patterns, and evaluate the relationship between market dynamics and retail investor interest across different cycle-relative stages. Exploratory results point to a possible recurring structure. The maxima of the aggregate market capitalization in the two most recent completed cycles occurred at 39.0% and 37.9% of cycle completion, and the highest value of the ongoing cycle observed to date at 38.1% (534-547 days after the respective halvings), although the corresponding multiple of the halving-day value fell from 66 to 1.8. Public attention shows a similar compression of peak multiples, but not a similar timing. The paper also discusses current data limitations and outlines future research directions, including formal lead-lag analyses and expanded multi-asset investigations.
