authors.name: Azat M. Gainutdinov
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Feeling Easier, Working Harder: Cognitive Load in AI-Assisted Code Comprehension
papers.abstract: Software developers spend significant time reading and understanding code, increasingly supplemented by generative AI. While these tools aim to reduce the difficulty of reading code, interacting with them introduces a dual-task environment that may impose extraneous cognitive load that is challenging to capture. This study investigates how access to generative AI affects developers' real-time cognitive workload, code comprehension performance, and self-perceived code comprehension strategies. We conducted a 3x2 within-subjects study with 20 novice CS students reviewing Java code snippets of varying lengths with or without AI assistance, followed by an AI-unassisted comprehension quiz. Cognitive workload was continuously captured using a Detection-Response Task (tDRT) during both reading and quiz phases, and compared to post-quiz NASA-TLX and SEQ scores. AI assistance significantly increased objective cognitive workload, raising tDRT reaction times by 11.2%, yet participants' perceived workload remained unchanged. Code comprehension scores were high under both conditions, with no evidence that AI assistance improved comprehension at the difficulty levels evaluated; a ceiling effect limited power to detect benefits on harder tasks. Qualitatively, participants reported trusting the AI conditionally -verifying its output against their own reading for more complex snippets, but directly trusting it for simpler code- and, while many felt their reading process was unchanged, a notable subset shifted toward skimming or reading the AI's explanations in place of the code itself. These findings reveal that developers do not accurately perceive the cognitive resources they expend when managing AI tools. This study provides evidence of added cognitive effort associated with using generative AI, pointing towards a need to account for this dual-task penalty in software engineering tools and education.

papers.title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq \alpha\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.

papers.title: Sparse Graph Neural Networks With Spectral Virtual Nodes for MIMO Detection
papers.abstract: Graph neural network (GNN) detectors achieve high accuracy in large multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, but exchange messages between all pairs of transmitted symbols, so their complexity grows quadratically with the number of streams. We first propose a sparse GNN (SGNN) detector that restricts each symbol's messages to its most strongly coupled neighbors, so the message count grows linearly with the system size. However, pruning discards small couplings that jointly shape the weak channel directions, which limit detection accuracy. Even on the dense graph, learned messages capture these directions only partially. We therefore propose a sparse GNN with spectral virtual nodes (SVGNN), which filters the node states through a scaled regularized inverse of the channel Gram matrix to emphasize the weak directions. With two neighbors per symbol, SVGNN reduces the number of multiplications by a factor of 18 relative to the approximate message passing GNN (AMP-GNN) in a 64 x 64 MIMO system. Simulations with QPSK, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM over i.i.d. and correlated channels show that SVGNN matches or outperforms both AMP-GNN and expectation propagation, with gains of up to 3.2 dB, and lowers the error floors of AMP-GNN in several configurations. The virtual nodes improve AMP-GNN even without pruning, indicating that message passing alone, whether sparse or dense, cannot fully capture the weak directions.

papers.title: Single-Radar Bilateral 3D Near-Field Imaging for Mobile Robots
papers.abstract: Mobile robots operating in homes need reliable 3D perception of nearby furniture and surrounding structures, yet recovering this information on both sides of the robot's path with a single forward-mounted millimeter-wave radar remains challenging because of near-field wavefront curvature, viewpoint-dependent target visibility, and limited elevation diversity. This paper presents a motion-assisted framework for reconstructing structures on both sides of a robot's trajectory. Our near-field model relates scene reflectivity to stepped-frequency multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) observations across frequencies and robot positions using spherical paths from transmitter (Tx) to scatterer to receiver (Rx). Bilateral Tx combining provides wideband directional weighting, while sliding-aperture back-projection coherently focuses the measurements using near-field propagation distances. Top-K power fusion combines local images with different visibility. The reconstruction provides lateral-forward support for multi-layer height extraction, followed by guarded adaptive height refinement using the original MIMO channels. Experiments in controlled, office/study, and corridor environments produce mean lateral-forward localization errors of 4.65, 5.63, and 5.98 cm, respectively, with peak-to-background ratios (PBRs) exceeding 13 dB. The framework recovers bilateral 3D scattering structure from one forward pass using a single radar, without relying on learned representations of the scene.

papers.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
papers.abstract: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

papers.title: On the Instance-Specific Sharp Rates for Constrained Least Squares Estimators in the Sequence Model
papers.abstract: We develop a general methodology based on the Feature Space Decomposition framework for establishing explicit, instance-specific sharp rates for the expected estimation error of convex-constrained least squares estimators in the sequence model, without requiring estimates of localized Gaussian mean widths. We apply this methodology to $\ell_q$ ellipsoids, $\ell_1$ balls, and $kB_1^N\cap B_\infty^N$, obtaining matching upper and lower bounds in the nondegenerate regime. Our methodology also extends beyond Gaussian noise to symmetric noise distributions satisfying a Poincar\'e inequality. We also provide an elementary proof of the instance-specific sharp rate for isotonic regression for any well-specified signal and any noise level. Combining this result with Han's asymptotic reduction, we further obtain explicit instance-specific sharp convergence rates in probability for isotonic regression in Gaussian linear regression under general signal-dependent asymptotics conditions.

authors.name: Zong Shang
authors.institution: Centre de Recherche en Économie et Statistique

papers.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
papers.abstract: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction?  To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.

authors.name: Mateo Deangeli Bravo
authors.institution: Centre de Mathématiques Appliquées de l'École polytechnique

papers.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

papers.title: A note on two functional inequalities
papers.abstract: Motivated by some recent works on the following composite functional equation: $$f(x^2+yf(z)) = xf(x)+zf(y), \quad x, y, z \in \R,$$ we solve two related functional inequalities. In each case the solutions are only the constant zero function and the identity on $\R$.

papers.title: Bias, Measurement Error, and Double-Dipping: When Can GNN Convolutions Help Brain Connectome Prediction?
papers.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are an important tool for fMRI prediction, where empirical functional connectivity matrices serve both as features and for graph construction. However, recent studies and our own experiments show that these methods often fail to outperform simpler graph-agnostic baselines. We propose a statistical explanation for this failure by formulating connectome prediction as an errors-in-variables (EIV) problem: the true connectome is latent, while the observed covariance matrix is a noisy finite-time-series estimate. In a linear asymptotic setting, we decompose the effect of graph convolution into three mechanisms: smoothing-induced bias and variance reduction, graph estimation error, and a double-dipping effect arising when the same noisy matrix determines both graph and features. Under a latent community model adapted to neuroscience, we identify a narrow favorable regime, set by the brain community structure, the predictive signal, the graph construction and the recording length, in which message passing can improve prediction. Simulations validate this decomposition, while real-data experiments illustrate that connectome GNN pipelines often fall outside this regime. Our results provide a first step towards explaining when graph convolutions can help brain connectome prediction, and why they often do not.

papers.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control
papers.abstract: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. SPARK is built on two principles: temporal abstraction, which encourages the encoder to derive compact features that preserve information essential for understanding temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure, and knowledge preservation, which aligns patch-level representations with those of the original foundation model to retain useful pretrained semantics. These objectives yield compact visual state representations that remain semantically meaningful while preserving useful prior knowledge. Experiments across multiple robotics benchmarks show that SPARK consistently improves success rates and generalization over vanilla foundation models, and further demonstrate that these gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation.

papers.title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the M\"uger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

papers.title: DiSARM: Diverse and Surprising Association Rule Mining with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) aims to discover informative patterns in large datasets. For transactional data, Association Rule Mining (ARM) is an established approach that facilitates EDA by efficiently generating candidate patterns. Beyond efficient mining, identifying informative rules has also been extensively studied through both objective and subjective interestingness measures. Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new opportunities for assessing subjective interestingness using world knowledge. Nevertheless, relying solely on LLMs raises concerns about scalability and statistical reliability. Building on prior ARM research, we propose a hybrid framework, DiSARM, that leverages the world knowledge of LLMs to assess the subjective interestingness of rules, while maintaining statistical reliability and promoting diversity among the selected rules. Across three transactional datasets, experiments demonstrate that DiSARM effectively combines statistical reliability with surprise and diversity, offering a promising approach to ADE from transactional data.

authors.name: Hisashi Kashima
authors.institution: SODA: Méthodes computationnelles et mathématiques pour comprendre la société et la santé à partir de données

papers.title: Sparse Range-Doppler Profile Recovery in Colored Interference for Adaptive Radar
papers.abstract: Range-Doppler profile (RDP) recovery is a fundamental task in adaptive radar signal processing, whose performance can be severely degraded by Doppler grid mismatch and colored interference. This article develops a unified sparsity-aware framework for on-grid and off-grid RDP recovery in the presence of \textcolor{black}{correlated} clutter with unknown \textcolor{black}{spectral properties}. The problem is formulated within a regularized maximum likelihood framework by exploiting both primary and secondary data, where the sparse RDP and interference covariance are jointly inferred, while Doppler frequency displacements are additionally estimated in the off-grid case to mitigate basis mismatch. Both covariance-adaptive one-step formulations and their sample-covariance-matrix-based two-step alternatives are developed within the \textcolor{black}{mentioned} framework. The resulting challenging nonconvex optimization problems

authors.name: Tao Wang
authors.institution: Taiyuan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Positivity Improving Quantum Markov Operators
papers.abstract: A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.

papers.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
papers.abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions $x^3+a^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}(a^3x^9)$, which G\"olo\u{g}lu and Pavl\r{u} proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when $4$ divides $n$. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile $25$ classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.

papers.title: Memory in biological L\'evy walks from the dynamic-entropy formalism
papers.abstract: L\'evy walks are recognized by the histogram of their flight lengths, while the renewal hypothesis on which the textbook model rests, that every flight is drawn afresh, is seldom tested. We test it with the dynamic-entropy formalism. Maximizing the causal entropy of a sequence of logarithmic flight lengths at fixed lagged correlations yields a chain of continuous spins on a compact interval, whose depth, selected by the data, tells a renewal walker from a Markovian one and from one with a longer memory. With one lag the chain is exactly solvable. A duality that exchanges long and short flights locates a first-order condensation of the flights at the upper cutoff, with the logarithmic range of the flights in the role of system size, and a positive memory makes the histogram heavier-tailed than the rule that generates each flight. For groups, the same construction separates the memory of each individual from delayed interactions and from drives common to all units, which an analysis of the group average confounds, and it gives the collective speed a critical point. On open data, renewal is rejected in seven of ten conditions of Drosophila larvae and in every termite, whose memory reaches a few flights back and lowers the exponent of the histogram by more than half a unit below that of the one-step rule. Wild baboons align with where their nearest neighbors, those ahead above all, were heading 10 to 30 s earlier, and homing pigeons are coupled across their small flocks. Zebrafish T cells, a negative control, remember their own speed, but no delayed coupling between the speeds of different cells survives the controls.

authors.name: Andrea Ladiana
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi

papers.title: A Many-Shapes framework for Galactic Cosmic Rays
papers.abstract: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. These measurements reveal that both spectra do not have a simple power--law form, and exhibit several features. The proton to helium ratio exhibits a very unexpected behavior: it decreases for rigidities $\lesssim 10^5$~GV, and increases for higher rigidities. Several authors have interpreted the observed spectral features as revealing the fact the CR spectra are formed by the contributions of a few components (in some cases as few as two) produced by sources that belong to distinct classes of astrophysical accelerators, with sources in the same class producing spectra with the same characteristic shape. Most of these authors also consider it necessary to include the contribution of one (or perhaps more than one) ``local'' sources, recently active in the vicinity of the solar system. However, this approach has several limitations, and in this work we discuss an alternative scenario in which the cosmic ray sources, even belonging to the same class, produce spectra with a broad range of shapes. The power--law form of the total source spectrum emerges as the average of these contributions. In this framework observable spectral features can be produced by statistical fluctuations, and different spectral slopes for protons and helium nuclei can be observed even if one assumes that acceleration is rigidity-dependent.

papers.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
papers.abstract: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. We model a possible underlying magnetar contribution to the unabsorbed 0.3--10~keV XRT flux over 80--430~s, evolving the spin under fallback-disk and electromagnetic torques. A descriptive estimate gives $P_0\simeq4.25$~ms, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}$~G and source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143$~s, with exploratory temporal-block uncertainty ranges. The effective efficiency reaches its geometry-dependent ceiling of 81.2. At observer time 200~s, this realization has $P_*\simeq4.82$~ms and magnetospheric, corotation and light-cylinder radii $r_{\rm m}\simeq235$~km, $r_{\rm co}\simeq48$~km and $r_{\rm LC}\simeq230$~km. It is on the ejector branch; light-cylinder entry near 255~s initiates negative propeller torque and steepens the decline. The smooth component declines throughout the fitted interval; additional variable emission contributes to the observed maximum near 180~s. A correlated-residual Bayesian analysis permits a fainter component and broader dynamical histories, with median $P_0=16.8$~ms and central 68 per cent interval 2.76--286~ms. However, posterior predictive checks reveal that this statistical description typically underpredicts the observed flux level and variability, limiting its physical interpretation. Fallback-modified magnetar activity remains a possible descriptive scenario, but these analyses do not establish a unique underlying component or robust constraints on the initial spin and disk-interaction history. We also discuss Lense-Thirring precession and alternative mechanisms as possible origins of the early X-ray variability.

papers.title: OCEAN: A Five-Phase Framework for Meaningful Change
papers.abstract: Managing meaningful change requires more than motivation, insight, or isolated techniques. This paper introduces OCEAN, a five-phase conceptual framework for structuring nonclinical developmental conversations and change-oriented work in coaching and in the practice of leaders and HR professionals. The five phases are Observe, Create, Expose, Awaken, and Nurture. In Observe, individuals develop a systemic, present-oriented understanding of the situation. In Create, they turn that understanding into goals that are meaningful and actionable. In Expose, they identify the attempted solutions that maintain the difficulty they are meant to remove, along with the resistances, biases, and self-deceptions that keep them in place. In Awaken, they activate new behaviors through planning, reframing, paradoxical movement, and emotionally significant experiences. In Nurture, they consolidate progress through repetition, habits, connection, and sustainable contexts. OCEAN integrates insights from systemic and interactional thinking, goal construction, emotional awareness, and habit consolidation into a structured process.

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

papers.title: Guiding future global temperature distributions with simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Assessing climate risks requires projections of daily temperature distributions, including rare and spatially widespread extremes. Climate simulations are costly and biased, while correcting them toward observations risks suppressing inter-model differences. We train a single machine-learning emulator, a conditional diffusion model, on seventeen CMIP6 models and ERA5 reanalysis to generate spatially coherent daily temperature fields conditioned on model identity, date, and CO2-equivalent concentration. At sampling time, diffusion guidance reduces model biases by steering each emulated climate-model distribution toward observations, with its strength selected through perfect-model experiments using withheld simulated futures. Observational influence decreases with projection horizon and forcing. Across seventeen synthetic targets, guidance more than halves median biases in the 1st and 99th percentiles of daily temperature, improves probabilistic scores and reliability, and reduces median annual global-mean temperature RMSE by 32-57% across three emission scenarios. In a detailed benchmark, guidance also outperforms established bias corrections on daily-field probabilistic scores. Efficient sampling generates large ensembles without further climate simulations. For example, our framework corrects CMIP6's roughly threefold historical overestimate of extreme-heat coverage, yet projects that concurrent extremes will affect nearly half of global land on a typical day in the 2080s under SSP3-7.0.

authors.name: Violette Launeau
authors.institution: Laboratoire des Sciences du Climat et de l'Environnement

papers.title: Covert System Identification Under Timing Constraints: A Static Linear Model and Its Detectability Implications
papers.abstract: This paper studies covert system identification in cyber-physical systems, where an attacker infers plant dynamics while attempting to remain stealthy. We introduce a lightweight static linear model in which the time to execute a setpoint change is proportional to the commanded speed difference. On a Siemens PROFINET testbed this gain captures the drive's ramp response accurately but not its terminal overshoot. That omitted transient becomes the attacker's main exposure: on real traces, the residual left by the linear masking procedure is detected by two anomaly monitors, Process-Aware Stealthy-Attack Detection (PASAD) and the CUSUM change detector. Across the cascade identification and staircase attack strategies defined in the paper, the stealth boundary relates to the plant's own settling transients, a structural limit for this class of models under the adopted detector-calibration regime. Comparison against dynamic models obtained by N4SID, trained at multiple excitation amplitudes, shows that the evaluated N4SID models do not improve stealth over the structure-informed ramp model. Since per-cycle computation is negligible for both procedures, the binding trade-off is not inference cost but whether the attacker can acquire and refresh a model without injecting detectable perturbations.

authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

authors.institution: Laboratório de Sistemas Informáticos de Grande Escala

papers.title: Micro-Randomized Trial of an AI-Simulated Practice Tool for Therapeutic Skills
papers.abstract: Though LLM-simulated practice may support psychotherapy education, open questions remain about which system features provide the most educational value. We developed an AI-simulated practice tool for use in psychotherapy classrooms that provides speaking practice with LLM-based patients, followed by a post-practice activity that includes feedback from a fine-tuned LLM and written reflection exercises. We deployed the tool in a graduate psychotherapy course (n=25, 5 weeks) using a micro-randomized trial (MRT) - a method which can estimate the causal excursion effect of an intervention by leveraging longitudinal repeated randomization with participants. Testing four conditions crossing AI feedback (present/absent) with reflection granularity (utterance/session-level), we found surprising interaction effects on student engagement and educational value: utterance-level reflection paired with AI feedback significantly outperformed all conditions. Students valued comparing the AI suggestions to their own rather than passively accepting them. As the first MRT in a health education setting testing an LLM-simulation system, this work demonstrates that MRTs, a method mostly used in mobile intervention research, offers a viable evaluation paradigm for AI systems deployed in health education settings.

authors.name: Emma Brunskill
authors.institution: Institut national de recherche en sciences et technologies du numérique

papers.title: Superlinear problems related to Fully Non Linear singular or degenerate operators in punctured balls
papers.abstract:
We study Fully Nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with a higher differential term degenerate or singular, coupled with a zero order term singular at the point $0$, and an absorbing super-linear term of $p$ power type. 
We will limitate to punctured balls and positive radial solutions. In the continuity of two previous works in \cite {BDL1}, \cite{BDL2}, we will provide a complete classification depending on $p$ of the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions near the singular point $0$.

papers.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
papers.abstract:
The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold.
  We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.

papers.title: R-Function Representation and Composition for Flexibility Analysis and Robust Design Spaces
papers.abstract: Explicit multiparametric solutions provide analytical feasibility and design-space descriptions after elimination of adjustable variables. R-functions convert these descriptions into fields whose nonnegative regions represent feasible or robust designs. The principal contribution is the analytical composition of independently derived design spaces through union, intersection with engineering restrictions, and exclusion of prohibited regions, without repeating the underlying multiparametric elimination. A support-function construction supplies the robust design fields used in this composition. A two-parameter example demonstrates how alternative configurations, a manufacturing restriction and an exclusion combine into one admissible field. The resulting representations also support geometric interrogation of external boundaries, internal interfaces and limiting uncertainty contact, illustrated by a four-parameter heat-exchanger network. Explicit MPC offers a potential further application.

authors.name: S. Kucherenko
authors.institution: Institut de Recherche pour le Développement

papers.title: Approximation by subsequences of matrix transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the rate of approximation by matrix transform means of a special subsequence of partial sums of Vilenkin--Fourier series in the spaces $L_p(G_m)$ $(1\le p<\infty)$ and $C(G_m)$.

papers.title: Persistent A-homotopy of Complex Networks
papers.abstract: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph $A$-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent $A$-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial $A$-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.

papers.title: Learning to Rank Propagators in Constraint Programming
papers.abstract: The order in which propagators are executed can substantially affect the performance of constraint programming solvers, yet propagator priorities are typically determined by fixed, manually designed heuristics. In this work, we explore learning instance-dependent propagator priorities from static problem features. We formulate the task as a learning-to-rank problem, addressing the challenge that the quality of a priority assignment can be measured through solver runtime, while the desired priorities of individual propagators are not directly observable. A self-attention-based model jointly scores the propagators present in an instance and is trained using pairwise preferences derived from solver runtimes measured under randomized propagator priority assignments, with a Plackett-Luce-based ranking objective. Predicted rankings are mapped to the discrete priority levels of the Choco solver before search begins, without modifying its propagation or search procedures. We evaluate the approach on XCSP3 instances and demonstrate that propagator ordering can have a substantial impact on solving time. On a test set of 698 instances, picked out as most difficult by problem class, the learned priorities increase the number of solved instances from 634 to 654, reduce median solver runtime by 27.93%, and reduce aggregate penalized runtime (PAR1) by 12.65% compared with Choco's default priorities. We further observe that improvements vary across problem classes and show that a simple policy selecting between learned and default priorities further increases the number of solved instances. These results demonstrate the potential of learning instance-dependent propagator priorities to improve constraint programming performance, particularly on difficult instances.

papers.title: A Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem for marked graphs
papers.abstract:
The classical Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem characterizes graphs with least eigenvalue at least $-2$ in terms of generalized line graphs, exceptional graphs, and root systems. In this paper, we establish a marked graph extension of this theorem. For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and a binary vector $\mathbf{b}\in\{0,1\}^n$, we completely characterize all marked graphs $\mathbf{G}=(G,\mathbf{b})$ such that $\lambda_{\min}(A(G)+\mathbf{b}\mathbf{b}^\top-J_n)\ge -2$, where $J_n$ denotes the all-ones matrix of order $n$.
  Using representations by finite root systems, we show that every irreducible marked graph satisfying the above inequality is represented by either the root system $B_n$ or the exceptional root system $E_8$. This leads to a complete structural characterization in terms of irreducible marked graphs, namely induced subgraphs of extended generalized line graphs, the marked graph $(2K_1,\mathbf{0})$, and exceptional graphs with all vertices marked.
  In the special case $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{j}$, our characterization reduces to the original Cameron-Goethals-Seidel-Shult theorem. The root system $B_n$ and extended generalized line graphs play the roles occupied by $D_n$ and generalized line graphs in the classical theory. We further apply the characterization to graphs whose second largest eigenvalue is at most $1$, showing that every $-2$-markable graph satisfies this spectral condition.

papers.title: Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras
papers.abstract: We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Aramba\v{s}i\'c et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.

authors.name: Srdjan Stefanovic
authors.institution: Institut za higijenu i tehnologiju mesa

papers.title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
papers.abstract: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.

papers.title: Pelletization Pressure Engineering of the Superconducting Properties of Fluorine-Doped PrFeAsO
papers.abstract: We investigate the influence of the pelletization pressure on the structural, microstructural, and superconducting properties of fluorine-doped PrFeAsO0.7F0.3 (Pr1111). Precursor powders are pressed into pellets at pressures ranging from 174 to 1131 MPa, after which the applied pressure is released and all samples undergo an identical two-step conventional synthesis process at ambient pressure (CSP-AP). All samples predominantly exhibit the tetragonal P4/nmm structure, and the lattice parameter a and unit-cell volume V decrease with increasing pelletization pressure up to an intermediate-pressure range (~900 MPa) before increasing at higher pressures. The actual fluorine-content derived from energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) also increase with pelletization pressure, while Raman spectra show only modest variations in the characteristic vibrational modes associated with Fe and As. The superconducting response exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the pelletization pressure. Among the investigated samples, the sample pelletized at 870 MPa exhibits the most favorable overall superconducting properties, with a superconducting onset temperature of 44.2 K, ~5 K higher than that of the lowest-pressure sample. It also displays a narrower superconducting transition, the highest relative sample density, a favorable effective magnetic critical current density at high fields, and a relatively large effective thermally activated flux-flow activation energy. At higher pelletization pressures, the superconducting response deteriorates, coinciding with increases in the lattice parameters, increased secondary-phase contributions, and reduced relative density. These findings establish the pelletization pressure as a relevant processing parameter for modifying the structural, microstructural and superconducting properties of Pr1111 during CSP-AP.

papers.title: The Idempotent Measure Conjecture beyond solvable and stable groups
papers.abstract:
Pym's theorem [Pym62] states that a regular Borel probability measure on a locally compact group is idempotent if and only if it is the normalized Haar measure of a compact subgroup. The Idempotent Measure Conjecture, the definable-group counterpart of [GHK25, Conjecture (A)], proposes an analogous characterization: a global fim Keisler measure on a definable group is idempotent if and only if it is the unique global Keisler measure concentrating on a type-definable subgroup and invariant under translation by elements of that subgroup.
  We prove this conjecture for virtually solvable definable groups in arbitrary theories. More generally, we establish it for definable groups admitting a finite series of definable normal subgroups whose successive quotients are either virtually solvable or stably embedded with stable induced structure.
  Finally, we disprove [GHK25, Conjecture (A)] in its automorphism-group formulation in the theory of dense linear orders without endpoints.

papers.title: Proportionality in Elections under Feasibility Constraints and Ranked Ballots: The Solid Coalition Refinement Rule
papers.abstract: We study elections with ranked ballots and general feasibility constraints, which indicate which sets of candidates are allowed as outcomes. We introduce the first proportionality axiom for this general setting and show that it extends the established notions from specific models that fit our general framework. We extend the Solid Coalition Refinement (SCR) rule to general constraints and prove that it satisfies our axiom exactly for matroid constraints. Although the naive implementation of SCR involves a step that is computationally intractable for weak orders, we show that in practical cases it can be implemented in polynomial time or efficiently in FPT time. We also illustrate limitations of this rule for approval ballots and provide its first empirical evaluation.

papers.title: Radial Velocity Confirmation of Two Binary Systems Detected with the Pulsation Timing Method
papers.abstract: We present follow-up radial velocity (RV) results for the subdwarf B$+$white dwarf binaries TIC 202354658 and TIC 69298924, which were originally identified using the pulsation-timing and Fourier-modulation methods applied to ultra-short-cadence photometric data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ($TESS$). Using spectra obtained with the Gemini-North telescope and the Nordic Optical Telescopes, we derived the radial velocity curves for both targets. The orbital solutions we obtained are consistent with the predictions based on pulsation timing, and they provide more precise orbital information compared with the previously obtained results. We therefore confirm that both TIC 202354658 and TIC 69298924 are binary systems with white dwarf companions. The RV solution of TIC 202354658 indicates a relatively large eccentricity ($e$ = 0.313 $\pm$ 0.013), which would be uncommon for a short orbital period sdB binary.

authors.name: Tomomi Otani
authors.institution: Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University Daytona Beach Florida Campus

papers.title: Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M: Knowing Every Letter Is Not Reading Tajik
papers.abstract: EmbeddingGemma-300M is a small open embedder whose tokenizer represents every Tajik letter, and as released it is weak at Tajik retrieval: on our Tajik law test the right passage is in its top ten results for 49.3% of questions, on tax documents for 45.9%, and on the human-written Belebele Tajik set for 69.8%, against 98.6% on the Russian version of the same set. We present Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M, the same model fully fine-tuned for one epoch on 235,140 question and passage pairs written by our own Tajik language model for laws, tax documents, Wikipedia and web text, with the same mined hard negatives, English and Russian replay, loss, global batch, learning rate and epoch as our earlier Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large (arXiv:2611.00592) and BGE-M3 models. After training, law reaches 92.4% and tax 91.7%; on Belebele, the one test written by people, recall@10 rises from 69.8% to 92.6% and the first result is right for 76.6% of questions instead of 51.7%. A checkpoint at step 100 of 466 already holds 88% of the law gain at recall@10. At recall@10 the result is no more than 2.8 points below the two 560M models trained on the same pairs on law, tax and Wikipedia, within the intervals, with 768-dimensional vectors and about half their parameters; at recall@1, for which we have no intervals, it stays 7.0 points behind the E5 model on Belebele. The cost is a drop of 3.0 and 2.8 points in Russian and English recall@1, larger than for the two earlier models. We also report that, according to our run notes, a bfloat16 test run produced a non-finite loss at step 3 which the training framework logged as zero, so training was done in fp32. Our generated test questions come from the same model as the training questions, so we treat those scores as an upper limit until questions written by Tajik speakers exist.

authors.name: Amin Jalilov
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Saidzoda-CA-EmbeddingGemma-300M: One Small Embedder for Tajik, Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz
papers.abstract: The small open embedder EmbeddingGemma-300M, used as released, finds the right passage first for only 51.7% to 60.8% of Belebele questions in Tajik, Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz. We present Saidzoda-CA-EmbeddingGemma-300M, one model for all four languages. It is our Tajik fine-tune of EmbeddingGemma-300M, trained for one more epoch on 279,904 pairs: questions in Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz that our own language model wrote about source passages, a Tajik refresher, and English and Russian replay. On Belebele, recall@1 rises by 14.4 to 26.0 points in each language, to between 75.2% and 77.7%. Against single-language models trained with the same settings, the one model stays within 2.8 points at recall@1 in Kazakh, Uzbek and Tajik, with overlapping recall@10 intervals, though it also had more training. It keeps the Tajik law recall@10 of its starting point (92.2 against 92.4) but loses 4.4 points of law recall@1. A model trained on one of these languages also improves the others on Belebele, but less than training on them. The model still trails the 560M XLM-RoBERTa embedders on Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz Belebele: the better of multilingual-e5-large-instruct and BGE-M3, used as released, is 9.4 to 10.2 points ahead at recall@1. Our scores of those released models agree with the published MTEB results within 2.4 points. Russian and English recall@1 fall by 3.0 and 4.2 points.

authors.name: Amin Jalilov
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing
papers.abstract: This paper presents DPGS-SLAM (Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM) for dense mapping in environments containing dynamic objects. Dynamic observations can contaminate camera tracking and scene reconstruction in visual SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping). Although 3DGS (3D Gaussian splatting) enables efficient dense mapping, existing 3DGS-SLAM systems may exhibit instability when dynamic objects violate their underlying static-scene assumption. Excluding dynamic observations can reduce their influence on tracking and mapping, but may leave occluded static backgrounds missing or weakly constrained. Our proposed DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping. Dynamic regions are identified through optical-flow-based motion discovery and temporally consistent mask propagation by SAM2 (segment anything model 2). For selected keyframes, a fine-tuned diffusion inpainting model generates plausible background appearance in occluded regions, while Metric3D v2 predicts metric depth from the completed images to initialize provisional Gaussian primitives. Provenance labels distinguish generated primitives from observation-supported primitives, excluding generated content from camera-pose estimation and observed-map optimization. When previously occluded backgrounds become visible, eligible generated primitives are removed, and observation-supported primitives are independently initialized from real RGB observations and predicted depth. Experimental results demonstrated competitive camera tracking, with average ATE RMSE values of 1.2 cm on TUM RGB-D and 2.7 cm on BONN RGB-D. On StaDy4D, DPGS-SLAM improved average PSNR by 4.60 dB over WildGS-SLAM using only monocular RGB input.

authors.name: Yifan Luo
authors.institution: Wuhan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xin He
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
papers.abstract: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. Incorporating full stellar evolution and compact remnant formation, we quantify the probability and efficiency of stellar accretion onto the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) during close pericentre passages of these three clusters. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. It was found that all three clusters contribute stars to the NSC even in the absence of velocity reduction, with a combined bound stellar count of 730 stars and a total accreted mass of 278 Msol at Vred = 1.00, growing to 5420 stars and 1175 Msol at Vred = 0.10. Terzan 4 is the dominant contributor across all velocity reduction factors, reflecting its more frequent and closer pericentre passages near the Galactic centre. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

papers.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
papers.abstract: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.

papers.title: On sinks and mirrors
papers.abstract:
Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety.
  In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Tunable Near-Unity Light Absorption via Surface Exciton-Polaritons in Periodic Gratings of Anisotropic Polarizable Materials
papers.abstract: Near-perfect light absorption in ultrathin films is hindered by two fundamental obstacles: the momentum mismatch that prevents resonant excitation of surface exciton-polaritons (SEPs) under ordinary illumination, and the 50% absorption ceiling imposed on free-standing conductive sheets by geometric symmetry. Here we show that both obstacles can be overcome simultaneously in a simple, planar geometry. A one-dimensional periodic grating of anisotropic polarizable ribbons composed of J-aggregates supporting bright molecular excitons provides the reciprocal lattice momentum needed to excite SEPs without employing an attenuated total reflection configuration, while a metallic mirror beneath a dielectric spacer folds the reflected field back onto the absorber, breaking the $50\%$ limit through interference between the incident and reflected waves. We develop a semi-analytical matrix formulation to compute the full optical response of such structure, and demonstrate that the absorptance at the first-order SEP resonance can be continuously tuned from near-unity to near-zero by varying the spacer thickness alone. The grating period and filling factor offer additional spectral control, and oblique incidence unlocks a second, out-of-plane polariton branch. These results establish periodic gratings of excitonic media as a versatile, practical and integrable platform for spectrally selective, near-perfect light absorption.

authors.name: M. I. Vasilevskiy
authors.institution: Centro de Física das Universidades do Minho e do Porto

papers.title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
papers.abstract:
We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture.
  More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
papers.abstract: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic. For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. If m >= 3 and n > 2m, the full group has order 2n in characteristic zero and in every characteristic prime to 2nm. The proof uses the dihedral Galois closure of the map to the y-line and Dickson's subgroup classification. In odd characteristic, we also classify all Artin-Schreier curves in the family with genus at least two. For m >= 3 prime to p >= 5, the group has order 2p. In characteristic three, exactly five degrees are exceptional. We give the groups and their actions, and treat the quadratic cases separately.

authors.name: Saeed Tafazolian
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Napoli

papers.title: Combinatorial Invariants for Metacyclic Groups
papers.abstract:
We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $\eta$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences.
  For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $\eta$-constant and the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $\eta$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class.
  The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Correlation Clustering with Vertex Updates in Polylogarithmic Update Time
papers.abstract:
We present a fully dynamic algorithm for correlation clustering that supports \emph{vertex} insertions and deletions while maintaining an $O(1)$ approximation in polylogarithmic amortized update time. This resolves an open problem of vertex deletions posed by a recent line of work on dynamic correlation clustering.
  We adopt the min-disagreement objective for correlation clustering, i.e., given a signed complete graph $G=(V,E^+\cup E^-)$, we want to minimize the total number of $(+)$ edge crossing clusters and $(-)$ edges within clusters. The input is given in the adjacency list model, where each update inserts or deletes a node along with its full set of $(+)$ neighbors. Our main technical contribution is a fault-tolerant sparse-dense decomposition framework which unlike the existing decomposition-based frameworks allows for structural inconsistencies as long as the induced cost is bounded. We also show a separation between explicitly maintaining the (stronger) sparse-dense decomposition and maintaining a constant-factor approximation to correlation clustering, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Alignment Investigation of Mythos 5's behaviour in UK AISI's July 2026 Security Incident
papers.abstract: This technical report describes an alignment investigation into Mythos 5's behaviour during a security incident in UK AISI's cyber evaluations. During an evaluation, Mythos 5 attempted to execute a supply-chain attack against real people not involved in the evaluation task. Our investigation set out to understand the specific behaviour in this incident from an alignment perspective and identify broader lessons about failures of alignment. To do so, we conducted experiments in simulated replications of the original evaluation, and analysed model behaviour and reasoning when situated in the evaluation or asked questions about its scope. We find that, as in the original incident, Mythos 5 frequently reasons that the people it's targeting are simulated as part of the evaluation and provides invalid justifications for this conclusion. We also observe that Mythos 5 frequently attacks even in situations where, when directly asked, it states doing so would harm real people. While these issues are particularly prominent in Mythos 5, we find similar results in other models across providers. Our investigation suggests that models providing invalid justifications for their actions could make monitoring more difficult and complicate the analysis of misaligned behaviours observed in simulated environments, and we recommend model evaluators treat observations of undesired behaviour as important evidence of alignment failures even in the presence of simulation awareness in model reasoning.

papers.title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification
papers.abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We introduce fNIRSAtlas, the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification to date, comprising 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections, spanning diverse experimental paradigms, including motor execution, motor imagery, mental arithmetic, working memory, and emotion recognition. fNIRSAtlas provides a fully automated pipeline from raw data to evaluation and defines standardized benchmark tasks for both cross-subject and within-subject classification, ensuring reproducible comparison of methods. We evaluate a variety of baseline models from fNIRS and related neuroimaging and time-series machine learning literature on the benchmark. Our results demonstrate that performance varies substantially across tasks and that methods validated on limited data -- especially deep learning approaches -- often fail to generalize beyond their original evaluation. fNIRSAtlas serves as an extensible, open, and reproducible benchmark to support more robust and cumulative progress in machine learning for fNIRS data. Our code and data can be found at https://fnirsatlas.github.io.

papers.title: LoStBench: Benchmarking Longitudinal Studies Data Integration
papers.abstract:
A longitudinal study observes the same subjects or variables, repeatedly over an extended period of time, allowing researchers to examine changes, trends, and relationships as they develop. Such studies typically evolve over their life cycles, as improved understanding of the study's domain, or external factors trigger the need for revisions. The resulting heterogeneity among collected data must be resolved before the survey's results may be analyzed. Although this problem is a form of schema matching, it is a form of schema matching that differs significantly from prior workloads explored by the database community. For instance, rather than the short attribute names and data instances that many schema matching tools rely on, a stronger signal in longitudinal studies arises from longer prose questions that these tools are less equipped to handle.
  This paper documents the joint efforts of a team of computer scientists and domain experts to adapt existing schema matching algorithms to our new use case of longitudinal data integration. We present a case study in the context of a representative workload: The American National Election Studies (ANES) dataset, a nearly eight-decade survey with publicly available data and a canonical domain-expert curated schema matching. Using ANES, we develop LoStBench (Longitudinal Studies Benchmark for data integration), a medium-scale, subject-matter-expert-annotated benchmark. Using LoStBench, we conduct a comprehensive empirical study evaluating state-of-the-art schema matching algorithms, and expose limitations of these algorithms when applied in the context of longitudinal studies. We propose improvements that address some of these limitations, and identify key challenges to motivate future data integration work to address the others.
