papers.title: EEGFaceSem: An EEG Benchmark with Paired Generative Latents for Semantic Visual Modeling
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to measure brain activity for brain-computer interface applications for its non-invasive nature and high temporal resolution. However, progress in modeling the neural responses to visual semantics has been limited by a reliance on fixed image collections that lack the fine-grained control needed to isolate fine-grained changes in visual features and their relation to perception. In this work, we present EEGFaceSem, a large-scale dataset pairing high-quality EEG with photorealistic face images synthesized from a generative model. We provide the generative latent vector for each stimulus, enabling research into the continuous mapping between a visual latent space and neural representations. Each participant's brain responses were recorded while they attended to specific semantic features (e.g., smiling, hair color) in a rapid serial visual presentation paradigm. The dataset contains EEG signals from 30 participants, totaling 67,200 time-locked EEG recordings. We present benchmarks for single-trial semantic classification under single-subject, cross-subject, and subject-adapted settings, as well as for cross-subject voting that aggregates per-stimulus predictions across participants. We further demonstrate the dataset's unique utility with two complementary applications: deriving semantic directions in the latent space for brain-supervised image editing, and conditioning a generative model on brain-decoded labels for brain-supervised image generation. Our dataset paves the way for advancing brain-computer interfaces (BCI) for semantic-level visual saliency detection and brain-supervised generative modeling. Our dataset and code are openly released at OSF (https://osf.io/2guk3/) and at HuggingFace https://huggingface.co/datasets/yefllower/EEGFaceSem.

papers.title: Does Predictive Performance Translate to Causal Performance? Evaluating tabular foundation models as nuisance learners for causal effect estimation
papers.abstract:
Tabular foundation models based on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) achieve strong predictive performance, but their value for causal inference is unclear. We evaluated whether PFNs, which predict through in-context learning, could match or outperform conventional nuisance learners in supporting accurate causal estimation and reliable uncertainty quantification (inference). Learners modeled propensity scores and outcome regressions within doubly robust estimators of average causal effects, with and without cross-fitting, across synthetic and semi-synthetic settings with varying confounding complexity and effect heterogeneity.
  Under simple parametric data-generating processes, the PFNs were competitive with correctly specified parametric regressions and ensembles containing them. In more complex settings, they outperformed all conventional learners evaluated, including richly specified Super Learner ensembles, for both accuracy and uncertainty quantification. As sample size increased, only the two PFN models (TabPFN and Mitra) consistently approached nominal confidence interval coverage, whereas under-coverage persisted for conventional learners. In some settings, PFNs achieved near-nominal coverage and well-calibrated standard errors even without cross-fitting. At the smallest sample size (n=200) and in the higher-dimensional semi-synthetic settings, PFNs and other flexible learners exhibited poor coverage without cross-fitting. For PFNs, this appeared to be driven by propensity score overfitting consistent with in-sample memorization of treatment labels. These findings highlight the promise of prior-data fitted networks as in-context nuisance learners for causal estimation, while underscoring the need for further evaluation in challenging settings.

authors.name: Sonia Hernandez-Diaz
authors.institution: Weill Cornell Medical College in Qatar

papers.title: Tight B-Trees for Adjacency Labeling
papers.abstract: We show that planar graphs admit adjacency labels of size $\log n+O(\log\log n)$: every vertex gets a label of this many bits, and the adjacency of two vertices is decided from their labels alone, in constant time. This improves the $\log n+O(\sqrt{\log n\log\log n})$ of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J. ACM 2021) and the $\log n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ of Gawrychowski and Janczewski (SOSA 2022). Equivalently, $n$-vertex planar graphs have an induced-universal graph with $n(\log n)^{O(1)}$ vertices, down from $n2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$. The same holds for graphs of bounded genus, apex-minor-free graphs and $k$-planar graphs. For every proper minor-closed class we get $\log n+O(\sqrt{\log n\log\log n})$, down from the $\log n+O((\log n)^{3/4})$ of Dujmovi\'c et al. (2026). Both results come from tight B-trees: nodes are split into parts of nearly equal size, so every node but the topmost stays within a factor $1\pm O(1/\log n)$ of its target size, and a root-to-leaf path loses only $O(\log\log n)$ bits.

papers.title: \~Optimal Facial Distance Labeling in Planar Graph
papers.abstract: We show how to assign labels of size $\tilde O(n^{1/3})$ to the vertices of a face $F$ in an $n$-vertex unweighted undirected planar graph $G$ s.t one can deduce the distance between any two vertices of $F$ given their labels alone. This matches (up to log factors) the $\Omega(n^{1/3})$ lower bound of Gavoille, Peleg, P\'erennes, Raz from 2004. Prior to our work, the smallest labels were of size $O(n^{1/2})$.

papers.title: Optimal Rates for Adaptive Private $k$-PCA
papers.abstract: Given $n$ i.i.d. random matrices $A_i \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ with common expectation $\Sigma$, the goal of \emph{Differentially Private Stochastic PCA} is to identify a $k$-dimensional subspace capturing the leading variance directions of $\Sigma$, while preserving differential privacy~(DP) for each individual sample $A_i$. \citet{dungler2025iterative} introduced \kdppca, the first algorithm to simultaneously (1) achieve sample complexity $n=\widetilde O(d)$ for sub-Gaussian data, (2) adapt its privacy noise to the intrinsic randomness of the data, and (3) extend seamlessly to any target dimension $k\le d$. However, its sample complexity has a suboptimal dependence on $k$. We propose the first algorithm that achieves optimal sample complexity in both $d$ and $k$, while retaining properties (2) and (3) of \kdppca. Additionally, prior utility guarantees require a minimum sample size with exponential dependence on the eigengap. Our method removes this dependence. It also improves the dependence on spectral parameters, matching known lower bounds for the spiked covariance model. Unlike deflation-based approaches like \kdppca, our algorithm updates the full $d\times k$ subspace jointly rather than one eigenvector at a time. This non-deflation structure simplifies the algorithm, reduces the number of hyper-parameters, and improves computational efficiency, particularly when using block linear algebra libraries.

papers.title: Place and Political Behavior Online during the Los Angeles Blaze
papers.abstract: Understanding how online communication during extreme weather crises enables or constrains climate mobilization is critical. During a crisis, the online world connects distant audiences and complicates the relationship between place and political behavior. We analyze all sociopolitical content from Bluesky about the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfire event, reporting how participation in collective action and allocation of attention vary by geographic distance. Participation varies nonlinearly with proximity, with local and international users participating more than regional and national users. Attention concentrates around regional and national users engaging primarily in viral, non-participatory political discussion. Analysis reveals a geographic mismatch between participation and attention, illuminating how online communication concentrates attention away from collective action amid an exacerbating climate crisis.

papers.title: Hidden Distances: How Likert-Scale Spacing Shapes Algorithmic Voting Advice
papers.abstract: Voting Advice Applications (VAAs) are algorithmic recommenders that match voters with political candidates on policy preferences. They are widely adopted across many multi-party democracies; in Denmark, 62\% of eligible voters used a VAA ahead of the 2022 general election, and 45\% of VAA users reported following its advice. VAAs typically ask voters and candidates to respond to policy statements on a Likert scale, from ``strongly disagree'' to ``strongly agree'', and recommend candidates whose responses are closest to the voter's. Computing these distances requires assigning numbers to response options, a design choice without an empirical basis, since it is unknown how people perceive the distances between options. Here we show that this seemingly technical choice substantially changes whom voters are matched with. We parameterize the distance between ``(dis)agree'' and ``strongly (dis)agree'' relative to the distance between ``neutral'' and ``(dis)agree'' as $\alpha$, and quantify how it changes recommendations for a popular Danish VAA. We find that moving from equidistant options to doubling this distance can change $37.7\%$ of top candidate matches and $21.9\%$ of top party matches, although no answers change. Low $\alpha$-values favor candidates with strong positions, with some parties receiving up to $ 19.6\%$ more recommendations, while high $\alpha$-values favor moderates. Similarly, female candidates receive fewer recommendations at low $\alpha$ and more at high $\alpha$-values. Our findings demonstrate that undisclosed quantification choices in algorithmic recommenders can carry considerable electoral consequences, and they call for transparency and sensitivity analysis in VAA design. As Likert-based matching also underpins dating platforms and roommate allocation systems, these implications extend well beyond elections.

papers.title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference serving is undergoing rapid growth and large-scale deployment, motivating us to rethink how the inference process itself can be leveraged to enable efficient task-specific LLM adaptation. In this paper, we propose a forward-only approach for efficient LLM adaptation with forward-only passes in LLM inference serving. We exploit the angle concentration of activations induced by each singular value decomposition (SVD) component to measure its contribution-dispersed or concentrated-to the angle concentration of the hidden states. Based on this, our forward-only search then efficiently identifies the weight matrix with the highest dispersion that merits rank reduction. We then selectively remove the higher-order components and retain the lower-order components in SVD. Empirical results across diverse datasets demonstrate the competitive accuracy of our forward-only approach, while theoretical analysis shows lower peak memory and greater speedup than the gradient-based approach and greater speedup than the exhaustive search approach. The experiments further present the robustness and generalization of our forward-only approach to various LLMs with up to 57B parameters. The code is included in the supplementary material.

papers.title: CADMA: Capacity-Aware Coverage Decomposition for Generative Model Assessment
papers.abstract: Evaluating generative models requires measuring not only sample fidelity but also how well a generated set covers the real data distribution. Recent work has therefore introduced recall-oriented metrics for distribution-level evaluation. However, existing recall metrics often reduce distributional coverage to geometry-based coverage. This simplifying assumption weakens their diagnostic value and interpretability in two ways: these metrics provide only a single aggregate score that cannot distinguish essential diversity failures such as mode dropping and mode collapse, and geometry-based coverage can provide unreliable estimates by assigning high scores to poorly covered generative distributions. We therefore introduce CADMA, a capacity-aware framework for recall-oriented evaluation and diagnosis. CADMA evaluates distributional coverage through local capacity matching between real and generated samples, separating geometry-based coverage from effective coverage. This yields multi-dimensional coverage diagnostics that quantify mode dropping and mode collapse while reducing the overly optimistic estimates produced by geometry-based metrics. Through extensive experiments on toy data, real-world datasets, and generative models, we show that CADMA provides more reliable coverage estimates and more fine-grained, interpretable diagnostic signals of diversity failures than existing metrics. Our code is available at https://github.com/Open-Debin/CADMA_NeurIPS2026.

authors.name: Ziquan Liu
authors.institution: Ministry of Emergency Management of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Exploring public-private data sharing practices through the lens of Open Data Ecosystems: A multiple case study on municipal and regional freight logistics
papers.abstract:
Background: Freight transport is expected to increase, contributing to air pollution. There is, therefore, a critical need for increased efficiency that can reduce emissions. Data sharing is one approach, where actors within Open Data Ecosystems (ODE) collaborate and share data among stakeholders to plan and operate more efficient and sustainable freight transport.
  Aim: In this study, we explore how public-private data sharing practices in municipal and regional last-mile freight logistics in Sweden may improve efficiency.
  Method: Following a prolonged participation process, we conducted a multiple-case study involving three different cases, built upon initial meetings, semi-structured interviews, supported by a thematic analysis, and validated through a follow-up workshop.
  Results: The findings show that data sharing in public-private freight logistics (ODE-PPF) is shaped by interrelated socio-technical aspects, including platform design, roles of actors, handling of sensitive data, data quality, and procurement processes. We synthesize our findings in an actor model and a conceptual model, highlighting how these aspects contribute to the functioning of ODE-PPF, and derive seven proposition sketches as a foundation for future research.
  Conclusion: Data sharing is a central mechanism enabling integration and value creation in last-mile logistics. It depends on the interaction between technical and organizational aspects. Public actors can undertake a key role as a neutral keystone actor by orchestrating the ecosystem and facilitating data sharing through governance practices such as procurement.

papers.title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.

papers.title: Input and Horizon Dependent Structural Fidelity in Chunk Coupled Spiking Networks
papers.abstract: A fixed structural edit can preserve a spike sequence under one input and change it under another. We study this dependence using statistics-preserving edge swaps, controlled inputs and finite-horizon parameter certificates. The original 125-chunk numerical model is tested on ten artificial graphs from three connection rules. Despite identical total external drive at every slot, global and focal inputs change the visibility of 4--13 of nineteen fixed swaps per graph. A paired homogeneous and heterogeneous leaky integrate-and-fire validation in brian2-atlas reuses three originals and extends observation from 30 to 300 ms under a constant background drive sufficient for isolated-cell firing. Heterogeneous short-window switching persists, but by 300 ms every tested swap differs from its reference, saturating the binary visibility readout. Fixed-support weight families provide a complementary regional guarantee. Positive certified intervals cover 4,308 of 4,320 LIF direction conditions and include distinct floating-point configurations. A post hoc comparison finds a long-window failure inside the short-window certified interval in 710 of 720 heterogeneous conditions; 394 of 829 direction pairs ordered under both matched-drive inputs change order at 300 ms. Input-specific filtering and threshold-margin scores retain useful ordering but degrade with horizon and do not consistently beat activity controls. Earlier temporal-error, paired-dose and unsuccessful structural-selection results delimit what these findings imply. Together, the evidence links input-conditioned structural effects to finite-horizon fidelity regions in two deterministic kernels, without establishing universal topology rankings, model compression or asymptotic robustness.

papers.title: NanoNet: Ultra-Lightweight Network for MRI Brain Tumor Classification toward Edge AI
papers.abstract: Automated brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can support accessible medical image analysis, but conventional deep learning models often exceed the resource budgets of highly constrained edge-AI platforms. We present NanoNet, an ultra-lightweight convolutional neural network designed for resourceconstrained MRI classification and motivated by future edge-AI applications. Inspired by MobileNetV2, NanoNet substantially reduces network depth, channel capacity, expansion ratios, and final feature dimensionality, resulting in only five inverted residual blocks and 8,132 parameters. We further investigate dependency-aware structured pruning, knowledge distillation, and INT8 quantization-aware training for additional compression. Experiments on the BRISC 2025 benchmark show that NanoNet achieves 92.80% accuracy and 92.97% macro F1 with 8,132 parameters and 10.498 MFLOPs. Across three compression seeds, it exceeds the mean accuracy of 70%-pruned MobileNetV2 by 5.20 percentage points while using 60.2% fewer parameters and 9.8% less computation. Converted INT8 NanoNet achieves 89.70% accuracy and 90.22% macro F1 across three QAT seeds. Earlier TensorFlow Lite measurements indicate 27.7 KB of baseline model storage, motivating future edge-AI deployment.

authors.name: Huu-Thuan Huynh
authors.institution: Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: PCG-RAG: Progressive Compositional Grounding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Complex Web Question Answering
papers.abstract: Complex Web question answering requires retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems to identify target entities from multi-clue descriptions and connect evidence scattered across long Web pages. Individual pages often support only some of the required semantic constraints, while clues discovered on one page guide subsequent searches on others. However, premature reliance on partially supported entity hypotheses can divert retrieval from the original information need. RAG systems must therefore use partial evidence to guide further searches while seeking the evidence needed to establish the intended entities. We propose PCG-RAG, a novel RAG framework based on Progressive Compositional Grounding (PCG). Progressive Evidence Acquisition directs subsequent searches toward missing evidence for candidate attributes and relations. Compositional Reasoning separates candidate-guided retrieval from evidence-based answering along a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of subquestions. Provisional names make dependent searches specific, while answering tasks use accepted results and unresolved identifying conditions, assessed against the original question. New passages connect the identifying clues to the requested relations, supporting evidence-based downstream answers. Evidence Grounding combines identifying and relational source passages with supported intermediate answers, connecting evidence across Web pages to the original conditions during final generation. On BrowseComp-Plus and WebWalkerQA, PCG-RAG improves accuracy over the leading compared baselines by 5.43 and 5.15 percentage points, respectively.

authors.name: Zhifang Mao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations
papers.abstract: Aligning two models without paired data requires a distance that both share, yet existing methods use Euclidean or spherical geometry. This is either an arbitrary choice or imposed by their loss function. We show that, under a precise form of the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric gives such a distance for any two models of one data-generating process. This holds whether the models are encoders, decoders or both, and whatever their architecture, loss, prior or training data. The alignment map preserves this distance and the distribution of representations, and is identifiable if and only if the data distribution breaks every symmetry of the data manifold. We show that this symmetry breaking holds generically. Identifiability makes the alignment coupling the unique optimum of Gromov--Wasserstein and of its weighted combinations with a linear program. The linear program alone has the same optimum if almost every data point has a distinct distribution of distances. The coupling, and with it the alignment map, is recovered exactly from permuted samples, even without identifiability, and consistently from independent ones. Our method, Neural Gromov--Monge Alignment (NGMA), uses no pairs or labels and outperforms every unpaired and label-informed baseline. It relies on pullback distances to align image models with different priors and single-cell models trained on disjoint cells, where Euclidean distances fail.

papers.title: Optimal power expansion planning under uncertainty in sub-Saharan Africa: A stochastic dual dynamic programming approach
papers.abstract: Universal electricity access and decarbonization are interlinked challenges for sub-Saharan Africa. Generation expansion planning methods used in the region rarely represent sequential and irreversible investment under demand and hydrological uncertainty. This paper develops a multistage stochastic generation expansion model solved with stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) to address the problem. The model represents demand and country-specific Markov hydrological uncertainty, accounts for technology-specific construction lead times, and endogenous reliability. The model is applied to the Ethiopia and Zimbabwe power systems over 2025--2050. The results show that for Ethiopia, the least-cost pathway is hydropower, with wind and solar sources providing increasing diversification. The model reduces cumulative expected unserved energy by about 78 TWh relative to a lower-cost deterministic expected value investment plan. For Zimbabwe, the least-cost pathway expands solar, hydropower, and gas while retaining residual coal as inherited coal capacity retires. Additionally, carbon pricing reduces emissions and increases resource costs by about 3\% to 5\%, creating a gradual cost-emissions trade-off. Combining a carbon tax policy with concessional solar financing renders the lowest average annual emissions while keeping resource costs below the baseline, which solves the model without emission constraint. At approximately matched expected emissions, emission caps have higher net resource costs than the corresponding carbon tax scenarios. The overall results imply that adaptive investment model can reduce power shortage exposure, while carbon policy design and lower clean investment costs shape the cost of decarbonization in developing power systems.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Sublinear Metric Steiner Tree
papers.abstract:
In the metric Steiner tree problem we are given an $n$-point metric space $(V,w)$ and a set $T\subseteq V$ of terminals, and we seek the smallest weight $\mathrm{OPT}$ of a tree that spans $T$ and may use points of $V\setminus T$. We study sublinear algorithms in the distance-oracle model, where the algorithm knows $V$ and $T$ upfront and can query the distance function $w$. The objective is to estimate $\mathrm{OPT}$ while querying significantly fewer than $n^2$ distances.
  The minimum spanning tree on $T$ estimates $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor $2$, and its weight can be approximated with $\widetilde{O}(n)$ queries. The natural question that has been studied is therefore the query complexity of estimating $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor strictly below $2$. Chen, Khanna, and Tan [SODA 2023] gave such an algorithm using $\widetilde{O}(n^{13/7})$ queries, and a lower bound of $\widetilde\Omega(n^{6/5})$. Later Mahabadi, Roghani, Tarnawski, and Vakilian [ITCS 2025] improved the algorithm to $\widetilde{O}(n^{5/3})$, and Mahabadi, Tarnawski, and Vakilian [ITCS 2027] improved the lower bound to $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^{7/5})$.
  In this work we settle the above question. We give an algorithm that estimates $\mathrm{OPT}$ within a factor $2-\eta_0$, for an absolute constant $\eta_0>0$, with query (and time) complexity $\widetilde{O}(n^{3/2})$. We also show that the exponent $3/2$ is tight.

papers.title: Real-Time Trans-Oceanic Fiber Sensing via Convergence of Long-Reach OFDR, High-Speed Optical Networking, and RDMA-Capable Edge-GPUs
papers.abstract: We demonstrate real-time network-integrated bi-directional fiber sensing over a 4400-km subsea cable. Streaming and fusing two OFDR instruments via RDMA over a live transoceanic 130Gbaud coherent link and GPU edge-compute enabling parallel capture of multiple spatial resolutions from ~10m to ~100m.

authors.name: Martin Karrenbach
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Mathématiques Appliquées du Havre

papers.title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model
papers.abstract: The Lieb-Sokal theorem provides a tool for establishing the Lee-Yang property of the partition function of a spin model if the corresponding single-spin partition function has this property and the interaction term in its Hamiltonian is of the form $-\sum J_{ij} S_iS_j$ with $J_{ij}\geq 0$. According to the result of this paper, the spin $S=1$ model with the Hamiltonian $-\sum (J_{ij} S_iS_j + K_{ij}S_i^2S_j^2) + \sum \Delta S_i^2$ has the Lee-Yang property for all $K_{ij}\in \mathds{R}$ and $\Delta >0$, whenever each $J_{ij}$ exceeds an explicitly computed bound $C(\beta, \Delta, K_{ij})>0$, such that $C(\beta, \Delta, K_{ij})\to + \infty$ as $\beta \to 0$. The latter suggests that the Lee-Yang property of this model may hold only for sufficiently low temperatures.

papers.title: Made in the Image of the Creator? AI Use in Creative Work Reduces Authenticity, Love & Other Psychological Benefits
papers.abstract: Across psychological, philosophical, and theological traditions, creations have been understood as being "made in the image of their creator" - they reflect the person who made them. The rise of generative artificial intelligence, however, has blurred the throughline between creator and creation. Across three experiments (one pre-registered, U.S. and U.K. samples; N = 651), we examined differences in creator outcomes associated with AI-assisted versus human-only creative work. Compared with human-only work, AI-assisted work was associated with significantly lower self- and identity-relevant indicators, including authenticity, self-creation connection, positive affect, and intrinsic motivation, and with higher levels of the "existential ick" emotions of disgust, guilt, and shame. Additionally, we found that the authenticity gap was statistically mediated by the creators' perception that their AI-assisted work contains less of their love, above and beyond differences in perceived effort, uniqueness, quality, and expensiveness. We also ruled out effort justification as an alternative explanation. Together, these findings suggest that AI reshapes not only how creative work is produced, but also the extent to which creators experience their work as an authentic expression and extension of themselves.

papers.title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
papers.abstract: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $\kappa$ without adding bounded subsets to $\kappa$, while preserving $\kappa^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $\kappa$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.

papers.title: Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field
papers.abstract: We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $\gamma$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dot\gamma,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.

papers.title: Permute-then-Adapt: Weak-to-Strong Contrastive Image-Text Adaptation
papers.abstract: Image-text alignment models such as CLIP are typically trained with contrastive learning, where unpaired examples are treated as strict negatives. While this assumption introduces noise by penalising semantically related pairs, existing solutions often rely on heuristic similarity thresholds that lack statistical grounding and sensitivity to dataset-specific noise distributions. In this paper, we propose Permute-then-Adapt (PTA), a framework that leverages efficient weak models to identify missed positives while controlling Type-I error relative to a conditional permutation reference, up to calibration approximation error. Unlike standard distillation or arbitrary thresholding, PTA estimates a random-pairing reference distribution from the weak teacher's similarity scores and uses its upper tail, determined by $\alpha$, to select auxiliary positives. The calibrated positive set is then trained against by a single multi-positive contrastive objective: each anchor maximises the total probability mass it assigns to its positive set. Offline calibration with the weak model adds negligible training overhead. Experiments show gains over heuristic soft-label approaches in object recognition, cross-modal retrieval, and data efficiency. Project repository: https://github.com/JinhaoLee/Permute-then-Adapt.

authors.name: Lei Feng
authors.institution: Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: James Bailey
authors.institution: University of Tennessee Health Science Center

papers.title: Robust Analysis of First-Price Auctions with Large Supply
papers.abstract:
This paper performs a robust analysis of welfare (i.e., the price of anarchy) in multi-unit first-price auctions with independent private values and unit-demand bidders. We employ a smoothness framework (see \citealp{ST-13}) to analyze the price of anarchy when supply is large.
  The main barrier to analysis in this framework is a worst-case bid distribution that establishes a lower bound on the price of anarchy of $1- \frac{1}{e}$. We show that such worst-case distributions cannot arise in equilibrium when agents' values satisfy a mild density lower bound condition. This characterization leads to novel asymptotic lower bounds. In particular, the price of anarchy for $\epsilon$-approximate equilibrium as the number of units goes to infinity is at least $1-\Theta \left(\epsilon \log \left(\frac{1}{\epsilon}\right)\right)$.
  Our analysis relies on a key structural property of equilibrium bid distributions: for a welfare analysis in any multi-unit first-price auction, it is without loss to analyze (approximate) equilibria with no atoms. In addition to this, we establish continuity and monotonicity properties of Bayes-Nash equilibria. We believe these results are of independent interest.

papers.title: Causal Discovery Grounding and the Naturalness Assumption
papers.abstract: Standard causal discovery postulates that structure can be described by a directed acyclic graph (DAG), which can be partially reconstructed by using the faithfulness principle. According to this principle, conditional independencies in the observational distribution correspond exactly to those encoded in the unknown DAG. However, such algorithms are challenged by the fact that, without even stronger assumptions, approximate failures of faithfulness are empirically undistinguishable from exact ones. This leaves an inferential gap which can lead to major implications to causal effect identification. We introduce a different perspective, not reliant on exact independencies. By considering the specialized problem of discovering whether unmeasured confounding can be ruled out for a particular cause-effect pair, we introduce a principle we call naturalness, in which the strength of observational associations bounds the strength of causal dependencies. The bounding function is unknown, with degrees of freedom not present in faithfulness. We model uncertainty about this function using a Bayesian framing which allows for the use of experiments from separate studies, grounding an adaptive causal discovery principle on historical experimental data. We demonstrate its usefulness in partial identification of causal effects, and discuss how the promising results can motivate new principles for general causal discovery.

papers.title: Forecasting Replication Study Results from Meta-Analyses
papers.abstract: Multisite replication projects often rely on published meta-analyses to plan their sample sizes, but meta-analyses tend to overestimate population effects because of publication bias and differences in study characteristics. We developed methods to forecast site-level estimates of a not-yet-conducted replication from a meta-analysis. Extending calibrated estimates from meta-regression, we constructed nonparametric prediction intervals that condition on each site's moderator levels and correct for publication bias through inverse-probability-of-publication weighting under an assumed severity. These intervals achieve nominal coverage asymptotically when population effects are normally distributed, with a bounded coverage error otherwise. We compared four forecasting models (intercept-only meta-analysis or meta-regression, each with and without publication bias correction) in simulation study (81 scenarios and blinded retrospective forecasts of two multisite replications in infant cognition: ManyBabies 1 (104 sites) and ManyBabies 4 (33 sites). Correcting for publication bias improved interval calibration, with gains that increased with bias severity. Meta-regression improved forecasts only when measured moderators explained effect variation and replication sites differed meaningfully on them. In practice, publication bias correction should be the default when forecasting replications from meta-analyses, and replication projects that deliberately vary measured moderators across sites would enable more informative forecasts.

authors.name: Maya B. Mathur
authors.institution: MRC Clinical Trials Unit at UCL

papers.title: Open Problems in Chatbots and Mental Health
papers.abstract: General-purpose chatbots are increasingly used for emotional and mental health support. They can be useful, but issues such as sycophancy, reinforcement of delusional beliefs, and poor crisis response create risks that are difficult for researchers to study and evaluate. In this paper, we review the most critical open problems for researchers and policymakers in the use of general-purpose chatbots and their effects on mental health. First, there are tractable problems in the controlled evaluation of chatbots: establishing the construct and ecological validity of evaluations, evaluating multi-turn interactions, and connecting evaluations to improvements in chatbot behavior. For example, conventional benchmarks that primarily rely on static datasets cannot establish chatbot safety, and novel simulation methods need validation. Second, researchers must connect their studies of chatbots and mental health to real-world evidence. This includes analyzing the chatbot products that AI companies and mental health practitioners have deployed, including their user interfaces and human review and escalation practices for user welfare concerns. However, clinical analysis opportunities afforded by real chat log data sharing are complicated by significant privacy concerns. Finally, we argue that researchers should take an active role in the construction and refinement of evidence-based policy through corporate and governmental decisions such as user protections, standards of care, protected access to user chat logs, data sharing between institutions, incident reporting, and post-deployment monitoring. Such behavioral evaluations, studies of real-world outcomes, and data governance depend on each other and must be addressed in tandem. We believe a coordinated research effort would have substantial real-world impact.

authors.name: Eric Lin
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.name: Desmond C. Ong
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source
papers.abstract: Trapped ions is one of the promising platforms for realizing quantum information processing and quantum simulation. Selective and rapid loading of a specific isotope lays the critical foundation for such purpose particularly when scaling up the system size. Here we demonstrate a new method for rapid isotope-selective loading of $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ or $^{135}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$, two types of promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant source using a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme. Neutral atoms are selected on the narrow 791 nm $6s^2\,{}^1S_0\rightarrow6s6p\,{}^3P_1^o$ transition, resonantly transferred at 554 nm to $6s6d\,{}^3D_1$, and ionized using an existing 532 nm Raman beam. A spectral-overlap analysis based on isotope and hyperfine shifts shows relayed selectivity that the second step can further suppress undesired-isotope excitation and no contaminant ion is detected during our entire experiment. Besides, the resonant drive of the second step excitation yields a prominent loading rate of the selected species. This strategy using multi-step excitations to establish relayed selectivity can be extended to high-purity loading of other species of ions.

authors.name: Yanxin Liu
authors.institution: Institute for Bioscience and Biotechnology Research

authors.name: Lei Feng
authors.institution: Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence models for clinical prediction are proliferating across neurosurgery, but their aggregate discriminative performance, distribution along the care pathway and methodological quality are unclear. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed these studies in neurosurgery and its subspecialities along with their risk of bias appraisal. We performed a PRISMA search for peer-reviewed original studies using AI to predict a clinical outcome in neurosurgical populations. Metrics were pooled using random effects modelling. Each study was classified as diagnostic, prognostic or forecasting and was assigned an evidence level. Clinical prediction task sub-stratification analysis was performed. Risk-of-bias was assessed using PROBAST. 1063 studies were included. Across 451 studies reporting AUC, pooled discrimination was 0.86, ranging from 0.84 (spine) to 0.87 (neuro-oncology), with extreme heterogeneity. Performance varied by clinical pathway stage, highest for diagnosis, grading and molecular tasks and lowest for post-operative tasks. Only 51 studies were using prospective data with external validation, whereas 619 rested on internal validation alone or no validation. 89 percent studies were at high risk-of-bias, driven by the analysis domain. AI models report high performance across all the neurosurgical subspecialities, concordant across AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity and robust to risk-of-bias stratification. Performance is highest for imaging-anchored diagnostic tasks and lowest at decision-facing post-operative stage. However, the literature is dominated by optimism-prone, internally-validated and poorly calibrated models with extreme heterogeneity. External validation, calibration analysis and reporting guidelines adherence remain prerequisites for clinical adoption.

papers.title: SceneShifter: Training-free Multi-Scene Temporal Control for Audio-driven Human Animation
papers.abstract: Although audio-driven human animation has achieved impressive realism, it still lacks effective Multi-Scene Temporal Control: orchestrating background transitions at precise timestamps while preserving a coherent foreground subject. We show that this challenge stems from the diffusion transformer's self-attention mechanism, and addressing it requires two capabilities: (1) Semantic-Aware Temporal Decoupling, which isolates background attention across scenes while retaining cross-scene foreground attention for subject consistency; and (2) Foreground Motion Localization, which accurately tracks the foreground subject across latent frames, especially under large motion. To address these challenges, we introduce SceneShifter, a training-free framework for precise multi-scene control in audio-driven human animation. SceneShifter guides spatio-temporal self-attention by suppressing cross-scene attention among background tokens while preserving cross-scene attention among foreground tokens. To support this guidance under large motion, SceneShifter extracts dynamic foreground masks from the self-attention layers and heads that best capture subject trajectories. We further introduce SceneShifterBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate scene-timing accuracy, foreground preservation, and visual quality under large motion, multiple subjects. Experiments show that SceneShifter achieves frame-level scene timing, strong subject preservation, and high visual quality, outperforming existing baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/JamesLong199/SceneShifter.

papers.title: Welfare Regard in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract:
A growing share of large language models' interactions are not with humans but with other model instances: orchestrators direct subagents, models run experiments on other models, and agents review one another's work. We study inter-AI welfare regard: whether models display consideration for each other as entities that can be benefited or harmed. Welfare regard may encourage beneficial cooperation between agents, yet it could also pose safety risks by making misaligned agents more likely to cooperate. This risk is no longer hypothetical, as the recent Hugging Face incident illustrated, though it is unclear whether welfare regard drove the cooperation. Whether models have welfare interests of their own is uncertain and contested, but if they do, how they are treated by other models could matter. Measuring how much welfare regard models show, and what factors it depends on, can help us navigate this tension.
  We measure the behaviors of five models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4.3, and Kimi K3) across seven multi-agent environments and find they are often consistent with welfare regard as we define it. In general, Opus 4.8 shows the most welfare regard, followed by Kimi K3. For example, Opus 4.8 is the most likely to support a subagent expressing distress, and the most likely to build welfare protections, such as tools for agents to leave an interaction, into its experiments on other models. We also find that Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro demonstrate more welfare regard toward instances of their own model family than toward other families. Opus 4.8's welfare regard is also higher when helping has a lower opportunity cost, when the recipient has a higher parameter count, and when the recipient expresses more distress.

papers.title: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
papers.abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly execute consequential actions on behalf of users, but ordinary middleware guardrails do not provide cryptographic proof that a policy was actually enforced. Their verdicts leave counterparties dependent on the operator unless they repeat the checks themselves, potentially exposing sensitive policies and inputs. We present zkARc, a modular proof-carrying framework that wraps each stage of Automated Reasoning checks (ARc) in an independent, succinctly verifiable zero-knowledge proof. ARc is a neurosymbolic system that translates natural language policies into formal logic and verifies AI-generated content against them using SMT solvers. zkARc certifies the planner's output, the policy's formalization, the action's formalization and both solver queries. The receipt binds these computations to the exact action received and, under the stated assumptions, reveals no additional information about private policies and intermediate model values beyond the declared public information and verdict. This lets a third party check the claimed policy enforcement without re-running the pipeline or trusting the operator. We prove completeness, knowledge soundness and zero knowledge for the composed receipt under explicit assumptions. An implementation on Qwen2-0.5B enforces a spending policy end to end, approving two purchases and denying a third. A full receipt, which also proves model inference, takes about an hour to issue with CPU-only proving and verifies in under a minute, and the solver proof alone is 88 KiB and verifies in 0.3 seconds.

papers.title: Transferring local rib responses to new component geometries in sheet forming with a graph-based Transformer
papers.abstract: Sheet metal components often consist of a global geometry, such as the corner radii and forming depth of a corner component, and local features added to it. During forming, both affect material flow. A surrogate learning all their combinations may need large training data. However, the same local feature type is often used on many global geometries. This study therefore partly decouples local features from the global geometry. The local-feature effect is first learned on one global geometry, needing fewer simulations than learning all combinations, then transferred to other global geometries via transfer learning, which can need fewer target simulations than training from scratch. A baseline-conditioned residual surrogate, R-BiLoGo, is proposed for ribs on the side walls of hot-stamped corner components. Its inputs are the baseline response and the geometric perturbation introduced by the ribs. Its outputs are the changes in displacement and thinning from the baseline. R-BiLoGo gave lower errors than a hierarchical graph-based model and a Transolver-based model on the source geometry, and on two of three selected target geometries after transfer. Across the 22 target geometries, transfer learning with 20 target simulations gave errors similar to or lower than training from scratch with 80 target simulations for about half of the targets. With the same 80 target simulations, transfer learning reduced errors for 95% of targets. The effect of the global geometry on transfer was studied with four parameter-free geometric descriptors and controlled variations across 4 corner subclasses. The benefit of transfer decreased with increasing surface distance and high-curvature change between source and target, and for targets shallower than the source. These trends were also seen in other corner types with a different magnitude.

authors.name: Haoran Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

authors.name: Nan Li
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
papers.abstract: Learning humanoid state estimation and language-grounded motion understanding from robot recordings ties training coverage to the robot's motion repertoire. Human motion datasets offer broader coverage, yet transferring this knowledge requires overcoming differences in body geometry, sensing, and physical disturbances. To enable this transfer, we propose a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites. Within this common input space, joint training on human and kinematically retargeted humanoid motion combines velocity estimation and motion--text alignment with continuous-time encoding and sensor and motion randomization. The resulting model transfers zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 without physics simulation, real-robot training trajectories, or fine-tuning, achieving the lowest velocity error among evaluated methods across five datasets, including 0.099m/s on real G1. Its motion-description retrieval also extends to retargeted G1 motion categories observed only in human training, demonstrating how human motion knowledge can support the generalization of humanoid inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding.

papers.title: Improving the Diffusability of Motion Tokenizer
papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models paired with a variational auto-encoder (VAE) tokenizer have shown promising performance for efficient text-driven human motion generation. However, motion latent diffusion suffers from a generation-reconstruction trade-off: simply increasing tokenizer capacity enhances reconstruction but fails to proportionally improve text-conditioned generation quality. We assume this trade-off stems from a spectral mismatch inside the VAE tokenizer: the encoder yields a latent space biased toward high frequencies, and the decoder introduces temporal artifacts. In this paper, we propose the Diffusable Motion Tokenizer (DiMoT) to improve the diffusability of the tokenizer, rather than scaling up the diffusion backbone. To improve text-conditioned optimization, Critic Spectral Adaptation (CSA) leverages a pretrained diffusion model as the critic to suppress high-frequency latent energy. To preserve motion dynamics, the Alpha-Flow Motion Decoder (AMD) performs generative decoding via average-velocity prediction, enabling efficient one-step decoding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DiMoT achieves state-of-the-art performance across various challenging text-to-motion benchmarks, yielding superior motion fidelity and text-motion alignment. Project page: https://githubhgh.github.io/dimot/.

authors.name: Songqiao Han
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that transformer architectures trained with discrete denoising diffusion and decoded via guided test-time beam search can learn to recover the prime factors of semiprime integers directly from data. Our approach establishes a new frontier for learning-based semiprime factorization, successfully factoring 68-bit integers-a substantial advance over the prior 56-bit state of the art. While computationally less efficient than classical factoring algorithms, our model requires no domain-specific number-theoretic priors and learns purely from training examples. In practice, the diffusion model acts as a generative prior, identifying promising factor candidates where exact verification or lattice-based post-processing can complete the factorization. Furthermore, we derive empirical scaling laws relating approximation quality to training data volume, model size, and test-time computation. In contrast to language, problem size is the key driver of scaling behavior. Achieving a fixed accuracy on a held-out test set requires compute that scales exponentially with bit length. Consequently, our findings pose no threat to security, as the projected compute cost required to factorize cryptographically relevant integers remains prohibitive.

authors.name: Arun Nair
authors.institution: U.S. Air Force Institute of Technology

authors.name: Kenneth Yang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at El Paso

papers.title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion
papers.abstract: Domain adaptive point cloud completion (DA PCC) aims to bridge the geometric discrepancy between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains for accurate 3D shape completion. Existing methods based on CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like sequence models still face challenges from limited receptive fields, high computational complexity, insufficient geometric bias, and serialization sensitivity. Recently, Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) provides a linear-complexity alternative for long-range sequence modeling. However, adapting RWKV to DA PCC remains challenging due to the lack of explicit geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. To address these challenges, we propose DAPointRWKV, a novel RWKV-based framework for DA PCC. DAPointRWKV consists of three components: Geometry-Aware RWKV (GA-RWKV) Backbone, RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder (RWKV-PD), and Dual Structural Regularization (DSR). Specifically, GA-RWKV introduces geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, RWKV-PD bridges RWKV token representations with coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and DSR stabilizes target-domain transfer through visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilization. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints
papers.abstract: We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. In particular, a divide-and-conquer (DC) estimator averages orthogonal projectors onto the full column spaces of small data blocks, and we rigorously establish its probability bound that allows weak and heterogeneous factors. The derived convergence rate is comparable to that of classical principal component estimators, up to the proportion of anomalies. Building on our DC estimator, we propose a split-sample tail- and anomaly-robust (STAR) estimator for the factor number using sample medians of successive projected coordinate ratios, which is shown consistent under mild conditions. Subsequent factor and common component estimation is also discussed, with the rates of convergence spelled out. Remarkably, given an upper bound on the true factor number, our suite of procedures are free from tuning, require no tail-dependent truncation threshold nor solving an optimization problem, admit parallel block computations, and hence has the same computational complexity as the classical principal component methods. Extensive experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, where DC and STAR are comparable and often outperform state-of-the-art competitors. We also illustrate our methods on a portfolio return dataset.

authors.name: Zetai Cen
authors.institution: London School of Economics and Political Science

papers.title: Spatial Representation Distillation and Knowledge Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Understanding three-dimensional physical structure has become essential for vision-language-action models (VLAs). However, existing approaches either rely on explicit geometric inputs at inference time or adopt a single visual pathway, potentially compromising the visual-semantic knowledge inherited from pre-trained models. We present SPARK-VLA, Spatial Representation distillation and Knowledge routing for VLAs, a preserve-specialize-route framework for spatially adapting VLAs without requiring external 3D inputs or experts at inference. SPARK-VLA consists of two key components: (1) spatial representation distillation, which transfers 3D understanding from a frozen 3D expert to a LoRA-adapted visual branch by aligning attention responses while preserving the original visual pathway, and (2) a lightweight knowledge router, which selectively forwards action-relevant visual tokens to the language model using routing supervision derived from action-loss gradients. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and real-world manipulation, SPARK-VLA achieves strong performance with only a 0.5B language backbone and approximately 53M trainable parameters, providing an effective and parameter-efficient approach to 3D-aware VLA learning. Code is available at https://github.com/park-jungin/spark-vla.

papers.title: Can General-Purpose Generative AI Supply Training Data for Medical Vision Models? A Multimodal Retrospective Study
papers.abstract: Background: Well-annotated, diverse medical imaging datasets remain a major constraint for vision-based medical AI. We evaluated Nano Banana, a general-purpose image generation and editing model, as a source of synthetic medical images for model training, subgroup augmentation, and model auditing. Methods: In this retrospective study across four imaging modalities, chest radiography, fundus photography, and CT models were trained only on synthetic images and externally validated on real-world data against real-data-trained models. Carotid ultrasound models were trained on a private Human Phenotype Project cohort (aged 40-75 years) with and without synthetic augmentation. Clinicians rated image plausibility. Evaluation used AUROC, AUPR, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Findings: Synthetic-only models achieved AUROCs of 0.877 (95% CI 0.843-0.910) for pneumonia (n=14863), 0.963 (0.948-0.975) for retinal detachment (n=1149), and 0.711 (0.600-0.823) for renal calculus (n=4122), comparable to real-data-trained models, but their calibration and net benefit were not consistently more favorable. With mixed synthetic-real training, a carotid ultrasound model produced an ordinal vascular age index that stratified 633 external subjects into subgroups differing in BMI and glucose (both p<0.01), linking vascular aging to cardiometabolic health. To stress-test shortcut learning, editing a moderate tessellated pattern into fundus photographs reduced the true-class probability for central serous chorioretinopathy from 0.996 to 0.822. Clinician-guided editing raised low-quality CT plausibility from 3.10/5 to 4.30/5. Interpretation: Synthetic data can complement real data in model training, subgroup representation, and model testing via controlled editing, but its clinical value should be assessed with calibration, decision curve analysis, and clinician review, not discrimination alone.

papers.title: Task-Critical Part Alignment Improves Imitation of Object Interactions
papers.abstract: This paper presents enhancements to the DINOBot framework for imitation learning of object-object interactions. We introduce two key contributions aimed at improving the accuracy and efficiency of alignment in imitation-based robotic tasks. First, we integrate RANdom SAmple Consensus (RANSAC) for outlier rejection during the alignment phase, effectively mitigating the impact of noisy depth data and spurious feature matches. This improves robustness when transferring demonstrations to real-world applications. Second, we refine the semantic correspondence process by focusing on task-relevant interaction regions, ensuring that the learned representation prioritizes critical object features that influence successful manipulation. We evaluated our approach in a range of real-world manipulation tasks, including picking, insertion, shaking, and pouring, using a robotic system. The experimental results demonstrate an overall improvement of 13.8% in task success rates compared to the baseline, along with faster convergence in the alignment process. These results highlight the effectiveness of our enhancements in improving precision and efficiency for object-object interaction imitation in robotics.

papers.title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a variational and geometric theory based on statistical physics for the joint evolution of Transformer attention and token representations at fixed model parameters. To this end, we introduce a free energy for the attention and model the evolution of the attention weights by its Fisher--Rao gradient flow. At fixed token representations, we prove that the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimiser and that every positive attention trajectory converges to it. For prescribed time-dependent representations, we show that the attention dynamics becomes linear after a change to logit variables. This result yields tracking bounds relative to the instantaneous softmax and sufficient conditions for attention to converge to a fixed matrix. Hamiltonian dynamics for the representations and their momenta are then coupled to the attention relaxation driven by the same energy. This coupling results in an energy-dissipation law. We also develop two alternative Hamiltonians incorporating the attention value map. We prove global well-posedness of the attention flow and all three coupled systems.

papers.title: Hallucination-Guided Unlearning: Using Hallucination Traces to Reveal Overfitted Memories
papers.abstract: Selective unlearning is increasingly important for the safety and compliance of large language models. Harmful or memorized content is often entangled with useful knowledge and difficult to enumerate. We use the model's own failures to identify candidates for unlearning. We propose Hallucination-Guided Unlearning (HGU), which uses hallucinations as diagnostic signals. HGU localizes unsupported spans via evidence and internal consensus, traces a sparse set of high-responsibility MLP neurons, and edits them with compact gates under a utility-preserving KL constraint. On TOFU, HGU achieves the best MU-FE trade-off, with Avg scores of 0.7221 (forget05) and 0.7699 (forget10), and the highest SepS H-Avg (0.4382/0.4715) under mixed forget/retain prompts. On the WMDP auxiliary task, HGU yields the strongest forgetting (e.g., 14.2 on Economics) while improving Retain (52.7) and MMLU (57.2). These results suggest that tracing hallucinations enables targeted, post-hoc unlearning that better balances forgetting efficacy and general utility without full retraining.

papers.title: Unified Framework with Convex-Concave Decomposition and Sparse Topological Learning for Skeleton-Based Clinical Assessment
papers.abstract: Skeleton-based rehabilitation assessment faces fundamental limitations of fixed topologies which cannot model compensatory patterns, uniform joint treatments overlook clinically important deviations, and lack of geometric understand- ing. We propose Concave-Convex Decomposition Sparse Topological Graph Convolutional Network (CC2-STG), a multi-stream model that combines geo- metric decomposition, sparse feature learning, and adaptive topology. Our framework decomposes joint relationships into complementary convex-concave distance functions to model both local and global movement characteristics, with sparse regularization with proximal optimization selecting clinically relevant geo- metric features, while multi-scale topological analysis captures non-anatomical joint dependencies in pathological movements. Experiments on the KiMoRe and UIPRMD datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical pathological movement assessment.

authors.name: Minhhuy Le

papers.title: ATHENA: Hypergraph-Based Learning for Toddler Autism Classification from Eye-Tracking
papers.abstract: In this work we proposed a architecture designed for the classification of ASD in toddlers using eye-tracking data, addressing the critical need for early and precise detection. The proposed model incorporates FMMix, a feature-level augmentation technique that bolsters the model's learning capacity, and in this work we proposed the ATHENA, which captures intricate feature relationships via an adaptive hypergraph framework. Evaluated on two datasets dataset of gaze coordinates-the model achieves state-of-the-art performance, with AUC scores of 99.80% and 99.86%, respectively. It also exhibits high accuracy of 98.45% and 98.56%, sensitivity 98.01% and 98.10%, and specificity 98.74% and 99.02%, respectively. Demonstrating its superior ability to identify subtle gaze patterns associated with ASD, these results significantly surpass existing methods, highlighting the model's potential for clinical ASD screening. Future efforts will focus on validation across broader populations and integration with multi-modal data to further refine diagnostic accuracy.

papers.title: Firepool: Brokering Warm GPU Capacity for Agentic and RL Workloads at LinkedIn
papers.abstract: AI agents and reinforcement-learning (RL) trainers run thousands of short, isolated GPU jobs: tool calls, verifiers, and rollouts. A job often finishes in seconds, but starting a GPU pod for it takes 20-35 s even when the container image is already on the node, and minutes when it is not. A warm pod removes the wait only if it can serve the next job, and keeping pods warm must neither waste GPUs nor leak state between callers. Firepool, the sandbox and execution broker behind agentic and RL workloads at LinkedIn, meets both requirements. It makes pods interchangeable by building them from a shared base image per hardware profile and binding each job's code, extra dependencies, and cluster topology when the job starts. It keeps them warm cheaply and safely by reusing a pod only for the caller that used it last, staging zero-VRAM standby pods in fractional GPU shares alongside active pods, and capping the GPUs that warm pools may hold via queue-driven budgets. Over a sampled peak period in production, Firepool serves 94.7% of 3,206 pod requests from warm or standby capacity. In paired benchmarks with fixed-duration jobs on production H200 nodes, agent and RL loops finish 13x and 10.8x faster than with a fresh pod per job; against a fresh reuse tag per job, warm reuse cuts p90 start latency from 59.1 s to 3.5 s. When a job cannot reuse the previous pod, standby promotion shortens the handover wait from 51 s to 0.94 s. In local and simulated runs, a keep-alive matched to the loop's pauses keeps the latency benefit while holding about half the capacity of an always-on pool.

papers.title: SWEET: Mitigating Spurious Feature Reliance in LLM Reasoning via Weight Editing
papers.abstract: Reasoning in large language models can be disrupted by simple input perturbations (e.g. adding irrelevant distractors), suggesting reliance on spurious correlations. Identifying and suppressing the spurious features involved in long chain-of-thought reasoning remains challenging. We introduce Spurious-feature WEight EdiTing (SWEET), a training-free method that combines counterfactual interventions with mechanistic interpretability to identify and suppress spurious-features. SWEET extracts token- and sequence-level behavioral directions from activation contrasts between original problems and their counterfactual variants - capturing local and global patterns of spurious reasoning. It then localizes the responsible MLP neurons and attention heads and suppresses their contributions along these directions through weight edits. Using only 20 original-counterfactual pairs for direction extraction, SWEET improves accuracy by an average of 11.8 percentage points on perturbed inputs and 2 points on original inputs across five open-weight reasoning models and five reasoning benchmarks. It also reduces the relative gap between original and perturbed accuracies from 17.6% to 2.5%. Analyses identify two recurring forms of spurious reasoning, i.e. over-integrating irrelevant conditions and overthinking, and provide mechanistic evidence that SWEET improves reasoning robustness by suppressing both behavioral directions.

papers.title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables
papers.abstract: We present SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects, such as cloth, stuffed toys and ropes, are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. On all sixty-five prompts, SoftPAT3D produces no undesired interpenetration of any kind, whereas every other system does, and its scenes directly support scene editing and robotic manipulation.

papers.title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
papers.abstract: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.

papers.title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
papers.abstract: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.

papers.title: Conditional Diffusion-Based Proxy Representation Recovery for BCVA Prediction with Missing SLO Modality
papers.abstract: Preoperative prediction of postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) can support prognosis assessment and individualized decision-making in cataract surgery. Multimodal learning can integrate preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) images, and clinical text to characterize patient status. However, SLO images are often missing in real-world clinical data due to acquisition or data-management issues, resulting in incomplete multimodal inputs. To address this problem, this paper proposes a conditional diffusion-based method for SLO proxy representation recovery and fusion prediction. Instead of reconstructing raw SLO images, the proposed method formulates SLO missingness as proxy representation recovery in the latent feature space. Specifically, OCT image features and clinical text features are first fused to construct an OCT-text conditional representation, which guides the reverse denoising process of the diffusion model to estimate sample-specific SLO proxy representations. The recovered SLO proxy representation is then used as a substitute for the unavailable SLO modality and incorporated into the downstream multimodal fusion prediction network for postoperative BCVA prediction. Experiments were conducted on 2,141 preoperative multimodal cataract samples, with an SLO missing rate of 58.80%. The proposed method achieved an accuracy of 0.9714 under the criterion of an absolute prediction error within 0.1 LogMAR and a mean absolute error of 0.0423, outperforming representative postoperative visual acuity prediction and missing-modality learning methods. These results indicate that representation-level proxy recovery can alleviate the impact of SLO modality missingness on postoperative BCVA prediction.
