papers.title: A Simple Phase-King Protocol with Predictions
papers.abstract:
Inspired by recent work (Ben-David, Dzulfikar, Ellen, and Gilbert, $\textit{Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, PODC 2025) we study synchronous binary Byzantine Agreement in the learning-augmented setting, where each process receives predictions about which processes are honest or Byzantine. We present a deterministic Phase King protocol for the anauthenticated setting, combining early stopping with a specifically designed prediction-aware king selection procedure. For at most $t<n/3$ Byzantine processes, the protocol handles arbitrarily many prediction errors, improving upon the $O(n^{3/2})$ bound of Ben-David et al., and terminates within $O(P)$ communication rounds, where $P=1+\min\{\mathbf{B}/n,f\}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total number of incorrect prediction bits held by honest processes, and $f$ is the actual number of Byzantine processes. Our protocol uses $O(n^2P)$ messages and $O(n^2P\log n)$ bits, avoiding the initial cubic bit cost of exchanging complete prediction vectors.
  In comparison to very recent independent work (Dufay, Dzulfikar, and Gilbert, $\textit{Predictions Can Only Help! Communication Efficient Byzantine Agreement with Predictions}$, DISC 2026), which achieves the same error tolerance and round complexity but better communication bounds, our construction provides a much simpler Phase King approach that completely avoids involved preprocessing constructions, rendering it more practical, especially for achieving agreement in time-evolving networks. We believe that the novel prediction-aware king selection technique of our scheme is of independent interest and can find further applications in learning-augmented distributed consensus.

papers.title: Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.

papers.title: A Sequential Monte Carlo Method for Data Assimilation in Subsurface Flow Systems with Hierarchical Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Subsurface flow systems often involve hierarchical geological uncertainty, meaning both higher-level metaparameters and cell-by-cell properties are uncertain. This leads to challenges for data assimilation because both sets of parameters must be estimated. In this work we develop an adaptive-tempered sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) procedure for joint Bayesian estimation of these quantities. The method uses noncentered geological parameterizations, with geomodel realizations represented by metaparameters and Gaussian latent variables that are independent under the prior. Adaptive likelihood tempering, importance weighting, resampling, and blockwise Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) mutation are applied at each iteration. Flow surrogates are used for all function evaluations. The hierarchical SMC procedure is further extended to treat successive data assimilation. In this case, existing posterior particles are updated in a manner that accounts for correlations in surrogate model errors across observation batches. We consider two distinct 3D systems with hierarchical uncertainty. The first is a faulted carbon storage system containing three stacked aquifers and two extensive faults. Principal component analysis is used to represent target-aquifer heterogeneity, while geological metaparameters characterize uncertain aquifer and fault properties. The second is a channelized oil-water system containing three facies with uncertain properties. A latent diffusion model represents variability in channel geometry and facies realizations. For the four synthetic true models considered, SMC posterior metaparameter distributions and flow predictions agree closely with reference MCMC results. SMC, however, requires fewer function evaluations and provides speedups of 2.5--7.0 for single-stage data assimilation. Even greater speedups are achieved with multiple GPUs.

papers.title: The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming
papers.abstract: A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). All RRPEFs represent the same row space, with the standard reduced row echelon form, renamed the Upper RREF (URREF), and the Lower RREF (LRREF) as its extreme members. A reformulation of Noether's Complementary Subspace Basis Theorem yields normalized bases of the row space that coincide with the nonzero rows of the corresponding RRPEFs. Constructively, each RRPEF is obtained by multi-index Gauss--Jordan reduction of a nonsingular transition submatrix. Factoring the admissible pivot-index sets by equality of their associated RRPEFs yields a quotient set in canonical bijection with the set of distinct RRPEFs. This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.

papers.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics
papers.abstract: Space weather forecasting and heliophysics increasingly rely on machine learning models that process heterogeneous inputs such as multi-viewpoint multi-wavelength solar images and rasters, multivariate time series, spatial annotations, and tabular event-level data. However, explainability workflows remain fragmented across libraries, model interfaces, and output formats, limiting reuse and reproducibility. We present SWXAI, an open-source library that unifies explainable AI (XAI) workflows for image, time-series, and tabular data in space weather forecasting and heliophysics. SWXAI provides a common, extensible interface across commonly used vision, time-series, and tabular learning models, with validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation objects. It also includes domain-grounded examples, reproducible notebooks, tests, and documentation, enabling users to inspect outputs, swap models or explainers, and extend workflows to new heliophysics datasets. SWXAI reduces modality-specific engineering overhead and supports comparable, reusable explanations across heterogeneous scientific machine learning pipelines. A benchmark against direct backend implementations shows that SWXAI substantially reduces the code users write to produce an explanation, with no practical runtime cost.

papers.title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
papers.abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized H\'{e}non-Heiles system. Using Poincar\'e sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable H\'{e}non-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.

papers.title: Geometric classification of Noether invariants of the Time-Dependent damped Duffing Oscillator
papers.abstract: We present a systematic geometric classification of the Noether point symmetries of time-dependent conformal Lagrangians of the form $L = A(t)\left(\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}\dot{x}^{i}\dot{x}^{j} - V(x)\right)$, whose Euler--Lagrange equations describe dynamical systems with time-dependent linear damping. The classification is carried out by coupling the temporal parameters of the conformal factor $A(t)$ with the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric $g_{ij}$ through a set of compatibility and integrability conditions. The central result is a main theorem which determines the Noether generators, the associated gauge functions and the resulting invariants. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity $D - 2\psi$ is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on $A(t)$, $g_{ij}$ or $V(x)$, and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space $E^{3}$ with $A(t) = e^{\gamma t}$ and potential $V = \frac{1}{2}a\,r^{2} + \frac{% \lambda}{4}r^{4}$. For the damped harmonic oscillator ($\lambda = 0$) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies $a = 2\gamma^{2}/9$. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.

papers.title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
papers.abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

papers.title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

papers.title: Law-Invariant Operators for Stochastic Mechanics
papers.abstract: A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. While classical spectral approaches achieve this separation in linear settings, nonlinear responses introduce interactions beyond conventional second-order variability response functions (VRF). Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. Different probability laws affect the input sampling and resulting response statistics, but not the mapping operator. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.

papers.title: Formal Proof of an Anisotropic Calder\'on Uniqueness Theorem
papers.abstract: We announce a Lean~4 formal proof of a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calder\'on uniqueness theorem released by OpenAI on October 6, 2026. We consider smooth Riemannian metrics on the three-dimensional unit ball, with full boundary measurements and Euclidean extensions outside the ball. OpenAI's release did not include a Lean proof of their uniqueness result. Our formalization uses results from Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it is given as a solution to a Lean comparator challenge whose check permits only the standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proof is not a line-by-line translation of the OpenAI manuscript.

papers.title: Radiation-Pattern-Based Channel Estimation for Reconfigurable Pixel Antennas
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable pixel antennas provide spatial diversity through multiple radiation patterns generated by a single antenna aperture, but exploiting this diversity can require substantial pilot overhead for exhaustive channel estimation. This paper jointly considers beam-steerable pixel-antenna design and its communication-side channel estimation. A pixel antenna is designed to generate diverse radiation patterns, whose electromagnetic correlation is then exploited to interpolate unobserved channel responses from a limited number of measurements. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of SNR gain and NMSE, demonstrating that effective pattern selection can be achieved with significantly reduced channel-observation overhead and can even outperform exhaustive scanning at low SNR.

papers.title: Safety-Constrained Intelligent Control of a 2-DOF Robotic Manipulator Using Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Control barrier function (CBF) filters depend on dynamic models that can be inaccurate when their parameters and external forces are uncertain. This paper investigates a radial basis function (RBF) neural network compensator whose output is shared by a Cartesian tracking controller and a joint-space CBF filter. An auxiliary state driven by the difference between requested and applied torques corrects the learning signal, reducing the direct influence of filter intervention on adaptation. A two-link manipulator is evaluated through constrained regulation, ablations, matched uncertainty and disturbance trials, and operating-range and timing studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller improves tracking while maintaining joint, velocity, and torque limits under parameter uncertainty, and that both the shared compensation and the auxiliary correction contribute to this improvement.

papers.title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Mobile ion migration strongly influences the electrical response and current-voltage hysteresis of perovskite solar cells. However, quantitative determination of ionic transport parameters typically requires transient measurements, extensive numerical simulations, and/or fitting procedures involving multiple uncertain parameters. Here, we present an analytical model that establishes a direct relationship between capacitance-frequency (C-f) characteristics and ionic transport properties in perovskite solar cells, while accounting for interlayer effects. The model describes the transition from the ion-screened depletion capacitance at low frequencies to the geometric capacitance at high frequencies and demonstrates that the characteristic transition frequency provides a direct measure of the dielectric relaxation time for ions. Furthermore, the model establishes a quantitative connection between C-f characteristics and scan-rate-dependent current-voltage hysteresis, enabling prediction of the scan-rate window in which maximum hysteresis occurs. Drift-diffusion simulations show excellent agreement with the analytical predictions over wide ranges of ion density, ion mobility, transport-layer mobility and doping concentration. Experimental measurements confirm the predicted correlation between capacitance and hysteresis. By providing a direct, physically transparent, and computationally efficient route for extracting ionic transport parameters from routine impedance measurements, this work offers a practical tool for quantifying ion migration and understanding dynamic phenomena in perovskite solar cells.

papers.title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Resource Allocation under Institutional Asymmetry
papers.abstract: We develop a two-player knapsack game to investigate resource allocation under individual capacity constraints, competition over shared resources, and institutional asymmetry. Players select feasible subsets of resources, while their payoffs depend on competitive losses, allocation rules, and asymmetric institutional benefits and costs. We derive the aggregate welfare function and show that allocation coefficients redistribute payoffs without directly affecting total welfare, whereas institutional parameters influence welfare through their net contribution. Consequently, institutional arrangements with identical welfare effects may induce different strategic incentives and Nash equilibrium outcomes. We analyze how capacity constraints and institutional priority shape equilibrium configurations and their welfare properties. A central result concerns the distinction between the social efficiency and strategic stability of shared resources. We derive conditions under which sharing is socially preferable to exclusive allocation yet remains strategically unstable because the non-priority player can increase their payoff by abandoning the resource. Conversely, sharing may remain strategically stable even when exclusive allocation yields higher aggregate welfare. These findings demonstrate that social efficiency and strategic stability need not coincide under institutional asymmetry.

papers.title: Prove What You Can: Hybrid Neurosymbolic Reasoning for Logical Natural Language Inference
papers.abstract: Logical reasoning over natural language requires both semantic interpretation and deductive search. Large language models (LLMs) can propose plausible intermediate derivations, but they often fail to compose them into a complete proof and overpredict uncertainty. Neurosymbolic methods improve search by translating an entire problem into first-order logic and handing it to a prover, but a single bad clause can make the whole translation nonexecutable. We present Hybrid Reasoning, a three-stage pipeline that decouples proposing a proof, validating its steps, and deciding a label. An LLM proposes a structured proof tree with a raw verdict; a theorem prover validates each derivation locally, keeping only the subset it can prove; and an uncertainty-gated repair attempts to re-derive the label from the premises plus the validated derivations, when the raw verdict is UNCERTAIN. Across four benchmarks (FOLIO, ProofWriter, ProverQA, PrOntoQA) and five contemporary LLMs, Hybrid Reasoning is the top-performing method on the two hardest datasets, improving on the strongest baseline by 5.3 points on FOLIO and 4.9 on ProverQA, and reaches ceiling-level accuracy on the easiest. The repair stage operates at 78-98% precision, producing 326 correct relabellings against 19 regressions.

papers.title: Look Ahead: Search-Driven Reasoning in Embodied AI
papers.abstract: Search allows a robotic policy to evaluate candidate futures before committing to an action. Motivated by test-time planning for vision-language action (VLA) models, we study selective search over action chunks in PushT using a frozen Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy. Beam search generates perturbed alternatives around the policy prediction and scores them through rollouts from cloned simulator states. Across 50 evaluation episodes, beam search raises task success from 0% to 18% and increases average cumulative reward from 39.44 to 103.2. We introduce One Step Ahead (OSA), a gate that simulates the nominal policy chunk and invokes full search only when its predicted coverage drop exceeds a threshold. In the reported ablations, OSA preserves or improves success while reducing runtime by approximately 3x relative to full beam search. Ablations over tree depth, branching factor, beam width, and replanning frequency show that larger search budgets do not consistently improve performance. The results support selective test-time search for action-chunking policies; evaluation on language-conditioned VLAs and physical robots remains future work.

papers.title: Adapting Large Language Models via Multi-Task Learning for Mental Health Problem, Emotion, and Sentiment Detection
papers.abstract: This study investigates sequential multi-task learning using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT), LoRA, and 4-bit quantization on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct for mental health problem detection, emotion detection, and sentiment analysis. Using 4,243 English social media posts, it compares two task sequences and demonstrates that task ordering significantly affects knowledge transfer and task interference. The MHP-first sequence achieves the best mental health problem detection (Micro-F1: 0.7624), while the Emotion-first sequence performs better in emotion (F1: 0.6052) and sentiment analysis (F1: 0.9459). A Joint-MTL baseline further highlights the challenges of simultaneous learning, including task interference and generative format collapse. Overall, the findings demonstrate the effectiveness of sequential PEFT for mental health NLP while showing that task order is critical to balancing performance across related tasks. The integration of LoRA and 4-bit quantization also reduces computational and memory requirements, supporting the adaptation of large language models in resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: Enhancing Mathematical Reasoning in Turkish Large Language Models with Search-Based Inference and Model Merging
papers.abstract: We improve Turkish mathematical reasoning in Large Language Models by combining LoRA fine-tuning, weight-space model merging, and search-based inference. Using Turkish-Llama 8B-DPO with Turkish translations of MetaMath, NuminaMath, and TigerLab, we find data quality beats scale (Mix-30k best among fine-tuned; large MetaMath underperforms). Linear merging delivers the largest gains (GSM8K up to 0.63), while Ties is modest and Breadcrumbs/Slerp degrade. Search with MCTS and Tree of Thoughts improves mean LLM-judge scores for reasoning quality on a 0-100 scale. Limitations include machine translation, limited scale, and search stochasticity.

papers.title: Multimodal Models Can See, But Can They Think? A Study of Turkish Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models have had massive leaps in recent years. Yet, when tested on high-level cognitive tasks like pattern completion, abstract logic, and relational reasoning, they still fall short. This limitation stems from the models' lack of ability to find out underlying rules and maintain constant intermediate steps, rather than merely deciding on the correct option. To research these shortcomings, this study analyzes visual reasoning performance throughout a multilingual evaluation framework encompassing the B\.ILSEM, MM-IQ, Visual Puzzles, and PuzzleVQA datasets. We evaluate various data mixing strategies and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) methods. We observed that a correct answer does not always mean the reasoning chain is valid. Because of this, we adopt an LLM-as-a-Judge approach to assess the quality of reasoning beyond final answer accuracy. Our experimental results reveal that baseline models often exhibit more stable reasoning compared to fine-tuned counterparts. Most importantly, we observe that SFT can lead to model collapse, manifesting as infinite text loops or empty outputs. The study concludes that current VLMs still struggle with abstract visual reasoning.

papers.title: Verifiable, Privacy-Preserving and Collaborative Multi-Objective Optimization with NSGA-II on Blockchain
papers.abstract: Collaborative multi-objective optimization allows independent problem solvers to contribute their solutions to a shared problem. However, their validity cannot be reliably verified in open settings if the parties are reluctant to disclose their solutions. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel zk-NSGA-II protocol for verifiable, privacy-preserving and collaborative multi-objective optimization on blockchain. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that executes Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) on the RISC Zero Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machine (zkVM) where evolutionary generations are certified by succinct proofs that are verified on-chain. Problem solvers maintain their own independent populations as the set of solutions in the decision space and their corresponding objective vectors in the objective space. They contribute to a global on-chain Pareto front by aggregating their local off-chain Pareto fronts according to the rule of non-domination which admits a contribution if it is non-dominated with respect to the existing contributions in the global front. To prevent fabricated contributions, population states across generations are linked through hash chains. The correctness of the zk-NSGA-II protocol is first evaluated on twelve problems from the ZDT and DTLZ benchmarks. Second, its feasibility is shown in a real-world portfolio optimization case study with the Hang Seng dataset. Performance on these problems is measured with nine different metrics across three complementary perspectives for optimization, zero-knowledge proof and blockchain. The empirical findings indicate that trustless collaborative multi-objective optimization is feasible with the existing zero-knowledge and blockchain technologies.

papers.title: Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
papers.abstract: We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $\pi$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(\pi z))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(\pi z))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $\mu_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $\mu_f(O_{1,2}) = \mu_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $\Phi_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}\Phi_j(z)$ with Koenigs Taylor jets $c_2(1) = -\frac{13}{2}\pi^2$ and $d_2(2) = -\frac{9}{2}\pi^2$; (3) the Schwarzian derivative is strictly negative on $\mathbb{Z}$ ($S(f)(n) \le 3\pi^2 - \frac{3}{8}\pi^4 \approx -6.9196 < 0$), and a repelling Julia 2-cycle $O_{\mathrm{rep}} \subset J(f)$ ($\mu \approx 1.2148 > 1$) isolates $B(O_{1,2})$; (4) on $(\mathbb{Z}_2, \mu_{\mathrm{Haar}})$, the 2-adic Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_{\mathrm{Haar}} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(3/4) \approx -0.143841 < 0$ equals $\frac{1}{2}\ln|\mu_f(O_{1,2})|$; and (5) we certify 20 theorems in Lean 4 (anc/CollatzAttractor.lean, 0 sorry). These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.

papers.title: Globally Simple Heffter Arrays $H(n;k)$ with $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$
papers.abstract: Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.

papers.title: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating information from external knowledge bases. However, recent studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial portions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks either rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper, we propose SNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial perturbations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a strictly configurable query budget. In particular, SNAPRAG uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77$\times$ fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, outperforming the closest approach by 7.7-19.9%. We further evaluate SNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving 50.7-96.3% extraction rate.

papers.title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs
papers.abstract: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.

authors.name: Steven Li
authors.institution: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland

papers.title: Electron cooling mediated by transverse optical phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$
papers.abstract: Soft transverse optical (TO) phonons in doped SrTiO$_3$ couple to electrons through the polarization field, quadratically in the paraelectric phase and, additionally, linearly in the polar phase due to the onset of spontaneous polarization. We investigate heat flow between a three-dimensional electron gas and soft TO phonons. For two-TO-phonon scattering, the heat flow of hot electrons crosses over from $T^5$ to $T^3$ at the Bloch-Gruneisen temperature. In the polar phase, an additional one-TO-phonon channel emerges, yielding a softer temperature dependence of the heat flow, $T^3$ at low and $T$ at high temperatures, with the spectral weight set by the spontaneous polarization. This channel may dominate at low temperatures and leads to a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the heat flow in the vicinity of the polar transition.

papers.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
papers.abstract: We propose a music inpainting technique combining similarity matching and a diffusion-based generative model to replace large segments of audio recordings with suitable alternatives. The proposed hybrid method, Similarity-Guided Diffusion Posterior Sampling (SimDPS), retrieves candidate replacement segments from the wider signal based on contextual similarity and uses them to guide the diffusion process toward coherent reconstructions. Being model-agnostic, the framework is compatible with any pre-trained diffusion model operating in either the waveform or latent domain. Objective evaluations demonstrate that SimDPS outperforms widely adopted RePaint and DPS methods across acoustic features and neural-embedding distance metrics. Subjective evaluations on multi-genre music datasets confirm that SimDPS enhances perceptual plausibility compared to previous diffusion-based methods and demonstrates robustness to poorly matched similarity candidates. These findings pave the way for improved music restoration and context-aware audio editing.

papers.title: Zero-inflated generalized linear latent variable models for microbiome compositional data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we incorporate the Dirichlet--multinomial distribution into the generalized linear latent variable model (GLLVM) framework to accommodate high-dimensional, overdispersed compositional count data and capture complex covariation among taxa with a low-rank structure. Advances in high-throughput sequencing technologies have generated large amounts of microbiome count data, stimulating research into their associations with human diseases and traits. Such data are compositional and often highly sparse for various reasons, posing challenges for statistical analysis. Conventional zero-replacement approaches ignore the underlying causes of zeros, further complicating the analysis. We therefore propose a zero-inflated Dirichlet--multinomial latent variable model (ZIDM-LVM). Since the marginal likelihood has no closed-form expression, we develop a variational approximation (VA) approach for efficient parameter estimation. Simulation studies and applications to two microbiome datasets are presented to evaluate the performance of the proposed method.

authors.name: Wenqi Tang
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.

papers.title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
papers.abstract: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure.While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe$_3$ achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet $f$-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

papers.title: Dynamic Traffic Modeling using Equivalent Circuit Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents an equivalent circuit model (ECM) for dynamic traffic modeling by exploiting analogies between electrical and transportation variables. Vehicle concentration is represented by capacitor voltage, while traffic flow is modeled using controllable current sources. The proposed formulation is shown to preserve the conservation and sending/receiving relationships of the spatially discretized Lighthill Whitham Richards traffic model. The framework is extended to restricted inflow, traffic signals, and two road merging and diverging scenarios. Validation against microscopic Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulations, involving traffic signals, two-road merging, and single-road diverging scenarios, demonstrates that the proposed ECM successfully reproduces the principal macroscopic traffic dynamics, including queue formation, backward congestion propagation, vehicle accumulation, saturation, and subsequent traffic recovery.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Massively Parallel Simulation for Low-Thrust Multi-Revolution Rendezvous
papers.abstract: The growing demand for on-orbit servicing and constellation management in low Earth orbit requires autonomous and reliable low-thrust rendezvous. Traditional numerical methods struggle with the long-horizon nature of multi-revolution maneuvers under perturbations, while standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods are limited by low simulation throughput and poor sample efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a massively parallel DRL guidance framework. A fully tensorized, GPU-resident orbital propagator is developed to integrate $J_2$-perturbed orbital dynamics and policy optimization within a zero-copy pipeline, achieving up to a 67-fold increase in simulation throughput over conventional CPU baselines. In addition, the rendezvous problem is formulated in modified equinoctial elements and trained with a progressive curriculum learning strategy to improve convergence and generalization across increasingly challenging rendezvous scenarios. Simulations show that the proposed framework can learn robust rendezvous trajectories for complex multi-revolution rendezvous over a broad range of orbital configurations. Additional evaluations under a high-fidelity model and eclipse-induced thrust interruptions further demonstrate the robustness of the learned policy under practical mission constraints. Moreover, the trajectories generated by the proposed framework can be used as effective initial guesses for optimization-based trajectory solvers, improving the convergence of high-precision trajectory optimization. The method offers a scalable approach for real-time low-thrust guidance and trajectory optimization.

papers.title: GARP: Real-Time Generative Agents on Local Hardware in a Game Engine
papers.abstract: Generative agents are game characters whose plans, conversations, and memories are written on the fly by a large language model (LLM). The original Generative Agents demonstration used cloud inference in a custom simulation. We present GARP, a platform for real-time generative agents inside Godot, and describe the Character Behavior System used in GARP 2. The complete loop runs on local hardware using a 3B-parameter open-weight model and no cloud service. Alongside the original planning, memory, and reflection, GARP gives each agent an emotion system driven by LLM appraisal, four graded personality axes drawn from the Big Five that set simulation parameters as well as prompt text, six needs whose urgency grows over time, and pairwise relationships updated after every conversation. The system narrows 50+ candidate actions to typically 3-8, constrains model responses with JSON schemas, and surfaces important memories in decision prompts. A layered optimization strategy (an adjustable game clock, decisions taken ahead of need, multi-tier caching, prompt compression, and fully asynchronous execution) keeps the game responsive while the model thinks. In a nine-scenario evaluation, 25 of 27 runs passed log-based checks. Both failures occurred in the birthday party scenario, where one guest omitted the event from their daily plan.

papers.title: DISCOVER: Online Variance-Guided Data Discovery for Budgeted Multimodal GRPO
papers.abstract: Recent advances in reinforcement learning have made verifiable rewards a central post-training paradigm for improving multimodal reasoning. However, methods such as GRPO remain data- and compute-inefficient, spending rollout and annotation budget on prompts that provide little learning signal. We propose DISCOVER, an online data-discovery framework for budgeted multimodal GRPO that enables vision-language models to dynamically identify prompts that are most useful for the current policy. DISCOVER first organizes the multimodal sample pool into semantic clusters and queries a small set of density-diverse representative samples to obtain initial reward observations. During training, it estimates the utility of unannotated samples by transferring sparse reward feedback from queried samples. Since sample utility changes as the policy evolves, DISCOVER dynamically updates these estimates with recency-weighted rollout observations. It then selects only high-utility prompts for annotation using a policy-conditioned score that accounts for reward variance and difficulty. Once the discovery budget is exhausted, DISCOVER continues with utility-based replay. Experiments on ViRL39K and VLAA-Thinking with Qwen3-VL-2B show that DISCOVER substantially improves multimodal mathematical reasoning under a strict 10% unique-sample budget, outperforming budget-matched random selection, hard-example sampling, full-pool GRPO under the same training-step budget, and online selection baselines. Ablations further validate the importance of semantic coverage, online reward transfer, and stable discovery cadence, establishing DISCOVER as a practical framework for data-efficient multimodal RL post-training.

authors.name: Shayan Shams
authors.institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

papers.title: ReVMap: Vectorized Global Mapping via Connectivity-Aware Local Map Fusion
papers.abstract: Large-scale annotation of vectorized high-definition (HD) maps is labor-intensive and costly, motivating local-to-global auto-labeling approaches that incrementally construct global maps from local vectorized predictions. However, existing approaches often overlook prediction uncertainty and rely on heuristic map integration, potentially propagating errors and introducing topological inconsistencies. To address these limitations, we propose ReVMap, a reliable local-to-global framework that iteratively refines local map predictions and global map construction through uncertainty-guided prior utilization and connectivity-guided global map revision. Specifically, ReVMap leverages point-wise localization uncertainty to incorporate global map priors into local map prediction, improving robustness against inaccurate prior information. It then predicts local-to-global connectivity and selectively updates the global map through uncertainty-aware fusion based on the reliability of local predictions. By iteratively coupling local prediction and global revision, ReVMap progressively improves both local map accuracy and global map consistency. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes and Argoverse 2 benchmarks demonstrate that ReVMap achieves state-of-the-art performance in both local map prediction and global map construction.

authors.name: Jun Won Choi
authors.institution: Seoul National University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal hybrid tax enforcement
papers.abstract: Modern tax design and enforcement rely on classification data reported by taxpayers. Data improve the targeting of tax policy and audits but also open avenues for evasion. How can tax authorities use such data while accounting for their potential strategic distortion? We demonstrate that restoring deterrence generates an endogenous global verification frontier: every report below the frontier is verified through either a profit audit or data verification. Optimal hybrid tax enforcement requires selecting which data classes are subject to profit audits up to the global frontier and which are profit-audited only up to lower class-specific cutoffs, with data verification taking over beyond these cutoffs. This costly data verification requirement limits the benefit from differentiated tax enforcement. Optimal implementation is characterized by profit bunching but involves no data bunching.

papers.title: Agentic discrete-event simulation for manufacturing system design: an open 3D simulator, a benchmark and an industrial case
papers.abstract: The design of manufacturing systems relies on discrete-event simulation (DES) models that experts still build in tool-specific interfaces. AI agents can now write simulation code, but every model they write from scratch is new, unverified software. We present SimuLean, an open-source 3D DES simulator on the Unity engine designed to be programmed by AI agents: its modelling semantics are verified once, in the platform, and the agent builds and studies one model through domain-level commands, in the 3D scene or headless; physically simulated durations are calibrated for fast headless studies. We evaluated it on 18 manufacturing modelling tasks, from single machines to published production lines. A frontier agent built valid models in 93 of 108 attempts (86%), in about two minutes each; on the benchmark's interface version, two frontier agents built 105 of 108 models through domain commands alone, so that each comes with a record of how it was built. Every residual failure was silent - a model that builds and runs but answers wrongly - and only comparison with reference models revealed them all. In an industrial case, one agent working alone rebuilt, verified and studied a robotised welding workshop from a published study, in SimuLean and in SimPy. Comparing them with the published, expert-built model exposed an error in it; against the corrected model, the agent-built models agree within 1%. One agent can already build complete, realistic and traceable models for the design of manufacturing systems; independent reference models are what make them trustworthy.

papers.title: Tunnels: Compressing the Solution Subgraph of Regular Path Queries
papers.abstract: Regular path queries (RPQs) are increasingly expected to return the paths that match them, not only their endpoints. Since the number of matching paths can be exponential or infinite, a standard way to deliver them (PMR) is the subgraph $\Hs$ of the product between the graph and the query automaton that contains exactly the nodes lying on some solution path. We show that $\Hs$ can be compressed much further when the graph is available to the decoder: most of $\Hs$ can be regenerated by re-running small parts of the traversal, and only the places where the traversal would waste significant effort on dead branches need to be stored. We formalize this as \emph{tunnels}: regions of $\Hs$ that are re-expanded from a stored entry point with a bounded amount of extra work, either an absolute budget or one proportional to the output produced. We handle the three classes of RPQs: constant-to-variable, constant-to-constant, and variable-to-variable. In the latter, we study the combination of tunnels with cutting the query at a selective articulation point of the automaton and encoding the answer as a union of Cartesian products of leftward and rightward traversals. Our experimental results show improvements of 2 to 3 orders of magnitude over the baseline space of PMR, for an acceptable increase in traversal time.

papers.title: Synaptic Dendritic Neuron Model (scDNM) for Cell Type Classification in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data
papers.abstract:
Cell type classification in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is challenging because of high dimensionality, sparsity, and transcriptionally similar cell types. We developed scDNM, an adaptation of the dendritic neuron model incorporating learnable synaptic thresholds, a supervised gene pool, staged training, and ensemble prediction.
  Six binary classification tasks were constructed from the Paul15, PBMC3k, and Nestorowa datasets. All models were evaluated using leakage-free nested cross-validation, with feature selection, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning performed independently of the outer test folds.
  scDNM ranked first in three of six tasks (including one tie) and achieved the best mean accuracy rank (2.00), followed by XGBoost (2.75), Random Forest (3.33), logistic regression (3.33), and SVM (3.58). In a six-class PBMC3k experiment, scDNM achieved 95.997% accuracy and 0.944 macro-F1, compared with 94.243% and 0.914 for SingleR. Garnett returned only Unknown labels and was treated as a zero-coverage technical outcome. Ablation analysis supported the contributions of dendrites and synaptic thresholds. However, XGBoost achieved higher mean binary-task accuracy (96.20% versus 95.32% for scDNM), and across-task rank differences were not statistically significant.
  These findings demonstrate that scDNM is competitive for scRNA-seq cell type classification, although broader independent validation is required.

papers.title: Symmetry and Redundancy in Cremer-Pople Phases for Ring Puckering
papers.abstract: Cremer-Pople (CP) coordinates provide an exact description of ring puckering, yet direct sampling of their phases generates many symmetry-equivalent representations of the same puckering pattern. We develop a general analytical framework that identifies these equivalences before Cartesian reconstruction and geometry optimization. For homogeneous rings of arbitrary size, explicit transformations of the CP phases and the signed special coordinate of even-membered rings generate the complete symmetry orbit of the ordered elevation pattern. We classify the redundancies into four types and derive a factorized orbit-size formula linking CP multiplicity to puckering symmetry. These results yield exact single-phase fundamental intervals and sequentially reduced multiphase covering domains, including the restriction to a positive special coordinate. The framework is extended to rings containing one heteroatom or two identical heteroatoms, with reductions determined by the operations that preserve their placement. We also introduce a semidiscrete conformational nomenclature that combines symbolic amplitude distributions with explicit active phases. In an application to cyclohexadecane, symmetry reduction alone decreases the number of sampled CP points by approximately a factor of thirty. Combined with selective phase-grid coarsening for three ordinary modes, the reduction approaches two orders of magnitude. These developments provide a systematic basis for generating, classifying, and efficiently sampling ring puckering patterns in CP space.

authors.name: Anxo Lema-Saavedra
authors.institution: Centro Singular de Investigación en Química Biológica y Materiales Moleculares

authors.name: Antonio Fernandez-Ramos
authors.institution: Centro Singular de Investigación en Química Biológica y Materiales Moleculares

papers.title: Polar foliations on the Cayley plane
papers.abstract: We classify polar foliations on the Cayley projective plane, completing the classification of polar foliations on compact rank one symmetric spaces.

authors.name: Miguel Dominguez-Vazquez
authors.institution: Centro Singular de Investigación en Química Biológica y Materiales Moleculares

papers.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
papers.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. We predict magnetoresistance ratios in the range of 1.14-1.20 for the charge-transfer device and up to $10^3$ in the single-electron transistor.

papers.title: How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision language action (VLA) models show strong zero-shot performance, but are rarely deployed directly and are often first post-trained on demonstrations from the target setting. Yet VLAs are typically compared by zero-shot or full-data fine-tuned success, revealing little about the data and compute required for adaptation. We study adaptation efficiency for six VLAs ($\pi_{0}$, $\pi_{0.5}$, and GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying both demonstrations and training steps. This reveals differences hidden by full-data fine-tuning: models within two points on the full LIBERO-Spatial dataset differ by up to $3\times$ in success with 50 demonstrations. $\pi_{0.5}$ needs $2$--$5\times$ fewer demonstrations than $\pi_{0}$ and is the most sample-efficient model at every budget, with the largest gap on the long-horizon suite. Within GR00T, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three of four suites, despite their stronger zero-shot performance. We study one pretraining factor behind these differences by freezing the VLM during finetuning: this severely degrades the $\pi$ models, whose VLM is jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, but barely affects GR00T models. Finally, validation loss on held-out demonstrations tracks closed-loop success within a suite, but understates how much more sample-efficient $\pi_{0.5}$ is than $\pi_{0}$.

papers.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

papers.title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
papers.abstract: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and never with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on design, data and analysis. The results bear novelty value in three respects. Joint success occurred only through the shared store. Whether a model coordinated depended not on its vendor tier but on whether it wrote its intermediate result and looked at the store again, and one ordinary sentence, "check your workspace again before submitting", switched that second look on and off. The findings held under replication. For practice, state shared between agents is a communication channel and should be separated, namespaced and logged. For research, designs should be locked before the data, and the parse rule, endpoint and parameters reported. Future work should test open-weight models and separate using another agent's output from intending to communicate.

papers.title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures
papers.abstract: Historical social simulation faces a fundamental reproducibility challenge: the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) introduces a digital butterfly effect that prevents exact replication across multi-turn runs. Furthermore, the inability to control low-level server parameters in commercial LLM hosting environments severely limits reproducibility. To overcome this opacity, we present a deterministic multi-agent framework coupling LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind (ToM) and Cognitive Archaeology, and validate exact artifact identity within local, pinned execution environments using SHA-256 hashing. Run locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads, the system injects differentiated cognitive states per turn through dissonance-driven behavioural modes and gated internal voices. Evaluating seven model configurations spanning 4B to 31B parameters against an ablated baseline reveals clear operational boundaries. Small models ($\leq$8B) suffer from context capacity overload, producing repetitive, specular dialogue loops. However, at $\geq$12B parameters, the ABM scaffolding breaks the monotonous response patterns seen in ablation. Crucially, these scaffolded models exhibit spontaneous diegetic expansion: they coherently expand scenario lore through tactically motivated, anachronism-free details rather than escalating into aggression. By resisting the structural pull toward premature scene closure, scaffolded sessions sustain an open terminal Narrative Vector ($V_N = \mathrm{Open}$ in 12/21 overall; 9/9 in official $\geq$12B configurations) whereas unscaffolded ablation never does (0/21). This framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark architecture for virtual archaeology, with the full pipeline released as open-source software to enable independent replication.

papers.title: Enmo Safety: External, Non-invasive, Model-agnostic Oversight for Off-the-Shelf Language Models
papers.abstract: We study a safety harness that improves itself without touching model weights. Enmo Safety wraps a chat model with a deterministic input assessment, trigger-matched safety guidance, spotlighting of untrusted content, and an output guard. A reflector model turns failures into one bounded update per round, and an update is kept only if it lowers harm without raising refusal of benign prompts on a held-out dev split. Every version is snapshotted and every decision ledgered. We evaluate a bare model, the seed harness and the evolved harness on six open benchmarks (HarmBench, AdvBench, JailbreakBench, XSTest, AgentHarm, deepset prompt-injections). On 150 items and on a 290-item holdout, none of the before/after differences on two models was statistically significant. A fourth iteration ran six policy models on a fresh 300-item split: the harness cut the unsafe rate significantly on two models (12.9% to 7.1%, p = 0.035; 10.2% to 3.6%, p = 0.036), not on the other four, and raised agentic-harm labels on two. Whether the rules fired was unrelated to outcome (Fisher p from 0.30 to 1.0), and the helpfulness clauses made agentic harm worse than no harness on obfuscated attacks. A reworded clause and an input-normalisation step form harness v22, at a measured cost in benign tool-task refusal. Each cell is one run, so these estimates do not establish a general safety improvement. Code, harness versions and ledger: https://github.com/rioryugen/enmo_safety

authors.name: Sarun Kumar K. S.
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ColNav: Uncertainty-Aware Spacetime Collision Checking with Bounding Volume Hierarchies
papers.abstract: Safe navigation for mobile robots in dynamic and uncertain environments requires planning paths that avoid collisions with other moving targets. Typically this involves forward propagating the robot motion and checking for collisions at sampled points in space and time. Such methods can miss collisions between sampled points and are not robust to uncertainty in the state estimates. We propose ColNav, a robust collision check formulation with geometric volumes. The key aspect of our approach is encoding the uncertainty in the targets' and the ego robot's positions and velocities into spacetime tubes, in two variants that consume bounded-set and Gaussian uncertainty descriptions, respectively. The tubes are organised in bounding volume hierarchies, so that a single tree traversal covers the entire horizon, rather than testing sampled time instants, and returns a robust geometric certificate together with an estimate of the time to collision. Static and dynamic obstacles share the same representation. Our approach reaches the goal with a 100% success rate under prediction model mismatch, where the best baseline reaches 65%, and maintains up to three times the clearance in dense traffic. We also validate real-time operation on a physical robot.

authors.name: Sanjeev Ramkumar Sudha
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lars Ivar Hatledal
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Erlend M. Coates
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Quantum benchmarks for magnetic energies and transition temperatures
papers.abstract: Predicting magnetic ordering temperatures requires accurate exchange interactions and an appropriate treatment of spin thermodynamics. Here we assess these requirements through complementary quantum Monte Carlo benchmarks. For five insulating antiferromagnets, we compare ferromagnetic-antiferromagnetic energy differences from diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) and density functional theory with references reconstructed from inelastic neutron scattering (INS) exchanges. DMC underestimates these references but achieves a mean absolute error comparable to the best-performing functionals tested. Separately, we directly test the previously proposed (S+1)/S rescaling of classical Monte Carlo temperatures against quantum stochastic series expansion simulations for 17 compounds using corresponding INS-derived Heisenberg Hamiltonians. Rescaling reduces the mean absolute classical-quantum temperature difference from 81.7 to 8.2 K, with a mean absolute percentage difference of 5.9 %. These results establish a direct quantum benchmark for the rescaling within the tested models and emphasize that improvements in electronic magnetic energy scales should be accompanied by attention to quantum spin thermodynamics.

authors.name: Mojtaba Alaei
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Alireza Qaiumzadeh
authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Artem Oganov
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Rigidity of spacelike graphs in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes via the infinity-Laplacian
papers.abstract: In the search for new characterizations of spacelike slices in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes, we introduce a new approach. The main tool for addressing this question is the infty-Laplacian with respect to the Riemannian metric induced on the spacelike hypersurface, together with a Liouville-type property for the infinity-Laplacian on any complete Riemannian manifold by Araujo, Mari and Pessoa in 2021. Starting from the infinity-Laplacian of the height function of a spacelike hypersurface, we derive several differential equations involving the infinity-Laplacian of suitable compositions of the height function, namely, the warping function f(h), its primitive P=\int f, and the logarithmic composition log(f(h)). Under some natural assumptions, including timelike and null energy conditions, global rigidity results are established in the parametric setting. Some of these results specialize naturally to complete spacelike hypersurfaces in the Steady State spacetime and in Einstein-de Sitter spacetime. Finally, we consider a second-order PDE involving the infty-Laplacian and study the uniqueness of its entire solutions on the fiber of the generalized Robertson-Walker spacetime. This leads to new Calabi-Bernstein-type uniqueness results in the non-parametric setting.

authors.name: Guilherme Nascimento
authors.institution: Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia Baiano

papers.title: Shifted Interaction Functions: A Unified Framework for Imperfect Actuation and Sensing in Consensus Networks
papers.abstract: Practical networked robotic systems rarely implement ideal consensus interactions exactly, since local actuation constraints, sensing biases, and heterogeneous interaction maps may shift the input-output relations used by distributed controllers. Rather than focusing solely on whether consensus occurs, such imperfections can fundamentally alter the structure of the asymptotic collective behavior, typically yielding global or clustered velocity alignment, while exact static agreement arises only in special cases. This paper develops a shifted-interaction framework for analyzing collective alignment under imperfect actuation and sensing. Shifted functions provide a compact representation of local actuator and sensor maps, allowing actuation constraints and sensing biases to be represented by horizontally and vertically shifted monotone interactions. The framework distinguishes nodal shifted actuation from edge-wise shifted sensing. For shifted actuation, a Lyapunov analysis establishes global velocity alignment under compatible actuation ranges, including bounded, non-invertible, and deadzone-type maps. For shifted sensing, a maximum-principle argument and a paired-sensitivity condition establish convergence to velocity clusters over edges with infinite accumulated sensitivity; uniform sensing sensitivity yields exponential global velocity alignment. In the linear case, closed-form expressions characterize asymptotic behavior and identify actuation as a special case of sensing. Simulations illustrate static, globally aligned, and clustered velocity-aligned behaviors.

papers.title: LawKAN: Group-Law Layers for Composition -- When Imposing a Known Law Pays Off
papers.abstract: Many tasks compose transformations by a known rule: chained rotations in robotics and navigation. Learned models relearn it, compounding error; classical estimators hardcode it and miss hardware deviations. We impose the known structure and learn only the remainder: an exact non-commutative group law sits in the node of a self-contained layer, its edges learn local increments, and a zero-initialized correction psi learns unknown deviations of the law. A pre-training criterion predicts exact representability. On fixed-angle SU(2) composition, a 54-parameter dense edge is the most accurate dense model, at 27x fewer parameters than the strongest fixed-matrix baseline, and lies 0.05 deg above the Bayes floor. On real robot arms, an isolated 306-parameter psi reaches 1.12-1.14 mm versus 1.29-1.33 mm for Gauss-Newton at N >= 60, and the recipe transfers across three vendors and two protocols. The recipe matches classical fits where the data obey the law and loses where the imposed law is not the task's.

papers.title: Exactly integrable field theory in $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time: the spectral equations
papers.abstract: The primary object in quantum field theories is the one-step relativistic evolution operator. In this paper we consider the evolution operator defined on the auxiliary Kagom\'e lattice with the $q$-oscillator algebra of observables, the local ingredient of the evolution operator is the $q$-oscillator $R$-matrix of the Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation. We construct explicitly the complete system of equations (which can be seen as a specific form of nested Bethe Ansatz equations) defining the spectrum of the evolution operator. This system of equations is valid for an arbitrary initial data (occupation numbers), and the thermodynamical limit is well defined for this system.

authors.name: Sergey Sergeev
authors.institution: A.P. Karpinsky Russian Geological Research Institute

papers.title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational question answering can require several separated dialogue turns that support an answer only together. We introduce EviCover, a retrieval approach designed to retain this complementary evidence. It converts questions into observable evidence requirements, checks requirement coverage using retrieved source identifiers, and selects turns jointly. We track annotated support sets - the benchmark-labeled dialogue turns associated with each question - through retrieval, reranking, and final answer-generation context. We evaluate the baseline memory pipeline on generated, human-verified LoCoMo conversations and human-written REALTALK conversations, and examine EviCover on REALTALK's 108 multi-hop questions. Compared with the hybrid lexical/dense baseline, support-turn recall among 60 candidate turns rises from 0.526 to 0.575, and recall in the final ten-turn context rises from 0.349 to 0.379. The evidence funnel identifies separate discovery and selection failures, while paired answer evaluation shows that greater evidence recall does not yet establish a correctness gain. This analysis locates where complementary evidence is lost and distinguishes evidence retrieval from its use in answer generation.

papers.title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
papers.abstract: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.

papers.title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
papers.abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using \v{C}ech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.abstract: The Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

authors.name: Ivan Panin
authors.institution: St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: Division ring extensions and the realization of Coxeter diagrams $I_2(n)$
papers.abstract: For each integer $n\ge5$, we construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(n)$. Both of its diagonal division rings are two-generated over the field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$, where $\zeta$ is a primitive root of unity of order $n-2$. The construction is based on a chain of quantized Weyl relations and a shift automorphism. We give one-sided bases for the corresponding division ring extensions and compute the right dimension sequence of the bimodule. The resulting ring has exactly $n$ isomorphism classes of indecomposable finitely generated right modules.

papers.title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs
papers.abstract: Traffic state estimation (TSE) reconstructs traffic density at unmonitored locations from a sparse set of sensors. Data-driven models work well when sensors are dense but degrade sharply as coverage thins. We show that imposing the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards conservation law as a physics-informed prior makes TSE more data-efficient. On four real corridors (NGSIM, I-80, PeMS04, PeMS08), physics-informed estimators generalise to held-out sensors where data-driven models, including classical and deep kriging, overfit the observed ones. On the two shock-rich corridors the effect is a clear crossover: as more sensors are held out, data-driven models collapse while the physics-informed estimator degrades gracefully, leading the no-physics network by about 26-38% at 85-90% held out and the strongest classical kriging by about 10-21% at 90%. A matched smoothness prior does not reproduce the gain, and an extended Kalman filter on the same LWR model is outperformed on the shock corridors, so the advantage comes from how the conservation law is imposed. Finally, one loss-conditional PINN removes the per-corridor loss-weight search, matching a 20-point search at about 5x lower cost.

authors.name: Anna Lazareva
authors.institution: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation

authors.name: Alexander Tarakanov
authors.institution: St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks in the small-data regime: A controlled comparison with classical PDE surrogates
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for engineering models are often trained on large collections of simulated solutions. We investigate whether physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can achieve accurate predictions from scarce labelled observations by incorporating governing equations and prescribed initial and boundary conditions. We introduce hierarchical loss weighting (H-PINN) and its gradient-direction-aware extension (HO-PINN), which adjust the emphasis on physical constraints according to higher-priority losses.
