Hierarchical PINNs are compared with Vanilla PINN, tuned gradient boosting, support-vector regression, and Gaussian-process regression on a heat equation and three heterogeneous two-phase-flow benchmarks. Experiments use 20--1000 labelled states and ten paired seeds. Each label is one coordinate--state observation, not a complete simulation. At least one PINN variant achieves the highest mean primary-target \(R^2\) in each interpolation and equation-assisted forecasting comparison at 20 and 50 labels. The advantage for water saturation persists across all tested budgets. Hierarchical weighting reduces variability across runs in selected settings. These results demonstrate that known physics can support accurate neural surrogate predictions from very few solution observations, at substantially higher fitting cost than the tested classical regressors.

authors.name: Kirill Katsuba
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

authors.name: Egor Bugaev
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

authors.name: Alexander Tarakanov
authors.institution: St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation

papers.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract:
The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products.
  The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces.
  Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

papers.title: Beyond Hash Matching: AI-Based Detection of Previously Unidentified CSAM and its Legal Implications in the EU
papers.abstract: The detection of previously unidentified Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) remains a significant challenge for law enforcement authorities, online service providers, and child protection organizations, as traditional hash-matching technologies are primarily designed to identify previously verified material. This paper reviews and classifies existing AI-based technologies that could complement hash-based approaches and support the detection, analysis, and prioritization of potentially harmful content. The reviewed approaches are organized into three categories: real-time image and video analysis, image and video classification and tagging, and AI-based behavioral monitoring. A comparative analysis examines the capabilities, limitations, and potential integration of general-purpose computer vision platforms, content moderation services, and specialized CSAM detection tools within existing detection workflows. An experimental evaluation was conducted using Google Cloud Vision AI and Sightengine to investigate sexual-content classification and child-adult age estimation. The results highlight differences in classification taxonomies and outputs across providers, as well as significant limitations in age classification, particularly for adolescents. These findings highlight the importance of using AI-based assessments as complementary tools for analysis and prioritization, rather than as definitive determination of CSAM. Finally, the paper examines the relevant European Union regulatory framework, with particular attention to the EU AI Act, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), fundamental rights, transparency, accountability, and human oversight. The legal analysis highlights how regulatory obligations and safeguards may differ depending on the deployment context, potentially creating inconsistencies across interconnected detection and reporting workflows.

papers.title: The role of preparation protocols in the Mpemba effect under time-delayed Newton cooling
papers.abstract: The Mpemba effect depends on both the relaxation dynamics and the protocol used to prepare the initial states. Here, this dependence is investigated using the time-delayed Newton cooling law, comparing protocols in which two samples are exposed to piecewise-constant bath temperatures before being placed in a common final bath. For protocols with at most two quenches and a common waiting time, exact conditions for the occurrence of the effect are derived. They rule out the Pontus protocol within this model and show that the synchronous two-reservoir protocol maximizes the effect magnitude within the class considered. The robustness of this optimum is then examined by allowing asynchronous quenches or an additional quench for one sample. Numerical optimization of these extensions identifies the synchronous two-reservoir protocol as the maximizing limit in the cases studied. This evidence motivates a conjecture that the same protocol remains optimal for more general bath histories, although that broader statement is not proved.

papers.title: The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem
papers.abstract: We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. In the positive-definite case, we determine the representing measures, prove their uniqueness and specify the admissible endpoint masses. No boundedness assumption on the support or asymptotic conditions on the recurrence coefficients are imposed.

papers.title: MedToolFault and MedGuard: evaluating and improving clinical agent reliability
papers.abstract: Clinical agents must retrieve patient-specific evidence and correctly update records despite unreliable tool responses. We introduce MedToolFault, a fault-injection benchmark linking six tool-failure classes to answer correctness, required state changes and forbidden mutations in public clinical-agent tasks. We also introduce MedGuard, a tool-layer method that verifies read evidence and attributes ambiguous writes through public interfaces. Across 127,861 formal episode evaluations, we assess fault recovery, mechanism controls, task expansion, constrained tool budgets and external question answering. Across nine model configurations, unguarded agents fail in 32.2-67.8% of fault-injected evaluations on tasks each configuration solves without faults. MedGuard improves paired safe success by 13.7-46.6 percentage points on these tasks.

authors.name: Sicheng Zhou
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Yifan Wu
authors.institution: Hefei CAS Ion Medical and Technical Devices (China)

papers.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
papers.abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

papers.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
papers.abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

papers.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
papers.abstract: Vector metric spaces in the sense of \c{C}evik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $\Gamma$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(\Gamma)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(\Gamma)$ without the transfer, while for countable $\Gamma$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.

papers.title: Robust Satisficing Ensemble: Scalable Model Aggregation Under Distribution Shifts
papers.abstract: Standard ensemble methods can improve robustness by mitigating individual model stochasticity, but they frequently fail to generalize beyond the training distribution, leaving systems vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) data. We introduce the Robust Satisficing Ensemble (RSE), a scalable probabilistic aggregation framework designed to secure model combinations by minimizing their fragility against distributional changes. By bridging a robust satisficing objective with a quadratic risk surrogate, RSE derives an analytical inner adversary. This fundamental reformulation enables highly efficient weight updates without the computational bottleneck of standard minimax optimization, crucially decoupling optimization complexity from sample size to scale effectively to large datasets. In particular, we prove a geometrically decaying truncation error for the fragility approximation via Lagrange-Burmann expansion and establish stationarity guarantees for RSE. We evaluate RSE across a comprehensive spectrum of distribution shifts, including adversarial label shift (SST-5, TREC), natural subpopulation and temporal shifts (CivilComments, HuffPost). Our results demonstrate that RSE consistently outperforms strong robust baselines, including GroupDRO, IRM, and SRM. These findings establish RSE as a practical, theoretically grounded safeguard for reliable model aggregation in dynamic environments.

papers.title: ShiftCache: Fast and Exact Indel Effect Prediction by Reusing Shifted Reference Encodings
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function models such as AlphaGenome and Borzoi read up to a megabase of DNA and score a genetic variant by comparing their predictions for the reference and alternate sequences. Insertions and deletions (indels) are costly to score, because an indel usually shifts the unchanged DNA after it onto a different pooling grid, which prevents direct reuse of the reference's encoder activations. The AlphaGenome Atlas scored more than 100 million indels with three full model passes each, although the DNA after an indel matches the reference shifted by the indel's length. We present ShiftCache, an exact reuse system that encodes each shifted reference once and shares it among all variants scored in the same window with the same shift. ShiftCache copies every encoder output a variant can reuse and recomputes the rest in batched tiles. On held-out AlphaGenome windows shared by many indels, in strict fp32 on one A6000, ShiftCache is 3.5 to 6.5$\times$ faster than deduplicated dense execution and 1.6 to 2.7$\times$ faster than our adaptation of layer-by-layer reuse to indels. It is 3.5 to 4.1$\times$ faster than dense reimplementations of two published analyses with Borzoi and AlphaGenome, and 2.6$\times$ faster than dense execution with Enformer. Scoring each variant in its own centered 131 kb window makes ShiftCache only 1.36$\times$ faster than deduplicated dense execution, and highly diverse insertion lengths or many dispersed edits can make it slower than layer-by-layer reuse or dense execution. For encoders that meet our conditions, ShiftCache computes the same predictions as dense execution in exact arithmetic. On an A6000, every checked output of the default AlphaGenome and Borzoi runs matches dense execution within an absolute and relative tolerance of $10^{-5}$. With larger tile batches, with Enformer or on an H100, a small fraction of values exceeds this tolerance.

papers.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
papers.abstract: Challenging repository-level benchmarks remain limited for many programming language ecosystems, where filtering scarce candidates with ambiguous descriptions or defective tests can discard valuable engineering problems. We introduce Longtail-SWE, a benchmark of 202 issue-resolution tasks across 13 languages with limited coverage in existing repository-level benchmarks: Clojure, Dart, Elixir, Erlang, F#, Haskell, Julia, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, R, Scala, and Swift. Its construction uses a solver--judge--repairer pipeline: a solver attempts each candidate task, and a judge reviews the task together with the solver's trajectory and test results to guide revisions to tests and task descriptions. These revisions aim to correct tests that reject valid alternative implementations or accept incorrect solutions while retaining challenging tasks and preserving their intended requirements. We evaluate nine model configurations, including frontier models, and analyze task-solving performance, consistency across repeated attempts, and resource usage. We release all benchmark instances, executable environments, complete construction and evaluation tooling, and agent trajectories, together with an additional set of easier tasks to support evaluation of smaller models.

authors.name: Alexander Golubev
authors.institution: Troitsk Institute for Innovation and Fusion Research

papers.title: Benchmarking Neural Image Compression with DCT-Based Spectral Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Neural image compression (NIC) models are commonly evaluated with scalar rate-distortion metrics, which do not show how a codec treats individual spatial frequencies. We propose a benchmark that probes codecs with the DCT basis matrix and single-frequency test images. We measure relative off-target energy (leakage), the fraction of reconstruction energy outside the probed frequency, together with target-frequency gain. Exact decompositions and bounds relate these measurements to reconstruction error. At operating points nearest 1 bpp, the BMSHJ, MBT, and Cheng2020 models leave 80-97% of their reconstructed high-band energy outside the target bin and have target-frequency gains of 0.02-0.23, whereas TCM and FTIC attain off-target energy in the classical-codec range. Both probe types identify behavior absent from scalar metrics: released Cheng2020-Anchor models produce extreme pre-clamp outputs on isolated single-frequency inputs. Finally, decoder-only fine-tuning with natural-image and leakage losses reduces basis off-target energy by 90-99.8% across all eight evaluated architectures while keeping the bitstream fixed, at a Kodak PSNR cost of 0.09-0.59 dB.

papers.title: Up or down by half: a family of Collatz-type maps
papers.abstract:
Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers. Define T_S(x)=(3x+1)/2 if m=0, 3x/2 if m is in S, and k otherwise. The map T_S^- differs only at odd x, which it sends to (x+1)/2. The usual Collatz map is T_emptyset.
  Assuming the independence of 2-adic valuations along odd-to-odd steps yields random-walk models with drifts (1+rho(S))log_2(3)-2 for T_S and rho(S)log_2(3)-2 for T_S^-, where rho(S) is an explicit series. Every T_S^- is contracting; T_S is contracting exactly when rho(S)<log_3(4/3), approximately 0.2619. We prove density results, classify interval sets S, and give a criterion ensuring every T_S^- orbit reaches 1 or (2,3). For seven contracting maps T_S, three with rho(S)=1/4 just below the threshold, computations show that every n<2^34 (n<1.668*10^10 for S={1}) reaches one of at most five cycles; stopping-time statistics match the model to 3-5 digits.
  We study branching maps, where any member of a family may be applied at each step. Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of {T_emptyset,T_{3}} would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For {T_emptyset,T_{1}}, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness.
  Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.

authors.name: Oleg Vasilyev
authors.institution: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sequential Candidate Entry: A Counterexample to the Osborne--Kats Conjecture
papers.abstract: Finitely many potential candidates sequentially choose an electoral position on the interval [0,1] or stay out, observing all prior choices. Voters have a uniform distribution of ideal positions on the same interval and vote non-strategically for a nearest candidate; candidates at the same position divide its votes. Candidates with the largest vote share divide a unit payoff equally, losing entrants receive a negative payoff, and staying out yields zero. In the mid-1980s, Osborne and Kats conjectured that, for every number $n\geq 2$ of players, the unique subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium (SPNE) outcome has only the first and last players entering at the median. We refute the conjecture by establishing the existence of a different SPNE outcome for 12 players. Starting from the first two entries proposed earlier by de Vries, we select an SPNE strategy profile after the first two locations 1/2 and 1/10 that gives the second player payoff at least 1/10.

papers.title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx^2-y^2 - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

authors.name: V. N. Neverov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: On transportation of constrictions on phase-lock areas of overdamped Josephson junction by means of isomonodromic deformation of the associated special double confluent Heun equation
papers.abstract: An example of computation of locations of constrictions on the phase-lock area in the parameter space for the equation modeling dynamics of overdamped Josephson junction is discussed. Several conjectures of qualitative character are inferred from the heuristic data thus obtained. The method applying isomonodromic deformations of the special double confluent Heun equation associated with the noted model is used. Such a deformation is controlled by the data provided by solution to a Third Painlev\`e equation for which a new representation in conjunction with the corresponding non-linear second order differential equation fairly efficient in the treatment of the problem in question is proposed.

authors.name: S. I. Tertychniy
authors.institution: All-Russian Scientific Research Institute of Physical-Technical and Radiotechnical Measurements

papers.title: Finite Time Analysis of Risk-Sensitive RL via Noisy Power Iteration
papers.abstract: Estimating the principal eigenpair of a positive operator from stochastic evaluations gives rise to a noisy form of normalized power iteration: each step applies a sampled operator estimate and then renormalizes. We establish finite-time stochastic-approximation guarantees for this procedure, working in Hilbert's projective metric, which is well-suited to the multiplicative geometry of Perron--Frobenius eigenproblems. Our main application is risk-sensitive average-cost reinforcement learning (RL) with exponential utility. In this setting the Bellman equations are multiplicative, and value functions are characterized by nonlinear eigenvalue problems rather than additive fixed points. We cast both policy evaluation and control in this framework, obtaining risk-sensitive TD- and Q-learning algorithms that learn from a single Markovian trajectory. Under explicit positivity, mixing, and linear function approximation assumptions, we prove finite-time bounds on the recovered eigenvector and eigenvalue with $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ sample complexity up to problem-dependent constants. The results cover both tabular and linear function approximation regimes, and through the duality between exponential utility and KL-robust control yield finite-time guarantees for KL-robust average-cost RL as well.

papers.title: Transformations of Hilbert Module Reference Frames
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide a functorial characterization of Hilbert module classical and quantum reference frames. Using the functorial characterization, we construct a category for equivariant couplings and Hilbert module reference frames. We prove the construction of the reference frame system from the equivariant coupling data yields a functor. We also deduce a ``unitary" groupoid as frame transformations for Hilbert module reference frames of a fixed Hilbert module dynamical system. We provide some examples of these frame transformations in the case of the indistinguishable classical two state switch and in the case of Hilbert spaces.

papers.intro:
In this paper, we continue the development of a Hilbert module framework for reference frames as described in [3]. In the prior work, we motivated and developed a framework for reference frames utilizing Hilbert modules and correspondences of C∗C^{*}-dynamical systems. Conceptually, the framework treats a reference frame as a physical system which acts as a background for another physical system. Due to the asymmetric relationship between the two systems, our model is designed to remember the reference system’s role so that observables in the joint system are relative to the background system. Motivated in the classical setting, the relationship between the two systems is naturally codified using a non-degenerate positive equivariant correspondence and Hilbert module dynamical system. We refer to this data as an equivariant coupling. Applying an equivariant version of both the KSGNS construction and interior tensor product to the data yields the relation joint system which we refer to as the reference frame system. In addition to the equivariant coupling, a choice of relativization map is required to describe how observables in the main system are conditioned/relativized to invariant relational observables in the reference frame system. We refer to the data of an equivariant coupling and relativization map as a Hilbert module reference frame.

We refer to this data as an equivariant coupling. Applying an equivariant version of both the KSGNS construction and interior tensor product to the data yields the relation joint system which we refer to as the reference frame system. In addition to the equivariant coupling, a choice of relativization map is required to describe how observables in the main system are conditioned/relativized to invariant relational observables in the reference frame system. We refer to the data of an equivariant coupling and relativization map as a Hilbert module reference frame.

For a fixed equivariant coupling, multiple relativization maps can exist (see the examples in Section 3.5 of [3]). Furthermore, for any two fixed C∗C^{*}-algebras, multiple equivariant couplings can exist between the two systems (see the examples in Section 3.5 of [3]). Due to the degeneracy of the data, we want to understand how these different choices are related, and we want to understand in what sense these different choices describe the same reference frame system. To answer both of these structural questions, we develop frame transformations for Hilbert module reference frames.

In our framework, frame transformations are defined at the level of the equivariant couplings and relativization map. As a result, a frame transformation codifies the ways of changing the reference system and equivariant coupling while preserving the relational observables. Due to the data involved for defining a Hilbert module reference frame, there is no obvious choice for defining frame transformations or even morphisms between two reference frames.

While these morphisms describe relationships between equivariant couplings, we still need to include the relativization map data. To describe how the morphisms of EqCpl interact with the relativization maps, we prove the construction of a reference frame system from the data of an equivariant coupling yields a functor on the subcategory EqCpl∗-iso\textnormal{EqCpl}_{*\textnormal{-iso}} of EqCpl to CCP∗\textnormal{C}^{*}_{\textnormal{CP}} (see Theorem 4.16), the category of C∗C^{*}-algebras with morphisms given by strict completely positive maps. Note that the restriction to the subcategory is a result of the functoriality of the KSGNS construction. Using the functor from the reference frame construction, we bootstrap our way to define a category, denoted by HMRF, whose objects are Hilbert module reference frames.

Fixing a Hilbert module dynamical system, we pass to a subcategory of HMRF whose objects represent Hilbert module reference frames for the fixed dynamical system. As a first pass, the groupoid/core of this subcategory is taken to define frame transformations. By requiring the induced morphisms between reference frame systems from a frame transformation to induce a map at the level of states, we are required to restrict to a sub-groupoid whose morphisms induce unitary maps (Theorem 5.6 and Theorem 5.10). Thus, we led to a “unitary” groupoid for frame transformations. These unitary frame transformations induce ∗*-algebra isomorphisms at the level of the reference frame systems (Corollary 5.7).

As a first pass, the groupoid/core of this subcategory is taken to define frame transformations. By requiring the induced morphisms between reference frame systems from a frame transformation to induce a map at the level of states, we are required to restrict to a sub-groupoid whose morphisms induce unitary maps (Theorem 5.6 and Theorem 5.10). Thus, we led to a “unitary” groupoid for frame transformations. These unitary frame transformations induce ∗*-algebra isomorphisms at the level of the reference frame systems (Corollary 5.7).

While the abstract view point of equivariant couplings and Hilbert module reference frames is introduced to define morphisms and frame transformations, there are concrete ways of obtaining both morphisms of equivariant couplings as well as unitary frame transformations. In fact, we prove a general template for constructing both morphisms (Corollary 3.14 and Corollary 5.11). Using these templates, we describe two classes of examples of unitary frame transformation. The first class of examples come from when both the main system and reference system are given by a classical indistinguishable two state system. The second class of examples come from when both the modules for the main system and correspondence are Hilbert spaces. In both settings, we provide a characterization of unitary frame transformations. From the characterization in the two state switch setting, we see how the choice of relativization map can allow for additional symmetry at the level of unitary frame transformations. This presents the question how relativization maps relate to the ideas of spontaneous symmetry breaking that we hope to answer in a future paper.

In fact, we prove a general template for constructing both morphisms (Corollary 3.14 and Corollary 5.11). Using these templates, we describe two classes of examples of unitary frame transformation. The first class of examples come from when both the main system and reference system are given by a classical indistinguishable two state system. The second class of examples come from when both the modules for the main system and correspondence are Hilbert spaces. In both settings, we provide a characterization of unitary frame transformations. From the characterization in the two state switch setting, we see how the choice of relativization map can allow for additional symmetry at the level of unitary frame transformations. This presents the question how relativization maps relate to the ideas of spontaneous symmetry breaking that we hope to answer in a future paper.

We now outline the layout of this paper. In Section 2, we build the category HMod, and we prove Hilbert dynamical systems are in one-to-one correspondence with unitary valued functors B​G→HModBG\to\textnormal{HMod}. In Section 3, we utilize the functorial characterization of equivariant correspondences and Hilbert module dynamical systems to develop the category EqCpl which contains all equivariant couplings as objects. In Section 4, we prove the reference frame construction from an equivariant coupling provides a functor from the subcategory EqCpl∗-iso\textnormal{EqCpl}_{*\textnormal{-iso}} to CCP∗\textnormal{C}^{*}_{\textnormal{CP}}. Finally, in Section 5, we use the functoriality of the reference frame construction to develop the category HMRF which contains Hilbert module reference frames as objects. Using this category and properties of the induced morphisms from the reference frame construction, we deduce unitary frame transformation as an appropriate notion of transformations for Hilbert module reference frames.

papers.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of $\Delta u=\lambda u^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

papers.title: ReGKG-2025: A GKG-Compatible Reconstruction of the GDELT Global Knowledge Graph for the Missing Period of 14 June to 2 July 2025
papers.abstract: The June 2025 outage in the Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone (GDELT) collection pipeline left a gap in the Global Knowledge Graph (GKG), interrupting article-level news metadata used in downstream research. ReGKG-2025 is an archive-derived sample of 281,620 reconstructed article records covering all 1,665 missing 15-minute batches. Articles were recovered from Common Crawl and the Wayback Machine using source quotas estimated from surrounding native GKG data. Text was screened and normalized, non-English bodies were translated, and flagged records were manually reviewed. Eligible articles were converted to the 27-column GKG 2.1 layout. The versioned package includes record-level provenance, archive replay and WARC locators, source summaries, source-by-day calibration weights, and the complete manual decision journal. The sample reaches about 14% of modeled native volume and represents sources accounting for 84% of selected reference record mass. In an intact-week test, 41% of recovered articles matched native GKG records; field agreement on matched pairs is close to the processor baseline (tone MAE 1.69). The dataset supports retrospective content analysis and source-level aggregates; its tone and theme distributions differ from native GKG, and it does not support exhaustive counts. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23964265.

papers.title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
papers.abstract:
We study properties of optimal trajectories for
  the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables
  is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs
  in general GJN.

papers.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

papers.title: Good Looks and the Academic Job Market: Measuring Attractiveness with Vision Embeddings
papers.abstract: We introduce a new approach to measure physical attractiveness---the relative vision embedding (RVE) score. The score maps a face to a vector in the embedding space of a pre-trained deep vision model and measures its proximity to a reference set of celebrity faces. It requires no additional training or fine-tuning, no hand-crafted features, and no human raters; it is continuous, inexpensive, scalable, and fully reproducible. Using publicly available photographs with human attractiveness ratings, we show that the RVE scores correlate strongly with human ratings and that rankings are consistent across several off-the-shelf vision models. We apply the measure to administrative hiring data from a research-oriented economics department, complemented by hand-collected photographs of the job applicants. Higher RVE scores are associated with better job-market outcomes, though the association is not robust across all specifications. In contrast, the association with reference-letter length and sentiment is strong and robust: candidates with higher RVE scores receive longer letters written in more favorable language, and this sentiment gradient is steeper for female candidates. The pattern is consistent with appearance affecting academic hiring in part through letters of recommendation.

authors.name: Fabian Slonimczyk
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
papers.abstract: We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.

papers.title: Resolvent Ellipsoid for Minty Set Inclusions
papers.abstract: We study Minty set inclusion on a compact convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with a set-valued operator $A : \mathcal{X} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}^d$. Under the Minty promise, the goal is to compute $x \in \mathcal{X}$ and $u \in A(x)$ such that $\sup_{y \in \mathcal{X}} \langle u, x - y \rangle \le \varepsilon$. Our approach is geometric and we work in the fixed-scale constrained-resolvent oracle model, where a query at anchor $a$ is assumed to return a resolvent point $x^+$ together with the Yosida vector $g_{\eta}(a) = (a - x^+)/\eta$. We prove that each oracle response yields a sharp dichotomy: either the returned point provides an $\varepsilon$-SVI certificate, or the Yosida vector defines a strict separating normal for the Minty set. Thus, a single black-box resolvent query supplies either a certified candidate solution or a valid geometric cut. Combining this separation principle with the ellipsoid method, we obtain RESOLVENT-ELLIPSOID, an algorithm that computes an $\varepsilon$-SVI in $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box oracle calls to the fixed-scale constrained resolvent. For monotone inclusions, our algorithm gives, to our knowledge, the first $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\mathrm{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box guarantee in the fixed-scale resolvent model.

papers.title: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games
papers.abstract: We study the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For prediction with expert advice, the optimal regret is $\Theta(\sqrt{T\log K})$, where $K$ is the number of experts, or equivalently, the number of normal-form actions. For treeplex strategy spaces, existing efficient algorithms, including KOMWU and online mirror descent with the weight-one dilated entropy regularizer, achieve regret $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$, where $\mathcal{V}$ is the set of reduced normal-form strategies. We prove that this logarithmic dependence is minimax optimal in the worst-case full-information reward model. The main difficulty is that pure plans in a treeplex are not independent experts: their rewards are correlated through the recursive structure of decisions and observations. To capture this correlation, we introduce tropical Gaussian formulae, recursive Gaussian expressions built from maxima and normalized sums which preserve the variance. The index count of such a formula matches the number of reduced normal-form continuation plans in the corresponding subtree. Our main analytic result shows that every log-balanced tropical Gaussian formula with index count $N$ has Gaussian width $\Omega(\sqrt{\log N})$. While a direct approach struggles to recover this lower bound, our proof uses a spherical entropy profile to measure scale-dependent separation among the Gaussian directions, and then applies Tur\'an's theorem and Sudakov minoration to obtain the width lower bound. Applying this result to treeplexes gives an oblivious hard distribution with valid transition outcome and Rademacher terminal rewards, establishing a regret lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$. This matches known upper bounds up to universal constants and shows that the DilEnt/KOMWU dependence on the reduced normal-form complexity is unavoidable.

authors.name: Lillian J. Ratliff
authors.institution: University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory

papers.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most na\"{\i}ve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups. As a consequence, for any integer $n>0$, these sheaves modulo $n$ also have Gersten property. The proof is an elementary application of the Voevodsky's $(-1)$-machinery and consists of assembling several well-known results.

authors.name: M. Rovinsky
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
papers.abstract: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$ for minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares regression with two input and two output coordinates, improving the upper bound $15/8$. More precisely, a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights. Together with the known lower bound, this gives $13/8\le F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$. No numerical value of $\varepsilon_0$ is claimed.

papers.title: From Likelihood Convergence to Parameter Convergence in POMDPs
papers.abstract: Likelihood-based methods are widely used to learn the parameters of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs). While finite-sample guarantees for policy suboptimality exist for certain POMDP subclasses, analogous guarantees for parameter recovery remain less well understood. For any candidate POMDP parameter, we bound its parameter recovery error in terms of its likelihood gap to the ground truth, the structural conditioning of the observation and transition kernels, and the behavior policy used to collect data. The bound applies in both the undercomplete and overcomplete regimes, with the latter following naturally from the undercomplete analysis. Because the result applies to any sufficiently good candidate, it yields finite-sample guarantees for the maximum-likelihood estimator and any procedure producing a parameter with controlled likelihood gap. This is particularly useful for near-optimal learning in infinite-horizon POMDPs, where existing approaches largely rely on model-based planning with accurate transition and observation kernel estimates. The bound separates the contributions of the behavior policy and model, showing how data-collection choices, including action coverage, and their effects on mixing can accelerate parameter learning.

authors.name: Jack Zhang
authors.institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

papers.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
papers.abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

authors.name: Veronika Kikteva
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: Correctness Boundaries of Typed Plans for Natural-Language Robot Fleet Control
papers.abstract: We examine what plan validation and execution reports establish in natural-language robot fleet control. Commands are traced through typed plans, deterministic corrections, fleet coordination and outcome checks in a three-level Robot Operating System 2 implementation with twenty simulated robots. An offline benchmark of 44 cases checks plan structure and selected command requirements. Across five local configurations without a response schema, 70.0-87.3% of responses pass. All runs in a selected 18-run simulation series meet their pose-based task conditions. This series includes two successful repeats that replaced incomplete runs after a software change. Saved plans and logs document duplicate pickup assignments and goal adjustments within the original task zones. Separate formation traces show a structurally accepted plan with the wrong formation shape and a rejected route, and an arrival report that omitted a requested robot after replanning. Carry completion records pickup and subsequent drop-off zone presence for the same robot. The cases distinguish changes to executable actions from changes to the requirements covered by a completion report. They motivate checking the effective assignments, goals and reported outcome against the original command.

papers.title: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels
papers.abstract: Magnetic edge channels, arising at the edge of a two-dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field, are topologically protected and propagate unidirectionally along the edge. Their group velocities at the Fermi level, being averaged harmonically, result in drift velocity, which is related to the edge density of states, quantum capacitance, and the velocity of edge magnetoplasmons. Using semiclassical quantization of electron skipping orbits, we show that the drift velocity equals 1/2 of the electron Fermi velocity in the limit of a large number of edge channels crossing the Fermi level. This result, being universal for a hard edge and for isotropic dispersion, is checked numerically for massive electrons and for massless electrons in graphene. The drift velocity at smooth electrostatically defined edges lacks such universality. In the case of anisotropic dispersion, the semiclassical drift velocity at the hard edge reduces to a coordinate-velocity correlation along the cyclotron orbit.

papers.title: Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations
papers.abstract: The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model). Conditions are found on the Buckley--Leverett function, the adsorption function, and the distribution function of the reagent in oil under which the original system, by means of a nonlinear change of variables on a five-dimensional manifold endowed with a contact structure, is reduced to a linear wave system with constant coefficients. Six families of such functions are indicated. For them, contact transformations and Legendre surfaces corresponding to general solutions in implicit form are constructed.

papers.title: Covariate-Conditioned One-Step Diffusion for Multi-Horizon 3D Brain MRI Prediction in Aging and Neurodegeneration
papers.abstract: Predicting longitudinal brain changes from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can help characterize structural progression associated with aging and neurodegeneration. However, diffusion-based forecasting typically requires iterative denoising, limiting inference efficiency. We propose a covariate-conditioned one-step diffusion framework for multi-horizon prediction of 3D gray-matter density (GMD) maps. Rather than directly generating future anatomy, the model predicts longitudinal GMD changes through residual prediction in a single denoising step. The predicted changes are added to the baseline GMD map to reconstruct future anatomy. The model is conditioned on baseline anatomy, age, diagnosis, APOE4 allele count, and continuous follow-up time. Training combines mean squared error with a Pearson correlation loss to improve the spatial agreement between predicted and observed GMD changes. A unified model supports prediction horizons from 2 to 10 years. On the held-out ADNI test set, our method achieves a $\Delta$-Pearson of 0.478, mean squared error (MSE) of $5.176 \times 10^{-3}$, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.979, with $\Delta$-Pearson reaching 0.582 at 10 years. Without retraining, external evaluation on AIBL yields a $\Delta$-Pearson of 0.450, MSE of $4.016 \times 10^{-3}$, and SSIM of 0.985. Ablation studies further demonstrate the benefits of residual prediction, covariate conditioning, and correlation-based supervision. Code: https://github.com/natenaile/OneStepBrainMRI.

papers.title: Hierarchical Nonlinear Control for Swarm Encirclement Around a Moving Target UAV
papers.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical inner-outer loop nonlinear control strategy using a geometric Lyapunov-based framework for the cooperative encirclement of a target by multi-ple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in three-dimensional space. The encirclement problem is formulated on a two-sphere with arbitrary radius and center, denoted Gamma-2, by projecting agent positions from R3 onto a spherical manifold centered at the target, being the unit two-sphere at the origin S2 used for intermediate calculations. Desired encirclement configurations are generated via a point separation method on Gamma-2, while stable convergence from R3 to these points is guaranteed using a Lyapunov-based reduced-attitude control law inspired by geometric control on the two-sphere. Formal stability results are derived using Lyapunov analysis and the framework is validated in simulation using a nonlinear quadrotor model and controller. Results demonstrate stable encirclement and highlight the suitability of the proposed approach for three-dimensional multi-agent aerial systems.

papers.title: Self-bound quantum dark fermion stars: saturation, a coupling-capped maximum mass, and tidal signatures of a vector dark sector
papers.abstract: I show that a dark sector whose fermions couple to both a scalar and a vector mediator saturates in close analogy with nuclear matter: the energy per particle develops a minimum at finite density, cold dark matter of this kind is self-bound, and its stars, computed here in full general relativity, possess the sharp surfaces of strange quark stars. Saturation makes the maximum stellar mass a property of the Lagrangian rather than an inheritance of the Chandrasekhar scaling: it rises eightfold across the saturation window, which a critical vector coupling closes, so the theory caps its own maximum mass, at $3.9\,M_\odot$ for a fermion of $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the fiducial saturation density, a ceiling shared by the whole family of couplings rather than by any single parameter set. Metastable couplings support two disconnected stable families, one dilute and gravitationally bound, the other dense and self-bound. The quantum-pressure correction, confined by saturation to a surface layer a few Compton wavelengths thick, governs the smallest dark nuggets whilst shifting stellar masses by less than one part in $10^{21}$. A $1.4\,M_\odot$ member of the fiducial family has a radius of $13.3\,\mathrm{km}$, a compactness of $0.155$, and a tidal deformability of $1.6\times 10^{3}$, almost an order of magnitude above the measured neutron-star value, so at a given particle mass and couplings a single well-measured inspiral distinguishes these stars from neutron stars and from their scalar-only counterparts, whilst the deformability surviving at the maximum mass separates them, in principle, from black holes.

papers.title: VIVID: Bringing Tool-Augmented Agents into Enterprises
papers.abstract: Tool-augmented large language model agents connect natural-language requests to enterprise services, yet their operational viability depends on reliable execution, organizational control, and system responsiveness. We present VIVID, a deployed tourism-management agent system designed to study these requirements in a real enterprise environment. On an audited dataset of 283 queries, its Qwen3-8B configuration achieves 59.06\% strict end-to-end success across the evaluated decision stages, indicating useful but bounded autonomous capability. Stage-wise KV-cache eviction reduces mean latency by 34.4\%, while targeted optimization reduces the mean latency of the five slowest measured business tools by 81.1--92.3\%. In a three-month deployment serving more than 1,500 personnel, VIVID reduced average per-order processing time from approximately ten minutes to under two minutes, with a final-task error rate below 1\% after human-in-the-loop control. These results show that enterprise agent viability requires system-level consideration beyond isolated tool-calling accuracy.

papers.title: RoadState: A Domain-Prior-Enhanced Vision-Language System for Industrial-Grade Lane-Level Map Updating
papers.abstract: Lane-level map updating requires temporally consistent, physically valid, and auditable road-scene semantics despite occlusions, ambiguous lane markings, temporary obstacles, and viewpoint changes. We present RoadState, a production-deployed vision-language system that transforms sequential road-scene observations into structured lane-level semantics for Baidu Maps' map-updating pipeline. Its core model, RoadState-VLM, formulates road-scene understanding as autoregressive state estimation, predicting the current structured road state from the previous observation and symbolic state together with the current observation. We introduce Geometric Chain-of-Thought (Geo-CoT), which uses a directed acyclic graph of semantic dependencies as a domain prior to improve semantic consistency and reasoning fidelity across interdependent road-state dimensions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that RoadState-VLM achieves 94.33% mean accuracy across six road-state dimensions, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned VLM baseline. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary effectiveness of Geo-CoT and temporal transition context. A cascaded routing pipeline directs routine cases to lightweight models while reserving complex cases for RoadState-VLM. Since its deployment in March 2025, RoadState has supported lane-level map updating across more than 360 cities and reduced overall production costs by 30%. Together with human-in-the-loop auditing, the system maintains robust performance under stress-test conditions. These results demonstrate how domain-prior-enhanced reasoning, structured state interfaces, selective routing, and human quality control can bridge the gap between VLM-based road-scene understanding and large-scale lane-level map updating.

papers.title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.

papers.title: DIY Customized Speech Recognition for a Person with Speech Disabilities
papers.abstract: General-purpose state-of-the-art automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems fail systematically for speakers with moderate to severe speech disabilities. This paper describes the design, implementation, and evaluation of a customized ASR system built for the first author, a researcher with cerebral palsy and dysarthria. We fine-tuned OpenAI's Whisper medium and large-v3 models using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on audio samples recorded from the first author's own speech on consumer-grade hardware. On a held-out test set of 100 previously unseen utterances, the corresponding transcriptions resulted in a Word Error Rate drop from 49% to 17% for medium and from 30% to 12% for large-v3, while the Character Error Rate fell from 26% to 7% for medium and from 16% to 5% for large-v3, indicating that the residual errors are minor phonemic substitutions. Based on these models, the first author developed AVoz, a mobile application that acts as a real-time interpreter, converting his speech into synthesized voice for the listener. All processing is performed locally, ensuring that no audio data leaves the user's machine. We argue that the methodology is replicable. Moreover, we publish the full LoRA configuration, the implementation, and a step-by-step recording and training protocol, so that other people with speech disabilities, or their family members and caregivers, can build their own systems with a few hours of labeled audio data and a couple of days of GPU time.

papers.title: Harmonic functions and comparsion geometry for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several sharp comparsion results for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and with a compact, connected boundary under a boundary mean curvature condition. Then we apply these gradient estimates to establish a Cohn-Vossen type bound for the average of the scalar curvature. This generalizes the work of Colding-Minicozzi \cite{Cold4} and Oronzio \cite{Oro2}.

papers.title: Silinx: An Open, Browser-Based HDL Design Platform for Teaching Digital Systems on FPGA Boards
papers.abstract: Many digital systems courses teach on FPGA boards whose vendor tool is no longer maintained: the Digilent Basys2 and Nexys2 (Xilinx Spartan-3E) and Nexys3 and Atlys (Spartan-6) need Xilinx ISE 14.7, discontinued since 2013 and hard to install on the computers and tablets students use today. The author presents Silinx, a free (AGPL-3.0) HDL design platform for teaching that keeps ISE's Project Navigator workflow but runs in a web browser with nothing to install. A module can be written in VHDL or Verilog, in C or C++ through Silinx HLS, which is compatible with AMD's Vitis HLS and passes all 73 of its introductory examples, or drawn as a schematic, an ASM chart, a state diagram, a Boolean function with its Karnaugh map, or a Petri net, from which its HDL is generated. Designs are checked with explanations written for beginners, simulated, run on an emulated board, built, and programmed onto a real board over WebUSB. The implementation flow is open and runs in the browser: Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, with Silinx's own device data, timing model and bitstream writer for the Spartan-3E and Spartan-6, built by black-box observation of ISE's documented tools; Lattice iCE40 boards use the existing open iCE40 tools, and further families are planned. ISE is the oracle: Silinx's bitstreams are byte-identical to those ISE writes for the same placed and routed design, and pass ISE's design rule check. Against ISE at the same optimization goal, the open flow uses 15% fewer slices with 14% shorter critical paths when optimizing for area, and 21% fewer slices with 8% shorter critical paths when optimizing for speed (geometric means over 45 open-source designs built by both flows). The author also describes how the platform was developed with AI coding agents under test-first project rules.

papers.title: Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have begun incorporating thermal sensing, but existing approaches typically treat thermal images as ordinary visual inputs, providing limited support for temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. To address this limitation, we propose Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation. We further construct six real-world robotic tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform, spanning basic grounding to relational reasoning. Experiments show that Thermo-VLA achieves an average success rate of 0.86 across four thermal-dependent tasks, outperforming a pi_0.5 baseline that directly incorporates RGB-thermal observations by 18 percentage points. Under unseen-object and scene variations, Thermo-VLA maintains an average success rate of 0.78, achieving the best generalisation performance among the compared methods. Beyond thermal sensing, we transfer the same residual modulation mechanism to colour attributes and observe consistent improvements in both simulation and real-robot experiments, indicating its potential to generalise beyond thermal attributes. Project website: https://j-x-chen.github.io/Thermo-VLA-web/

papers.title: On semigroups of order-decreasing partial isometries: presentations and ranks of certain ideals
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the monoid of all order-decreasing partial isometries on a chain with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{ODP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the submonoid of $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ consisting of all order-preserving partial isometries. In this paper, for each $1\leq r\leq n$, we determine minimal generating sets of the ideals $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$, thereby determining their ranks. Furthermore, we give presentations for the monoids $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$.

papers.title: MATA: Motion-aligned Temporal Adapter
papers.abstract: Few-shot fine-grained video action recognition requires recognizing novel action classes from only a few labeled examples. The difficulty is that visually similar actions often share actors, scenes, poses, and objects, differing only in the order, timing, and short duration of motion changes. We study this problem under three practical constraints: few tunable parameters, low compute cost, and use of the video modality alone. We propose Motion-aligned Temporal Adapter (MATA), a parameter-efficient adapter on top of a frozen CLIP backbone. MATA specializes CLIP features along the temporal dimension using two components: temporal phase alignment through learnable temporal positional embeddings, and a local motion transition operator through depth-wise convolution. With only ~3.6M tunable parameters, MATA achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple fine-grained benchmarks while remaining robust to both visual corruptions and temporal disruptions induced by frame dropping. Code is available at https://github.com/prakashchhipa/MATA-Motion-aligned-Temporal-Adapter

papers.title: MicroSim: Contrastive Graph Neural Networks for Binary Code Similarity Detection
papers.abstract: We present MicroSim, a system for binary code similarity detection that represents each function as a graph built from IDA Pro Hex-Rays microcode and compares such graphs with a contrastive Siamese graph neural network (GNN). We evaluate on the TREX cross-optimization benchmark, a corpus of 849,072 function-level microcode graphs spanning optimization levels -O0 through -O3, under a strict class-disjoint split in which no function key is shared between train and test. Under this protocol, MicroSim reaches 0.9972 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) and 0.9762 Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), outperforming Gemini (0.9332 ROC-AUC), SAFE (0.9752), and jTrans (0.9740) retrained on the same split, as well as a structure-free Bag-of-Words (BoW) baseline (0.9484). We analyze the gap between pair classification and ranked retrieval in graph transformers, showing that Cross-domain Similarity Local Scaling (CSLS) under unified tie-resolved evaluation raises GraphGPS mean reciprocal rank (MRR) from 0.2542 to 0.2559 (R@1 = 0.1639, R@10 = 0.4561), strictly satisfying the theoretical MRR upper bound. Finally, over 5 seeds with equal compute, the pairwise cosine-embedding loss attains a slightly higher ROC-AUC ({\Delta} = -0.0256, 95% confidence interval [-0.3282, +0.2770]), whereas the supervised-contrastive information noise-contrastive estimation (InfoNCE) loss is significantly better on thresholded classification and ranked retrieval.

papers.title: On the nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene: a first-principles study
papers.abstract: The nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the magic angle has been extensively discussed in the literature on qualitative grounds, since these states play a key role in the construction of effective few-band models toward a many-body theory. Here, we report extensive and systematic first-principles calculations of TBG electronic states in the magic-angle range, using density functional theory with no further approximations. We construct moir\'e-scale localized Wannier states for the low-energy bands and develop an effective ten-band model for each $K$ valley. The Wannier orbitals contain both atomic and moir\'e-scale details and are centered near the high-symmetry stackings in the moir\'e cell. We calculate Coulomb and exchange integrals of these localized states, quantities that are the basic ingredients in many-body models. We also compare the values of these integrals to those obtained or assumed in previous works. By symmetrizing the ten-band Hamiltonians and basis orbitals, we provide insight into how the dominant hoppings between the flat-band orbitals evolve as a function of twist angle.

papers.title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
papers.abstract: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_\gamma - \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates. In the neutral regime, using Fa\`a di Bruno equations and Malgrange preparation, we derive quantitative $1/k$-H\"older estimates for order-$k$ anchor perturbations. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. Numerical benchmarks on circular-core return geometries validate these theoretical convergence rates and square-root laws.

papers.title: An Algebraic Foundation of Rate-Product Style Quantity Calculus
papers.abstract: Using the new notion of a scalable (right) monoid-heap, the quantity calculus in [1] is generalized to include quantities that may not be possible to multiply as well as both (weak) rates and products of quantities. Several examples are given of applications in metrology and physics

authors.name: Dan Jonsson
authors.institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

papers.title: On Symmetric Chain Decompositions for Bruhat--Chevalley Posets
papers.abstract: We consider Stanley's problem on describing symmetric chain decompositions for the Bruhat--Chevalley posets of partial flag varieties and, more generally, Schubert varieties. These posets describe the containment relations of cell closures in the partial flag variety $G/P$ of a connected complex reductive algebraic group $G$. A famous instance of this problem asks whether the poset of partitions that fit inside a rectangle ordered by containment admits a symmetric chain decomposition (SCD), corresponding to the case of Grassmannian Schubert varieties in type $A$. Our first main result applies the ``complete BP decomposition" of Richmond--Slofstra to show that the SCD problem for any rationally smooth Schubert variety reduces to the (generalized) Grassmannian case, in any semisimple type. We further study the SCDs provided by codes for Bruhat--Chevalley posets in type $A$. These SCDs can be viewed as a consequence of a particular form of complete BP decomposition. In particular, we show that a poset of permutation-labeled partitions in a rectangle corresponding to the quotient $\mathcal{S}_n/\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ admits an SCD. Further, posets of weak compositions inside a rectangle are realized as Bruhat--Chevalley intervals with associated codes and SCDs.

papers.title: Uncertainty, Not Concealment: A Mechanistic Reappraisal of Sycophancy in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) in medical retrieval-augmented generation must be able to say when a retrieved report contradicts the X-ray, so understanding whether they can detect such conflicts is important for safe deployment. The sycophancy mask hypothesis holds that these models internally detect conflicts but refuse to report them, concealing a detected contradiction. We introduce a three-part diagnostic that separates concealment from uncertainty: representation probing, activation steering, and two-way forced choice. Across four instruction-tuned VLMs on chest X-rays, we confirm behavioral suppression of contradiction and find that a linear probe separates matched from mismatched inputs, beyond what a simple CLIP model achieves. Steering the learned conflict direction never elicits contradiction, and forcing a binary choice does not recover one; instead, cross-modal attention to the image drops on mismatched pairs. We conclude that these models fail to contradict because the mismatch registers as hedged, gated uncertainty rather than concealed knowledge, calling for re-grounding and uncertainty surfacing. Code is available at https://github.com/mohamed-eldagla/Uncertainty-Not-Concealment/.
