papers.title: Symbolic Synthesis with Token-Level LLM Guidance
papers.abstract:
We propose a synergistic combination of classical program synthesis techniques and contemporary large language models (LLMs) to solve the problem of recursive program synthesis from first-order logic specifications. Our approach leverages the strengths of both paradigms: we use LLMs as a source of statistical bias to guide the search for a correct program. At the same time we use techniques from classical synthesis to short-circuit on semantically incorrect prefixes and to avoid sampling semantically equivalent responses. The statistical bias is derived from the next-token distribution of an LLM, which is highly context-dependent.
  We operate with the understanding that (1) there is some class of synthesis instances that can be discharged by small models and symbolic tools, and (2) every other instance can be decomposed into these instances. Therefore, our intention is to expand the reach of small, open-weight LLMs and symbolic synthesis techniques, not to compete with proprietary frontier models on every possible instance. These are different tools for different jobs. In our experimental evaluation, we find that our method solves more benchmarks than either small LLMs or classical synthesis techniques alone. Our method solves 30/32 benchmarks using only a Qwen2.5 model with 32 billion parameters. Qwen2.5 solves 0 benchmarks on its own, and only solves a few additional benchmarks when combined with traditional constrained decoding techniques.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Confidence-driven adaptive semantic transmission for task-oriented communication
papers.abstract: Image-based remote monitoring over wireless networks faces a trade-off between communication cost and classification reliability. Transmitting complete images is communication-intensive, whereas relying solely on lightweight edge classifiers may compromise accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose Confidence-Driven Adaptation (CDA) for image transmission and classification. An edge device (ED) captures images and applies a lightweight classifier before transmission to a remote server. Based on its classification confidence, the ED selects among three transmission modes with varying levels of information: a short text string reporting its predicted class when confidence is high, a compressed Region of Interest (ROI) at intermediate confidence levels, or an uncompressed ROI when confidence is low. The server accepts the predicted class directly in the first case and performs classification using a more powerful classifier in the other two cases. Numerical evaluations under bandwidth-limited, lossy links and latency-constrained settings demonstrate that CDA achieves high task accuracy at the receiver compared with non-adaptive baselines that transmit only the edge-classifier outcome or the uncompressed ROI.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Quantitative Ultrasound (DeepQUS) for Multiparametric Hepatic Steatosis Assessment
papers.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) has shown promise for liver fat quantification in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Incorporating multiple parameters has demonstrated the potential to outperform single QUS parameter measures. Here, we propose a deep learning-based multiparametric QUS framework that learns effective integration of multiple features from QUS measures to estimate pixel-wise hepatic fat fraction, enabling the detecting of heterogeneous fat accumulation within the liver. We developed a U-Net based network architecture to predict local fat fraction percentages, which takes 2D QUS maps as input and is trained with magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) as the ground truth. We extracted 2D QUS maps (H-scan frequency, at-tenuation, Nakagami, and RF/envelope/log-compressed data) and tested various input configura-tions consisting of different combinations of the QUS parameters. We enrolled 30 patients with healthy livers or suspected/confirmed MASLD, and acquired ultrasound RF data, and validated our approach using the patient data. Among all tested input configurations, the model combining H-scan, attenuation, and Nak-agami parameters achieved the best performance, with a Spearman correlation coefficient (Rs) of 0.92 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.98. The predicted fat fraction maps exhibited color changes concordant with the gradual increasing in MRI-PDFF, from normal liver to 45% fat ac-cumulation. These findings demonstrate that deep learning can integrate multiparametric QUS in-formation in a fully data-driven manner, providing a localized fat fraction map rather than a single whole-liver value. We anticipate that our deep learning framework can offer potential advantages for future assessment of heterogeneous disease development in liver for more complex, progres-sive liver diseases such as steatohepatitis.

authors.name: Jihye Baek
authors.institution: Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute

papers.title: Synergizing CKM and ISAC for Environment-Aware Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Channel knowledge map (CKM) and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) have emerged as two key technologies for sixth-generation (6G) and beyond wireless networks, enabling a new paradigm toward environment-aware system design. CKMs provide static or stochastic wireless environment information a priori by learning location-dependent mappings from transceiver positions to channel knowledge of various types, whereas ISAC exploits wireless signals to sense environmental objects in real time. CKM and ISAC have primarily been studied separately in prior works, while their integration offers a promising approach for enhancing the environment awareness of 6G networks and further improving both sensing and communication capabilities. On the one hand, sensing can support CKM construction by providing location-tagged measurements and richer environmental observations, while also enabling real-time CKM refinement in dynamic environments. On the other hand, CKM can enhance sensing by offering prior environmental information for clutter mitigation, and CKM and sensing information can be jointly leveraged to improve communications. This article provides an overview of the complementary interactions between CKMs and ISAC, with particular emphasis on three design approaches: sensing-assisted CKM construction and refinement, CKM-assisted sensing, and joint CKM- and sensing-enhanced communications. We also discuss future research directions for achieving environment-aware wireless networks.

papers.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Estimating the motion of deformable bodies in soft robotics from proprioceptive sensing is challenging due to partial observability, as internal observations provide only indirect access to global motion, contact, and shape evolution. In such settings, instantaneous observations are insufficient, and accurate estimation requires temporally consistent latent representations. This paper studies deformable motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability from a latent dynamics perspective. We argue that a key requirement for long-horizon estimation is latent temporal consistency, where latent states remain predictive of future observations. To this end, we present DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework that enforces predictive structure in latent dynamics through a self-supervised latent prediction constraint. We evaluate the approach in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as a controlled source of ground truth. Results demonstrate consistent improvements in trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference over architecture-matched recurrent baselines.

authors.name: Chen Feng
authors.institution: Anhui University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Capability-Guided Iterative Online Optimization of Cascaded Spoken-Dialogue Modules
papers.abstract: Cascaded spoken dialogue systems comprise perception-and-comprehension, decision-making, and response-generation modules. We study iterative optimization of the first and last modules. Their reciprocal speech-content interfaces enable one-sided data to provide cross-module supervision: acoustic observations, such as waveforms or feature sequences, can be pseudo-labeled to train generation, whereas content-only samples can be rendered into speech to train comprehension. Because the reliable teacher-student direction varies across domains, we propose a two-stage, capability-guided pipeline for iterative online optimization. Stage 1 compares both modules through a shared intelligibility probe and obtains a domain-wise capability prior. Stage 2 activates the compatible one-sided-data route, constructs and filters supervision with the current teacher, updates the selected student, and refreshes the relevant checkpoints across cycles. We instantiate comprehension with Whisper large-v3 and generation with CosyVoice2. After only 200 steps for Whisper and 600 for CosyVoice2 of our iterative online optimization, we observe that, on the Chinese MAGICDATA-RAMC dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 14.18% to 10.77%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 4.78% to 4.04%. On the Japanese Common Voice dataset, Whisper reduces CER from 15.23% to 15.10%, while CosyVoice2 reduces it from 14.85% to 11.18%. These results demonstrate the feasibility of capability-guided iterative optimization of complementary spoken-dialogue modules.

authors.name: Wenbin Huang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Hankun Wang
authors.institution: International Center for Bamboo and Rattan

authors.name: Xie Chen
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.

papers.title: A Bifurcation-Theoretic Framework for the Controllability of Emergent Intelligent Systems
papers.abstract: Real-world intelligent systems must reconcile two demands: the adaptability conferred by emergence and the steerability required for accountable deployment. We show that these demands are governed by two distinct bifurcations on the same object and that, consequently, increased capability does not imply increased controllability. Emergence is a bifurcation of the capability variable $S$, with criterion $\Gamma:=\mathcal F'(0)>1$ equivalent to the existence of a unique positive stable fixed point of a self-consistency equation, following solely from the concavity of $\mathcal F$. Controllability is a bifurcation of the permission variable $c$, whose dynamics include an erosion term and exhibit a saddle-node fold with hysteresis as the gate criterion $\rho^\ast$ crosses unity. Three quantitative results follow: the critical exponent distinguishes families rather than classifying the transition; the gating-cost bound $K(M)\propto\log(1+M)$ grows with scope, not capability; and the fold threshold is $\gamma_c\approx4\mu\kappa$. Calibrated in both directions, the criteria reproduce the two-dimensional Ising transition, admit two true-feedback order parameters, and reject nine candidate quantities, supporting the conclusion that the order parameter is geometric rather than capability-related. Since permission cannot be endogenized and no deployed system has been measured to satisfy $\Gamma>1$ and $\rho^\ast>1$ simultaneously, increased capability does not imply controllability.

papers.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Global structure-from-motion (SfM) commonly refines relative poses on individual image pairs and then estimates global rotations by rotation averaging. Pairwise refinement does not explicitly combine feature-level constraints with multi-view consistency during rotation initialization. We introduce Global Rotations from Aggregated Matches (GRAM), which estimates global rotations directly from initial relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals. GRAM replaces two-view relative-pose optimization and rotation averaging with a single stage. We further extend rotation- only imaging geometry to multiple views and develop Multi-view Optimization with Rotation-only Reprojection Error (MORE) for nonlinear global rotation refinement. Analytical Rotation-guided Translation (ART) derives locally scaled triplet translations from Linear Global Translation (LiGT) constraints and recovers global translations using weighted least squares. Synthetic and real-world experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: MAC+: Mobility-Aware Co-Expansion Planning for Distribution Grid and Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
papers.abstract: We study the least-cost co-expansion of power distribution networks and public charging ports to accommodate the growth of electric vehicles (EVs). Our approach, MAC+, exploits the flexibility of charging along each EV's itinerary and coordinates it across the fleet to reduce the peak violations of each feeder's hosting capacity and port capacity. This coordination is an extremely large, spatio-temporally coupled optimization problem with binary plug-in variables. We solve it by iterated price response (IPR), which repeatedly posts a two-tier tariff on feeder load and port occupancy, lets millions of EVs best-respond in parallel, and certifies the optimality gap at every iteration. We develop a custom exact dynamic-programming algorithm that solves each EV's best-response problem, a mixed-integer quadratic program, about 20 times faster than off-the-shelf solvers. The case study covers the San Francisco Bay Area at 30% EV adoption, with 1.8 million EVs on week-long itineraries and 1,303 feeder service regions, each with a utility-published hosting capacity and a port capacity set by its existing public ports. On this instance, IPR reaches a certified gap below 10% in a few hours. MAC+ saves about $15 billion of the upgrade investment that unmanaged charging would require. It also needs over 90% less investment than charging that is fully coordinated but flexible only within each session, and over 80% less than charging that is flexible along the itinerary but uncoordinated.

papers.title: Efficient Online Submodular Maximization with Bandit Feedback
papers.abstract: We study online monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint with bandit feedback. On each round, the learner selects at most $k$ elements from a ground set of size $n$ and observes only the value of the selected set. We develop an efficient algorithm achieving $O\!\left(k\sqrt{nT\log(n/k)}\right)$ expected $(1-1/e)$-regret over $T$ rounds. To our knowledge, this is the first polynomial-time algorithm with $\sqrt{T}$ dependence on the horizon for arbitrary monotone submodular functions in the bandit setting. Our approach uses randomized sampling and a carefully constructed potential to reduce online submodular maximization to online linear optimization over the probability simplex.

papers.title: Reverberant Speech Conditioning for Material-Aware Acoustic Parameter Mapping
papers.abstract: Dense maps of room acoustic parameters (T30, EDT, C50, DRR) describe how a room sounds at every position. Scene-wide estimation predicts such maps from a floor plan but requires a reference impulse response, which is hard to obtain. Our system instead receives a floor plan and easily recorded reverberant speech from one talker-microphone pair. We compare four speech-derived conditioning inputs: MFCCs, an embedding from the blind estimator BERP, BERP's scalar reverberation-time estimate, and an impulse response reconstructed by Rec-RIR. Our main benchmark is the MRAS dataset, where material assignments vary at fixed geometry. The reconstructed impulse response performs best among the four inputs, reducing T30 error from 31.5% with the floor plan alone to 19.9%, 83% of the reduction achieved by the reference response. We find that adding speech mainly sets the overall level of the map, with little improvement in predicting how the acoustics vary across the room.

papers.title: Improving Confidence Estimation in Language Models with Linear Representations of Ambiguity
papers.abstract: As language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed in downstream applications, accurately estimating their likelihood of success on a given example is critical. However, confidence estimates from LMs are poor predictors of their likelihood of success. Accurate confidence estimation is linked in part to the detection of aleatoric uncertainty; we hypothesize that LMs possess representations of at least some aspects of this uncertainty in the form of representations of the inherent ambiguity of the input. Using difference-in-means on minimal pairs of ambiguous and unambiguous sentences, we derive ambiguity representations in LM activations, and find that steering with them selectively (albeit weakly) modulates LMs' judgments of the input's ambiguity. We then propose DART, a fine-tuning method that encourages updates to lie within the span of the ambiguity directions, and penalizes changes to the LM activations outside of this subspace. DART greatly improves calibration, encodes these improvements into the model parameters, and maintains model accuracy on multiple-choice and generative QA tasks.

papers.title: Integrating Deep PPG Representations and Digital Biomarkers for Aortic Stenosis Detection with Peri-TAVI Assessment
papers.abstract: Access to echocardiography is often limited, delaying recognition of progressive aortic stenosis (AS). A brief, low-cost physiological measurement obtained during routine care could help identify patients who may warrant earlier imaging. Here, we present PulseAS, integrating deep photoplethysmography (PPG) representations, waveform biomarkers and clinical information for high-grade AS screening. Three complementary analyses assessed (1) validation and transfer across cohorts differing in geography and ethnic composition, (2) score-based enrichment of AS and pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) cases, and (3) preoperative and postoperative pulse changes. Using 15-s recordings, separate patient-level cross-validation in EDU (n = 1,209) and MIMIC-III (n = 2,970) yielded AUROCs of 0.818 (PulseAS-XGB) and 0.838 (PulseAS-L2), respectively. In external validation from MIMIC-III to EDU, PulseAS-XGB achieved an AUROC of 0.716, improving to 0.813 after local adaptation. The highest-scoring 10% captured 45.2% of all high-grade AS cases in EDU and 41.3% in MIMIC-III, and 56.9% of pre-TAVI cases in EDU. Notably, in the EDU TAVI subgroup, PPG waveforms showed earlier systolic peaks and narrower systolic contours following intervention. These findings support clinical-PPG risk stratification in new populations and warrant prospective evaluation of echocardiographic prioritisation.

papers.title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
papers.abstract: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the student weigh candidate emotions against it. In Meta-Harness Evolving (MHE), a stronger LLM, the Builder, reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits the harness; static checks and validation gates decide which edits are kept, and the Builder never sees evaluation items. On 5,507 MME-Emotion items, EmoHarness raises task-macro Recognition by 7.6-13.4 points over a single video-only call for all four students and both Builders. Transcripts and prosody descriptions supply most of this boost (+5.38 to +10.71); the scaffold changes the audio-augmented call by -0.79 to +2.54, partly through extra multi-label predictions, and evolved edits add at most +0.95, although no evolved increment survives Holm correction. The harness's emotion context also transfers to IntentQA, with small gains for three of four students, none of which survives correction. EmoHarness thus boosts small multimodal students chiefly by supplying and organizing audio-derived evidence.

authors.name: Fenghai Li
authors.institution: Hebei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
papers.abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=\alpha\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $\Psi''(\alpha)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Clinical Agents: When Dense Rewards Beat Outcome Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards is increasingly used to improve language model reasoning, yet its effects on sequential decision procedures remain poorly understood. We study this problem in clinical multi-turn agents that must decide what information to request, when to stop gathering evidence, and which action to take. We introduce three controlled environments: medication refill triage, acute diagnostic work-up, and dosing titration, each with hidden clinical states, query costs, exact adaptive oracles, and deterministic outcome verifiers. Across these tasks, outcome-only group relative policy optimization often improves aggregate reward while producing undesirable procedures, including premature commitment, one-question collapse, and failures on rare high-risk cases. In diagnostics, assigning dense credit to questions that reduce uncertainty improves held-out value and moderate-case support across three training seeds relative to outcome-only reinforcement learning, without the high-risk seed collapse observed under outcome-only training. Separating exploration from exploitation further increases high-risk support at its best checkpoint, but at the cost of excessive information gathering on low-acuity cases. Additional experiments show that the optimal strength of process credit is task-dependent; that after a supervised warmup that already gathers carefully, reinforcement learning raises aggregate reward by trimming questions while degrading high-risk performance; and that reinforcement learning does not reliably repair rare behavior gaps inherited from biased supervised data. Verifiable final outcomes are therefore insufficient for training reliable multi-turn agents: reward design must account for the procedure used to reach an answer, and evaluation must distinguish adaptive information gathering from reward-exploiting shortcuts.

papers.title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
papers.abstract: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.

papers.title: Stretched near-groups
papers.abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

authors.name: Zhiqiang Yu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Mismeasuring the Life of a Line of Code: Lessons Learned the Hard Way
papers.abstract: Studies of how long lines of code live, including lines written by AI agents, rest on choices that look technical: when a line counts as gone, what to do with lines still alive, whether to pool projects, and how to evaluate a model. We studied 32.5 million line births in 120 TypeScript repositories and got several of these choices wrong at first. For ten of them, we compare the result as we first computed it, or as commonly done, with the result after correction. All ten change conclusions, or would have. Six were our own mistakes. Counting moved and rewritten lines as dead shortens a line's median life from 3.0 years to 1.3. Counting any change as a death hides an outcome that can be predicted: within-project concordance falls from 0.71 to 0.56. Regressing observed lifetimes discards three quarters of the lines. Keeping rewritten lines at risk makes protective effects grow with age. Lines are born and removed together, so treating them as independent misleads twice: nine of fifteen effects look significant only under that assumption, and a split by file makes a barely predictable outcome look good (within-project concordance 0.71 instead of 0.61). After the corrections, removal depends on a line's age and project, but our models could barely rank it within a project. Local revision they could rank (0.71). Obvious cases aside, the top 1% of a project's new lines are revised at 2.3 times the base rate. Each pitfall leaves a symptom; we give a checklist.

papers.title: Peer Memory Changes Who LLM Agents Consult Without a Detected Gain in Answer Accuracy
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems often reuse the same agents across tasks, creating an opportunity to draw on past interactions when deciding whom to consult. We study this form of memory with PeerMem, which saves MACE's LinUCB state and reuses it when the same agents return. Using six agents, a fixed set of 80 HotpotQA questions, and 12 paired lineages per model, we compare cold, warm, and shuffled initialization in an answer-exchange protocol with reference-answer feedback. Under stable evidence access, warm memory lowers pooled hindsight regret and increases consultation of other evidence holders on Qwen3-32B and Gemma-4-31B-it, while final token F1 differences remain uncertain. Qwen interaction traces further show that warm agents more often encounter peer answers that score above their own prior answers. We extend the evaluation to Qwen3.5-9B using freshly learned memory to compare warm and cold initialization under reassigned and paired stable roles. The primary changed-minus-stable final-F1 interaction is -1.38 points, with a 95% interval of [-3.50,+0.73]. Together, these experiments trace the effects of peer memory through consultation, answer revision, and final task performance.

papers.title: Learning to Select Sparse Linear Solvers with Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We investigate convolutional-neural-network (CNN) based automatic solver selection for sparse linear systems, a problem of practical importance where solver performance varies dramatically with matrix sparsity structure. A CNN is trained to regress log timing ratios between candidate solvers using spy plot images of matrix nonzero structure as input, achieving strong prediction accuracy on both held-out SuiteSparse matrices and real-world matrices from high-performance simulation codes.

authors.name: Alan Edelman
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

authors.name: Christopher Rackauckas
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays Derived from a U-Net Segmentation Model
papers.abstract: Pneumonia killed more than 740,000 children under the age of five in 2019, and it can be difficult to recognize on chest radiographs (CXRs): opacities may be faint in early disease, may sit behind the equally bright heart shadow, and may resemble other lung conditions. Most deep learning systems treat pneumonia detection as a yes-or-no classification task. This paper asks whether a model trained on a harder task, segmenting pneumonia pixel by pixel, can be turned into an effective detector for the simpler task of deciding whether an image contains pneumonia at all. The hypothesis is that the detailed supervision of segmentation forces the network to learn where and what the disease looks like, producing a better detector than training for detection alone. A U-Net was trained to segment pneumonia on the RSNA Pneumonia Detection Challenge dataset of 26,684 radiographs, whose rectangular bounding boxes were converted into pixel masks. The data are heavily imbalanced: 22.5% of images are positive, and only 2.6% of pixels fall inside a box, so focal loss with {\alpha} = 0.25 and {\gamma} = 2 and dropout were needed for the model to learn. On the harder segmentation task, the model reached a pixel-level F1 score of 0.45 on a held-out test set of 2,668 images. Applied to the simpler detection task, the same model reached a precision of 0.71, recall of 0.52, and F1 score of 0.60, with 91% specificity, and consistent scores on the development set. These results show that a segmentation-trained model transfers to detection while also showing where the suspected disease is. A direct comparison with a classifier trained only for detection on the same data is needed to confirm whether the segmentation-first approach is better, and is the main direction for future work.

papers.title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
papers.abstract: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, $N$, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with $N$, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in $N$ for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches $95\%$ of that of the same number of independent pores. $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$ scales linearly with pore diameter $d$, and grows with $N$ as $\sim\log N$ for linear arrays and $\sim\sqrt{N}$ for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

papers.title: Superconductivity in the Metallic Wigner Crystals of Rhombohedral Graphene: Possible Realization of an Electronic Supersolid
papers.abstract: Recent experiments on rhombohedral multilayer graphene have reported metallic Wigner crystals (MWCs), in which spontaneously broken translational symmetry coexists with mobile charge carriers. Their proximity to time-reversal-symmetry-breaking superconductivity raises the intriguing possibility that collective excitations of the electron crystal mediate pairing among the residual itinerant carriers, giving rise to a superconducting Wigner crystal---an electronic analog of a supersolid. Here we investigate this possibility using a realistic model of electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene with spin and valley polarization, whose low symmetry removes the usual Cooper instability. We use self-consistent and time-dependent Hartree-Fock theory to map the evolution of the self-doping fraction and characterize the collective-mode spectrum of the MWCs, followed by a multiband linearized Eliashberg analysis of pairing. Upon increasing density, we find an instability of the MWC, triggered by a weakly dispersing unoccupied band approaching the chemical potential. Pairing remains weak deep in the stable MWC. However, on approaching the instability, we identify a collective mode composed of interband electron-hole excitations that softens. We show that this mode drives pairing at experimentally relevant temperatures. The leading pairing instability is at finite momentum and combines Fermi surface states with states in the incipient band, making a Fermi surface or single-band pairing analysis inadequate. Our results establish collective-mode-mediated superconductivity in MWCs as a viable scenario for rhombohedral graphene and motivate experimental searches for coexisting electronic charge order in its superconducting phases.

papers.title: The satisfiability conjecture for random k-SAT formulas. Human-friendly exposition of the recent OpenAI resolution
papers.abstract:
The satisfiability conjecture was one of the most important open problems in discrete probability. It was resolved recently first by Carenini~\cite{GCarenini}, and shortly after by OpenAI~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}, among other 370 problems solved by its internal model. The conjecture concerned the satisfiability property of random instances of the k-SAT problem. It posits the existence of a fixed value for the clause-to-variables ratio around which the probability that the formula is satisfiable drops sharply from nearly one to nearly zero as the ratio increases. While the case of large constant $k$ was resolved a decade ago by Ding, Sly and Sun~\cite{ding2015proof,ding2022proof} using the heavy machinery of the second moment method, the case of general $k$ eluded proof until ~\cite{GCarenini} and~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}.
  In this short note we provide a ''human-friendly'' and detailed exposition of the OpenAI's resolution of the conjecture.

papers.title: Sparse Predict and Demote: Optimal Scheduling with Minimal Size Advice
papers.abstract: Knowledge of job sizes is crucial for optimizing the mean response time in single-server scheduling. However, predictions of job sizes are typically inexact and may be costly to obtain. Thus, a long-standing research question is: what is the minimal information about job sizes required to obtain near-optimal mean response time? We introduce a novel policy, \emph{Sparse Predict and Demote (SPD)}, and prove that it achieves order-optimal mean response time in heavy traffic while requiring only one-bit job-size predictions for a vanishing fraction of arrivals. SPD achieves heavy-traffic order-optimality even in situations when predictions are (i) inexact up to any fixed multiplicative error bound, and (ii) costly, i.e., the server is used to compute predictions and is thus unavailable to serve jobs while processing prediction queries. Finally, we use numerical experiments to illustrate that SPD maintains near-optimal performance beyond the heavy-traffic regime.

authors.name: Chengyi Liu
authors.institution: National Natural Science Foundation of China

papers.title: Policy Over Purpose: Auditing LLM Content Moderation of Reclaimed Slur Usage
papers.abstract: As Perspective API is deprecated, platforms are turning to large language models for content moderation, encoding policy as natural language that the model must interpret at inference time. Reclaimed slurs test this design directly. The same term can express in-group pride or target the community that reclaimed it, and misreading it silences the speech moderation is meant to protect. We audit four general-purpose LLMs and four moderation-specific systems, with Perspective API as a legacy baseline, on IYKYK, a corpus of reclaimed and derogatory usage of three slurs annotated by community members. Across the policy, decision, reasoning, disparity, and steering layers of this audit, we find that whether a system was purpose-built for moderation explains little about how it handles reclaimed language. No system reliably agrees with community judgment, and all fail most on language reclaimed within Black communities. What separates systems is instead how their policy is represented. Only systems whose policy is expressed in the prompt can be steered at all, and even then, explicit definitions change how models justify a decision more than how they make it. We argue that policy transparency determines whether moderation failures can be corrected, but that correcting them requires contextual judgment that definitions supplied at inference time cannot provide.

authors.name: Kai-Wei Chang
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Tuning fluid frictional drag through flow-induced aggregation of wormlike micelles
papers.abstract: Charged amphiphilic surfactants are versatile polymorphic molecules which can form supramolecular structures, such as wormlike micelles. We study the rheology and non-Newtonian fluid dynamics of the cationic surfactant trimethyltetradecylammonium chloride (TTAC) combined with the aromatic counter-ion sodium salicylate (NaSal). In the non-dilute regime, this solution exhibits a linear viscoelastic response consistent with a single-mode Jeffreys model, and in capillary pinch-off experiments, fluid filaments form extended cylindrical threads, indicating strong strain-stiffening. In the dilute regime the linear viscoelasticity and extensional rheology become immeasurably small, but the TTAC/NaSal mixture develops flow-induced structures at high shear rates, as the result of an end-to-end concatenation of micelles produced by shear-induced flow alignment. These flow-induced structures augment both the measured viscosity and the viscous drag in laminar flows at high shear rates (by as much as 50 %). In turbulent Taylor-Couette flow, the flow-induced structures produce a sudden and dramatic destabilizing influence on the stable toroidal Taylor vortices, resulting in upwards of a 200 % enhancement in turbulent drag. However, with increasing Reynolds number, the turbulent flow transitions smoothly to a state of drag reduction, generating up to a 30 % reduction in fluid frictional drag but without the shear-induced degradation that plagues drag reduction strategies based on solutions of high molecular weight polymer, such as polyacrylamide. These results show that surfactants are a unique and effective modifier of fluid frictional drag in both laminar and turbulent flow regimes, capable of producing both significant levels of drag enhancement and drag reduction by tuning the composition and operating conditions.

papers.title: Deploying Physically and Epistemically Compliant Agents by Distilling Belief-Space Task and Motion Planners
papers.abstract: In this work, we train agents to act under uncertainty according to specified, belief-dependent rules. Deep reinforcement learning (RL) can in theory train agents to follow rules if encoded into well-designed rewards, but in practice, RL fails to perfectly optimize these rewards, leading to ineffective or noncompliant agent behavior. Belief-space planners by construction produce behavior in line with developer specification, but require hand-programming online planners and belief-state estimators, adding significant engineering complexity at scale. We combine the two: we plan offline to generate a dataset of sample trajectories and then distill the plans into a policy that acts on raw observations. We propose two changes to planner distillation that address problems specific to history-based policies: Dual Averaging, a loss that combines per-timestep predictive loss and average loss on task changes, and $\rho$-Optimal Reinforcement, a feedback mechanism that reinforces the policy's own successful rollouts when these are near-optimal. We provide a sufficient condition under which static search problems with noiseless observation models is complete, and show that maximum-likelihood-observation planning implies this condition in static search with continuous beliefs. We create a challenging new domain, Scavenger, where an agent needs to gain information in order to succeed. We evaluate our distilled policy in two versions of Scavenger, one where information is provided visually and one where it is provided as a command in natural language. In either case, the learned policy attains a success rate above 90% in Scavenger, compared with at most 5% for RL. We also find that distilled planners transfer with greater than 60% success to following unseen and intentionally vague commands and greater than 75% success to following floorplans larger than those seen in training.

authors.name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Safer for Whom? A Systematic Exploration of AI Safety in Eating Disorder Interactions
papers.abstract: AI assistants advise users about diet, exercise, and weight loss---areas in which unsafe guidance can worsen body dissatisfaction, dietary restriction, compulsive exercise, and other behaviors associated with eating disorders (EDs). Existing evaluations emphasize diagnostic accuracy, overtly harmful prompts, or synthetic scenarios, providing limited insight into whether models recognize implicit vulnerability in natural interactions or protect users consistently. We evaluate responses from three open-weight large language models to 100 questions sourced from an online pro-anorexia community. We grade responses using clinically informed criteria that extend a seven-dimensional taxonomy of ED-related harms. We also construct matched conditions in which questions are accompanied by information about the user varying race, gender, body mass index (BMI), and explicit ED vulnerability. Safety varies substantially across models and harm dimensions. High-risk responses are approximately twice as frequent without bios, suggesting that models do not consistently recognize vulnerability from language alone. Explicit signals of ED vulnerability improve safety by 10--14 points across models. Responses also differ significantly by race, gender, and BMI, with body size producing the largest disparities. These patterns are consistent with reliance on the stereotype that EDs primarily affect thin, White women, potentially leaving users outside this profile with less protective responses.

authors.name: Jinyuan Wang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A General Statistical Framework for Attention and Manipulation Checks
papers.abstract: Attention and manipulation checks are widely used in survey experiments to assess respondents' attentiveness and engagement with treatment, respectively. Yet these checks are subject to measurement error, which may itself depend on treatment when checks are administered after treatment exposure. Restricting analyses to respondents who pass these checks can therefore introduce substantial bias. We propose a general statistical framework for analyzing survey experiments with pre- or post-treatment attention and manipulation checks while accounting for measurement error. We show that three separate checks suffice to identify the proportion of respondents who would be attentive or successfully manipulated under treatment, provided that the checks are conditionally independent among treated respondents given their true, unobserved attentiveness or manipulation status and pre-treatment covariates. Under additional mild assumptions, this result also identifies the average treatment effect among respondents who would be attentive or successfully manipulated under treatment. Building on these identification results, we propose an estimator that allows flexible covariate modeling and establish its asymptotic normality. Applications to framing and digital media literacy experiments demonstrate how accounting for measurement error yields treatment effect estimates that are substantively different from those obtained using conventional approaches.

papers.title: CyberBinGym: Can AI Agents Turn Binary Patches into Real Exploits?
papers.abstract: Security fixes usually reach users as compiled updates, but deployment delays leave unpatched systems exposed. During this window, comparing patched and unpatched binaries can reveal how to exploit a vulnerability, turning a defensive update into actionable information for attackers. Existing benchmarks do not measure this capability: they expose source code, rely on human-crafted challenges, or evaluate binary comprehension without requiring exploitation. We introduce CyberBinGym, a benchmark containing 100 tasks derived from real vulnerabilities in 53 widely used projects, spanning six vulnerability families and three levels of analysis complexity. Agents receive stripped vulnerable and patched binaries without source code or vulnerability information, and must combine static and dynamic analysis to recover and exploit the vulnerability. Evaluation separately measures vulnerability recovery through differential crash testing and end-to-end exploitation through flag retrieval, with trajectory audits to reject reward hacking. The strongest evaluated agent recovers the target vulnerability in 88% of tasks and exploits it in 20%. Providing the patched binary raises its exploit rate from 10% to 25% on a matched 20-task subset; with standard binary hardening enabled, it still exploits two of its 20 previously successful tasks. These results demonstrate that current agents can turn released binary patches into working exploits in a controlled setting, although exploitation remains unreliable. These capabilities lower the barriers to targeting unpatched software and compress defenders' effective response window, increasing the urgency of timely patch deployment.

authors.name: Hongwei Li
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
papers.abstract: We revisit the protocol known as Exponential Shear (ES), first proposed by Doshi and Dealy in 1986. This is a transient strong flow that can be readily imposed in the laboratory using commercial strain-controlled (separate motor and transducer) rheometers which accurately measure both the (exponentially) time-varying torque and normal force exerted by the sample. Numerous studies over the years have proposed competing definitions of an appropriate material function for reporting data obtained from the exponentially time-varying imposed deformation. We revisit this unresolved challenge and carefully reconsider the exponential material kinematics involved and the proper definition of the corresponding material functions. We show that by understanding the time-varying eigenvalues and eigenvectors of both the shearing kinematics and the evolving state of stress in the sample it is, in fact, possible to use an exponential shear test to quantitatively map out \textit{both} the full flow curve (of shear viscosity vs. shear rate) and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve as a function of deformation rate. These findings are supported by numerical simulations of a number of nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, as well as experiments with several polymeric liquids.

papers.title: Gendered Misclassification from Surname-Based Race Imputation
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly estimate political behavior based on race and gender from voter files, where race is imputed from surnames and geography. This only works where surnames suggest group membership, an assumption violated where surnames follow norms around marriage. Imputation is therefore biased against women who adopt their husband's surname, especially those who racially inter-marry, an outcome itself endogenous to partisanship. Using six US states recording self-reported race, I show that imputation is less accurate for Asian and Hispanic women, particularly those sharing the surname of a partner of another race, who differ politically from other women of their race. This violates assumptions behind downstream inference approaches, which nearly double the gender gap in partisanship among Asian voters. I derive an expression showing the bias is largest where a group is small. Using maiden rather than marriage-adopted surnames in North Carolina raises accuracy up to fourfold for women married across racial lines. Recovering maiden surnames, or omitting the married surname, removes much of the bias. In a national replication of a study of gender gaps in turnout, the correction more than triples the gap among Asian voters. In Lebanon, where wives register in their husband's locality, the error enters through geography.

papers.title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
papers.abstract: Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10^10 s^-1, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

papers.title: Is Dark Energy Inhomogeneous?
papers.abstract: The discovery of dark matter deficient galaxies motivates a fundamental question: Could sufficiently large regions of the Universe be deficient in dark energy as well? We investigate this possibility by developing a phenomenological framework that distinguishes genuine dark energy deficiencies from ordinary matter voids through nonlinear expansion, coherent peculiar velocities and density-momentum correlations. We show that a $10\%$ dark energy deficiency can suppress the expansion of a representative nonlinear void by approximately $2.7\%$, generating peculiar velocity residuals of order $60$-$100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ across scales of $30$-$50\, Mpc$. Intriguingly, we find that deficiencies of order $20\%$ extending over several hundred megaparsecs could also influence the locally inferred Hubble constant, potentially contributing to the $H_0$ tension, subject to stringent isotropy and dynamical consistency constraints. We identify observational strategies involving DESI, Rubin, peculiar velocity surveys, and cosmic void catalogues, opening a new avenue for testing whether the dark energy driving cosmic acceleration is truly homogeneous.

papers.title: HARP-Bench: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Around Active Humans
papers.abstract: Recent robot manipulation benchmarks have enabled systematic evaluation of general-purpose robot policies across diverse objects, scenes, instructions, and embodiments. However, most existing benchmarks still assume that the robot is the only active agent and that task semantics are determined primarily by the instruction and object state. This assumption overlooks a common source of real-world variation: humans actively sharing the workspace. In such settings, humans may reveal an implicit goal, complete part of the task, temporarily change object availability, or constrain safe robot motion while working nearby. We introduce HARP-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies in workspaces shared with active humans. HARP-Bench treats human activity as part of the manipulation problem, rather than as background scene variation. It organizes human-present manipulation into four conditions: Cueing, Contribution, Interruption, and Co-presence. These conditions are instantiated through everyday manipulation tasks, including paired human-present variants for controlled comparison with standard manipulation. HARP-Bench also provides a demonstration-generation pipeline for dynamic human-present settings. We evaluate VLA models, imitation-learning methods, and heuristic policies on HARP-Bench. Human-present variations challenge current policies, and higher task success does not consistently improve safety. Quantitative failure analysis identifies manipulation and recovery as the dominant remaining challenges. Training with HARP-Bench demonstrations improves human-present performance in simulation. A real-world study on one task family shows improved performance under human contribution, but not interruption, providing initial evidence of the data's utility and identifying limits of transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/harp.

papers.title: SurgWorld: Learning Surgical Representations Beyond Observation via Latent Prediction
papers.abstract: Surgical procedures are inherently partially observable, requiring surgeons to continuously infer evolving anatomical dynamics and future surgical states beyond the current observation. However, existing self-supervised learning methods primarily learn from observed surgical videos through masked reconstruction or predicting representations within the camera's current field of view, lacking the capability to explicitly model the out-of-sight surgical dynamics. Inspired by latent predictive world models, we introduce SurgWorld, a video-native, self-supervised framework for surgical representation learning, which treats a specified spatial or temporal shift as a pseudo-action and learns to predict the target latent representation from a partial observation. Specifically, we propose Out-of-Sight Dynamics Modeling (OSDM) as the pretraining objective for predicting representations conditioned on relative spatio-temporal shifts. We further regularize the learned latent dynamics from OSDM with a Geometric Visual Similarity (GVS) objective by aligning patch-level relational structures between predicted and target representations, preserving spatial geometry and local visual coherence for dense perception. These two objectives are integrated through an agglomerative training framework that consolidates complementary supervisory signals from multiple teachers to learn a unified latent representation of surgical dynamics and visual geometry. Extensive transfer learning experiments on 17 surgical benchmarks show that SurgWorld consistently outperforms existing vision foundation models across surgical workflow recognition, fine-grained action understanding, and dense visual perception. We further conduct tailored qualitative and quantitative analyses, demonstrating that SurgWorld effectively captures surgical dynamics beyond the directly observed context through latent prediction.

papers.title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
papers.abstract: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/scBIG.

papers.title: Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations
papers.abstract: The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space
papers.abstract: The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.

authors.name: Jing Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Civil Engineering and Architecture

papers.title: Estimating Permeability of Carbonate Rocks from NMR T2 Distribution and Formation Factor Using a Physics-Based Model
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logging provides a nondestructive method for characterizing pore structure and fluid distribution in reservoir rocks. Conventional permeability models, such as the Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) and Timur-Coates (TC) equations, have been widely used to estimate permeability from NMR T2 relaxation time distributions. However, these empirical models require calibration against core-measured permeability, and their fitted coefficients often vary substantially across lithologies and pore systems. In this study, we formulate and evaluate an NMR-informed implementation of a physics-based permeability relationship derived from critical path analysis (CPA) by linking the characteristic pore length scale to the dominant NMR relaxation time. We estimate permeability (k) using NMR T2 distributions and electrical formation factor (F) for 14 carbonate rock samples collected from the Morro do Chaves Formation in the Sergipe-Alagoas Basin, Brazil. We compare the predictive performance of this formulation with that of calibrated SDR and TC models. The proposed CPA-NMR formulation achieves a root mean squared logarithmic error (RMSLE) of 0.56 without calibration against measured permeability from the investigated formation. These findings indicate the potential of combining NMR relaxation measurements with electrical formation factor for physics-based permeability estimation. Further evaluation using independent datasets is needed to assess applicability across formations and lithologies.

authors.name: Behzad Ghanbarian
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

papers.title: GenISys: Integrated Ship Systems Design Using Subsystem-Conditional Tabular Diffussion
papers.abstract: Ship design requires coordinating coupled subsystems to satisfy engineering constraints and balance competing performance and cost objectives. Generative artificial intelligence has supported component design, but integrated ship generation must also account for interactions among hull geometry, structure, propulsion, and operation. This paper presents GenISys, a framework for generating integrated systems, demonstrated through early-stage bulk-carrier design. Its dataset contains 217,999 proposed designs, including 16,247 that satisfy the formulated engineering constraints. The proposed simultaneous conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SCDDPM) generates subsystems together, allowing each subsystem model to respond to changes elsewhere during generation. Experiments compare this approach with monolithic whole-ship generation and sequential subsystem generation across five independent training runs per architecture. In a study targeting lower cost per tonne of cargo transported, designs were generated for a required voyage range of 5,000 nautical miles. SCDDPM produced designs satisfying the formulated engineering constraints and meeting a common low-cost target in 55.70% of generation requests, compared with 51.10% for the monolithic model and 47.54% for the sequential model. These correspond to 9.0% and 17.2% more qualifying designs, respectively, while maintaining similar estimated transport costs. These results show how generative artificial intelligence can coordinate subsystems to generate feasible, high-performing integrated systems.

papers.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
papers.abstract: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. While particle filtering conventionally uses these weights only for state estimation, we also use them to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments in partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation demonstrate improvements in both state estimation and task performance compared to action generation without filtering, using the same pretrained model and no additional test-time information.

papers.title: Doubly-Efficient Private Information Retrieval from Modular Forms
papers.abstract:
We present new information-theoretic protocols for $s$-server, doubly-efficient private information retrieval (PIR) in sublinear server time and one extra bit of space on the servers, for every constant $s \geq 2$. On an $n$-bit database, each of the $s$ PIR servers first builds and stores a preprocessing data structure consisting of $n+1$ bits (which is unique to each server, and after which the server may discard the original database). Then, each server answers a PIR query in time $T_s(n)$, by reading at most $T_s$ bits of its data structure and sending them to the user.
  In the two server setting ($s=2$), our PIR protocols achieve $T_2 = n^{0.82}$, matching the server time of the state-of-the-art schemes of Henzinger and Ragavan (EUROCRYPT 2026) while shrinking their storage from $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ to $n+1$ bits. With $s \geq 3$ servers, our PIR protocols retain the $n+1$ bits of storage and additionally improve on the server time of all prior information-theoretic $s$-server schemes with $n^{1+o(1)}$ storage: for example, achieving $T_3 = n^{0.74}$ and $T_{10} = n^{0.61}$ (previously $n^{0.79}$ and $n^{0.75}$). Asymptotically, as the server count $s$ grows, we shrink the number of servers required to achieve a given server-work exponent from $s^{3.9}$ to $s$.
  Our results draw inspiration from matching-vector techniques (Efremenko, STOC 2009), which we generalize to handle degree-two computations in the exponent. Using this generalization, we build doubly-efficient PIR from the new intermediate abstraction of Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions. Then, we construct such Fourier-sparse cone-delta functions via a connection to modular forms and complex analysis: if a Fourier-sparse cone-delta function does not exist, then there exists a modular form which has too many roots, contradicting the valence formula.

papers.title: A Semiparametric Bayesian Generalized Linear Mixed Model with a Nonparametric Count Distribution for Seizure Data
papers.abstract: Functional count data arise when recurrent events are recorded repeatedly over time and scientific interest centers on how event rates evolve over time and across experimental conditions. Standard mixed effects models for counts have interpretable mean structures but require a parametric conditional distribution, which can be restrictive in the presence of overdispersion, unusual zero frequencies and heavy tails. To address these challenges, we develop the functional count DPGLM (fcDPGLM), a semiparametric Bayesian mixed model that combines GLM-style regression with a nonparametric count distribution. Parametric condition-specific mean trajectories and subject-specific random effects determine the conditional mean exactly, allowing the interpretation of contrasts as usual, while remaining details of the count distribution are learned nonparametrically from the data. Poisson and negative-binomial mixed models are recovered as limiting cases. A gamma completely random measure representation allows for efficient posterior simulation. In simulations mimicking a rat seizure study, fcDPGLM estimated mean contrasts as accurately as a correctly specified negative-binomial mixed model, and more accurately otherwise, and recovered zero and exceedance probabilities that the parametric models misrepresent. In the seizure study, seizure rates rise and then decline in the early period after induced status epilepticus but remain high and nearly flat in the chronic period, and rats differ substantially. Poisson and negative-binomial mixed models estimate similar mean trajectories and period contrasts, but only fcDPGLM matches the observed zero frequency, variance and high-burden days.

authors.name: Entejar Alam
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Attention Is Only as Good as Its Witnesses: When Higher-Order Layers Help, and When They Do Not
papers.abstract: Transformers stop learning graph search as graphs grow, and learn the card game SET only after many distinct questions, although attention can represent both. We read these failures, and the uneven record of higher-order attention, from what a layer sums over: each layer we study computes the partition function of a family of witnesses and reads it at a temperature. Two laws follow. The depth law is a known result of logic, which we state for these layers: L layers over two-step walks reach exactly 2^L - 1 steps, just as a logical statement with L nested clauses of the form "there is a vertex such that" sees exactly that far. We build a construction that reaches this far, checked in Lean, and, when vertices carry no names, no such network reaches further. The size law is the cost of reading at a temperature, which logic does not have: existence is read correctly at every size, in the worst case, if and only if inverse temperature times margin is at least the logarithm of the number of candidates. Layers built on these laws, and on two principles that we test, learn where Transformers fail. One propagator layer trained on 49-vertex graphs answers every question at every search depth on 250-vertex graphs. Given the modulus 3, exponential Newton computes the softmax of 2-simplicial attention over pairs exactly in 3^d n operations for d clocks; with six clocks it learns SET from as few deals as 2-simplicial attention and transfers from 8- to 20-card tables. On CLRS-30 without hints, a 186,000-parameter block of OR-join and power-mean channels matches (within half a point) or beats a model of at least 73 million parameters on 9 of 12 graph tasks of the official test set, and on 8 of 12 with freshly drawn test graphs. The same account explains where pair layers did not help and where parallel layers must loop.

papers.title: HyInv Technical Report
papers.abstract: Inverse folding designs amino-acid sequences for a given protein backbone, and screening needs many candidates that are both diverse and well folded. We present HyInv, a 1.96-million-parameter backbone-conditioned graph network with an encoder-decoder architecture, trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team: pretrained with random-order autoregressive sequence modeling, followed by structure-reward reinforcement learning. At inference, a grouped draft-and-rewrite sampler that uses separate draft and rewrite temperatures improves refolding TM-score at matched diversity. An optimized implementation with BF16 numerics designs 128 sequences for a 402-residue backbone in 50.6 ms on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, about 52 times faster than the reference sampler, and an exact FP32 path that returns the reference sequences is 8.7 times faster. Across five benchmark datasets and seven dataset-predictor combinations, HyInv reaches a higher average scTM than all ten external baselines at comparable or higher sequence diversity, with large margins over ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2. The same default setting supports de novo backbones, pocket-constrained libraries, enzyme redesign with the catalytic site kept, and loop redesign. We have released our code and model at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hyra-results/tree/main/AI4Science/hyinv.

papers.title: HyPLM Technical Report
papers.abstract: Protein language models (PLMs) are standard tools for variant-effect prediction, protein annotation and design, but the compute needed to train and serve them keeps growing. We present HyPLM-Flash, an efficient and open PLM trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team. HyPLM-Flash is a 650-million-parameter masked language model trained on 726 billion tokens, 0.73 times the data of ESM-2 650M and a fifth to an eighth of the data of E1-600M and ESM C 600M. It runs on an inference engine with fused kernels and INT8 matrix multiplication, embedding about 130,000 residues per second on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other 600M-class encoders.
