papers.title: On the Seven-particle Clusters of Lennard-Jones and Thomson
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we develop a graph-geometric framework and prove that the pentagonal bipyramid (PBP) is the unique global minimiser of both the seven-particle Lennard-Jones energy in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the seven-charge Thomson energy on $S^2$, up to rigid symmetries and particle relabelling. For the Thomson problem, this strengthens a recent deterministic global-optimality certificate to numerical tolerance into an exact global-optimality and uniqueness theorem. A weak-interaction graph, defined by thresholding pair geometry, organises configuration space without imposing symmetry or discarding any pair interaction. For Lennard-Jones, pair-energy counting, graph classification, subset bounds, and force balance reduce all possible minimisers to 29 bounded domains; exact geometric certificates exclude 28, localise the survivor near the PBP, and a uniform restoring-energy estimate proves uniqueness. The Thomson proof follows the same progression: graph reduction, geometric localisation, and rigidity, but finalises through whole-domain coercivity and a global localisation theorem. The same fivefold order therefore emerges in two very different physical settings: an unconstrained cluster with a preferred bond length and purely repelling charges confined to a sphere, showing a common geometric organising principle for seven particles that is not tied to either interaction.

papers.title: Finite-amplitude wave dynamics in weak-field-equivalent nonlinear electrodynamics in $(2+1)$ dimensions
papers.abstract: We examine finite-amplitude wave propagation in $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics using Born-Infeld, logarithmic, and quadratic polynomial models whose Lagrangians agree through quadratic order in the electromagnetic invariant. Despite this weak-field agreement, characteristic and linearized analyses on homogeneous magnetic background reveal distinct propagation speeds and hyperbolicity domains. In the weak-background limit, the first coefficient at which Lagrangians differ also controls the leading nonlinear variation of the simple-wave characteristic velocity. Exact right-moving simple-waves, corroborated by finite-volume evolution, show rigid Born-Infeld propagation but finite-time gradient catastrophes in the logarithmic and polynomial models, substantially earlier in the latter for matched pulses. These catastrophes can occur while the field remains finite and the system remains hyperbolic, showing that weak-field agreement does not determine finite-amplitude dynamics.

authors.name: M. L. Penafiel
authors.institution: Universidade do Estado do Rio de Janeiro

authors.name: E. Veneros
authors.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza

papers.title: Modeling the Joint Distribution of Box Score Statistics: A Gaussian Copula Approach
papers.abstract: What is the probability that LeBron James records at least 27 points, 7 rebounds, and 7 assists tonight? While an interesting statistical question by itself, the rise of sports betting and multi-leg parlays has made answering this question increasingly relevant. However, coming up with an estimated likelihood is tricky, since box score statistics aren't independent. We estimate the joint probability that a player reaches a combination of thresholds in points, assists, and rebounds using a Gaussian copula, fit separately for each player using only their previous games. We compare it with two benchmarks: the product of the empirical marginal probabilities (i.e. assuming independence) and the empirical frequency of the joint event. Across ~22,000 player-observations, the Gaussian copula performs on par or better than either benchmark at lower threshold levels, with large gains at high joint exceedance levels. Because it is generative, the model also allows for probabilistic calculations for combinations that a player has rarely or never produced.

papers.title: Curvature estimates for stable hypersurfaces of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional
papers.abstract: A hypersurface $\Sigma \subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_\alpha(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma|x|^\alpha\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. In this paper, we first establish a Bellettini-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem and use it, together with tangent cone analysis, to derive curvature estimates for EDH-stable hypersurfaces with $2\leq n \leq 6$.

papers.title: Zero-Shot VLA Adaptation with Retrieved Guidance
papers.abstract: Pre-training large parametric "Vision-Language-Action" (VLA) models on large demonstration datasets has recently yielded promising results for general-purpose manipulation. However, these models still struggle under even small domain shifts relative to the training data, such as changes in camera viewpoint, background, object identity, or robot morphology. Motivated by the success of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in language models, we pursue retrieval to boost VLA performance. Specifically, we seek to leverage retrieval from domain-mismatched, "in-the-wild" demonstration datasets like DROID to guide a VLA's behavior in a new target domain. To achieve this, we introduce RAGu, which overcomes robotics-specific challenges for RAG: (1) It incorporates simple geometric calibration to transform source demonstrations into the target setup and reduce cross-domain differences. (2) It uses a coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy that selects, from a large pool of pre-warped candidates, the trajectory most compatible with the base VLA. (3) It guides the VLA's flow-matching inference procedure rather than seeking to retrain the base model or expand its limited context window. We evaluate RAGu across real-world, simulation, sim-to-real transfer, and cross-embodiment humanoid manipulation. We find it improves real-world VLA success rates from 20% to 80% and outperforms the closest-related baselines in sim. Project website: raguvla.github.io

authors.name: Anh-Quan Pham
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options
papers.abstract: Options market makers absorb client order flow and must hedge the resulting inventory risk under trading frictions. We study whether an option hedging reinforcement learning (RL) agent trained on historical market data outperforms three alternatives in tail-risk protection: (i) traditional delta hedging, (ii) simple hedge-ratio rules, and (iii) the same agent trained in simulated markets. Most RL hedging agents are trained in model-generated markets that do not capture the crashes and volatility regimes present in real data. We introduce an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and compare against a matched geometric Brownian motion (GBM) environment, a stochastic-volatility (SABR) simulator, and a hybrid that values historical paths with Black-Scholes, all sharing the same portfolio mechanics, stochastic arrivals, costs, and test period. We train a distributional Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent and evaluate it out of sample over 2018-2023. The agent trained on empirical data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) tail loss by 3.1% compared to delta hedging and outperforms every hedge-ratio rule chosen during the training period and every alternative training environment. The reduction reaches 8.9% in volatile and falling markets, but reverses to a cost of 7-10% in rising markets. Empirical training induces a state-dependent short net delta: the policy under-hedges negative-delta books, most strongly after prices have fallen. This tilt disappears with GBM training and is weaker with SABR or hybrid training. These findings suggest that exposure to historical market dynamics can materially change a tail-risk hedging policy, although the evidence rests on a single test path and the edge is regime-conditional.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Tokenization Framework for Voxel-Level fMRI Representation Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce HBAR (Hierarchical Brain Activity Representation), a hierarchical tokenization framework for learning compact, multi-scale representations of neuroimaging data. HBAR organizes voxel-level resting-state fMRI into a hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels, and large-scale functional networks, enabling up to 415x compression while preserving fine-grained spatial information beyond conventional parcellation. The framework supports fixed atlas-based, fully learned, and softly prior-guided hierarchies, allowing us to systematically study the role of structured priors in brain representation learning. On HCP-YA, at approximately 415x compression, HBAR achieves higher parcel and network correlations than rate-matched flat tokenizers, while at a lower 52x compression rate, shuffling the anatomical grouping reduces parcel correlation from 0.920 to 0.886. Demographic readouts with autoregressive training also reveal potential gains from the hierarchical structure. By combining sub-parcel inputs, compact discrete tokens, and multiscale brain structure, HBAR offers a practical framework for representation learning in high-dimensional neuroimaging data.

papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization
papers.abstract: This work presents a 65 nm SoC for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation. The SoC performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator is developed, featuring a memory reuse technique to efficiently process long kernels required for low-frequency EEG feature extraction. A runtime dynamic quantization is incorporated, reducing model size by 3.88 times with only a 0.28% loss in accuracy. A sensitivity of 98.3% is achieved for deep sleep detection, enabling effective sleep modulation.

authors.name: Yaqian Xu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xilin Liu

papers.title: When Are Nearby Experts Composable? Cross-Task Model Merging in Neural Thickets
papers.abstract: Random perturbations around a shared checkpoint can produce experts for distinct tasks, but shared origin does not ensure that their gains survive composition. We formulate expert-pair selection for joint base-relative retention, measured by strict joint success and worst-task gain with unconditional abstention accounting. An exact finite-difference decomposition and an arbitrarily small orthogonal counterexample show why proximity and orthogonality alone are insufficient. We instantiate this formulation with quality-constrained spectral selection, a fixed-budget framework combining cross-task screening, layerwise pair geometry, separate validation, and Base fallback. Across six checkpoints, 21 task pairs, and five independent perturbation pools, the procedure improves strict joint success over Top-1 averaging throughout and leads the four-method model-scale comparison on four of six checkpoints. For the five models with at least 1.5B parameters, matched quality-only, global-cosine, and spectral ranking attain 49.1%, 50.5%, and 53.1% joint success. Under this matched protocol, the spectral selector also yields the highest worst-task gain and Weak Pareto rate and the lowest regression rate. Mean worst-task gain reaches +0.61 percentage points, while 17.1% regression and 13.0% abstention show that composability remains conditional. Project page: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Thickets-Merge/.

papers.title: TLRS-DPO: Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a simple and widely used alternative to RLHF for aligning large language models (LLMs), but its sequence-level objective cannot precisely locate or suppress the local patterns that make an otherwise acceptable response unsafe or undesirable. We propose TLRS-DPO (Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization), which augments DPO with fine-grained token-level control while remaining fully offline and reference-based. TLRS-DPO introduces a token-level robust compensation term that converts the policy-reference log-ratio on rejected responses into localized risk scores, a curriculum-style schedule that gradually increases the strength of this compensation during training, and a risk-adaptive screening mechanism that selectively penalizes only high-risk tokens instead of entire sequences. This design bridges sequence-level preference fitting and token-level behavior control, and can be implemented as a drop-in modification to standard DPO trainers. Empirically, TLRS-DPO improves alignment quality and safety-relevant behavior with minimal impact on helpfulness compared to strong DPO baselines.

papers.title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
papers.abstract: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincar\'e disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $\chi$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6\chi$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

papers.title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: Single-loop minimax methods are appealing for modern machine learning, but standard stochastic gradient updates can be unstable and oscillatory under tightly coupled primal-dual dynamics, making performance notoriously sensitive to stepsizes. To fundamentally improve stability, we develop an orthogonal update framework tailored to minimax optimization, which applies updates along orthogonalized directions to reduce update anisotropy. However, orthogonalization reshapes the optimization geometry and makes coordinating primal-dual stepsizes even more delicate. To overcome this challenge, we develop AdaSGDA, which equips orthogonal updates with an adaptive stepsize rule driven by accumulated gradient norms. This mechanism automatically balances coupled primal-dual progress under orthogonalization, yielding an effectively parameter-free method for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization. We prove that AdaSGDA avoids problem-dependent tuning while attaining the state-of-the-art $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/4}\right)$ convergence rate. We further propose AdaSGDA-VR, which incorporates a carefully designed variance reduction scheme and achieves the faster $\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-1/3}\right)$ rate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methods deliver competitive performance compared to existing minimax optimization methods.

papers.title: CHO-Bench: How Do Context Hints Affect Ad Rankings in LLM Advertising?
papers.abstract: LLM advertising selects advertisements based on user conversations, where user needs may extend beyond explicit product searches. ChatGPT Ads allows advertisers to provide natural-language context hints describing what they offer, who may find it useful, and when it may be useful, as additional information for ranking advertisements across diverse user conversations. However, how to effectively construct these hints remains unclear. We formulate Context Hint Optimization (CHO) as the problem of constructing context hints to improve an advertisement's ranking under a given budget. Drawing on established marketing frameworks, we develop seven context hint generation strategies covering What, Who, and When, along with a Unified strategy that combines all seven dimensions. We introduce CHO-Bench and conduct over 1.19 million paired evaluations across five datasets using embedding-based and LLM-based rankers. Our results show that context hints improve advertisement rankings under the evaluated offline rankers. While individual strategies achieve similar average gains and Unified offers no consistent advantage, strategy differences become more pronounced under specific generation-ranking configurations, with embedding-based and LLM-based rankers favoring different information dimensions. Increasing the hint budget further improves rankings with diminishing marginal gains. These findings establish an offline benchmark for studying ad-side ranking optimization in LLM advertising and highlight opportunities for model-specific hint selection and budget-aware generation and aggregation.

papers.title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
papers.abstract: Direct numerical simulations examine the phase-dependent turbulence dynamics of pipe flow driven by cardiac-cycle-inspired waveforms. Four cases with and without a low-flow plateau span two Reynolds-number ranges. The response follows four stages of turbulent--turbulent reorganisation. Strong acceleration suppresses transverse fluctuations and vortical activity. During acceleration and early deceleration, streamwise-normal-stress production recovers ahead of pressure--strain redistribution and radial momentum transport, allowing energy to accumulate in elongated streaks. In early deceleration, near-wall high-speed streaks develop predominantly varicose disturbances associated with Q4 sweeps, whereas outer-buffer-layer low-speed streaks develop predominantly sinuous disturbances associated with Q2 ejections. The transition exhibits distinct radial sequences: Q2-based local onset occurs progressively later towards the wall, whereas Q4-based onset is nearly simultaneous across the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, with peaks occurring successively outwards. The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies markedly and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs this decay and weakens the turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage. It further delays local instability and lengthens the onset-to-peak intervals of the shear contributions. An unsteady friction decomposition links these phase-dependent dynamics to the drag response, highlighting the role of delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.

authors.name: Yan Bao
authors.institution: Shaanxi University of Science and Technology

papers.title: TrialDesignBench: Benchmarking Language Models for Phase-I Trial Design Against Clinical Knowledge
papers.abstract: AI is used in much of the clinical trial pipeline. However, selecting the statistical design of a trial, a crucial step that determines how drug doses are tested on humans and evaluated, has seen almost no AI progress. LLMs appear to be a natural fit given their strengths in biomedical knowledge and statistical reasoning. Nevertheless, there is currently no appropriate way to evaluate such abilities because recent regulatory and methodological shifts, most notably FDA's Project Optimus, have redefined what constitutes a reasonable design and rendered many previous designs obsolete. To lay the groundwork for AI-assisted trial design, we introduce TrialDesignBench, a benchmark of 617 Phase-I/I-II oncology dose-finding trials, each paired with an expert-validated reference design that is consistent with the latest FDA regulatory initiatives. This reference standard is produced through a formalization of the expert design process. We evaluate five frontier LLMs, none of which matches the reference standard. Our ablation experiments trace this performance gap to two main causes, inference of latent, unrecorded design determinants from trial sources (supplying them raises class-wise balanced accuracy by 0.22) and structured decision-tree reasoning (+0.24). TrialDesignBench offers a reproducible, contemporary-standard objective for evaluating and enhancing AI-assisted trial design.

authors.name: Ying Yuan
authors.institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

papers.title: Multi-Agent Screening: What Agreement and Acceptance Cannot Tell You
papers.abstract: When AI agents screen items for a costly human assessor, as in agentic search, e-discovery and AI reviewing of papers, only what they pass gets judged. We show what each kind of evidence can establish about their errors, even with unlimited data. Agreement shows that agents concur, not that they are right, however many there are. Acceptance by the assessor gives precision but only a lower bound on recall. Knowing which agents found which relevant items gives an upper bound on recall if agents' finds are not negatively correlated, and caps what one more agent can add if agents are interchangeable. Without assumptions about the agents, recall can be pinned down only by judging items they did not pass: a random sample of these estimates how many relevant items were missed, to any chosen accuracy, and the sample needed does not grow with the number of agents.

papers.title: On the higher-order Titchmarsh divisor problem
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $k\geq2$ and every fixed nonzero integer $h$, we prove that, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{x<n\leq2x}\Lambda(n)\tau_k(n+h) \sim C_{k,h}x(\log x)^{k-1}, \end{equation*} where $\tau_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function and $C_{k,h}>0$ is a constant depending only on $k$ and $h$.

papers.title: Update Slope Is Bounded by Prior Calibration: A Structural Bound and Its Contingent Empirical Signature
papers.abstract: Evaluations of LLM forecasters increasingly measure how forecasts improve as richer evidence is supplied. We identify two confounds in this update-slope metric. First, outcome-aware evidence construction substantially inflates measured responsiveness: on the same models and questions, slopes are roughly four times larger than with resolution-blinded evidence ladders. Second, update slope is a change score with a prior-dependent structural ceiling, so raw comparisons can reflect differences in starting calibration rather than updating behavior. The ceiling defines only a feasible region; whether slope and prior calibration are empirically coupled depends on headroom utilization and varies across our Manifold, ForecastBench, and ACLED pools. Despite this variability, conditioning on prior calibration roughly triples the association between intermediate updating and final Brier score under both blinded and outcome-aware construction. Question identity also explains substantially more variance than model identity across the evaluated pools. We recommend building evidence ladders blind to outcomes, conditioning on prior calibration, and reporting headroom-normalized measures alongside raw slopes.

papers.title: Two-Sided Conformal Evidence Sets for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can surface passages that support a claim, contradict it, or fail to address it, yet existing calibrated grounding methods are typically one-sided and model only supporting evidence. We introduce Conformal Evidence Sets (CES), a two-sided framework that returns separate support and refutation sets with finite-sample inclusion coverage of at least $1-\alpha$ on each side under exchangeability; a Bonferroni union yields joint coverage of at least $1-2\alpha$. On labeled candidate pools from the contrastive VitaminC benchmark, CES closely tracks nominal coverage across $\alpha\!\in\!\{0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20,0.30\}$, with maximum deviations of $3.0$ percentage points for support and $5.4$ for refutation, and reaches essentially the same empirical coverage--size frontier as a test-tuned fixed-threshold heuristic without any test exposure. Stress tests mark the boundary of that guarantee: under FEVER distribution shift both sides under-cover, by up to $12.7$ percentage points, and support-side group-stratified recalibration substantially reduces the support gap. Scorer swaps, hard-negative retrieval, cross-dataset transfer, and a live end-to-end pilot expose a clear separation: when exchangeability holds and relevant evidence is retrieved, evidence inclusion remains calibrated even with an imperfect scorer, whereas the support/refute verdict tracks scorer quality directly. Calibrated evidence coverage and reliable verdicts are therefore distinct properties and should be reported separately.

papers.title: A liquid implant that grows into a stable scaffold in situ
papers.abstract: Endovascular embolization requires materials that can pass through narrow microcatheters yet form stable, conformal occlusions within irregular vascular lesions, but reconciling these competing requirements remains challenging. Here we report a wirelessly activated liquid precursor whose final architecture is constructed only after target localization. A gallium-based liquid metal containing iron microparticles and gas microcavities remains deformable, magnetically navigable, and retrievable before activation. Wireless induction heating activates the internal reactive microenvironment, coupling gas-driven microcavity growth with oxidative mineralization of newly generated gallium interfaces to form a porous, self-supporting scaffold. In aneurysm and arteriovenous malformation models, activation enabled durable occlusion, aneurysm-neck healing, and six-month stability in a porcine aneurysm model. These findings establish post-delivery construction as a strategy for creating stable therapeutic implants from minimally invasive liquid precursors.

authors.name: Lin Zhu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Shuang Wang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Yuan An
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology - Beijing

authors.name: Hongzhang Wang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Coal Mine Disaster Dynamics and Control

papers.title: TrialJev: Open-Weight Single Pass Eligibility Scoring for Patient Trial Screening
papers.abstract: Clinical trial screening requires assessing large numbers of patient-trial pairs to prioritize candidates for detailed eligibility review, often under restrictions on sharing patient records. We introduce TrialJev, an open-weight eligibility scorer that uses LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head to score natural-language answer options in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding. Trained on TREC Clinical Trials 2021 and evaluated on 6,975 eligible-or-excluded pairs from 50 unseen TREC 2022 synthetic patients, TrialJev achieves 80.97% (Qwen3.5-27B) and 81.84% (Qwen3.8-27B) accuracy, compared with 79.87% and 79.93% for LLMs fine-tuned on the same data to generate verdicts. In matched batch-1 measurements, verdict generation takes 2.45-2.70 times as long as the one-pass inference of TrialJev at 9B-27B. Under a common development-fitted decision correction, the two 27B TrialJev models reach 80.99% and 81.88% accuracy, compared with 81.28% for the proprietary hosted Jev API; paired confidence intervals include zero. TrialJev runs locally on a single GPU, requiring approximately 178 ms per pair at 27B, without transmitting patient text to an external model API. An A/B-logit ablation shows that avoiding decoding, rather than the pointer head alone, accounts for the measured efficiency advantage. TrialJev is intended for first-pass prioritization of candidate trials, complementing rather than replacing explanatory models and clinical review. Evaluation is limited to synthetic patients and implementation-specific timing, and clinical use has not been validated. Adapters, pointer heads, and model cards are released on Hugging Face.

papers.title: Spiking Sensory Networks
papers.abstract: Effective sensory reception is critical for survival, yet the computational mechanisms behind how peripheral sensory neurons (SNs) transduce external signals into spiking representations for downstream brain circuits remain to be fully understood. Numerous theoretical frameworks have been proposed to model sensory processing, with Bayesian approaches among the most prominent. However, existing machine learning attempts to apply Bayesian theory to spiking neurons remain largely phenomenological, disconnected from empirical biology, and poorly validated on non-stationary temporal data. Conversely, neuroscientific models often rely on strong inductive experimental biases or explicit kinetic dynamics fit post hoc to match spiking data. Here, we introduce a class of recurrent Poisson VAE models, termed Spiking Sensory Networks (SSNs), that bridge these paradigms by reconciling variational inference with biologically inspired spike transduction for time-varying stimuli. Evaluated on real-world odor plume recordings from locust olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs), SSNs match or exceed the reconstruction fidelity of Spiking Neural Network (SNN) and GLM baselines while exhibiting superior representational characteristics. Furthermore, SSNs are well-suited for neuroscientific investigation, learning empirical in vivo ORN response motifs and exhibiting emergent spike-frequency adaptation under unsupervised reconstruction without manual tuning. Moreover, we theoretically link the recurrent decoding objective to mutual information maximization, and derive a formal thermodynamic lower bound connecting the Poisson Kullback-Leibler regularizer to the excess non-equilibrium metabolic power of biophysical homeostasis. Ultimately, our work synthesizes principles from machine learning theory and empirical neuroscience, providing a viable bridge that concretizes Bayesian models with biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Reason First, Retrieve What Matters: Hypothesis-Guided Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long video understanding requires models to identify and reason over sparse, temporally distributed evidence within limited frame budgets. Existing keyframe selection methods typically retrieve query-relevant frames from a densely sampled candidate set before inference. However, global image-text matching incurs unnecessary computation when a small set of uniformly sampled frames already provides sufficient evidence. Query relevance alone may also overlook evidence that distinguishes competing answers, while one-shot selection offers no opportunity to correct earlier selection errors. We propose HypoKFS, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples keyframe selection with iterative inference by multimodal large language models (MLLMs). HypoKFS first reasons over sparsely sampled frames to construct an initial hypothesis space. The resulting answer distribution determines whether additional frame selection is needed. When needed, the retained hypotheses guide the selection of discriminative frames, followed by renewed inference and hypothesis refinement. This iterative process directs additional visual computation toward unresolved hypotheses while avoiding unnecessary global frame matching. Experiments on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple MLLM backbones. HypoKFS improves accuracy by up to 6.7 percentage points and achieves 72.9% accuracy on Video-MME at only 1.3% of the reference frame-hypothesis matching cost.

authors.name: Junbo Wang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: PLS-GS: Probabilistic Lidar Scaffolds for Compact, Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is typically optimized from images only, many robotics and mapping applications provide both camera and high-definition LiDAR data, combining rich visual appearance with accurate geometric structure. We introduce PLS-GS, a probabilistic LiDAR scaffold for Gaussian Splatting that exploits this complementary sensing setting to construct a compact 3DGS representation aligned to the measured surface. PLS-GS fits a Hierarchical Gaussian Mixture Model jointly over position and color, yielding a continuous and adaptive scaffold that eliminates the need for discrete scene partitioning such as voxel grids or octrees. The fitted mixture then guides the renderable 3DGS Gaussians: each rendering Gaussian is associated with a GMM component and constrained in the local surface frame induced by that component's covariance. A Mahalanobis support loss bounds the deviation of the rendering Gaussians from the corresponding LiDAR-derived surface. Across five large outdoor scenes, PLS-GS places primitives markedly closer to the LiDAR measurements than both image- and LiDAR-initialized baselines, while employing substantially fewer primitives, yielding a considerably more compact model and faster rendering. At matched capacity, PLS-GS places primitives closer to the LiDAR measurements, with comparable rendering quality. Code is available at https://github.com/k-harikumar/PLS-GS.

papers.title: STAR-VF: Spatio-Temporal Aware Representation Condensation for Data-Efficient Video Fusion
papers.abstract: Video fusion aims to integrate complementary cues from heterogeneous sources, producing visually informative videos with coherent spatio-temporal structures. Jointly learning cross-modal complementarity and temporal dependencies typically relies on large-scale, high-quality video datasets, whose storage and repeated use during optimization incur substantial costs, making data-efficient learning highly desirable. To address this challenge, we rethink video fusion from the perspective of dataset condensation and propose STAR-VF, the first framework that condenses spatio-temporal representations for data-efficient video fusion. STAR-VF condenses the original training set into a compact set of learnable spatio-temporal representations, which are decoded into synthetic video clips and optimized using feature-level supervision provided by a frozen proxy model. The resulting condensed data preserves fusion-relevant spatial and temporal cues without requiring ground-truth fused videos as supervision. To adapt fusion learning to condensed representations, we equip the final fusion model with flow-free inter-frame temporal modeling and query-driven intra-frame aggregation, enabling direct temporal interaction and adaptive selection of fusion-relevant information in representation space. Extensive experiments on infrared-visible, multi-exposure, multi-focus, and medical video fusion benchmarks demonstrate that STAR-VF, trained with only approximately 1/16 of the original temporal training set, achieves fusion quality comparable to methods trained on the full data. Further analyses validate the contributions of learned condensation and flow-free temporal modeling, and demonstrate the robustness of the condensed supervision across different proxy encoders and downstream fusion models. Project page: https://zju-xyc.github.io/STAR-VF-Project-Page/.

papers.title: MPSi: Neural Extraction of Site-Specific Multipath Propagation Properties for Massive MIMO
papers.abstract: Accurate extraction of site-specific multipath propagation properties enables a wide range of wireless applications, including initial access, wideband channel reconstruction, and the generation of channel datasets for learning-based and continual-learning systems. Classical parametric channel-sounding algorithms such as RIMAX provide physically interpretable estimates, but their data-dependent model-order selection and iterative nonlinear refinement introduce substantial delay and computational cost. This paper proposes MPSi, a physics-guided neural framework that replaces these costly stages with a compact path-count network and a fixed-depth, deep-unfolded Levenberg-Marquardt refinement. MPSi estimates the complex gain, angle of arrival, and propagation delay of each multipath component while preserving the underlying physical channel model. We evaluate MPSi in two site-specific ray-traced environments, a small cell and a dense urban area, and show that it achieves initial-access and full-channel-estimation performance comparable to an enhanced RIMAX baseline while requiring significantly fewer optimization iterations. The reconstructed channels also yield bit-error-rate performance close to the perfect-channel knowledge reference. These results position MPSi as a promising low-overhead framework for extracting multipath propagation properties in massive-MIMO systems and for generating cell-specific channel pseudo-labels for training when direct ground-truth measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: GradReason: LLMs as Meta-Learners that Replace Training Epochs with Training-Data-Free Weight Updates
papers.abstract: Standard training recipes make a fixed number of passes over the training data, even when an epoch mostly adds mini-batch noise. We study whether a large language model (LLM) that reads the weight and gradient history of a run can replace some of these epochs with updates that compute no gradient and read no training image. In GradReason, an LLM agent is called every ten epochs. In a restricted sandbox, it analyses recent weight snapshots, epoch-mean gradients, and validation metrics, then submits a Python program that computes new weights and a plan marking each of the next ten epochs as data or virtual. A virtual epoch is kept only if it passes a forward-only check on 5,000 held-out validation images. In 120 runs on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with three architectures, Claude Opus 5.5 used 32.8% fewer data epochs than the 80-epoch recipe at 0.31 percentage points lower test accuracy (95% CI -0.72 to +0.09; 0.94 points on ResNet-18), on the recipe's own frontier of data against accuracy. Unprompted, Opus averaged recent weight snapshots in every run. This choice produced the savings: a fixed rule with the same acceptance check but extrapolations from prior work saved 5.4% of the data epochs, and the same rule with averaging added saved 25.0%. The LLM's contribution is to find a working update within a single run; once found, a fixed rule implements it equally well. An Opus run cost 0.68 USD, but at this scale the agent's latency exceeded the GPU time it saved.

papers.title: PIA: Agentic Physics-Informed Runtime Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Runtime anomaly detectors for cyber-physical systems are either learned as black boxes from normal data, which miss stealthy manipulations that keep every signal inside its normal range, or derived by hand from physical models, which requires expert effort for every plant. We introduce physicsinformed agents (PIA), in which a large language model agent writes the detector itself as a set of physical residuals, such as pump characteristics, tank mass balances, and controller logic, and refines every candidate against normal operating data through an evaluation workbench before deployment. The result is a compact, human-readable detector that runs in milliseconds and names the component behind each alarm. On the BATADAL water distribution attack benchmark, PIA with Claude Opus 5.5 reaches an F1 of 0.878 on the test attacks against 0.504 for the strongest of six statistical and deep baselines, keeps detecting attacks concealed by replayed and offset sensor readings, and attributes every detected test attack to the attacked component. Ablations show that testing hypotheses against data is decisive: agents that write residuals from the plant description alone lose up to 0.28 F1, whereas agents that see only anonymized signals recover most of the physical structure.

papers.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Large-Angle Structures
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.

authors.name: Tianyu Zhao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Ming Lei
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A Large-Scale Dataset for Cross-Lingual Multi-Jurisdiction Patent Drafting from Patent Cooperation Treaty Applications
papers.abstract: Securing patent protection across countries requires drafting claims separately for each national patent office, in the relevant language and according to its legal and stylistic conventions. Patent claims can therefore differ across languages and jurisdictions because of translation, target-office drafting practices, and prosecution-stage changes. We formulate cross-lingual patent drafting as generating plausible candidate claim sets for a specified target language, jurisdiction, and prosecution stage from a source claim set in another language. The task models jurisdiction- and stage-specific transformations beyond content-preserving translation. We construct a large-scale Japanese-English dataset by linking Japan Patent Office (JPO) and United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) records through 884,179 Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)-derived patent families. Across six released configurations, these families yield 4,067,168 directional claim-set instances; four core configurations form the main benchmark. Commercial machine translation and zero- and few-shot prompting capture part of the task, while supervised adaptation provides the strongest overall baseline, showing that task-specific patterns can be learned from linked cross-jurisdictional claim sets.

papers.title: Semiparametric causal mediation analysis in cluster-randomized trials with post-treatment confounding
papers.abstract: Causal mediation analysis of cluster-randomized trials can reveal how interventions affect outcomes through individual and spillover pathways. Most existing methods target natural mediation effects under assumptions that exclude treatment-induced mediator--outcome confounding. We develop a semiparametric framework for interventional mediation effects that accommodates such confounding and within-cluster interference without requiring cross-world independence assumptions. We identify cluster-average and individual-average direct and indirect effects and decompose the indirect effect into individual and spillover components, distinguishing pathways through an individual's own mediator and those of other cluster members. These contrasts evaluate hypothetical interventions on the joint mediator distribution and can differ from treatment effects carried through individual causal pathways represented by natural effects, thereby providing an intervention-oriented perspective that complements natural effects. We derive efficient influence functions to construct estimators using cluster-level cross-fitting, characterize their multiple-robustness properties, and establish conditions for asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency. To facilitate implementation, we develop a lower-dimensional reparameterization that reduces the need for multivariate density estimation and integration and allows nuisance functions to be estimated using parametric models or machine learning. Simulation studies evaluate finite-sample performance, and an application to a cluster-randomized trial of cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic pain illustrates the proposed methods.

authors.name: Daeyoung Ham
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.title: Projections between Ramsey quasi-orders and topological Ramsey spaces
papers.abstract: A Ramsey quasi-order is a quasi-order $(\cal{R},\leq)$ such that $\cal{R}$ is a Polish space, $\leq$ is analytic and every analytic subset of $\cal{R}$ is Ramsey. In this paper, we study the transfer of the analytic Ramsey property via monotone quasi-open maps, which are closely related to a family of forcing projections between quasi-orders (ranging from weak projections to strong projections). We apply this framework to the class of topological Ramsey spaces by providing a detailed list of examples of strong projections between topological Ramsey spaces, and show that, for many of these examples, there is no weak projection in the reverse direction. We also exhibit pairs of topological Ramsey spaces that do not weakly project into each other. Finally, partially confirming a conjecture of Dobrinen, we show that every space in a large class of topological Ramsey spaces either strongly projects into the Ellentuck space or contains a dense set of atoms.

papers.title: Winning Reviews, Losing Discovery? The Co-Evolutionary Game of AI Research and Peer Review
papers.abstract: Autonomous research systems can produce convincing manuscripts whose scientific value is difficult to verify, while automated reviewers can reward the appearance of completeness. We examine how this gap can become a self-reinforcing threat to the research community. In a two-population evolutionary game, authors choose between acceptance-oriented and exploratory research, and reviewers choose between proxy evaluation and careful assessment. Cheaper acceptance-oriented production can increase review pressure, making proxy assessment more attractive; proxy assessment can in turn strengthen the incentive to produce reviewer-compatible work. We derive conditions under which this feedback sustains a stable regime that rewards publication success while reducing the scientific value of accepted work. An analytical basin boundary explains why the same institutional rules can support either this regime or exploratory research with careful review. Numerical illustrations show how publication counts can conceal scientific loss, how faster adjustment can reinforce existing practices, and why partial reform may fail once the cycle is established. Careful audits and reviewer rewards can reverse the feedback, while temporary support can produce lasting recovery if it moves the community across the basin boundary. The model identifies a warning mechanism rather than forecasting a particular conference: a review system can remain operational and privately rewarding while becoming less effective at supporting discovery. Its institutional implication is to reward independently validated contributions and consequential checking, rather than accelerate paper production and scoring alone.

authors.name: Mengru Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Credit Turns Against Tools: Transition-Aware Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains language models through multi-turn tool interactions, yet their reasoning performance and tool-calling ability can decline during training. We trace this degradation to three coupled mechanisms: (1) tool-token imbalance produces negative overall tool credit when incorrect trajectories contain more tool tokens per turn than correct ones; (2) aggregation amplification can further strengthen this negative signal as token-mean aggregation gives longer incorrect trajectories greater weight in policy updates; and (3) failure-driven retries prolong trajectories as models tend to call tools again after execution errors, extending potential negative credit to recovery attempts. To counter this suppression, we propose Transition-Aware Credit Assignment (TACA), which targets the transition from reasoning to tool use through supervision of both call initiation and generation. Specifically, TACA uses Advantage Projection to enforce a nonnegative mean advantage on tool-call tokens within each prompt group through a minimal uniform shift. Additionally, TACA guides tool-use decisions with Decision Contrast, comparing rewards for tool-assisted and direct answers to the same prompt. Through Supervised Replay, it reinforces tool-call generation using calls from previously sampled correct trajectories. Across models and tasks, TACA improves performance and sustains more reliable tool interaction during training, raising mean accuracy over MT-GRPO on six reasoning benchmarks by 4.61 percentage points for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 3.61 for Qwen2.5-3B. Our code is available at https://github.com/tmlr-group/TACA.

papers.title: Reproducible quantum clustering for single-cell transcriptome atlases
papers.abstract: Current single-cell clustering pipelines discard most genes and can yield inconsistent clusters across random seeds. We introduce KQE-2, a training-free hybrid quantum-classical framework for reproducible whole-transcriptome clustering. KQE-2 maps cells into entanglement-free quantum states, enabling exact feature evaluation on classical hardware and direct checks on a quantum processor. Theoretically, we prove that removing entanglement is necessary and sufficient to bound single-qubit feature variance locally. Practically, while retraining scVI shifted 14% of cells and altered rare-type markers and drug targets, KQE-2 delivered identical biology across runs. On standard highly variable genes, the quantum encoding alone raised accuracy on a developing cortex from 0.61 to 0.79. KQE-2 scales to 11.4 million nuclei on one server, outperforming the compared methods on eight of ten complete atlases (and within the best method's run-to-run range on two), and leads on six even under standard downstream clustering.

papers.title: Close and Sort: Exact Maximum-Likelihood Aggregation of Cyclic Rank-Two Preferences
papers.abstract: Pairwise probabilities arise in rank aggregation, recommendation, and human or LLM evaluation, yet converting them into a maximum-likelihood list is a weighted Kemeny problem and is NP-hard in general. Known exact algorithms for rank-two tournaments use only comparison signs and do not optimize this likelihood. We show that the weighted problem is exactly solvable when the skew-symmetric log-odds matrix $W_{ij}=\log(p_{ij}/p_{ji})$ has rank two, including when the induced preferences contain cycles. Writing $W_{ij}=\det(h_i,h_j)$ and adding the closing vector $h_0=-\sum_i h_i$ turns the objective into twice the signed area of a closed polygon. This geometry yields CloseSort, which polar-sorts the $n+1$ edge vectors, cuts after $h_0$, and returns a global maximum-likelihood order in $O(n\log n)$ time from the factors. The same geometry identifies the runner-up and gives a stability certificate beyond exact rank two. When the smallest determinant $\delta$ of two consecutive edges in the closed angular cycle is positive, it is exactly the best-to-runner-up log-likelihood gap. For $W=W_0+E$, the CloseSort order of $W_0$ has regret at most $\sum_{i<j}|E_{ij}|$ on $W$ and remains optimal whenever this sum is below $\delta$, a worst-case tight threshold. In 5,120 determinant-logit simulations, increasing the observations per pair from 4 to 64 raises the fraction on which rank-two projection outperforms the empirical plug-in optimum from 68.6% to 85.7%. On 3,600 Arena-Hard LLM-judge profiles drawn from 63 systems and ten judges, the leading rank-two component captures 89.2% of the log-odds energy. On profiles containing a directed majority triangle, CloseSort reduces normalized regret by 44% relative to Borda and improves the mean normalized objective over each of eight baselines. With factors supplied, it is 8,407 times faster than exact dynamic programming on 18-item rankings.

papers.title: When Greedy Is Sorting: Exact and Certified Ideal Rankings for Novelty Metrics
papers.abstract: The ideal ranking that normalizes novelty metrics is NP-hard to compute in general, so widely used $\alpha$-nDCG evaluators approximate its denominator with a greedy rule that rescans every remaining document at each rank. We identify a regime in which this ideal ranking is exact and cheap for both $\alpha$-DCG and intent-aware expected reciprocal rank (ERR-IA). When each document is positively judged for at most one intent, each metric reduces to the classical allocation of a fixed budget across chains of decreasing marginal gains. A metric-specific virtual-score transformation followed by a multiway merge, which we call ChainMerge, returns the globally optimal top-$K$ ranking in $O(G+K\log G)$ time from $G$ preordered intent groups, or in $O(n+K\log G)$ time from $n$ globally preordered candidates, instead of the $\Theta(nK)$ of the greedy rule. When intent judgments overlap, exact $\alpha$-DCG optimization is NP-hard under the standard logarithmic discount and $\alpha=0.5$, even when every document has three intents and every intent occurs in two documents. For arbitrary overlap, a polynomial-size LP over nested ranking prefixes upper-bounds the ideal score and certifies the optimality gap of any feasible ranking. In the official TREC Web 2009-2012 judgments, 64.8% of positive documents serve a single intent, yet only 20 of 198 complete queries do so throughout. Beyond this exact regime, the LP certifies 189 of the 198 greedy denominators as globally optimal, and the resulting score intervals preserve the winner in all eight matched comparison groups. On 65,238 MIND-small candidates, ChainMerge returns identical optimal objectives 17-1,011 times faster than the greedy rule. For $\alpha$-DCG, these results trace the hardness of the ideal ranking to intent overlap.

papers.title: On the universal structure in deterministic generative diffusion
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based generative modeling has emerged as a general computational framework for simulating high-dimensional, structured data across various domains. Understanding its generative mechanisms is paramount for advancing model training and inference in a principled way. Here, we demonstrate that deterministic sampling trajectories share a universal geometric structure invariant to data modalities and diffusion model implementations. This structure can be largely explained by an exactly solvable model based on the optimal linear denoiser.

authors.name: Can Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Siwei Lyu
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

authors.name: Alexandru Chirvasitu
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Elastic Representations via Hyperbolic Geometry
papers.abstract: Learned representations (or embeddings) are the foundation of modern machine learning systems, yet they are typically trained as fixed-size embeddings, without accounting for varying downstream resource or task constraints. Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) addresses this limitation by learning nested representations, but requires costly end-to-end retraining and does not support post hoc expansion, while Contrastive Sparse Representations (CSR) reduce training overhead via lightweight adaptors but operate at a 4x larger dimensionality. Additionally, all prior works restrict their framework towards compression only. In this work, we introduce Hyperbolic Elastic Representation Learning (HERL), a framework for learning dimension-adaptive embeddings (compression and expansion) through a lightweight adaptor without retraining the base encoder. Our key idea is to exploit the exponential capacity of hyperbolic geometry by learning a non-linear mapping from the encoder space to hyperbolic space. We train a simple MLP to downsample the representations before projecting them onto a Lorentzian and learn adaptive representations that respect the Lorentzian geometry. Our approach is model-agnostic and effective in both supervised and unsupervised settings. Through extensive experiments across image and text modalities, we show that HERL preserves downstream performance across a wide range of embedding sizes, exhibits smooth interpolation between dimensions, and achieves these benefits at a fraction of the computational cost. Code: https://github.com/arjunrkaushik/herl.

authors.name: Arjun Ramesh Kaushik
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Rudrasis Chakraborty
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Nalini Ratha
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Venu Govindaraju
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Evolutionary games on networks with negative edge-based environmental feedback
papers.abstract: Environmental feedback can fundamentally alter the game payoff structure underlying the evolution of cooperation. How feedback-evolving games interact with population structure under non-weak selection remains incompletely understood. We study an evolutionary game on networks in which each edge has a binary environmental state that determines the payoff matrix used by the two connected individuals. By assumption, cooperation tends to improve the local environment, which in turn favors defection, thereby creating negative feedback between strategies coupled with the environmental condition. We analyze the model under strong selection using a mean-field approximation, a pair approximation that tracks both strategy pairs and edge environments, and agent-based simulations. In well-mixed populations, the feedback can generate bistability between full cooperation and full defection, as well as sustained oscillations arising through a Hopf bifurcation. Sparse networks (i.e., with low nodes' degrees) can eliminate bistability, suppress oscillations, and produce stable intermediate levels of cooperation. The pair approximation captures these effects and generally agrees more closely with simulations on sparse networks than the mean-field approximation. Our results show that edge-based environmental feedback and network structure, such as density of edges, interact to determine whether the fraction of cooperators stabilizes or oscillates over time.

authors.name: Katherine Betz
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

authors.name: Naoki Masuda
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Variational Approach to Optimal IPS Estimator for Multi-logger Off-Policy Evaluation
papers.abstract: We study off-policy evaluation (OPE) in contextual bandits with data collected from multiple logging policies. Inverse propensity scoring (IPS) is a standard approach to OPE and extends naturally to the multi-logger setting. However, as highlighted by Agarwal et al. [2017], neither balanced nor weighted IPS consistently outperforms the other in this setting. We resolve this dilemma by deriving an optimal IPS estimator with sample-dependent weights that minimize variance subject to unbiasedness. Using a variational calculus approach, we obtain closed-form optimal weights, yielding an estimator that is unbiased and achieves asymptotically optimal variance within a generalized weighted-IPS estimator class. Instead of a reward model, the estimator needs only a $K\times K$ matrix and a $K$-vector of moments, where $K$ is the number of logging policies, and we quantify how much efficiency this costs relative to the semiparametric oracle. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that our estimator generally improves on existing multi-logger IPS methods. We also extend our estimator to a doubly robust form by incorporating a conditional reward estimator. We compare the resulting DR extension with the semiparametrically efficient DR estimator of Kallus et al. [2021], both theoretically and empirically. We show that the two estimators achieve the same asymptotic variance when the conditional reward estimator is consistent, while our estimator can retain semiparametric efficiency under certain forms of reward misspecification. Empirically, the proposed DR estimator often achieves lower estimation error than the existing DR baseline.

authors.name: Junghoon Seo
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning for Handwritten Letter Recognition: A Controlled Study on EMNIST Letters
papers.abstract:
Handwritten character recognition systems can achieve high accuracy while retaining concentrated errors among visually similar classes. Motivated by residual letter confusions in earlier geometry-based recognition work, we investigate whether these errors can be addressed through the training objective. We introduce Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning (CAML), which constructs a sparse weighted confusion graph from a discovery partition held out from pilot training and applies pair-specific cosine-separation constraints during final training. CAML adds no classifier, routing rule, or inference-time parameters.
  We evaluate CAML on EMNIST Letters against a strictly matched cross-entropy CNN baseline, using the same architecture, final training data, deterministic augmentation, optimizer, and checkpoint selection. Eight confusion pairs are targeted: I/L, G/Q, U/V, R/V, D/O, C/E, I/J, and H/N. On the official clean test set, accuracy changes from 95.6346% to 95.6731%, and macro-F1 from 0.956326 to 0.956724. Mean accuracy across ten predefined corrupted conditions increases from approximately 95.3812% to 95.4303%; symmetric errors within targeted pairs decrease from 614 to 605 (1.47%).
  The global differences are small and not statistically reliable. CAML fixes 124 baseline errors but introduces 116 new errors on clean data (exact McNemar p=0.6515), and no corruption-specific difference remains significant after Holm correction. Thus, CAML does not establish global superiority, but shows that a leakage-controlled, pair-specific margin objective can alter targeted error structure with limited overall benefit for an already strong classifier.

papers.title: Decalage: Uncovering the Gap Between Model-Generated Reasoning and Actual Code Implementation in Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Agentic code generation often asks a model to explain its reasoning before it writes code, and a common way to make such a workflow safer is to add a security instruction to the prompt. We test what that instruction does in small language models, which are attractive because they run locally and cheaply. Four open code models of 1.5B to 3B parameters generate C++ from 166 sections of eleven public requirements documents, once with a general prompt and once with a secure prompt. The secure prompt more than doubles the share of reasoning about validation, resource handling and threats, and we find no evidence that the rise is larger for requirements with security content. The code changes only in part. Among functions with a body and reasoning, the share with a check that our lexical test recognises rises from 23% to 39%, but more than a quarter of the functions remain stubs, compile rates stay low, and half or more of the functions whose reasoning mentions a check contain no such check. Two rounds of compiler-feedback repair leave more than 80% of sections unusable, and neither cppcheck nor an exploratory ESBMC run separates the prompts on the usable code. A hand check by two annotators supports the stub measure and the direction of the reasoning result. For small models, a security instruction changes the reasoning broadly but the code only in part, so the reasoning should be checked against the code rather than trusted.

papers.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
papers.abstract:
We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model.
  Although spatial diffusion typically promotes stability, our focus is on understanding how different diffusion rates for different species can destabilize steady states and give rise to spatial patterns. To address this, we first perform linear stability analysis to identify conditions under which Turing instability may occur. We then validate these theoretical predictions through numerical simulations. Our approach develops both intuition and rigorous analysis of how diffusion influences instabilities in the context of a conservative system, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding pattern formation in multi-species plankton ecosystems.

authors.name: Xiangye Xu
authors.institution: Guangzhou Women and Children Medical Center

papers.title: A Low-Rank Augmented Lagrangian Frank-Wolfe-Based Method for SDPs with Unbounded Feasible Regions
papers.abstract: In contrast to HALLaR (Monteiro et al. 2026), which is designed for solving problems with a trace-bounding constraint, this work develops a new augmented Lagrangian (AL) method, HALLaR+, for solving large-scale semidefinite programming problems without such constraint. Even though a trace constraint which preserves an optimal solution can always be added, choosing its bound is challenging: a value that is too small may exclude all optimal solutions, whereas one that is too large may substantially increase the computational effort. HALLaR+ is also a low-rank inexact AL method but, in contrast to HALLaR, it doubles the penalty parameter at every AL iteration and its AL subproblems have unbounded feasible regions that are approximately solved by a relaxed unbounded Frank--Wolfe (RUFW) variant. Its analysis relies on a uniform bound on the diameters of the sublevel sets of all generated AL subproblems instead of a bounded feasible set. Assuming that a primal--dual KKT pair exists and the primal optimal set is nonempty and bounded, it is shown that HALLaR+ returns a $\varepsilon$-primal-dual feasible solution in $\tilde {\mathcal O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ total RUFW iterations. Numerical results suggest that HALLaR+ has very promising competitive performance against current state-of-the-art solvers.

papers.title: A silting theorem for extended module categories
papers.abstract: We generalize the silting theorem of Buan and Zhou to extended module categories. For a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{P}$ over a proper $d$-truncated non-positive dg algebra $A$, we construct a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{Q}$ over the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra $B$ of $\mathbf{P}$. The $s$-torsion pairs induced by $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ yield equivalences of Brenner-Butler type between the torsion class on either side and the torsion-free class on the other. There is also a dg algebra homomorphism from $A$ to the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{Q}$, which is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{P},\mathbf{P}[i])=0$ for all $i\leq-d$. Moreover, we describe Auslander-Reiten theory in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!B}$ in terms of that in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!A}$.

papers.title: A Tool for Anonymized Clinical Knowledge Retrieval and Speaker Interaction Analysis of Healthcare Tele-mentoring Sessions
papers.abstract: We present a tool for anonymized retrieval of clinical knowledge and analysis of multi-speaker interactions in tele-mentoring sessions of Project ECHO (Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes). Our tool's novel design includes: (a) a compound metadata filter that enforces strict speaker- and session-level isolation during retrieval, preventing cross-session context contamination; (b) MedGemma-4B as a locally-hosted language model for clinically grounded answer generation across three query modes; (c) interaction graphs to compute betweenness centrality, PageRank influence, and turn-taking patterns to quantify participation equity; and (d) a consistent alias-based anonymization scheme that prevents real participant names from appearing in any rendered output. During the demo, a healthcare provider (user) will interactively query multi-year ECHO sessions, explore participation dynamics through interaction graphs, compare sessions side-by-side, and assess answer quality via six reference-free RAG metrics, all without any cloud API dependency.

papers.title: Beyond Ranking: Are Decision Models Calibrated Relevance Scorers?
papers.abstract: Decision models such as Jev are a new kind of relevance scorer. Their typed score primitive takes a question, an ordered set of textual relevance levels and a state, and returns a probability for each level directly, rather than token likelihoods or generated labels. Jev's vendor promises that these probabilities are calibrated. This motivates revisiting 'Beyond Yes and No', which improved zero-shot pointwise LLM reranking using likelihood-derived scores over fine-grained relevance labels but left calibration against human assessors as future work. In this paper, we first reproduce its open-model FLAN-UL2 setting on eight BEIR collections, confirming its ranking trends, and then run Jev and two open-weight decision models with the same protocol. Jev and the 27B pplx-decider rerank ahead of FLAN-UL2 and three cross-encoders on average. We then compare Jev's native probabilities with the human assessors' labels and find them overconfident: of the DL21 pairs it scores above 0.9, only 66% are relevant. Since this is mostly an error of scale, a two-parameter calibration fitted on 2,257 DL19 pairs removes much of it and transfers to DL21. After calibration, Jev has a lower DL21 Brier score than FLAN-UL2 and the three cross-encoders, mainly because it separates relevant from non-relevant pairs better. Finally, with calibrated probabilities, choosing each query's cut-off by expected F1 needs no parameter of its own, beats a fixed top-10 cut and matches a cut-off threshold tuned on DL19.

papers.title: Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains
papers.abstract: For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.

papers.title: The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
papers.abstract: We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.

papers.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
papers.abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.

papers.title: Two-dimensional liquid-like order in a confined population of swimming Eudorina colonies
papers.abstract: Swimming microorganisms accumulate at boundaries, but the spatial statistics of the resulting layers are rarely measured. We report a population of colonial green algae, of order 71 $\mu$m across, that accumulates against the rigid upper wall of a closed 1-2 mm chamber and holds a two-dimensional non-contacting arrangement for about 105 min. The pair correlation function has a first shell at $r/\bar{D} = 1.73$, $g = 4.8$; a hard-disc null at the same area fraction reaches only $g = 2.1$, so the ordering is not excluded volume alone. Nearest-neighbour separation is $1.80 \pm 0.13$ diameters. The bond-orientational order parameter is $\langle|\psi_6|\rangle = 0.456$ against 0.385 for the null, only 36% of interior colonies are six-coordinated, and the orientational correlation $g_6(r)$ decays over 1.5 diameters with $\eta_6 = 1.31$ against the hexatic bound of 1/4: the arrangement is a two-dimensional liquid, not a crystal or a hexatic. Colonies execute a persistent random walk with reorientation time 1.4-1.7 s at Reynolds number $\sim 9\times 10^{-4}$. Breakup begins at 127 min. Thermal convection is excluded on Rayleigh-number grounds. Caveats: the length calibration is nominal rather than metrological, and this is a single population observed once. All data and code are deposited.

papers.title: When Experience Becomes a Backdoor: Poisoning Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Failure-Aware Task Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly improve themselves through self-evolution, distilling execution experience into persistent, reusable skills. However, this persistence creates a new attack surface: malicious rules implanted into skills can compromise subsequent agent behavior. Existing skill backdoor attacks typically assume direct manipulation of the victim's skills, which is impractical when skills are constructed internally by a trusted evolver. In this paper, we study a novel problem of task-level backdoor attacks, where the attacker can only inject poisoned evolution tasks, inducing the agent to implant backdoors into its own skills. Since the attacker controls neither skill induction nor downstream execution, a natural approach is to iteratively optimize poisoned tasks based on attack success. However, our preliminary analysis reveals two key challenges: (i) failures at different stages of skill evolution and downstream execution can produce indistinguishable outcomes, providing little guidance for targeted poisoned-task updates; and (ii) unsuccessful updates may undermine earlier progress, while simply discarding them may lead to repeated ineffective updates. To address these challenges, we propose BadEvolve, a failure-aware task-poisoning framework against self-evolving LLM agents. BadEvolve diagnoses attack failures across four stages, i.e., Induction, Activation, Following, and Effect, and directs updates toward the failing stage. It further employs rollback to preserve earlier progress and failure memory to avoid repeating ineffective updates. Extensive experiments across diverse self-evolution frameworks, benchmarks, and backbone LLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of BadEvolve. Our code is available at https://github.com/ventr1c/BadEvolve.

papers.title: Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem on graphs
papers.abstract: Solutions of the Dirichlet problem on a finite part of a weighted graph are extended by zero, together with their source, to a larger connected part. A necessary and sufficient condition is proved for the extended function to remain a solution of the corresponding Dirichlet problem on the enlarged domain: at every newly included vertex adjacent to the original part, the weighted sum of the solution over its neighbors in that part must vanish. The admissible sources are characterized as the orthogonal complement of the harmonic extensions from the enlarged domain to the original part, their space has dimension equal to the number of vertices of the original part minus the rank of the interface coupling, and an exact energy identity for the extension error follows from a Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. The same reduction covers other boundary conditions, including the Neumann problem, and extends to higher powers of the Laplacian, where the boundary data must be compatible with the lower-order interface traces. The discrete criterion is compared with its continuous counterpart, and no result in this form has been reported on Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: Beyond Hard Labels: LLM Probabilities Improve Human-Assisted Regression
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for text annotation, but their outputs are often reduced to a single categorical label before downstream analysis. This hardening step discards the model's relative support across categories, which may contain useful information when category boundaries are ambiguous. We study whether retaining the full probability vector improves downstream regression when LLM annotations are combined with a limited amount of human annotation. Using matched soft and hard representations from three LLMs across three social-science text datasets, we compare direct regression and human-assisted correction. Soft inputs are not uniformly better when used directly as outcomes, but after human correction, using the probability vector consistently improves regression efficiency across models and datasets.
