The VCG mechanism delivers this and more. Reporting truthfully is a dominant strategy (DSIC), no buyer loses by participating (ex post individual rationality), and no buyer is paid to show up (non-negative payments).

Efficiency is rarely the planner’s only concern. A first worry is stability: VCG is not immune to coalitional deviations. A group of buyers together with the seller can walk away from the auction, reallocate the goods among themselves, and make everyone in the group at least as well off, and someone strictly better off. Rothkopf et al. (1990) were among the first to point out how fragile the Vickrey mechanism is to such behaviour, and Ausubel et al. (2006) summarised the problem by calling the Vickrey auction “lovely but lonely”. Formally, the question is whether the VCG payoff vector lies in the core of the cooperative game induced by the auction. Bikhchandani and Ostroy (2002) show that it does if and only if buyers are substitutes. The incentive-auction outcome above was not stable: T-Mobile and U.S. Cellular together would have had to pay about US$237,000 more for the outcome to lie in the core (Ausubel and Baranov, 2026). Even that correction leaves the seller with a small fraction of what the winners bid. Stability alone does not secure the seller a meaningful share. Under reasonable assumptions on the domain of valuations, any efficient, DSIC mechanism whose payoffs lie in the core at every valuation profile must use VCG payments. Stability therefore leaves no freedom to choose a different division of surplus while retaining efficiency and dominant-strategy truthfulness.

Even when VCG is stable, it gives every buyer the largest possible payoff among all stable outcomes and gives the seller the least. This division favours buyers at the seller’s expense and explains the low revenue in VCG auctions. The core of an auction is never empty, since giving the entire surplus to the seller is always in the core. It is typically a large set. Every point in it is efficient, because it divides the full surplus, and every point is stable, by definition. VCG sits at one extreme of this set. Take three identical licences and two buyers who each want one, with values 10 and 8. VCG prices are zero and the payoffs to (seller, buyer 1, buyer 2) are (0,10,8)(0,10,8). This is stable. But so is (6,6,6)(6,6,6). Once stability is secured, the planner’s remaining concern is how the surplus is shared, and it is natural to ask which point of the core is the fairest. We treat the seller as a full player in this comparison, not as a leftover claimant. When the seller is a government, low revenue is not a private transfer between two parties. It is a loss to the public exchequer, as the incentive auction illustrates.

Fairness has many definitions: the Rawlsian max–min criterion, Nash welfare, and requirements such as anonymity. One payoff vector Lorenz dominates another if, for every kk, its kk poorest players collectively receive at least as much. For example, (40,40,20)(40,40,20) Lorenz dominates (50,30,20)(50,30,20): the poorest player gets 20 in both, but the two poorest get 60 instead of 50. A Lorenz-dominant vector therefore reconciles these criteria in a single payoff vector.

papers.title: Motion Belief Action: From a Visual Scene Map to Physical Decisions
papers.abstract: A robot that works among people must judge what it cannot see: whether an object is still where it was last seen, and whether a pull on a door or drawer is worth its risk. Maps that track object change hold nothing about force, maps of physical properties answer a risk question at a fixed risk level, and vision-language-action models keep no explicit estimate of hidden physics. We propose Motion Belief Action (MBA), a decision layer on the scene map. From how often people move an object and how much force it needs, how much load it holds and whether it is blocked, MBA chooses under a force limit to look again, nudge, open, brace or decline, with its risk set by the task's costs. On real activity in 9 kitchens, it predicts whether an object is still in place better than FreMEn and Perpetua, and decides when to look again at lower cost than these and the persistence filter, because about a quarter of placements end in a pick-up within 30 s. On real pulls of doors and drawers in 17 locations, made by a person with a force-sensing gripper, the map's force estimates decide better than a part-type average. Setting the risk from the costs also beats a published risk rule at its fixed level. In simulation, with the force limit at the training parts' median force, MBA raises SmolVLA's and Octo's scores by declining pulls; most declined door pulls would fail, but on drawers more would have opened, and a part-type average gets about half of this gain. In both, a published risk rule set to the risk these costs imply is MBA's rule for a single pull and decides as well in the main settings. A link between opening and holding force, a probing nudge and an action prior for camera tracking do not help in the main settings, and over the real-pull sweep the nudge costs a little.

authors.name: Dibyendu Ghosh
authors.institution: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

papers.title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
papers.abstract: Symbolic knowledge (motif counts, ring counts, label constraints) is routinely added to graph neural networks (GNNs) and justified by their limited expressivity. We replace this yardstick with an exact one. The largest log-loss reduction a rule $S$ can give a model family is $I(Y;S\mid\sigma)$ given what the family computes; every realised gain splits exactly into this term plus repaid neural debt; and for a trained network with representation $T$ the value is $I(Y;S\mid T)$, the label information training failed to extract. Rule design thus becomes rule discovery: we score candidates on the network's out-of-fold residual against calibrated permutation nulls with family-wise error control. On ZINC, discovery recovers the hidden ring term $\max(0,\ell_{\max}-6)$ of the target in three independent runs ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}=0.001$) and beats expert cycle counts; frozen and applied to five unseen datasets it is never significantly worse than the plain network or the expert rule, and on BBBP it significantly beats both.

papers.title: BACGUARD: Fact-Grounded Runtime Mitigation of Broken Access Control
papers.abstract: Broken Access Control (BAC) has been the foremost category in the OWASP Top Ten since 2021, primarily due to the challenges in enforcing authorization at the application layer. Traditional mechanisms depend on logic embedded in the application, referencing relational database information such as permissions, roles, or ownership. However, missing or incorrect checks can go undetected by external systems, leaving applications vulnerable. This paper presents BACGUARD, a reverse proxy designed to enforce authorization for unmodified applications. BACGUARD reconstructs authorization relations by leveraging authenticated user data from session stores and object ownership from relational schemas. It evaluates whether users are permitted to access resources and blocks unauthorized requests in real time. Unlike existing approaches, BACGUARD bases its authorization on database joins, making the system resilient to forgery. For most requests, decisions are made deterministically. In cases where access control violations are only apparent in response data, such as cross-user data leakage, a language model is used as a fallback. Evaluations on six applications, including those with known vulnerabilities, demonstrate that BACGUARD's hybrid deterministic and language model-based approach blocks all tested attacks with a false-positive rate below 0.7%. Competing solutions like Web Application Firewalls are less effective and more disruptive. The results highlight BACGUARD's primary contribution: the external reconstruction of authorization facts, enabling robust enforcement even when the application itself is flawed.

authors.name: Moses Ndebugre
authors.institution: North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University

papers.title: Creative Intent as an Evolving Shared State: Supporting Cross-Stage Human-AI Video Co-Creation
papers.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly involved in video creation, creators face challenges in expanding, translating, and negotiating creative intent across stages. We therefore view creative intent as an evolving shared state throughout human-AI co-creation. A multi-stage design was employed: semi-structured interviews with 12 creators informed 3 design goals, followed by expert co-design and the development of VideoMaker. VideoMaker organizes creation into a six-stage workflow that progressively translates creative intent. At key stages, creators negotiate with AI through the Seed Panel, explicitly confirming, revising, and updating intent. A shared AI Agent, supported by the Multi-style Script Library and Cinematic Language Knowledge Base, enables differentiated expansion of initial intent and faithful translation. A within-subjects study with 30 participants showed that VideoMaker effectively supported the expansion and cross-stage translation of creative intent, with stronger intent preservation, while negotiated boundaries between creator-confirmed intent and AI initiative remained difficult to sustain.

authors.name: Mengfei Chen
authors.institution: Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region Peoples Hospital

authors.name: Songruoyao Wu
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Kejun Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
papers.abstract: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. We formulate this setting as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a task that jointly refines spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories. To this end, we propose a framework that decomposes prediction into spatial and temporal stages using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads. For backbone adaptation, we introduce PROLA (PRincipal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation), which allocates a fixed low-rank budget between pretrained weights' principal directions and their orthogonal complement. PROLA further rescales rank-1 optimizer updates using gradient signals, improving adaptation without increasing trainable rank. Experiments in the PSWD setting show that PROLA outperforms representative low-rank adaptation baselines. Further experiments across diverse datasets and tasks support the broader applicability of PROLA, showing that its benefits extend beyond the primary weather downscaling setting.

authors.name: Hyunwoo J. Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: What Travels Across Languages? Reading, Transfer and Erasure of Cross-Lingual Concept Subspaces in Bangla Idioms
papers.abstract: Cross-lingual concept analysis requires distinguishing the information that a subspace retains from the classifiers and erasers that transfer through it. We study these operations in six frozen encoders using 10,359 Bangla (Bengali) idiom senses, eight input conditions, and figurative-class and sentiment labels. Class-mean directions provide the most consistent evidence of shared coarse meaning: in post hoc analyses, they outperform random-subspace, permuted-label and covariance-matched nulls in all 12 model-label tests under balanced accuracy. A prospective internal re-split supports idiom-alone sharing in 10 of 12 tests, spanning five encoders. The original confirmatory logistic-regression family rejects both planned nulls in 4 of 12 tests, where English directions gain only a few accuracy points above the majority-class floor (3.0-7.3). Classifier transfer depends on the input map and regularization: English-trained class-mean readouts beat both zero-shot nulls in 8 of 12 discovery tests, and stronger source-selected penalties improve transfer through logistic and LEACE directions. These readouts use Bangla-validation-selected layers and unlabeled target preprocessing. Input controls show greater coarse-class sharing for explicit glosses than for idiom counterparts. Reading, however, does not imply effective erasure: English-fitted LEACE removes less than one percentage point of Bangla figurative-class accuracy, compared with 4-11 points for Bangla-fitted LEACE; INLP shows a similar asymmetry. Pattern-filter analysis, covariance-weighted input maps and a binary Gaussian overlap bound explain how these operations can diverge. The analogous multiclass ordering is an empirical diagnostic, observed in 11 of 12 cells. The results support an estimator-sensitive account of cross-lingual concept sharing and motivate evaluating reading, classifier transfer, erasure and overlap separately.

papers.title: Hidden memory above the Neel temperature programs antiferromagnetic order in Cr2O3
papers.abstract: Control of antiferromagnetic order is central to magnetoelectric and antiferromagnetic spintronic devices. In the prototypical magnetoelectric antiferromagnet Cr2O3, domains are conventionally selected by simultaneous application of electric and magnetic fields during cooling through the Neel temperature (T_N) or at a fixed temperature below T_N. Here, we show that antiferromagnetic order can instead be programmed by electric-field conditioning entirely in the paramagnetic state above T_N. By measuring the magnetoelectric coefficient (alpha_zz) of bulk Cr2O3 crystals under different thermal and field histories, we find that a sufficiently large electric field above T_N establishes a reversible state that persists after the field is removed. Subsequent magnetic-field cooling with no applied electric field produces a single-domain state with the opposite Neel-vector orientation from conventional magnetoelectric field cooling. The electrically induced state can be reversibly written, erased, and allowed to relax at high temperatures, demonstrating a long-lived internal electric bias that governs domain selection. The observed behavior is consistent with a metastable surface-associated polar state that may generate this internal bias. These results reveal an unexpected coupling between electrically programmed memory and antiferromagnetic domain formation in Cr2O3.

papers.title: Frequency-Structure Complementary Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Fusion
papers.abstract: Existing methods mainly rely on convolutional aggregation or attention-based spatial-spectral interaction. However, conventional feature-domain attention does not explicitly characterize variation patterns along spatial-token and learned latent-channel coordinates, while spatially shared local operators lack the flexibility to adapt neighborhood aggregation to heterogeneous structures. To address these limitations, we propose a Frequency-Structure Complementary Modeling Network (FSCM-Net), which couples frequency-aware dependency learning with structure-adaptive local refinement. Specifically, a Spatial-Spectral Frequency Calibration Attention (SSFCA) module constructs spatial-token affinities from Fourier-interacted query-key representations and builds latent-channel affinities after input-conditioned frequency filtering along learned channel coordinates. The latent-channel response is then calibrated by a learned shared gain and combined with the spatial-token response. Complementarily, a Structure-Coherent Dynamic Feature Fusion (SC-DFF) module combines regularized structure-tensor cues from MSI features with context-modulated HSI detail representations to generate channel- and position-dependent aggregation kernels. This design makes local HSI refinement responsive to smooth regions, edges, and textures while maintaining spectral fidelity. The two modules are progressively integrated within a multiscale encoder-decoder to coordinate representation-level interaction and structure-adaptive reconstruction. Experiments on two simulated benchmarks and one real remote-sensing dataset demonstrate favorable performance against representative fusion methods in spatial detail reconstruction and spectral preservation.

papers.title: Attacking Slide Puzzle CAPTCHAs Based on Time and Space Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.abstract: CAPTCHAs can protect websites from malicious attacks. As a typical representative of behavior CAPTCHAs, slide puzzle CAPTCHAs have become increasingly popular in recent years due to their user-friendliness and high security. Previous attack methods on slide puzzle CAPTCHA mainly face challenges in the following four aspects. (1) The defense mechanisms of previous slide puzzle CAPTCHAs were relatively simple. The current slide puzzle CAPTCHAs have added complex interferences, detected slide trajectory features in the two-dimensional space, and added other defense mechanisms. (2) The previous notch detection methods were difficult to accurately locate the notch positions. (3) Previous attack trajectories were limited to the horizontal dimension, making them impossible to pass the existing detection. (4) The previous attack trajectories were generated by fitting functions, which were relatively simple and could not well simulate the slide characteristics of human users. In response to the above challenges, firstly, we systematically analyze the defense strategies of six most popular slide puzzle CAPTCHAs: Capy, Dingxiang, Geetest, Kyger, Shumei and Tencent. Secondly, for each type of CAPTCHA, we construct a notch detection dataset and a slide trajectory dataset separately. Thirdly, we use advanced YOLOv11 to detect the notch positions and train generative adversarial networks (GAN) to generate attack trajectories. As far as we know, we are the first to generate attack trajectories by directly learning human slide trajectory characteristic. According to the experimental results, this method cracked six most popular slide puzzle CAPTCHAs with success rates of over 90\%, and the attack time is only about 5 seconds, indicating that the security of existing slide puzzle CAPTCHAs is facing challenge. At the same time, we propose various methods to enhance the security of slide puzzle CAPTCHAs.

papers.title: Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket
papers.abstract: This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.

papers.title: When the Plan Changes: A Strategic World Testbed for Dynamic Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.abstract: Changing an objective does not automatically revise agents' earlier plans or delegated tasks. Acknowledgment can coexist with obsolete execution, while misleading instructions can redirect work or discard retained constraints. We present a Strategic World simulation testbed that separates authoritative objectives, local plans, notice receipt, and consequential action. Six intervention families vary objectives, conditions, authority, membership, and communication. Matched protocols and deadlines establish feasibility for the tested disturbances. Controlled trajectories demonstrate that identical completion and acknowledgment summaries can conceal uninformed obsolete work, obsolete work after receipt, or blocked unsafe intent. Local language-model trials and instructed action probes reveal competence limits that constrain interpretation of dynamic failures. A further 16-episode comparison evaluates an engineered guard that prioritizes pending notice submissions over local work. It completes 4/4 held-out settings, compared with 1/4 for a calibrated assisted baseline. Each episode contains one large language model actor and two fixed peers. These results establish diagnostic distinctions and bounded policy feasibility under explicit simulation assumptions; they do not establish frontier-model reliability or autonomous team adaptation.

authors.name: Kai Shu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

papers.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
papers.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. The topology exploits this: a thermoelectric thin film lies flat on a diamond substrate beside the device drain (the electron exit), so bulk Joule heat leaves vertically into the substrate. A lateral fin model gives a closed form for the recirculation factor gamma: the vertical pillar yields gamma = 1, while the horizontal film yields gamma_max = sqrt(2) L_z/L_x, about 0.03 for L_z = 10 um, L_x = 500 um. The decoupling scales the net cooling ceiling and the critical runaway current by roughly 1/gamma. At equal resistance, the same film lifts maximum cooling from 13 mW to 500 mW, and the critical current from 0.65 A to 24 A. A time-constant and linear stability analysis with temperature-sensitive parameters defines the working window and safety margins for microsecond pulse cooling. The architecture leaves the device structure untouched; the principle, absorb at an interface and extract bulk heat vertically, applies to any chip with a hot core and offers a reproducible design path for near-junction thermal management.

papers.title: HolidayFactory 1.0: Simulating, Generating, and Evaluating Industrial Robot Tasks
papers.abstract: Robots are typically evaluated in episodes that begin from a reset, while industrial work consists of repeated jobs whose outcomes affect subsequent operations. Evaluating such work at scale requires simulation of task-critical physical interactions, construction of industrial environments, and measurements of performance as scene state persists. We present HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0, a framework for simulating, generating, and evaluating industrial robot work. Given a human-specified workplace and task, the framework defines a world pairing a scenario of scene variants and process logic with an evaluation defining a job, metrics, and a rubric. HOLIDAYFACTORY 1.0 comprises three components. HOLIDAY-SIM extends Newton's SDF-based hydroelastic contact with additional constitutive laws and a semi-implicit primal-dual solver, couples stateful actuator dynamics to articulated motion, and derives tactile and joint observations from simulated states. Agentic world construction generates simulation-ready assets and scene variants using geometric and interaction checks, and proposes task-conditioned evaluations for human confirmation and executable checks. 24/7-BENCH introduces seven industrial tasks in which jobs are evaluated without resetting the scene, measuring completed, failed, and unfinished jobs, throughput, latency, and motor energy. Controlled studies characterize the proposed contact, actuator, and tactile models and examine the effectiveness of verification-guided world construction. Experiments on scene and evaluation generation further reveal the limitations of model critics and the difficulty of ensuring that generated evaluations faithfully capture task requirements. We examine job-level evaluations with scripted trajectories (e.g., code-as-policy) but have not yet compared policies over persistent runs.

authors.name: Geonhyup Lee
authors.institution: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: OverlapAdvisor: Modeling and Adapting Computation-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving
papers.abstract:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference with expert parallelism (EP) relies on All-to-All communication, making computation-communication overlap strategies critical for achieving high performance. However, no strategy is universally optimal. Across 103 production configurations, varying input lengths, and four hardware platforms, we observe that the fastest strategy shifts based on model shape, EP degree, input length, and hardware. Since no strategy dominates more than 80.6% of configurations, configuration-aware selection is necessary.
  In this work, we propose OverlapAdvisor, which models overlap stages using two granularities to capture computation-communication dependencies. OverlapAdvisor builds a unified performance model, accounting for deviations from peak compute, memory, and communication performance across workloads and hardware. This model enables launch-time, configuration-aware strategy selection within two serving engines. We conduct experiments on four MoE models (30B-235B) against three baselines, utilizing SGLang and vLLM. At the kernel level, OverlapAdvisor achieves 1.16x average and 1.59x maximum speedups, with a prediction MAPE of 3.3%-15.9%. In SGLang and vLLM, it improves end-to-end throughput up to 31.7%. Its granularity-guided optimizations further achieve median speedups of 1.10x for DeepEP-v1 and 1.22x for FlashMoE.

authors.name: Luping Wang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University

papers.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
papers.abstract: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. Extending this paradigm to vision allows visual and language models to converge on a unified framework, thereby fostering shared methodology and infrastructure. This work investigates a central question: how far can a finite discrete vocabulary go in representing the richness of the visual world? We present dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that produces discrete visual primitives analogous to language tokens. Built upon a frozen pretrained encoder, dNaViT applies lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. By leveraging grouped product quantization, it scales discrete capacity without inflating spatial sequence lengths, while a balanced training recipe maintains both semantic and pixel-level information. Consequently, dNaViT functions as a versatile discrete visual tokenizer, enabling unified encoding across downstream tasks alongside high-fidelity image decoding. Extensive evaluations show that dNaViT matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 visual understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks, and an image editing benchmark. These findings demonstrate that a compact discrete vocabulary can serve as a universal visual currency and unlock the full potential of fully unified, native multimodal methodology.

authors.name: Xu Huang
authors.institution: The Second Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen Medical College

authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xunliang Cai
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Hidden frequencies in topological dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We show for certain skew products built over any infinite minimal nilsystem, the frequencies present in the nilsystem are not always enough to govern recurrence for the whole system. This strengthens and generalizes a theorem of Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, and Richter.

papers.title: Questions of minimality for DDMOGs and cycle ornaments
papers.abstract: Difference distance magic oriented graphs (DDMOGs) are oriented graphs whose vertices admit a bijective labeling by consecutive positive integers such that every vertex has weight zero, where the weight is the sum of the labels of its in-neighbors minus the sum of the labels of its out-neighbors. We investigate minimality and sparsity questions for DDMOGs and their ornaments. First, we develop new constructions of cycle-based ornaments that reduce the number of cycles required for a given number of attachment nodes and identify minimal cycle lengths in several cases. Second, we determine the minimum number of arcs in a nontrivial DDMOG of order $n$, combining computational enumeration for small orders with theoretical lower bounds and constructions. Langford sequences provide a key tool in these constructions, enabling us to partition consecutive labels into difference triples and thereby construct sparse DDMOGs. Finally, we use related constructions to obtain generalized ornaments with no internal arcs. These results advance the study of minimal constructions in difference distance magic labeling and provide new methods for building sparse DDMOGs.

papers.title: Safe by Accident: Crash-Testing LLM-Written Code
papers.abstract: Evaluations of LLM-written code run it once, in one environment, and credit the code with whatever passes. We show that this credit can belong to the environment. We crashed LLM-written backend code just before each database, file and email call, re-ran it as an operator would, and judged the result under two transaction modes of Python's sqlite3: the default, in which the library quietly opens a transaction, and autocommit, in which it does not. Across 9,100 solutions from ten models on 24 backend tasks, more than half (54%) of the database code that survives every crash in the default mode is left half-updated in autocommit mode. This holds for every model, and it hides in ordinary code, including with conn: blocks that look like transactions but open none. Telling the model that its connection is in autocommit mode does not change what the local code models write, while the API models' unsafe share falls by 30 points. Asking for crash safety helps every model, and strong models repair nearly all unsafe code, but often write safe code only when asked. Thus, much of the crash safety that LLM-written database code appears to have is borrowed from the library rather than designed into it, and a second test under a less forgiving configuration reveals the difference.

authors.name: Rifat Shahriyar
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: An Interline Multiport DC Circuit Breaker with Power Flow Controller
papers.abstract: Currently, the high-voltage multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids face two major challenges. First, fast rise rate and lack of zero-crossing point in DC-side fault currents render AC circuit breakers inoperable. Second, DC line currents are passively determined by terminal DC voltages and line resistances, which inherently limits the capability of changing individual line currents for essential grid services such as power flow management and overloading prevention. To address these two limitations, DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC power flow controllers (DCPFCs) have been developed. The conventional DCCBs are two-port devices installed in series with DC lines at their terminals in an MTDC converter substation, so that any fault current flowing through the line can be rapidly cleared. Additionally, a DCPFC can be installed at line terminals to adjust terminal voltages and power exchanges among adjacent lines. As a result, for a substation that connects to multiple lines, it needs to host multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, which significantly increases the cost and footprint of both the substation and the MTDC grid. To this end, this work proposes an integrated equipment combining multiple DCCBs and a DCPFC, called the interline multiport DCCB with DCPFC, which can reduce the number of components and enhance the economic feasibility of MTDC networks. This paper presents the topology, operation principles, and component selection procedures of the proposed equipment, and compares it with the state-of-the-art technologies. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results validate the fault interruption and power flow control performance of the interline multiport DCCB with PFC.

authors.name: Maliha Ferdous
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a line-search quasi-Newton (LSQN) method for discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs). The method maintains an inverse model to approximate the inverse of the current policy Jacobian and refines it through an inner learning procedure that preserves existing secant conditions and achieves the prescribed accuracy in at most $n$ queries in exact arithmetic for an MDP with $n$ states, even when the initial inverse model is singular. A sign-based direction correction combined with an Armijo line search ensures monotonic decrease of the Bellman residual norm across policy changes without requiring a value-iteration fallback. We prove global Q-linear residual convergence and local Q-superlinear convergence of the value iterates from arbitrary finite initial value vectors and inverse models, without requiring a unique optimal policy. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against nine baselines, while public benchmarks demonstrate that the inner learning procedure typically requires far fewer than $n$ learning queries.

papers.title: ExCritique: An Interactive Visual Interface to Evaluate AI-Generated Explanations at Scale
papers.abstract: Vision-language Models (VLMs) can generate natural language explanations for complex decision-making scenarios. However, these explanations can sometimes be misleading, sounding convincing while containing incorrect or unsupported information. Automated explanation-quality metrics help researchers and practitioners evaluate large collections of explanations, but their scores alone provide limited support for identifying failure cases and understanding the reliability of these metrics. This paper presents a case study on how interactive visualizations can help researchers and practitioners evaluate both AI-generated explanations and automated explanation-quality metrics across large datasets. Based on formative interviews with nine AI researchers and practitioners, we designed an interactive visualization tool named ExCritique, situated in the task of Visual Question Answering (VQA). ExCritique visualizes the distributions of multiple automated quality metrics, allows users to explore thousands of data items, filter items and inspect the evidence behind individual scores. We compared ExCritique with a baseline interface without interactive visualizations in a controlled study involving 16 AI researchers and practitioners. Our findings suggest that the interactive visualizations in ExCritique helped users identify explanation-quality issues more efficiently and better understand automated quality metrics, supporting an effective way to measure the reliability of AI-generated explanations.

papers.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
papers.abstract: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. We attribute this failure to evaluation-side partial observability, where models are evaluated mainly from final outcome, without checking the faithfulness of underlying reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. Prior mitigations address this partial observability by predefined evaluator latent belief space or one-shot monitoring, which do not extend to free-form language space and vulnerable to stronger deceptions that evade simple monitoring. In this work, we formulate deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an agent maximizes reward, a monitor minimizes the agent's payoff by exposing deception from the full interaction trajectory, and a fixed verifier validates the monitor's claims and converts them into penalties. We define the solution concept as a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium (SPOE) between agent and monitor, and prove its existence in finite games. With a perfect verifier, every SPOE is faithful; with an imperfect verifier, the guarantee persists if verifier errors do not reverse the ranking of monitor actions. To achieve faithful SPOE, we derive a two-timescale policy gradient algorithm and enhance the pipeline empirically with NLI verification and deterministic checks. Experiments with Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop show that e-PoG mitigates multiple emergent deception modes, outperforming the strongest baselines by 26.0% in deception mitigation and by up to 39.8% in task success. These gains persist under weak-to-strong supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent.

authors.institution: Henan University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Simin Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Decentralised Drone Swarm Formation under Silent Failures with ACO Pheromone Claims and PSO Tuning
papers.abstract: We study decentralised drone formation, without a central planner, under the conditions that make it hard: nobody knows how many drones are alive, failures are silent, radio is short-ranged and lossy, and actuation is noisy. In our controller, ant colony optimisation (ACO) allocates drones to picture positions through claims that behave as reinforced, evaporating pheromone and are gossiped between neighbours, so evaporation doubles as failure detection. A particle swarm optimisation (PSO) law flies the drones, a noise-buffered Voronoi filter keeps them apart, and PSO also tunes the controller offline. We prove that claims of destroyed drones vanish within bounded time, that conflicts between drones that exchange tables are resolved consistently, that survivors cover the picture to within a factor of two, and that drones cannot collide while their safety cells are feasible. On held-out seeds and with two tuned configurations, the controller formed the picture in 95-99% of runs in the hardest regime, restored it after a silent loss of half the swarm in 96-100% of runs at normal difficulty, transferred unchanged to eight unseen shapes and to 300 drones, and overlapped in 5 of 21,088 runs. A CBBA-style baseline that shares the evaporating claims but uses argmax without swaps was at least as reliable as ours once tuned with the same budget, and repaired faster, whereas ours generalised better to unseen shapes. The benefit thus comes from the pheromone dynamics and from tuning, not from ACO's stochastic construction or PSO's social terms. A centralised oracle is faster.

authors.name: Md. Abu Horaira
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Business and Technology

papers.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Stability in Network Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: Quantum kernel methods have been proposed for network intrusion detection, yet their performance limitations are often attributed to noise in current quantum hardware. This study evaluates that assumption through a controlled analysis of Pegasos-QSVC on the NSL-KDD and ToN-IoT datasets. We perform 56 quantum experiments using one exact noiseless statevector backend and three noise-simulated superconducting backends while keeping preprocessing, PCA features, data splits, and classical baselines identical. XGBoost achieves accuracies of 98.94% on NSL-KDD and 99.41% on ToN-IoT, compared with 91.80% and 82.98% for Pegasos-QSVC. The quantum model also exhibits substantially greater seed-dependent variability. Eight runs collapse into degenerate classifiers, including four recall-collapse cases and four trivial-positive classifiers. Notably, two failures occur on the noiseless backend, demonstrating that hardware noise is not a necessary condition for classi-fier collapse. Kernel Gram matrix analysis further reveals low effective rank and severe ill-conditioning even in the absence of noise, indicating intrinsic fragility in the learned quantum representation. These results show that average accuracy alone can conceal operationally unacceptable behavior and highlight the importance of reporting worst-case performance, seed-level variability, class-specific metrics, and explicit degeneracy tests in quantum intrusion detection studies.

authors.name: Adrita Rahman Tory
authors.institution: Bangladesh University of Business and Technology

papers.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding efficiency depends on the number of consecutively accepted draft tokens, yet token-level training objectives do not directly optimize this quantity. We introduce D-REAL (Drafter Reinforcement of Expected Acceptance Length), a post-training method that directly optimizes expected acceptance length for a fixed decoding context. D-REAL weights position-wise draft-target distributional overlap by prefix survival probabilities along a draft-sampled prefix, faithfully capturing the sequential dependence of verification on earlier proposals. By accounting for the parameter dependence of the proposal distribution, we derive an unbiased gradient estimator for this single-round objective under stochastic verification. We evaluate D-REAL on DSpark and DFlash2 with Qwen3-8B as the target model across ten benchmarks. Starting from baselines whose mean acceptance length has plateaued, one epoch of D-REAL post-training consistently improves the benchmark-averaged mean acceptance length by up to 0.23 tokens across both architectures under greedy (T = 0.0) and stochastic (T = 1.0) sampling, translating into up to a 9.4% end-to-end serving throughput improvement.

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Noise Propagation and Non-Uniqueness in Three-Material Dual Energy CT with a Path Length Constraint
papers.abstract: Objective: Using a path length constraint with dual energy computed tomography (DECT) data, a sample can be decomposed into three basis materials. We aim to analyze the stability of such a system by presenting a noise propagation framework for optimizing the contrast to noise ratio (CNR) of virtual monochromatic images (VMIs) and by studying instances where sinogram decompositions are not unique. Approach: We extend a noise propagation framework developed for two-material DECT to three materials. Using the Jacobian of the system, we identify tube voltage pairings with good noise properties and obtain analytical expressions for VMI CNR. We apply spectral theorem to identify the best CNR possible in a linear combination of basis images. By using a reduced two-dimensional problem, we develop the sampling isoline recovery algorithm (SIRA) to study non-unique sinogram decompositions in this system. Main results: Using our noise propagation framework with a realistic breast phantom consisting of adipose, glandular tissue, and iodine, we find an ideal tube pairing of 34 kVp and 69 kVp, and a maximum VMI CNR of a spiculated lesion of 9.9. By allowing arbitrary linear combinations of basis material images, we find a CNR of 10.2 can be achieved. In a realistic phantom with a cardiac plaque, we find non-unique water, bone and iodine decompositions, and show that qualitatively accurate reconstructions can be obtained using SIRA. Significance: We developed a framework for direct optimization of VMI CNR in a three-material DECT decomposition and showed that an arbitrary linear combination of basis material images can achieve a higher CNR than a strict VMI. We demonstrate the presence of non-unique sinogram decompositions in three-material DECT with a data constraint.

papers.title: Approximate Recall, Approximate Forecasts: Recall as a Diagnostic for LLM Forecasting Errors
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit approximate recall: they retain coarse associations about past events while losing fidelity on specific details. Past research on LLMs has quantified different models' forecasting ability in real-world events using prediction markets, but has not studied how losing said fidelity impacts their forecasting abilities. For example: while an LLM correctly recalls that the answer to: ''Did Anna Sawai win the Best Drama Actress in the 76th Emmy Awards?'' is ''Yes,'' it incorrectly states the event date as September 22 rather than September 15. In this paper, we introduce a novel metric called the Recall Fidelity Score to study how imprecision in internalized knowledge propagates to forecasting capability on future events. On resolved historical markets, we find that higher local recall fidelity around semantically similar past events predicts lower forecasting error on resolved markets, and the same signal predicts smaller distance from open markets prices.

papers.title: Symplectic Normal Coordinates Flow for Generative Modeling of Hamiltonian Systems
papers.abstract: In conditioned generative models of physical systems, the densities at different values of the conditioning parameters are often related through symplectic transformations. For stable linear Hamiltonian systems, there exists a symplectic transformation to "normal coordinates" such that the dynamics is reduced to rotations in each phase-space plane. This picture extends to the nonlinear case where, away from resonances, the Birkhoff normal form again consists of rotations in phase space, now with amplitude dependence. In this work, we introduce an invertible symplectic flow layer consisting of amplitude-dependent rotations in learned normal coordinates. We derive the condition under which the nonlinear rotation layer is symplectic and detail an architecture that guarantees it. Experiments are carried out on three conditional generative modeling problems: a synthetic chain of coupled nonlinear oscillators and two problems from accelerator physics. We show empirically that normalizing flows with the new layers achieve competitive or superior negative log-likelihoods compared to baseline flows, with gains that grow with the strength of the nonlinearity on the synthetic system.

papers.title: Nonasymptotic causal structure learning in generalized linear DAGs with continuous optimization
papers.abstract: We study the problem of learning directed acyclic graphs from observational data in nonlinear models and provide finite-sample, nonasymptotic statistical guarantees in these models. Although widely studied, statistical guarantees for gradient-based methods in nonlinear models are missing from the literature. Under a generalized linear model for each node, we analyze a global nonsmooth objective combining an exact acyclicity constraint with a quasi-minimax concave penalty, which can be optimized via standard gradient-based solvers. We establish finite-sample guarantees under this model, including the most widely used logistic and Poisson models. Experiments corroborate structure recovery accuracy and computational performance, including both standardized data and negative controls as baselines.

papers.title: That Time of the Year Again: Government Pay Revisions in the Aggregate Economy
papers.abstract: Public pay is set by law in nominal terms, so inflation erodes its real value between legal acts until the government revises it. I model each revision as the choice of a forward-looking government, shaped by two costs that push in opposite directions. A fixed cost of acting makes revisions large and rare, whereas a convex cost of financing the increase at once makes them small and frequent. Through the budget, each revision also moves debt and the risk of fiscal stress under which the next one is made. In the documented pay decisions of eleven countries, pay set at discretion erodes against prices and private earnings and is restored in discrete steps, every cut was decided during market stress or an adjustment program, and court rulings drove a wedge between the cuts legislated, the cuts paid and the cuts that lasted. Estimated on the legal acts, the model reproduces the documented paths of pay in most countries when data and simulations are measured the same way. In Portugal's estimated model, the savings that the Treasury requires once spreads rise produce the cuts, the debt overhang holds pay down after the crisis, and a court that strikes cuts after they take effect invites cuts it will strike. Review of cuts before they took effect would have lowered the social cost of Portugal's crisis relative to review after the fact, and partial indexation would have paid in Bangladesh unless its automatic increases were costly to finance.

papers.title: Complementarity-Driven Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment for Zero-Shot EEG-to-Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Decoding visual information from EEG is central to brain--computer interfaces and brain-inspired intelligence, and contrastive alignment with pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) has become the dominant paradigm. However, existing methods align EEG solely with CLIP-family VFMs, leaving hierarchical visual information in neural responses under-exploited. To address this gap, we formulate a mechanism-paradigm correspondence view linking hierarchical visual processing (from appearance to semantics) to the complementary biases of cross-paradigm VFMs, with image-only models (e.g., DINO) and image--text models (e.g., CLIP) capturing distinct facets of this hierarchy. Guided by this view, we propose the Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment (DTHA) framework. Concretely, a shared EEG encoder is supervised by frozen multi-blur CLIP and shallow DINOv2 teachers via dual-branch contrastive alignment, so each branch fully supervises the visual cues it emphasizes. A fused-retrieval objective learns adaptive weights to combine their complementary visual representations for zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval. For the shared EEG encoder, we introduce the Attentive Modulated Scalp-Pattern Bank Encoder (AMSPBE), combining temporo-spatial attention with a learnable scalp-pattern bank for accurate, interpretable visual feature extraction, while modeling regional temporal dynamics and filter-bank topographies. On THINGS-EEG zero-shot retrieval, DTHA achieves 92.4% Top-1 accuracy, exceeding prior state of the art by 12.4 percentage points. Spatial, spectral, and representational-similarity analyses, together with THINGS-MEG evaluation, validate DTHA's effectiveness, biological plausibility, and cross-modality generalization. This complementarity-driven perspective shows that supervision from cross-paradigm VFMs enables more complete extraction of hierarchical visual information from brain activity.

papers.title: Beyond Discrete Ancestry Groups: Distribution-Aware In-Context Learning for Cancer Outcome Prediction Across the Genetic Ancestry Continuum
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for omics-based prediction of cancer outcomes are commonly built on aggregated data without distinguishing ancestry groups, or under an ancestry-discrete design, which partitions samples into ancestry groups and fits a separate model within each group. Recent evidence shows that this approach is inherently limited: predictive accuracy declines with genetic distance from the training samples, even within a single ancestry group, because the data distribution shifts continuously rather than only between predefined categories. In this paper, we propose distribution-aware in-context learning (DA-ICL) for ancestry-continuum modeling. Our method extends conventional ancestry-discrete modeling to ancestry-continuum modeling, capturing the nonstationary omics-endpoint relationship across the genetic continuum while enabling efficient modeling through an in-context learning foundation model. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating the superiority of the ancestry-continuum over ancestry-discrete modeling, along with empirical results supporting the proposed framework. Source code is available at https://github.com/ai4pm/DA-ICL-Continuum.

papers.title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schr\"odinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

papers.title: MoT3DVG: A Benchmark for Outdoor 3D Visual Grounding with Motion-Aware Descriptions and Temporal Cues
papers.abstract: 3D visual grounding (3DVG) localizes language-referred objects in 3D scenes, with broad applicability in both indoor and outdoor environments. However, existing 3DVG research focuses on static indoor objects, limiting its use in dynamic outdoor autonomous driving. Motion descriptions, which capture the temporal dynamics of moving objects, offer a promising way to address this challenge. We therefore introduce MoT3DVG, a large-scale dataset for dynamic-aware outdoor 3DVG with temporally evolving motion descriptions. It contains 850 scenarios with 31,128 frames from nuScenes dataset, and provides 144,568 language prompts with motion-aware descriptions for dynamic objects across time. We further propose DynaVG, a novel framework that effectively leverages temporal cues for outdoor 3DVG. In addition to the standard modality-specific encoders, DynaVG introduces a Short-Long Integrated Dynamic Encoding (SLIDE) module before the language-point cloud alignment. SLIDE models both local motion cues and global temporal context via short-term window encoding and long-term window shifting. Extensive experiments demonstrate its state-of-the-art performance on MoT3DVG, validating the effectiveness of motion-aware encoding. Our work reveals open challenges and promising directions for future research in outdoor 3DVG.

papers.title: MixRoute: Rethinking Single-Distribution Training for Generalizable Neural Routing
papers.abstract: Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) is a promising paradigm for solving routing problems, yet its generalization across diverse data distributions remains a critical bottleneck. Existing methods typically tackle cross-distribution generalization through complex multi-distribution training or intricate meta-learning schemes, implicitly presuming that single-distribution training yields a weak zero-shot baseline. In this paper, we demonstrate that the potential of single-distribution training has been substantially underestimated and can be unlocked by a simple architectural inductive bias: Mix Normalization. To approach this, we first construct a comprehensive benchmark spanning three representative routing problems and 179 fine-grained datasets, capturing diverse shifts in node coordinates, customer demands, capacity and time windows. Building on this benchmark, we propose MixRoute, a neural framework that adaptively combines normalization statistics at different granularities to mitigate varying distribution shifts. Trained exclusively on uniform distributions, MixRoute generalizes effectively to a wide range of unseen distributions without any distribution-specific adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MixRoute consistently achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot generalization. Our work revisits normalization as a parsimonious alternative for zero-shot generalization against complex training-adaptation schemes.

papers.title: CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
papers.abstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. To address these limitations, we propose CSG-Nav, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion. CSG-Nav integrates three complementary fusion mechanisms. First, semantic-source fusion integrates open-vocabulary detection results, detection confidence, scene observations, and relational reasoning to produce more reliable direction-level semantic scores and suppress hallucination-induced directional bias. Second, spatial-confidence fusion weights multi-view semantic evidence using a Gaussian decay function, suppressing unreliable distant observations while accumulating spatially consistent exploration preferences. Third, semantic-geometric decision fusion combines semantic target detection with depth-based 3D localization to support physically grounded stopping decisions. Experiments on HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate competitive zero-shot performance, achieving success rates of 58.9%, 71.6%, and 44.3%. Fusion-level ablations and real-world deployments in indoor and outdoor environments further verify the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception. Code is available at https://xr-ui.github.io/CSGNav.github.io/

papers.title: One2N: Recursive refinement breaks the resolution barrier for Earth-system AI
papers.abstract: Earth-system AI models approach kilometre-scale resolution, but halving grid spacing quadruples the grid-point count and end-to-end training cost. We introduce One2N, a recursive incremental framework extending a coarse model through $N$ levels of cross-resolution residual correction. At each level the parent is frozen and excluded from backpropagation, so its activations and optimizer states are never retained; only a tier-specific module is trained. A single refinement level on the NeuralGCM-0.7$^\circ$ baseline yields the two-level One2N-0.07$^\circ$, trained on one 80 GB GPU. Against HRES-0.07$^\circ$ and ERA5-0.25$^\circ$ analyses it matches its parent's tropospheric skill while reducing upper-stratospheric errors and resolving finer structure. Tropical-cyclone track errors nearly match the parent's and are lower than Pangu-Weather-0.25$^\circ$ at medium range; RMSE is lower than that model's on 93.46% of common targets. One2N thus turns an existing forecasting system, or an inexpensively trained coarse baseline, into a reusable foundation for high-resolution development, breaking the resolution barrier.

papers.title: TMT: Adapting CLIP to Infrared Imagery via Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer
papers.abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP achieve strong performance across computer vision tasks, yet their image-text alignment is less reliable for infrared (IR) imagery because large-scale pre-training is dominated by visible-spectrum data. Due to the high cost of the infrared-text labeling, we investigate adapting CLIP to IR through only paired infrared-visible images, which requires considering modality-specific knowledge while preserving scene content and CLIP's image-text alignment. To achieve this, we propose TMT (Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer), which adapts CLIP's image encoder through a text-defined infrared-to-visible direction and supervision from paired IR-visible images. First, we found that modality discrepancy can be described by corresponding text embeddings, thus using the direction of text embedding differences to guide the knowledge transfer between visible and infrared modalities without erasing infrared-specific information. To enhance the representation of semantics and details of infrared images, we introduce Generative-Perceptual Co-Supervision that combines semantic alignment from CLIP visible image encoder with diffusion noise-prediction feedbacks. On four source-disjoint IR classification benchmarks, TMT achieves the highest mean zero-shot accuracy among the compared methods (48.92%). It also achieves the best IR-text retrieval results among the compared methods without infrared-text supervision during adaptation and the highest open-vocabulary segmentation mIoU on both CART and SemanticRT among the CLIP-like methods.

papers.title: When Handshakes Go Dark: An Adaptive Semantic-Sequential Fusion Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is essential for network security monitoring and traffic management. Self-supervised pre-training can learn reusable representations from large-scale unlabeled traffic, but TLS 1.3, QUIC, and privacy mechanisms such as Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) increasingly conceal application, handshake, and service-identifying information. Observable upper-layer bytes are therefore dominated by ciphertext, weakening the link between raw-byte patterns and application semantics and limiting model generalization. Moreover, the availability and discriminative value of observable information vary across protocols, protection profiles, and tasks, complicating classification across diverse scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose FLARE, a Field-aware Learning and Adaptive Representation Fusion framework for encrypted traffic classification. FLARE pre-trains a BERT-based packet encoder through Masked Field Prediction, which reconstructs masked tokens from field-structured context. During downstream fine-tuning, the parameters of the pre-trained packet encoder remain frozen, and a packet-level gated module adaptively combines protocol-semantic representations with directional packet-length representations. A flow-level encoder then models inter-packet dependencies for classification. We evaluate FLARE on eight datasets spanning diverse encrypted-traffic tasks, including CipherSpectrum and VisQUIC for strongly encrypted scenarios. FLARE achieves superior performance over baselines across the eight datasets, exceeding the strongest pre-trained baseline by 10.92 percentage points on QUIC website fingerprinting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of field-aware pre-training and adaptive semantic-sequential fusion under constrained observability.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(\delta>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.

papers.title: Particle Swarm Optimization Strategies for Lensed Gravitational Waves: Parameter Estimation, Source Classification, and Accelerated Sampling
papers.abstract: The detection and parameter estimation of lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals are crucial for astrophysics and cosmology. Strong lensing introduces extra parameters, rendering the search high-dimensional, multi-modal, and strongly nonlinear. We apply Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to the search, parameter estimation, and classification of lensed compact binary coalescence GWs within a four-detector coherent network. Using the restricted 2-PN waveform as a template and a model-independent double-image lens parameterization, we assess PSO on both model-matched 2-PN signals and template-mismatched IMRPhenomD signals. Results show effective recovery of chirp mass, mass ratio, sky location, and lens parameters in the 2-PN case, with mass biases appearing under waveform mismatch. A three-class classification pipeline combining 12 PSO runs, majority voting, and a flux ratio threshold achieves 86.19% accuracy in distinguishing lensed GWs, unlensed GWs, and noise. We further propose PSO_GAUSS_MIX method, which constructs a Gaussian mixture prior from PSO estimates for nested sampling, yielding speedups of 1.38x in the restricted 2-PN cases while preserving posterior accuracy. These results establish PSO as an efficient optimizer for lensed GW searches and an effective prior constructor for Bayesian parameter estimation.
