Building upon our interacting mean-field neural stochastic differential equation framework, we present stMIND (Spatiotemporal Multiscale Interaction Neural Dynamics), a continuous-time generative framework that infers coupled molecular, spatial, and proliferation dynamics from unmatched spatiotemporal snapshots. stMIND decomposes cellular expression velocity vector/drift into three interpretable operators: a cell-intrinsic program, a local graph-difference attention operator that aggregates relative expression differences and spatial geometry within a co-evolving physical radius, and a nonlocal mean-field attention operator that captures long-range population context beyond the immediate neighborhood. By evolving dynamic spatial neighborhoods alongside cellular migration and enforcing orthogonality between intrinsic and interaction-driven drifts, stMIND resolves scale-specific intercellular influences through optimal transport in joint expression-position space. In axolotl and zebrafish benchmarks, stMIND leads in expression prediction, anatomical consistency and spatial coherence. Ablations confirm the need to combine disjoint local and nonlocal operators. It reveals a regenerative transition in axolotl telencephalon 10 to 15 days after injury, with a drift energy surge followed by nonlocal dominance and local counterbalance varying by cell type in reactive ependymoglial niches. It tracks developmental vector fields across zebrafish stages.

papers.title: Optical frequency combs on thin-film lithium niobate: from principles to applications
papers.abstract: Optical frequency combs, consisting of mutually coherent and equally spaced spectral lines, provide a powerful means of synthesizing, distributing, and processing optical frequencies on chip. Among integrated photonic platforms, thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is particularly attractive for comb generation because it combines strong electro-optic (EO) functionality, accessible $\chi^{(2)}$ and $\chi^{(3)}$ nonlinearities, low-loss nanophotonic confinement, and versatile dispersion engineering. This review summarizes the physical foundations and representative realizations of TFLN combs, and discusses their applications in optical communication, microwave photonics, optical computing, and precision metrology. The integration of nonlinear functionality, EO control, and passive photonic components is expected to advance compact, energy-efficient comb sources and broaden the utility of TFLN in integrated photonics and quantum optics.

authors.name: Yikun Chen
authors.institution: Macau University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Cheng Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
papers.abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $\Pi$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(\Pi)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(\eta)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(\eta)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(\eta))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

papers.title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
papers.abstract:
For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations.
  We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

authors.name: Ping Zhong
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

papers.title: Cross-Modal Associations in Creativity: Evaluating Word-Image Pairing in Humans and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Given differences in the associative memory architectures of humans and AI, it is not clear whether AI generates and interprets visual-linguistic associations the way humans do. To investigate this, human participants and two large language models (LLMs), ChatGPT and Gemini, were asked to generate novel words and corresponding images that form meaningfully linked dyads. The LLMs and a second group of human participants were presented with shuffled sets of these words and images and asked to rematch them in ways they felt were most meaningful. Humans performed similarly regardless of whether the pairs were human or LLM-generated, while LLMs were better at matching LLM-generated pairs. Overall, LLMs outperformed humans at recovering the intended pairings. These findings suggest that despite architectural differences, the way in which AI generates and detects associations between language and visual stimuli is not only like that of hu-mans, but they may be superior at recognizing cross-domain associations that humans find meaningful.

authors.name: Liane Gabora
authors.institution: University of British Columbia, Okanagan Campus

papers.title: TALK: One-Shot Batch Design for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
papers.abstract: Protein variant effect prediction is central to understanding protein function and guiding protein engineering, yet experimental labels remain costly. In many protein experiments, the variants that can be assayed are dictated by protocol constraints, while the variants that need accurate prediction may lie in a different or broader region of the landscape. This assay-prediction mismatch makes candidate-local criteria such as predicted function, uncertainty, or exploration value insufficient for measurement design. Given a protocol-defined accessible space and a limited budget, we ask which variants should be assayed so that the resulting data best improves landscape prediction. We propose TALK, which estimates each candidate's contribution through posterior coupling between accessible and target variants and reduces redundant information within the batch. Across retrospective ProteinGym and FLIP protocols, TALK generally improves target-space prediction under limited measurement budgets. These results point to a practical two-stage workflow: first, spend a limited assay budget on variants selected to be informative for the target landscape and train a predictive model from the measured labels; then use this model to score and prioritize high-potential variants. Code is available at https://github.com/joehuang618/TALK.

authors.name: Ao Shen
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
papers.abstract: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

authors.name: Shuai Xue
authors.institution: First Bethune Hospital of Jilin University

papers.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

authors.name: Xiang Bai
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Answer or Defer? Testing VLMs' Stated Confidence on Brain MRI
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) could support medical-image interpretation, but their use requires deciding which interpretations to accept and which images to refer to a clinician. We test whether thresholding stated confidence can retain useful coverage while limiting errors among accepted answers, and how this depends on the population. Eight open-weight VLMs, including two reasoning models, assess 3,888 brain MRI slices from post-treatment glioma patients (BraTS 2024) and healthy volunteers (IXI) for tumor or gross abnormality. BraTS labels are mask-derived; IXI slices are treated as negatives. On BraTS, no threshold selects a nonempty set with at most 5% empirical error for any model, even when chosen retrospectively. This also holds for four models evaluated on a large-lesion, distant-negative subset. At a 10% error budget, Gemma-4-12B retains 24.4% of slices and every other model at most 2.5%. To investigate this limited selection ability, we separate confidence differences between predicted answers from differences within each answer. For four models with available outcome-level summaries, pooled mean confidence differs more between answers than between correct and incorrect responses within each answer. A covariance decomposition explains how this pattern can produce opposite confidence-correctness associations across populations. At a 20% error budget, accepting every "tumor" answer covers more slices than any confidence threshold for two models. These findings caution against using unvalidated stated confidence as a standalone deferral signal and support population-specific validation before deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/amir-sbg/VLM-Answer-or-Defer.

authors.name: Amir Sabbaghziarani
authors.institution: Center for Translational Research in Neuroimaging and Data Science

authors.name: Sergey Plis
authors.institution: Center for Translational Research in Neuroimaging and Data Science

papers.title: Soft-then-Hard: Joint Link Association and Precoding Optimization for LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Spatial multiplexing in dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks is hindered by two bottlenecks. First, line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant propagation from a high orbital altitude places the users in a narrow angular region, which limits the spatial resolution achievable by a single satellite. Second, the visible satellites cause severe inter-satellite interference. Both effects call for joint link association and precoding, because the association decides which users are served together and which streams interfere. However, conventional block coordinate descent with hard association updates suffers from premature turning-off, where an inactive link loses precoder power and cannot be reactivated in subsequent iterations. To overcome this limitation, we propose a soft-then-hard update scheme that relaxes the association into continuous weights via iterative scaling, keeping candidate links active. Annealing progressively concentrates the association weights as the precoders are updated, after which a single hard matching determines the serving links. We further extend this framework to the LEO space-time channel, where distinct Doppler shifts provide user separability beyond angular geometry. Numerical results show that, over the space-time channel, the proposed design outperforms the baselines while effectively exploiting this separability.

authors.name: Jeonghun Park
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: Tracing MCP Security Vulnerabilities: Constructing and Analyzing an MCP Security Vulnerability Dataset
papers.abstract: As a core protocol for integrating large language models (LLMs) with external data sources and tools, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has quickly become a key interface in emerging AI agent systems. As the MCP ecosystem expands, reported vulnerabilities have also increased, creating a growing software-security attack surface. However, MCP vulnerability information remains scattered, noisy, and difficult to study systematically. This paper addresses that gap by constructing a curated MCP vulnerability dataset from CVE disclosures. Starting from 119 MCP-related records retrieved through February 2026, we filter unrelated cases out and obtain a validated snapshot of 24 MCP vulnerabilities. Our filtering methodology explicitly addresses acronym ambiguity and achieves 96.7% inter-rater agreement on a sampled exclusion audit while retaining all known high-severity MCP cases identified in public advisories. Using this initial dataset snapshot, we find that 87.5% of validated vulnerabilities are Critical or High severity, and that injection and path traversal vulnerabilities account for 66.7% of cases. We further identify recurring issues involving insufficient input validation, inadequate access control, and protocol-level security gaps. Through six representative case studies, we illustrate common exploitation patterns and map them to practical defenses. We release the dataset, reproducibility tooling, and a sustainable maintenance workflow as a foundation for future MCP security measurement, benchmarking, and defense research.

authors.name: Xu He
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: CoRA-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation by Context Selectors Under Token Budgets
papers.abstract: Context selection can reduce input length during long-input inference but can remove evidence required to answer a query. We introduce CoRA-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating evidence preservation under shared token budgets. We compare head and tail truncation, BM25, dense retrieval, dense retrieval with reranking, LLMLingua-2, and Provence across BABILong, LOONG Financial Spotlight, a custom NoLiMa diagnostic, and LongMemEval. Evidence-preservation results reveal task-dependent tradeoffs: BM25 achieves 0.921 supporting-fact recall on BABILong at 128K, dense retrieval and dense reranking each achieve 0.908 needle recall on NoLiMa at 64K, and dense retrieval achieves 0.993 answer-bearing-turn recall on LongMemEval at 64K. Evidence, token retention, and complementary reader evaluations use the same selected contexts. Reader evaluations use dataset-native answer metrics and three runs on the same questions, with paired bootstrap confidence intervals. At a 32K budget, BM25 achieves 46.20% BABILong answer accuracy and dense retrieval achieves 71.13% LongMemEval accuracy. The results show that method rankings vary across evidence types and between evidence recall and downstream accuracy.

papers.title: Thermally unfavorable conditions of volatile existence in near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the Hayabusa extended mission's target
papers.abstract: The near-Earth asteroid 1998 KY26, the target of the Hayabusa2# extended mission, has been proposed as a dark comet that may host volatiles, particularly water, owing to an anomalous out-of-plane nongravitational acceleration that may result from outgassing. This asteroid, however, may also belong to a largely anhydrous taxonomic group. Whether outgassing-driven acceleration is possible strongly depends on how the asteroid stores volatiles in its interior and releases them upon heating at the surface. Thus far, the contentious topic of the existence of volatiles on 1998 KY26 that can cause outgassing has not been extensively examined from a thermophysical standpoint. Here, we show that all locations on the surface or in the interior of 1998 KY26 have orbit-averaged temperatures significantly above the sublimation point of volatiles in vacuum. Across 13 thermal characterizations, this observation is found to be consistent despite parameter variations in equivalent diameter, thermal conductivity, Bond albedo, specific heat capacity, and spin pole ecliptic latitude and longitude. Our temperature model results indicate that the water outgassing rate on 1998 KY26 would be too high to maintain buried ice, refining the understanding of the asteroid's composition.

papers.title: Vision Language Models for Primary Structure Threat Identification in Wildland Urban Interface Fires
papers.abstract: Wildland urban interface (WUI) fires increasingly threaten communities and infrastructure, motivating the need for rapid visual assessment. Recent research has focused primarily on detecting fire and assessing post-event damage. However, structure-level fire threat identification during active WUI fire events remains underexplored. This study evaluates Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct for this active-fire decision using two separately scored tracks: 1,824 synthetic images from 491 designed WUI scenarios and 45 frames from a controlled-burn experiment conducted in collaboration with Columbus Fire & EMS Department. Under zero-shot prompting, the model returned valid target fields for 1,808 synthetic images and 39 controlled-burn frames. Accuracy among valid outputs was 94.0% for the synthetic track and 69.2% for the controlled-burn track, compared with a 16.0% random-selection baseline for the latter. On the synthetic track, the model generally identified the intended target across varied designed WUI scenarios when the relevant fire-spread cues were visually distinct. Controlled-burn performance was well above random selection, but errors showed difficulty interpreting spatial relations in complex scenes. The dual-track protocol provides scalable stress testing in designed scenarios and a controlled-burn reference for assessing model behavior under physical fire conditions. Future work can use the synthetic data for VLM post-training and then evaluate the adapted models on larger and more diverse real WUI fire datasets.

papers.title: Learning Actionable Information Landscapes for Multimodal Active Sensing in Hawkmoths
papers.abstract: Animals integrate information across sensory modalities to guide exploration, suggesting that they maintain internal estimates of where actions are expected to reduce uncertainty. However, how such action-conditioned information maps are learned from multimodal sensory experience remains unclear, as previous studies have been largely confined to unimodal sensing frameworks. We introduce a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks. A variational generative model trained on simulated environments recovers modality-specific information landscapes over the action space, capturing how visual patterns, surface geometry, and mechanosensory cues shape the value of exploratory actions. These learned maps are consistent with several features of hawkmoth behavior, including nonzero tracking offsets, probing along visual patterns, and geometry-dependent exploration. Applying the model to behavioral data from flower tracking and nectary search, we find that natural trajectories tend to occupy regions of high uncertainty reduction in these learned maps. Building on these observations, we develop an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty. In nectary search, uncertainty gating improves learning relative to exploit-only, $\epsilon$-greedy, fixed-time, and uncertainty-calibrated non-lexicographic controls, with better generalization and robustness to sensory and curvature shifts. These results link information landscapes learned through generative modeling to biological sensing and embodied exploration.

authors.name: Yaqing Wang
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

papers.title: Scalable Counterfactual Explanations for Time Series via Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Generating counterfactual (CF) explanations for time series is challenging due to complex temporal dependencies and the computational inefficiency of traditional instance-specific optimization. We propose a policy learning framework for counterfactual explanation in time series, trained as a one-step contextual-bandit policy-learning problem. By training an actor-critic agent in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder, our method learns a transferable policy that captures global structural regularities. Unlike existing methods that rely on iterative optimization for each new input, the learned policy enables direct generation of valid and plausible counterfactuals through a single forward pass, avoiding per-instance optimization at inference time. Experiments on 13 UCR benchmark datasets show that our framework achieves high validity and strong plausibility across multiple anomaly detection metrics. Overall, by decoupling counterfactual generation from per-instance optimization, the proposed method provides an efficient and scalable alternative to existing approaches for time series counterfactual explanations.

papers.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
papers.abstract: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

papers.title: Distilling Instructions into Weights: Closed-Form Edits Fix a Robot Policy's Misreading
papers.abstract: Generalist robot policies often fail at one step of a task they can otherwise perform. We ask whether such a failure can be repaired by editing the policy's weights directly, without gradients, training data, or a change to the instruction. Told to put the cube then the banana in the bowl, a zero-shot $\pi_{0.5}$ vision-language-action policy in RoboLab releases the cube before it reaches the bowl. Replaying 21 of these decisions under rewordings shows that it binds "in the bowl" to the wrong object. Closed-form instruction distillation copies the per-layer effect of an explicit rewording into the language model's MLP weights. On 128 held-out seeds, success rises from 27 to 106 episodes, with 81 fixed and 2 broken ($p=7\times10^{-22}$), while an update of the same size in random directions leaves success unchanged. The edit also lifts two other tasks without detectable harm on the remaining 13, and a variant that stores 0.16% of the parameter count keeps most of its effect. Placed in the action expert or action head instead, the same distillation helps less or not at all. Our released tool reproduced the fix end to end on new held-out seeds, from 8/64 to 36/64. Edits aimed at perception, a missing grasp, contact physics, or the gripper threshold did not help, and of seven blind Claude Opus editors, only the one given the misread instruction produced an edit that passed held-out scoring. These results suggest that weight edits work best when a known-good input already exists to distil. Because reruns with unchanged weights flip about a third of paired outcomes, evaluations should pair seeds, rerun the unedited policy, and confirm gains on held-out seeds.

papers.title: Can LLM Agents Organize Their Own Memory?
papers.abstract: In most LLM agents, weights are fixed after deployment, so new information must be retained in external memory. Existing approaches often rely on predefined records and fixed organizational rules, which cannot readily accommodate evolving tasks and interactions. This raises the question: can LLM agents organize their own memory using ordinary documents? We introduce self-organized memory (SoMem), a framework that stores memory in linked documents. The agent decides what to summarize, how to group related information, and when to revise existing topics, and every summary it produces stays linked to the original interactions as evidence. The runtime validates updates and automatically derives temporal, relational, and recent-memory views from the organized content. At query time, the agent chooses what to search and read, following document links and inspecting original evidence as needed. On LoCoMo, BEAM-100K, and LongMemEval-S, SoMem outperforms the strongest baseline by 2.66, 3.10, and 2.00 percentage points, respectively. The constructed memory can be reused across models, and additional reasoning effort can further improve answer quality. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of agents organizing and using their own persistent memory through ordinary documents. Code is available at: https://github.com/Qi202/SoMem.

authors.name: Jinyang Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xiangyu Zhao
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.abstract: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only $3$K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

authors.name: Harold Haodong Chen
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

authors.name: Zilong Dong
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Nanoenergy and Nanosystems

papers.title: Domain Generalization for Style-Debiased Object Detection via Label-Consistent Training across Multiple Styles
papers.abstract: Domain generalization (DG) for object detection aims to improve model performance on unseen target domains. Existing detectors, however, suffer substantial degradation on visually distinct unseen domains, as models confined to limited training styles tend to overfit superficial statistical cues rather than object-level semantics. Motivated by human perception, which attends primarily to semantically relevant features while ignoring irrelevant style cues, we propose Origin-Anchored Multi-Style Consistency (OAMSC), a source-only framework that couples multi-style data synthesis with cross-style consistency learning to suppress style-sensitive shortcut learning. For data preparation, we leverage off-the-shelf diffusion models to expand the source datasets into 20 distinct styles, with all generated images manually verified to ensure that object instances and annotations remain consistent across style variants. During training, we impose Origin-anchored consistency constraints at scene and object levels to reinforce the learning of domain-stable features while suppressing the influence of style-sensitive cues. Extensive experiments and ablation studies on multiple challenging DG benchmarks demonstrate the consistent effectiveness and strong generalization performance of OAMSC across diverse domain shifts. Notably, our approach applies to both one-stage and two-stage detectors, while its data-centric design is complementary in principle to other DG methods. The training code and two style-transfer datasets constructed for the experiments, comprising approximately 180K images in total, are publicly available on GitHub.

papers.title: Scaling Optimization-Oriented Hypernetworks for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.abstract: We present a hypernetwork that generates the parameters of an implicit neural representation (INR) for a given signal in a single forward pass, without test-time optimization. Existing hypernetworks for this problem either ignore the chain-rule structure of the test-time optimization that produces an INR or, when they preserve it, instantiate the structure with MLPs whose parameter count grows quartically in target-network width. Our central contribution is to show that this parameter-count cost is structural to the MLP instantiation, not to the optimization-oriented principle of preserving chain-rule structure, and to resolve it by replacing the MLP body with attention. The resulting hypernetwork combines three design choices: an output-neuron-centric tokenization that aligns the token axis with each layer's output-neuron axis; an information-flow consistency rule that fixes the role of every cross-attention module from the representation its output should occupy; and a token-space iterative rollout that realizes the five quantities one optimization step on the target INR computes as five cross-attention modules with parameter count independent of target-network width. Across five 2D and 3D INR generation benchmarks, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art single-pass and optimization-oriented baselines; scales to target-network widths at which the MLP-based optimization-oriented paradigm exhausts GPU memory; and produces the highest result on NeRF generation without ground-truth INR weights supervision.

authors.name: Lulu Cai
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

authors.name: Youyi Zheng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yanchao Yang
authors.institution: Macau University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: Modern visuotactile sensors primarily sense contact by imaging the deformation of a compliant interface. Using techniques such as photometric stereo, they can recover detailed contact geometry, often represented as surface normals or depth. However, force-related information typically still needs to be inferred indirectly through calibration, geometric reconstruction, or learned mappings. Mechanochromic photonic-crystal (PC) materials offer an alternative physical encoding mechanism: contact loading changes their periodic microstructure and spectral response, directly transforming local stress into a spatially resolved structural-color field. Despite this potential, PC materials have rarely been explored as visuotactile sensors for closed-loop robot learning. We present PCTac, an open-source mechanochromic PC fingertip that uses a dense hue field as its tactile observation. Loading characterization demonstrates a repeatable relationship between the applied normal load and the observed hue response. We further integrate this representation directly into a Diffusion Policy and evaluate it on three real-robot manipulation tasks. Across 90 physical rollouts, PCTac Hue achieves 68 successes (75.6\%), compared with 60 (66.7\%) for PCTac RGB, 57 (63.3\%) for Wedge RGB, and 29 (32.2\%) for vision-only. PCTac Hue also achieves the highest observed success rate on each evaluated task, including Perturbed Test-Tube Insertion, where it achieves 16/30 successes versus 13/30 for tactile RGB baselines and 1/30 for vision-only. These results demonstrate the potential of mechanochromic structural color as a compact, load-sensitive tactile representation for robot learning and closed-loop manipulation. Project page: https://bey0ndt1me.github.io/PCTac-page/.

authors.name: Xuanshuo Liu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Junzhe Dai
authors.institution: Sichuan Academy of Medical Sciences & Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital

authors.name: Ziyuan Jiao
authors.institution: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation
papers.abstract: Ensuring safe and reliable navigation under diverse sources of uncertainty remains a central challenge for autonomous systems. Within distributional reinforcement learning (DistRL), Implicit Quantile Networks (IQN) have attracted interest for navigation under uncertainty because they enable risk adaptation through flexible quantile sampling. Existing approaches, however, typically use a fixed or randomly sampled Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) level during training and adjust the risk level during deployment using hand-tuned hyperparameters or external sensor signals. This scalar-CVaR formulation confines learning to a narrow family of tail-risk preferences, creating a mismatch between training-time preference exposure and deployment-time risk adjustment. We instead represent variations in risk preference as shifts in quantile-weight distributions and expose the agent to diverse preferences through preference-guided exploration. At deployment, we optimize against the worst-case preference distribution to derive a conservative policy that accounts for multiple risk profiles. This reduces hyperparameter tuning and reliance on limited sensor signals under partial observability. Experiments across simulated environments and vehicle platforms show that our method reduces collisions while improving task success.

papers.title: Local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates for the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on collapsing manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates for positive solutions to the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with a small scale-invariant integral bound on the negative part of the Ricci curvature in $L^p$, where $p>n/2$. No uniform lower bound on the volume of unit balls is assumed, and hence the results apply to manifolds that may collapse. For the fast diffusion equation, we obtain the estimate in the range $1-2/n<m<1$. The auxiliary function method, which was designed for the heat equation under integral curvature conditions, is not directly applicable to those two nonlinear equations. The pressure operator in both cases contains a solution-dependent coefficient, which produces a residual term involving $\partial_t J$ in the evolution inequality. Its treatment requires a positive lower bound for $J$, and moreover, control of $-\partial_t\log J$. We obtain these bounds by linearizing the auxiliary equation, applying Duhamel's formula, and combining local Dirichlet heat kernel estimates with a singular Volterra inequality. Additionally, in the fast diffusion case, the negativity of $v$ changes the sign structure of the evolution inequality, so a separate coercive estimate is required to close the argument. Local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates follow for both diffusion regimes and integrating them along space-time curves gives the corresponding Harnack inequalities.

papers.title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we consider a degenerate elliptic equation on a Riemannian manifold whose weight vanishes at an interior point $p$, and prove the strong unique continuation property (SUCP) at $p$. The curved setting gives rise to intrinsic geometric error terms that obstruct the analytic estimates available in the Euclidean case. To overcome this, we introduce a convexified radial weight that restores coercivity in the Carleman commutator. Combining the resulting Carleman estimate with a Hardy-type inequality and a Caccioppoli inequality, we show that any weak solution vanishing to infinite order at the degeneracy point must be identically zero on the connected domain. This result is the first SUCP theorem for this class of degenerate operators on general Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: Parabolic frequency and backward uniqueness on compact Finsler metric measure spaces
papers.abstract: We establish monotonicity formulas for parabolic frequency functions on closed Finsler metric measure spaces with fixed or evolving metrics and measures. When the reference measure is fixed, an integral bound on the metric variation yields monotonicity for the Finsler heat equation. For coupled metric measure flows, we construct positive global supersolutions and subsolutions of a linearized conjugate heat equation from local radial barriers. These weights define a frequency function whose monotonicity follows from an integral bound involving the metric variation and the change in weighted Ricci curvature. For parabolic equations with a source controlled by the solution and its gradient, we obtain a differential inequality for the frequency and prove that a solution vanishing at the terminal time must vanish throughout the preceding interval. The proof controls the comparison of the two weights through an energy quotient computed with the subsolution measure.

papers.title: Linear Convergence of Nesterov's Acceleration for All Momentum Parameter
papers.abstract: We study the convergence rate of the Nesetrov's accelerated proximal gradient method for a smooth, strongly convex composite minimization objective across a range of value of the momentum extrapolation. The literature proves a convergence rate of the method for a specific momentum extrapolation parameter choice based on the knowledge of strong convexity and Lipschitz smoothness constants. For the heavy ball method it is established that every choice of the momentum parameter either fails to accelerate or fails to converge on the same function class. We prove in this paper that a range of Nesterov style constant momentum extrapolation parameters produces a linear convergence rate. We corroborate these results numerically via performance estimation which computes a method's exact worst case rate as a semidefinite program.

papers.title: STAIRS: Staging the Inverse Problem via Admissible-Support Scheduling for Unrolled MRI Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) forms images from incomplete Fourier measurements, shifting acquisition burden to computational reconstruction. Deep unrolled networks interleave learned regularization and data consistency, yet typically estimate the full unmeasured spectrum at every cascade. We propose STAIRS (Staging the Inverse Problem via Admissible-Support Scheduling), which projects intermediate reconstructions onto nested Fourier supports that expand to the full spectrum and conditions each update on its support transition. Conditional increments of a regularized log-determinant score of training covariance define a normalized spectral coordinate, accounting for dependencies between newly and previously admitted frequencies. Dyadic targets allocate larger coordinate increments to earlier cascades and are mapped to fixed supports before training, enabling coarse-to-fine reconstruction with unchanged sampling masks and data consistency. On fastMRI and Stanford2D, STAIRS improves matched Transformer (HUMUSNet) and convolutional (NAFNet) backbones in single- and multi-coil reconstruction, including radiologist-annotated pathology regions. It also outperforms predictor-based progression with lower parameter overhead and inference latency. Stage-wise analysis shows repeated error correction by projection and lower intermediate reconstruction errors than the backbones alone throughout support expansion. Ablations favor dyadic allocation over uniform expansion for square and line-band supports and over manual front-loading for square windows. Support projection alone improves reconstruction, and transition conditioning strengthens the gain. Cross-dataset evaluation shows improvements for both backbones in both directions. Support allocation thus complements regularizer design in unrolled MRI reconstruction.

authors.name: Rong-Rong Chen
authors.institution: Institute of Botany, Jiangsu Province and Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

papers.title: ReSkill: Selective Self-Improvement for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Self-improvement on compositional manipulation tasks requires deciding what to reuse, where to improve, and which changes to retain. We present ReSkill, a selective self-improvement framework that concentrates revision on capability gaps. A coding agent constructs an object-centric task graph from an instruction and a skill library, then uses node-level execution records to locate failures. At the task level, it revises stage organization, hand-off conditions, and recovery routes; at the skill level, it strengthens perception, motion, manipulation, and verification capabilities that repeatedly fail. Candidate revisions undergo full-task evaluation and paired comparisons before adoption, allowing local changes to accumulate into validated skills and an independently executable policy. The agent participates only during development; the deployed policy calls the retained skills without invoking the agent at run time. On the same development set, average success across ten RoboDojo tasks rises from 30.0% for the initial versions to 86.2% for the final adopted programs; retained programs achieve 83.6% in recorded robustness and model-selection evaluations. Across eight real-world tasks, ReSkill succeeds in 72 of 80 rebuilt-simulation trials and 62 of 80 real-robot trials (77.5%). The median revision changes only three functions, approximately 0.5% of a program, while 39% of task-specific functions in later-added tasks directly reuse existing implementations. These results show how locating local deficiencies, validating candidate changes, and accumulating reusable skills can improve execution of compositional manipulation tasks.

papers.title: CompositionEvidence: Controlling Geometric Evidence for Cinematic Composition Reasoning with Frozen Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Cinematic composition questions depend on in-frame geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) use inconsistently. External perception tools can expose this geometry, but naive prompt injection can overwrite useful visual predictions. On ShotBench composition, pre-question geometry reduces Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 49.5% to 46.3%; corrupted measurements lower it to 33.6%. CompositionEvidence derives nine reproducible features from frozen detection, depth, and line experts and supplies their shared 24-dimensional representation through two interfaces. A training-free channel appends gated neutral evidence after the question, reaching 56.2% (+6.7, exact McNemar p=0.0018) and 48.4% under corrupted evidence. A minimal-training channel maps the same representation to four soft tokens with a 7.37M-parameter projector while leaving the VLM frozen; it reaches 61.0% (+11.5). Across nine VLMs, including five commercial models queried through official provider APIs, zero-shot accuracy ranges from 43.8% to 63.0%, and the text channel changes it by +6.7 to -6.9 points; the highest baseline is among the regressions. The effect of explicit geometry depends on measurement reliability and on how the receiving model integrates it.

papers.title: Intelligent Reflecting Surface for ISAC: From Beamforming to Joint Design With Surface Orientation
papers.abstract: Rotatable semi-passive intelligent reflecting surfaces (SIRSs) provide an additional spatial degree of freedom (DoF) by proactively adjusting the orientation, while dedicated sensors directly receive target echoes. To exploit this DoF for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), we investigate the joint optimization of SIRS rotation, base station (BS) transmit beamforming, and SIRS phase-shifts to minimize the Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB) for target's spatial-frequency estimation subject to per-user communication signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints. We first establish an orientation-dependent system model that characterizes the effective aperture gains, based on which the CRB is derived. To gain useful insights, closed-form expressions of the beamforming and rotation designs are derived in the sensing-only and communication-only cases. For the co-located user and target case, we further characterize the condition under which the sensing-oriented rotation design also satisfies the communication requirement. In the single-user single-target case with ideal unit aperture gains, we analyze the channel correlation and its impact on ISAC performance. For the general multi-user case, an effective method based on the genetic algorithm is developed. Numerical results demonstrate the superiorities of the rotatable SIRS over the fixed-orientation SIRS and show that jointly optimizing the SIRS orientation and beamforming can improve the effective aperture gains and the correlation between communication and sensing channels.

papers.title: On the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers
papers.abstract: Combining the frameworks of Chamizo--Iwaniec and Chamizo--Ubis with the recent character-sum and exponential-sum estimates of Bellotti and Kerr, we improve the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers of binary quadratic forms from $O(N^{21/32+\eps})$ to $O(N^{55/84+\eps})$. If no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in $\mathrm{Re}\,s>7/8$, the exponent becomes $2274811/3487744$; under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions, it becomes $118/181$.

papers.title: Remarks on spectral gaps on Gaussian path space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the relationship between spectral gaps of Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/$L^2$ operators on Gaussian path space and the underlying Volterra kernel $F$. This framework includes fractional Brownian motion $B^H$ with Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. For the fractional Wiener measure $\mu_H$, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with respect to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Dirichlet form holds for $H\geq\frac12$, whereas the corresponding weak Poincar\'e inequality fails for $0<H<\frac12$. The damped/$L^2$ Dirichlet forms satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for every $H\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: Same Measurements, Different Velocity Risk: Complementary Rolling-Shutter Readouts under Clock Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Camera rigs with identical measurement budgets can have different velocity estimation rates when exposure timing is uncertain. We establish this distinction for rolling-shutter reconstruction with two calibrated moving anchors, unknown scene points, and independently unknown auxiliary poses and clocks. On the same fixed local physical class near a separated lateral rig, repeated readouts have worst-case squared velocity risk at least of order $\sigma\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}$, whereas complementary readouts have minimax risk of order $\sigma^2$, for a fixed admissible clock displacement $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}>0$ as the noise standard deviation $\sigma$ tends to zero. A finite physical compensation path gives the lower bound; a nonlinear velocity inverse proves complementary stability. All motion, structure, pose, and clock nuisances remain unknown. We identify mounting configurations in which both designs become regular and quantify the risk floor induced by metric uncertainty. We quantify full-parameter domains with independent 6-ms clocks and test in-domain reconstruction under paired noise and a depth-offset intervention. Raster studies examine image formation and calibration sensitivity.

authors.name: Lunshuo Tian
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
papers.abstract: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.

papers.title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
papers.abstract: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. These results support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

papers.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

papers.title: Sharp bounds for posterior causal attribution given complete factual records
papers.abstract: Retrospective causal attribution evaluates whether altering an earlier event would have prevented an observed outcome. Observational data determine marginal potential-response probabilities at fixed inputs while leaving cross-world joint distributions unspecified. Conditional on a complete factual record in a finite Markovian structural causal model, independence across mechanisms is preserved and each unobserved conditional response distribution is restricted to a capped probability simplex. Every collection of conditional distributions satisfying these local bounds is jointly attainable within a single compatible structural causal model. Optimizing the counterfactual expectation over the resulting product domain yields sharp attribution bounds for multistage interventions and mediated effects, and compatible response-vector polytopes extend these bounds to structural response restrictions. Exact algorithms for causal chains and general directed acyclic graphs, consistent plug-in endpoint estimators, and finite-sample and asymptotic confidence intervals are developed and illustrated using synthetic reactor experiments and health survey data.

papers.title: Linear Set Reconciliation with $O(d)$ Additive Redundancy
papers.abstract:
In set reconciliation, two parties holding sets $A, B \subseteq [n]$ with $|A \triangle B| \le d$ seek to recover their symmetric difference from short $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketches, which is equivalent to recovering a $d$-sparse vector $x = \mathbf{1}_{A \triangle B} \in \mathbb{F}_2^n$ from its syndrome $Hx \in \mathbb{F}_2^m$. While the information-theoretic counting bound requires $L(n,d) := \log \sum_{i=0}^d \binom{n}{i} = d\log(n/d) + \Theta(d)$ bits, existing polynomial-time schemes either use at least $d\lceil\log(n+1)\rceil$ bits (algebraic sketches, leaving an $\Omega(d\log d)$-bit gap) or incur a multiplicative $(1+\delta)L(n,d)$ overhead (peeling-based sketches), raising the question of whether $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits is achievable with fast updates and decoding.
  We construct a public-coin randomized $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear sketch of length $L(n,d) + O(d) + \lambda\log^{O(1)} n$ that recovers each fixed input of weight at most $d$ with probability at least $1 - 2^{-\lambda}$, with $\log^{O(1)} n$ update time and $d\exp(O((\log\log n)^2)) = dn^{o(1)}$ worst-case decoding time. In particular, for $n \le 2^{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}$ and $\lambda \le d^{1-\Omega(1)}$, this achieves $L(n,d) + O(d)$ bits with $\operatorname{polylog}(d)$ update time and $d^{1+o(1)}$ decoding time.
  Our construction encodes $d$ permuted rows via randomly scaled Pinsketch syndromes and sketches the resulting bit array column by column. Decoding columns sequentially from prefix predictions cancels recovered rows and exposes undecided rows as decoder-side hints, reducing each column to a hinted sparse recovery problem that we solve via a recursive sketch, HintSketch.

authors.name: Rui Xu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
papers.abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

authors.name: Yifan Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: LangDepth: Vision-Language Scene Priors for Semantic Binning and Cross-Domain Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.abstract:
Monocular depth estimation has advanced through large-scale pretraining and strong visual backbones, yet metric depth remains sensitive to scene-level scale. Indoor rooms and outdoor driving scenes occupy very different depth ranges, but most depth decoders infer this global structure implicitly from visual features. We ask whether scene-level semantic structure can instead act as an upstream prior that shapes the metric output space before dense prediction.
  We present LangDepth (SemanticBins), a monocular depth architecture that couples strong visual features with a scene-conditioned output space. A frozen CLIP encoder and a learnable bank of scene- and geometry-oriented concept keys convert image features into a compact scene descriptor, without requiring per-image text or an external captioner. A Scene Prior Module (SPM) maps this descriptor to a scene-conditioned metric depth interval, providing a global range anchor before dense decoding. In parallel, a DINOv2-L backbone with a lightweight FPN extracts dense visual features, and a Per-Pixel Assignment Network (PPAN) assigns pixels to the scene-prescribed bin structure. A confidence gate fuses the dense visual estimate with the SPM prior.
  We train LangDepth jointly on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI under a modest supervised depth budget, without web-scale depth supervision or pseudo-labelled depth data. A single model achieves delta_1 = 0.960 on NYU, 0.960 on KITTI, 0.887 on DIODE indoor, 0.946 on iBims-1, and 0.861 on SUN RGB-D. Beyond aggregate accuracy, the SPM predicts compact indoor ranges and much wider outdoor KITTI ranges, the gate becomes SPM-dominant on outdoor scenes, and perturbing the routed scene context causes large drops on KITTI and iBims-1. These results support scene-conditioned output spaces as a practical and interpretable mechanism for cross-domain monocular depth estimation.

papers.title: Rethinking Adaptive Routing on Dragonfly
papers.abstract: The Dragonfly topology is widely deployed in leading supercomputers, where adaptive routing is crucial for high-performance interconnection. Despite years of research, a dilemma remains: state-of-the-art adaptive routing algorithms achieve excellent performance but demand hardware budgets far beyond what real router chips can afford -- prohibitive buffers, logically dependent floating-point operations, or exhaustive path-set traversals -- whereas realizable algorithms deliver unsatisfactory performance. Furthermore, existing algorithms fail to exploit the abundant almost-minimal paths in Dragonfly: when only the local channels of a minimal path are congested, they reroute packets to significantly longer global non-minimal paths, wasting global bandwidth and increasing latency. To address both limitations, we analyze intra-group path contention and propose the Decoupled Incremental Adaptive Routing (DIAR) algorithm, which decouples routing into global path selection at the source and incremental local detours onto almost-minimal paths, guaranteeing deadlock freedom without additional virtual channels, escape rings, or turn models. Requiring only a few comparators, shifters, adders, and multiplexers, DIAR reduces buffer overhead by up to four orders of magnitude compared with state-of-the-art algorithms, while achieving comparable or superior performance across all evaluated scenarios: relative to the strongest realizable adaptive routing algorithm in each scenario, DIAR improves saturation throughput by up to 30.0% across synthetic traffic patterns and improves performance by up to 34.9% (13.2% on average) across HPC workloads.

papers.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
papers.abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.

papers.title: Capture-Aware Predictive OFDM Reacquisition in Clock-Asynchronous Space-Air-Ground Networks
papers.abstract: Reliable orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reacquisition must validate an intended burst and return its delay and carrier frequency offset (CFO) correc- tions within capture tolerances. In clock-asynchronous space- air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), shared geometry and timing uncertainty couples distributed observations, while public- preamble replay creates competing peaks. We propose Capture- Aware Predictive Reacquisition (CAPR), a Bayesian receiver that models competition under both hypotheses and marginalizes unknown spatial interference covariance and target complex amplitude before shared-state fusion. CAPR maximizes posterior probability mass within the capture rectangle and constrains continuous L-BFGS-B refinement through a mass-loss budget. We derive closed-form predictive likelihood reductions, an exact finite-cell action optimizer, a conditional approximation regret bound, and finite-sample false-acceptance calibration. Across 150 primary scenarios and five seeds, CAPR achieves 83.8% strict capture at 4.68% realized false acceptance, improving over Gaussian joint-MAP by 12.5 percentage points overall and 54.2 points across all 32 replay scenarios. Diffuse multipath, degraded assistance, and indistinguishable sources delineate its operational boundaries.

papers.title: Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
papers.abstract: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system's effective temperature with density.

authors.name: Yaocai Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Da Wei
