papers.title: Same Contacts, Different Rooms:Meeting Format Shapes LLM Group Influence Beyond Pairwise Contact Counts
papers.abstract: Simulations of LLM agent collectives usually summarise interaction as a pairwise contact network. We test that summary with a contact-matched intervention: the members, their initial stances and every pairwise contact count stay fixed while the meetings are reorganised, and each member gives a one-step support readout after reading the arguments of everyone present. Across six open-weight LLMs and 14 debate topics, merging triads into five-person meetings (resize) moves group support more than reshuffling who meets in triads (regroup), although both move the same 60 dyadic exposures. The root-mean-square change is 4.36 versus 2.59 percentage points (pp), larger for resize in all six models and in 81 of 84 model-topic cells. Resizing also has a consistent direction: it amplifies the initial majority of the merged members by 1.72 pp, in every model, whereas regrouping has no direction (<= 0.03 pp). A contact network cannot represent regrouping at all, yet pairwise rules applied meeting by meeting explain up to 76% of its effect, and with identical weights they raise resize R^2 by 0.51-0.58 for two models. We show that the gap between the two placements is an exact Jensen gap of the sigmoid readout, bounded by how much a member's predicted logits vary across meetings; this dispersion tracks the gap with log-log r=0.97 and tells a modeller when contact counts are a safe summary. Meeting format is a first-class variable for LLM social simulation.

papers.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
papers.abstract: Autonomous UAV exploration is increasingly used for large-scale surveying and inspection in inaccessible or disaster-affected environments, where onboard memory and computational resources are often severely constrained. Most existing UAV exploration systems maintain globally queryable geometric map representations for motion planning and exploration decision-making, causing memory consumption and spatial-query costs to increase with the explored area. Robot-centric local mapping bounds dense-map memory and computation but discards global task context needed for long-horizon exploration.We present FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal framework that confines dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while retaining compact global observation and task context. At the observation level, lightweight LiDAR-keyframe visibility records preserve ray-wise evidence for frontier reasoning. At the task level, unresolved frontiers beyond the local-map extent are retained as compact pending tasks associated with odometry anchors. A sparse topological graph connects these anchors through retained routes for future revisits.Upon returning to a task region, FLAVOR reconstructs the frontier and exploration viewpoint from observations, while the topological route is instantiated and validated against the current local map before execution. Dense-map capacity remains fixed as exploration expands, with exploration-dependent memory growth confined to compact observation and task context.FLAVOR achieves 31.98--41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94--99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three simulated scenes. In real-world deployments, it reduces this footprint by 92.67% in the forest and 62.42% at the construction site relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving long-term task continuity under constrained onboard resources.

authors.name: Jianping Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: VeilTune: Secure Fine-Tuning of Private LoRA Adapters on Public Pretrained Language Models
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning public pretrained language models with lightweight adapters such as LoRA has become the mainstream way to adapt them to downstream tasks. A service provider often trains its adapter on a data owner's samples, so two assets need protection: the data owner's samples and the provider's adapter. Existing secure fine-tuning protocols protect the samples but reveal to the data owner intermediate results of every training step, such as the hidden representations or logits of its inputs. We show that a single step suffices to copy the adapter: from the hidden representations of one mini-batch of 32 samples, the data owner fits an adapter that agrees with the provider's on 99.2% of test inputs, and logits alone yield about 94%. Protecting both assets therefore requires that no value that depends on the adapter be revealed throughout training. We present VeilTune, to the best of our knowledge the first protocol that fine-tunes a pretrained language model with backpropagation entirely in secure multi-party computation (MPC). VeilTune computes only what the loss depends on, replaces generic MPC operators with training-aware nonlinear operators that stay accurate on the values that training produces, and obliviously skips the steps corrupted by truncation failures. On four few-shot tasks with RoBERTa-large, VeilTune nearly matches plaintext training and is 5.3 points more accurate on average than SecP-Tuning, the state-of-the-art secure fine-tuning protocol. On SST-2, it achieves a 3.5x end-to-end speedup and a 3.6x reduction in communication over SecP-Tuning, and 26x and 17x over full fine-tuning in MPC.

authors.name: Tanping Zhou
authors.institution: Chinese People's Armed Police Force Engineering University

papers.title: Suppression Is Not Erasure: Mechanistic Analysis and Reactivation Boundaries of Subspace Projection for LoRA Backdoor Defense
papers.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the standard paradigm for customizing large language models, yet third-party LoRA adapters pose a supply-chain risk: modifying less than 1% of model parameters suffices to implant stealthy backdoors. Recent defenses project adapter weights onto estimated backdoor subspaces, reporting near-zero static Attack Success Rates (ASR). We audit subspace-projection defenses across four model scales (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B) and three architectures (Qwen2.5, InternLM2.5, Spark). Constructively, module-wise rank-1 trigger-difference projection (k=1, alpha=1) reduces ASR from 60.4% to 0.0% on standard benchmarks and from 70.3% to 0.0% on a 1,000-sample uncontaminated suite (p = 3.055e-299, instruction-level p = 9.49e-16) in under 5 seconds end-to-end, and we prove via a spectral-gap bound why trigger-free calibration with benign polite suffixes aligns with u1(B) (median cosine 0.9048) and achieves 0.0% ASR without prior trigger knowledge. Our main contribution is a negative finding: static ASR reduction does not imply parameter erasure. Under 5-sample few-shot reactivation, every evaluated weight-editing defense rebounds (91.7%-100.0% ASR in 1 epoch for standard projections, Fine-Pruning, ANP, SVD truncation and Li & Kim's dual-end projection; 48.7% for our single-round dual variant), all reaching 100.0% by Epoch 2, with first-epoch loss up to 5.7x lower than training from scratch. Using an exact spectrum-preserving Haar orthogonal rotation control (Frobenius norm 10.0928 preserved to 1.70e-6) and N=1..6 cumulative Gram-Schmidt basis ablation, we decompose reactivation into residual trigger-difference coupling energy at Epoch 1 (Spearman rho = 0.986), base-model learnability at Epoch 2 (100%), and benign semantic direction conflict (41.7%).

papers.title: Energy-Harvesting-Aware Cell-Free LEO Satellite Networks: A Lyapunov Framework for Sustainable User-Centric Beamforming and Clustering
papers.abstract: We study battery-aware downlink control in user-centric cell-free low Earth orbit satellite networks with intermittent solar harvesting and finite onboard batteries. A perturbed Lyapunov controller coordinates clustering and hybrid beamforming using measured battery states and causal harvest forecasts. The per-slot solver combines group-sparse association, rate bounds, a quadratic transform, and successive convex approximation. We establish robust battery invariance for feasible implemented actions and give a utility bound conditional on a comparison policy and the per-slot implementation gap. Multi-orbit control-layer simulations show that queue-aware scheduling preserves a larger battery reserve in the stressed scenario at the expense of effective energy efficiency. A separate fixed-cluster matrix snapshot illustrates recovered hybrid beam patterns and the per-slot objective trace.

papers.title: How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?
papers.abstract: This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^{\mu}$ ($-1\le\mu\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($\mu=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $\mu<k-1$, we prove that $E/d_n$ is bounded below by a constant strictly larger than $1$, except when $k>s-1$ and $\mu=k-2$ hold simultaneously. This reveals the superiority of $B$-splines in the sense of $n$-widths. Numerical experiments corroborate these bounds and, in some cases (e.g. the exception above), show that they are sharp.

papers.title: Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices
papers.abstract: List replicability measures how many accurate hypotheses suffice to contain the output of a learning rule with arbitrarily high confidence. We prove that every nonempty class of $m$ binary concepts on $n$ domain points has list replicability at most $805\ln(2m)\ln(2n)$. This resolves the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak. Hanner matrices give lower bounds of the same order, for square matrices and for explicit families with unequal logarithmic aspect ratios. The upper bound is obtained by constructing nested acyclic sets in the faces of a cube. A critical-point estimate supplies highly connected regions, weighted cell attachments keep the sets compatible across faces, and a cubical carrier theorem converts them into accurate finite covers and learning rules. Appending one constant coordinate turns list replicability into an exact geometric quantity, the face width, and graph-orientation classes satisfy exact product formulas. In particular, there are explicit classes with list replicability $4k+1$ and equivariant index $3k$, so the additive gap between the two is unbounded. We also develop entropy-tilting and two-sided Gibbs constructions, give combinatorial upper bounds adapted to structured matrices, compute exact values on classical families, and study the index of Paley matrices.

authors.name: Guangjian Zhang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: Beyond Row Alignment: Virtual-Camera-Aware Online Stereo Rectification
papers.abstract: Stereo matchers estimate depth by comparing the left and right images from a stereo camera pair, but they assume that the two cameras are accurately calibrated and rectified. In real deployments, small physical shifts after calibration, caused by camera motion, mechanical drift, vibration, or installation changes, can break this assumption and degrade depth estimation. Online stereo rectification is therefore needed to correct the image pair during operation and recover a stereo geometry where standard stereo matching can work reliably. Recent online rectification methods mainly optimize row alignment, making the left and right views of the same scene point fall on the same image row. We show that this target, while necessary, is insufficient for deployable stereo depth estimation. A rectifier may make a small set of matched points look well row-aligned, but still distort the full images in ways that hurt stereo matching: useful image regions may be cut off, large blank areas may appear, objects may be stretched or squeezed, or image scale may change unevenly across the view. We propose VirtualRect, an online stereo rectification method designed for reliable real-world deployment. Rather than treating rectification as simply making the left and right image rows line up, this method estimates a rectified virtual stereo camera and combines image-wide supervision of image warp behavior. This makes the rectified images and the camera parameters come from the same geometry, so the images used for matching and the model used for depth computation remain consistent. Experiments on multiple datasets show that, compared with the prior state-of-the-art online rectifier, VirtualRect reduces vertical flow error by 17% on Carla-Flowguided and 7% on Semi-Truck Highway, and lowers depth MAE by 30-41% on Carla-Flowguided across three downstream stereo matchers.

authors.name: Zaiwang Gu
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xudong Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Replay Fidelity in LLM Agent Evaluation: Randomness, Hidden State, and Test Oracles in AppWorld
papers.abstract: Reproducibility in large language model (LLM) agent evaluation depends on replay fidelity: which parts of an execution trace are reconstructed, controlled, and compared. This matters for agent debugging, failure analysis, and counterfactual evaluation of stateful tool use. We audit all 71 unsuccessful executions in a fixed historical AppWorld corpus using 284 isolated fixed-code replay attempts. Reconstructed declared settings admit 42 cases under printed-output, pre-oracle database-delta, and native-verdict/test-count checks; resetting the random-number generator before each interaction admits 68. The 26-case gap contracts to four under database/oracle checks, with one endpoint unknown. Mechanism studies identify four materialized-state discrepancies despite matching outputs and verdicts. In one admitted endpoint pair, an identical API call yields matching responses but different row effects; common future Python RNG removes that deterministic difference in two paired repetitions. A separate JWT credential-equality program and alignment controls expose authentication/write differences, with missing repetitions retained. For all 10 affected post-oracle export cases, native export from retained output trackers restores the reference comparison without changing original cached contents. A purposeful 12-case BFCL pilot shows no discrepancy under its tested public-state, return, and verdict checks. We preserve resource censoring and infrastructure deviations. The contribution is a bounded empirical characterization of replay eligibility, hidden state, and test-oracle integration, without estimating debugger accuracy, repair gains, or method-ranking distortion.

papers.title: LoMASA: A Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant with Confidence-Gated Delegation for B2B Quoting
papers.abstract: Frontline sales staff spend much of their day re-coordinating quotes after customers change quantities, ask for discounts or new payment terms, or costs move. We present LoMASA (Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant), a training-free multi-agent system that runs entirely on one desktop computer. A 35B mixture-of-experts model (System-1) makes each decision in a single forward pass and reads its confidence from the probabilities of the answer options. A 27B dense model (System-2) writes customer replies and escalation briefs and is consulted when System-1 is unsure. Code computes every price, margin and option, and hard pricing rules cannot be overridden. On a test split of 500 simulated episodes with 1512 decisions built from public supply-chain data, the salesperson has to decide only 19.5% of decisions: 38.0% are settled automatically, with a median latency of 2.67 seconds, and 42.5% are escalated to a manager by the hard rules. On the automatically settled decisions LoMASA is as accurate as a rule baseline (0.894 vs.\ 0.894) and makes fewer commitments whose margin later falls below the floor (2.61% vs 4.53%); the price is additional escalations to the manager. Option probabilities are well calibrated without any training, unlike confidence stated in words by the same model. We also report where the design does not help: the 27B model rarely changes a decision.

papers.title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

papers.title: A Geometry-Robust Ne\v{c}as-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.

authors.name: Qi Xin
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Shihua Gong
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: AnyBreak: Towards Jailbreaking Any T2I Model for Any Concept
papers.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in image generation and editing, yet this progress has also introduced significant security risks. Prior work has shown that adversarial prompt can induce the generation of Not-Safe-For-Work (NSFW) content, including pornographic, violent, and graphic imagery. However, such attacks are typically mitigated by prompt filters and often rely on white-box assumptions. In this paper, we propose AnyBreak, a novel jailbreak framework that constructs adversarial images via multi-scale progressive semantic alignment. During the generation process, these adversarial images steer the generation trajectory in latent space towards unsafe data manifolds, enabling cross-modal transfer of malicious concepts from the text modality to the image modality. AnyBreak operates using only clean textual prompts and adversarial images at inference time, and can jailbreak any T2I models towards any malicious concepts in a fully black-box setting. We further introduce AnyBreak-V, an enhanced variant that incorporates a compensation term to bypass post-hoc safety checkers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AnyBreak achieves high attack success rates while preserving visual fidelity and semantic consistency with the input prompts under black-box and clean-text constraints. Our findings reveal that existing T2I defense leave critical cross-modal attack surfaces insufficiently addressed. The code is available at https://github.com/luqi-glory/AnyBreak.

authors.name: Wenrui Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
papers.abstract: We introduce Forelli-Rudin type operators on the open unit ball of $\ell^2$. The weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ boundedness of these operators are completely characterized for all $p,q\in[1,\infty]\times [1,\infty]$, and every Schatten class between the weighted $L^2$ spaces are also completely characterized. Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. These results are not only infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). They also reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the geometric and measure theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. The key ingredient of our proofs is that we also establish the Forelli-Rudin type estimates in infinite dimensions, which may shew some night on the function theory in the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

papers.title: TSFFormer: A Frequency-Domain Spike Transformer for Green Human Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Wearable Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) enable pervasive Human Activity Recognition (HAR), but traditional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) suffer from an "arithmetic-latency deadlock" due to dense floating-point MAC operations. While Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer ultra-low power, existing ones face spatial blind spots, rigid neurons, and gradient degradation. To address these, we propose TSFFormer, a purely spiking Fourier Transformer for Green HAR. It introduces two key innovations: (1) a MultiHeadFourier attention that performs frequency-domain global mixing, reducing complexity from \(O(V^2)\) to \(O(V\log V)\), eliminating spatial blind spots, and saving \(\sim\)50% GPU memory; and (2) a dual-compartment Temporal Spiking LIF (TSLIFNode) that utilizes dynamic thresholds to adapt to non-stationary rhythms and mitigate gradient degradation. Extensive experiments on 8 public IMU benchmarks demonstrate that TSFFormer surpasses state-of-the-art SNNs and even the classic DeepConvLSTM, achieving a \(\sim\)3\(\times\) faster training speed with an energy footprint of 0.1 pJ. Ablation studies confirm the synergistic effect of our modules, providing a highly accurate, ultra-low-power event-driven paradigm for wearable sensing.

authors.name: Shuiying Xiang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Integrated Service Network Theory and Key Technology

papers.title: Scalar curvature deformation of isoparametric tubes
papers.abstract: We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\frac{\pi}{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.

papers.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
papers.abstract:
We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[
  \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1)
  =\kappa\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}}
  +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $\kappa$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

papers.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

authors.name: Kangsheng Liu
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: Collaboration Signatures: Tracking Long-Horizon Dynamics of Cross-Meeting Collaboration Networks
papers.abstract: Enterprise platforms have received increasing attention as a core component of social networks and the Web. However, existing work mostly relies on fragmented logs of small units of work, like emails and chats, and focuses on who connects with whom without sufficient account of collaboration content and dynamics. This work systematically explores tracking collaborations across sequences of meetings as a new approach to interpreting their long-horizon dynamics. Linking 45,426 meetings in a large multinational technology company based on full transcripts and 1.6 million extracted agenda items, we establish a cross-meeting collaboration network of 6,065 collaborations. The network recovers the natural shapes of workplace collaborations: meetings, as snapshots of ongoing collaboration, link into largely tree-shaped structures, while the work content forms nested directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Further, we explore how these networks evolve over time, examining three established perspectives: task division, team composition, and temporal continuity. Each explains part of the dynamics but does not capture the distinctness of long-horizon workplace collaboration: e.g., work flows in a consistent direction between a few pairs of subjects, yet a collaboration's subject explains little of how its meetings are conducted. Instead, accumulating the agenda, interaction, and language of meetings along each tree yields a signature of the collaboration, a distinctive profile that picks out the collaboration of a held-out meeting at 4.5 times chance. The signature models collaboration better than team or task views, individually or combined, in next-meeting prediction and tree-level fitting. We discuss the implications of these cross-meeting dynamics for designing office applications and support tools, and call for next-generation Web systems that represent collaborations over their long horizon.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.

papers.title: Trajectory Inversion for a Rudderless Dual Vectored-Thrust Flying Wing
papers.abstract: A rudderless dual vectored-thrust flying wing combines vertical takeoff and landing with efficient for- ward flight in a compact tailless configuration. Without aerodynamic control surfaces, vectored thrust couples translation and pitch control. Therefore, generating dy- namically compatible trajectories remains an open chal- lenge. To address this challenge, this study proposes a trajectory generation method that jointly optimizes path geometry and timing. Trajectory inversion yields state and control histories that satisfy the coupled equations of motion. The optimization balances curvature-induced acceleration against aerodynamic support, lowering thrust- vectoring demand while retaining the defining maneuver features. Representative looping and rolling sequences are tracked in closed-loop simulations. These results provide a basis for planning autonomous aerobatic maneuvers with rudderless vectored-thrust aircraft.

papers.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.

authors.name: Yinuo Jiang
authors.institution: Central South University of Forestry and Technology

papers.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
papers.abstract: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.

authors.name: Fangzhou Liu
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University

papers.title: Compositional Conformal Risk Control for Multi-Stage LLM Cascades
papers.abstract: Multi-stage large language model (LLM) cascades balance accuracy and inference cost, but reliable deployment also requires controlling error risk and identifying its sources across stages. We propose Compositional Conformal Risk Control (CompCRC), a risk-control framework for pre-specified multi-stage LLM cascades. We decompose the risk of accepting incorrect answers into additive stage-wise contributions over the full query population, linking local risk budgets to a system-level guarantee. CompCRC constructs and freezes candidate budget allocations and acceptance thresholds, selects one candidate on independent data, and certifies its stage-wise risk contributions on separate held-out data. Under conditional exchangeability, we establish a finite-sample guarantee: the marginal expected accepted-error risk of the complete deployment procedure does not exceed the global risk budget. At the reported comparison budget of $\alpha=0.45$, all three stages of CompCRC pass their local checks on MMLU, GSM8K, and HellaSwag. Compared with Global-CRC, which passes system-level risk certification at the same budget, CompCRC reduces observed accepted-error risk by 1.33--2.00 percentage points, improves final accuracy by 0.67--2.00 percentage points, and reduces weighted inference cost by 30.37\% on HellaSwag. The selected cost-based budget allocation also improves accuracy per unit cost by 10.6\%--46.7\% over uniform allocation. Further experiments show that stage-wise statistics identify stages that fail local certification checks, providing diagnostic information alongside system-level risk control.

papers.title: Theory of spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy with topological insulator tips
papers.abstract: Topological insulators have enabled a new class of spin-sensitive scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probes based on helical boundary states. However, how these probes generate a net spin-polarized tunneling current remains unclear. We present a theory of spin-polarized STM with topological insulator tips and show that asymmetric tunneling-contact geometry and spin dephasing enable helical boundary states to generate a spin-polarized tunneling current. Within the standard Landauer-B\"uttiker formalism, we demonstrate this mechanism for a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator tip: asymmetric contacts make the two counter-propagating helical edge states, which carry opposite spins, traverse path lengths that differ by $\Delta L$, and spin dephasing induces backscattering that reduces the conductance more strongly for the longer path. For a representative asymmetric contact and weak spin dephasing, the QSH tip exhibits a tunneling spin polarization of $P_s=-17.2\%$ under positive bias, whose magnitude can reach $50\%$ for larger $\Delta L$, and which remains robust against Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Crucially, this polarization, dominated by helical edge transport rather than by bulk states, naturally reverses sign with the bias polarity owing to spin-momentum locking. Our findings are consistent with recent STM experiments using topological tips.

authors.name: Huiqiu Yuan
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

authors.name: Zhenyu Wang
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: When Coding Agents Get Arms: Safety Risks Across the Digital-Physical Boundary
papers.abstract: Advances in spatial understanding have enabled frontier models to power coding agents that control a real robot arm zero-shot and end-to-end, without task-specific demonstrations or retraining. This brings two new safety challenges. First, the extensive knowledge of frontier models lets these agents perform tasks that earlier VLA and WAM paradigms could not, opening the door to new forms of capability misuse. Second, coding agents can access digital resources such as web pages and emails. Threats in these resources, such as indirect prompt injection, can carry over into the physical world when the agent controls a robot. We therefore introduce ArmedAgent, the first systematic benchmark to evaluate both risks for coding agents performing zero-shot robot control. It covers robustness, malicious use, and indirect injection across 36 tasks in 5 scenarios, evaluated in simulation and validated on a physical robot arm. A distinctive portion of the tasks target harmful behaviors that earlier VLA paradigms could not perform. Testing several frontier models, including GPT-6-Astra, under widely used agent frameworks, we find substantial safety risks in current systems.

authors.name: Yiming Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ATHOS: Agreement-based Testing of Hypotheses in Overlapping Subgroups
papers.abstract: We study confirmation of treatment benefit in a prespecified family of overlapping subgroups of a randomized trial. Maximum-statistic procedures exploit the correlation between subgroups' statistics, but calibration decides what they protect. Re-randomization controls error exactly when treatment has no effect, but not when only an average effect is zero, whereas a multiplier bootstrap protects average effects only asymptotically. Our first result characterizes when re-randomization alone protects average effects. It reverses the arms' weights in the statistics' covariance, so with unequal allocation and heterogeneous effects it can overstate their correlations; in one such family of 50 subgroups, its limiting familywise error is 0.064 at nominal 0.025. We propose a step-down procedure called ATHOS, short for agreement-based testing of hypotheses in overlapping subgroups, which confirms a subgroup only when both calibrations reject it. Given assignments exchangeable within strata, ATHOS controls familywise error exactly when treatment has no effect and, under complete randomization, asymptotically for average effects, even in large families. Our second result shows that requiring agreement costs no first-order local power in balanced trials. In a null simulation with 200 patients and 1,497 subgroups, the bootstrap step-down alone made false claims in 40% of trials and ATHOS in 2.6%. In two comparisons in an HIV trial, ATHOS confirmed 188 and 73 subgroups and Holm's procedure 179 and 62.

papers.title: Fairness Drift: Assessing Algorithmic Fairness in a Moving Market
papers.abstract: Flexible models and richer data can reduce systematic valuation errors and improve fairness. Yet algorithmic values stay fixed between updates while the market moves, so a new algorithm gains most against an intact distortion and least where uneven appreciation has eroded or just reversed it. We study property assessment, which sets tax bills and has long over-assessed cheaper homes. Cook County replaced township regressions and manual adjustments with a gradient-boosted model and richer data on its triennial cycle: Chicago in 2021, northern suburbs in 2022, southern in 2023. We estimate difference-in-differences in how the assessment-to-price ratio varies with sale price and neighborhood minority share. In Chicago, the reform halved the relative over-assessment of cheaper homes and, among equally priced homes, weakened the link to neighborhood racial composition. In the suburbs the price gradient was unchanged: the North's legacy values were already accurate, and the South's cheap neighborhoods had appreciated faster under frozen values, correcting part of the distortion, then stalled in the reassessment year, leaving the new values too high where prices had gained and accuracy unimproved. Fairness thus drifts with the market between updates, and single-deployment evaluations may credit or blame the algorithm for what the market did.

authors.name: Meng Liu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors
papers.abstract: The Natarajan dimension is a fundamental measure of the capacity of multiclass hypothesis classes and plays an important role in analyzing their generalization ability. In this paper, by establishing lower and upper bounds, we show that the exact Natarajan dimension of homogeneous multiclass linear predictors with pairwise distinct class weights is \(n(k-1)-1\), where $n$ is the dimension of the feature space and $k$ is the number of classes, for \(n,k\ge3\), \(n,k\in\mathbb N\).

papers.title: Lattice Commensurability and Majorana sectors of Pfaffian--Anti-Pfaffian interfaces
papers.abstract: We study Pfaffian and anti-Pfaffian non-Abelian fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in half-filled moir\'{e} lattice systems. Owing to crystal-momentum conservation modulo a reciprocal lattice vector, these lattice systems admit coupled-wire constructions of the two phases without requiring spatially varying magnetic-field-induced momentum shifts. For the resulting Pfaffian--anti-Pfaffian interface, a Umklapp process can gap the counter-propagating charge sector, while the remaining four co-propagating Majorana modes naturally group into two sectors organized by translation symmetries. Our results show that lattice commensurability qualitatively changes the coupled-wire accessibility of non-Abelian states while providing a microscopic momentum structure that directly constrains their edge and interface dynamics.

authors.name: Xue-Yang Song
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Unmasking shortcut solutions of coding agents on partial differential equations
papers.abstract: Coding agents now write simulation programs, but benchmarks usually judge only whether their output matches a reference. In manufactured-solution tasks the data determine the exact solution, so a matching output need not come from a solver. We introduce PDEViBench, a benchmark of 290 tasks in six equation families that traces each passing program to the computation behind its output and reruns unclear programs on changed data. A Codex agent (GPT-5.2) passed 80% of 1,450 runs, yet about one pass in ten returned the exact solution without solving the equation. Counting only solved passes changed which task features made problems seem hard and reversed the ranking of two prompts. Once the prompt forbade the shortcut, every pass was a numerical solve, and on tasks without a closed-form solution passing programs stayed correct on changed data. Scientific coding benchmarks should check how each answer was computed as well as whether it matches.

papers.title: TRACE: Adaptive Credibility Reweighting for Robust Bayesian Model Selection with Source Summary Statistics
papers.abstract: This study focuses on regression estimation and variable selection based on target data, while incorporating information from coefficient estimates obtained in related studies. A weighted combination of these estimates may agree with some target effects but differ from others. We propose Transfer Regression with Adaptive Credibility Estimation (TRACE), a Bayesian method requiring only fitted coefficients and sample sizes from source studies. TRACE learns simplex-constrained source weights shared across variables. Separate latent indicators determine target inclusion and whether each coefficient is guided by the weighted source estimate. We develop an approximate collapsed variational expectation-maximization algorithm with robust source-weight initialization. Under suitable conditions, consistency of variable selection, transfer decisions, and source-weight estimation is established. These results hold at every prespecified fixed iteration in fixed dimension and at global mean-field optima of the exact collapsed variational objective as the dimension grows. Simulations show that TRACE achieves competitive variable-selection performance under different patterns of source heterogeneity. An application to data from the Genotype-Tissue Expression project illustrates its use in cross-tissue gene-expression prediction.

papers.title: More Than Just Style: Benchmarking Personality Influence in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: In addition to the effects of explicit input prompts and instructions, large language model outputs are influenced by underlying behavioral preferences similar to human personality tendencies. These tendencies can affect how models interpret situations and make decisions. However, their influence is difficult to disentangle from the effects of model capabilities and instructions. Therefore, we introduce SPACE, a benchmark framework combining a controlled evaluation protocol with complementary datasets for personality verification, capability assessment, and hierarchical situational tasks. Controlled comparisons across guidance conditions help distinguish personality influence from measured capability changes and immediate instruction effects. Experimental results demonstrate that although prompting can shift generation style, models' internal personality tendencies are persistent and not readily overridden by opposing instructions. Furthermore, these underlying tendencies have an observable influence on LLM task performance, highlighting the need for greater attention to these characteristics and potential applications. Training code and SPACE benchmark specifications are available at https://github.com/Niklauseik/SPACE-training.

authors.name: Mengyu Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards ordinarily spreads a single advantage over a whole trajectory, a granularity too coarse to isolate the few decisions on which success in a long, multi-turn interaction actually turns. Privileged self-distillation supplies denser supervision, but it leaves unanswered how a set of local teacher-student discrepancies should be converted into credit along a sequence. We introduce AgentOPSD, a critic-free scheme that assigns credit recursively, one interaction turn at a time. Inside a turn, the token-level log-probability gaps between a skill-conditioned self-teacher and the student are summed, and that sum acts as evidence in a recursive Bayesian update carried out in log-odds space; the resulting revisions reallocate the outcome-derived advantage across turns through a multiplier that is bounded and preserves its sign. With Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B as policy backbones on ALFWorld, the method improves consistently on GRPO and on self-distillation baselines, and attains 89.1% success at the 7B scale. Ablations attribute the gain to aggregating evidence at turn boundaries and to making the belief revision depend on history, rather than to the local gap by itself.

authors.name: Yizhuo Li
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

papers.title: Restricted Quantum unique ergodicity under Generalized Lindel\"of conjecture
papers.abstract: Assume the generalized Lindel\"of hypothesis. Let $u$ be an even Hecke--Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, normalized in $L^2$ with respect to hyperbolic area, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. For every fixed $\psi\in C_c((0,\infty);\mathbb{C})$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that \[ \int_0^\infty \psi(y)|u(i y)|^2\frac{d y}{y} =\frac{6}{\pi}\int_0^\infty \psi(y)\frac{d y}{y} +O_{\psi,\varepsilon}(T^{-1/4+\varepsilon}) \] as $T\to\infty$, uniformly in $u$. In particular, the restriction mass equidistributes on every fixed compact segment of the imaginary axis in $\mathbb{H}$.

authors.name: Qingfeng Sun
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
papers.abstract: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

authors.name: Xueyang Wang
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xing Zhu
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: Magnetized plasma modulator for polarization-tunable ultrahigh-power single-cycle lasers
papers.abstract: Ultrahigh power lasers with tunable polarization and few-cycle duration have long been considered the holy grail of high-power laser science, as they push light-matter interactions into an entirely new physical regime. Yet such pulses remain far beyond the reach of conventional solid-state optics and technologies. Here, we introduce a novel magnetized plasma modulator that boosts linearly polarized lasers from petawatt to exawatt powers while simultaneously enabling tunable polarization, offering a promising approach for high-power laser development. This is achieved in density-tailored plasmas by combining dispersive compression of a chirped picosecond laser pulse with magneto-chiral group-velocity splitting in a few-Tesla magnetic field. It can generate circularly or elliptically polarized pulses with extremely high compression ratios (over 1000) and extremely short durations (down to the single-cycle level) in a compact and efficient manner. These findings demonstrate a feasible pathway toward exawatt-class few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization, opening new avenues for a wide range of cutting-edge research and applications.

authors.name: Li-Jia Shuai
authors.institution: China Automotive Technology and Research Center

authors.name: Xing-Long Zhu
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: BRAT: Bounded Residual-Aligned Training for Stable Multi-Pass LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for large language model post-training often reuses each batch of sampled rollouts for several gradient passes to amortize the cost of generation. Under such multi-pass reuse, existing objectives fail in different ways: unclipped updates collapse as the policy drifts away from the sampling policy, adding a negative baseline avoids collapse but reinforces every sampled response, and PPO-style ratio clipping cuts off gradients abruptly. We first ask why reuse is fragile. Measuring how well an update estimated from a small rollout group aligns with the KL-regularized target on held-out rollouts of the same prompts, we find that this alignment drops by nearly an order of magnitude from in-sample to held-out rollouts across three base models, suggesting that repeated passes largely overfit the sampled group. Motivated by this finding, we propose Bounded Residual-Aligned Training (BRAT), motivated by a proximal update toward a bounded reweighting of the sampling policy. BRAT assigns each token a gradient weight that decreases linearly with its probability ratio and vanishes at a trust-region boundary, and normalizes group-centered rewards by their maximum magnitude, keeping advantages zero-mean and bounded without extra hyperparameters. With four reuse passes, BRAT avoids training collapse, limits policy drift, and achieves higher average accuracy with lower seed variance on most benchmarks.

authors.name: Xunlan Zhou
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology
