papers.title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
papers.abstract: We determine the interval between the varieties generated by the nonempty and full power semirings of a semigroup satisfying \(xy\approx x^2\). It has two elements for a one-element semigroup, three for a nontrivial left-zero or null semigroup, and seven otherwise, without any finiteness assumption. In the seven-element case the interval is \([\Rvar,\Rvar^0]\), where \(\Rvar=\Mod_{\rm ai}\{xy\approx xz\}\) and \(\Rvar^0\) is its zero-adjunction variety. Every word absorption valid in \(\Rvar\) but not in \(\Rvar^0\) is equivalent over \(\Rvar^0\) to one of six relative identities. We give exact absorption criteria and finite bases for all seven varieties. Three have basis rank two and four have basis rank three; their two-generated free algebras have orders \(15\), \(24\), or \(35\). We also count the finite-rank free algebras of both endpoints.

papers.title: Jointly Optimizing Memory, Computing and Offloading for Energy-Efficient DNN Inference
papers.abstract: In edge intelligence systems, computation offloading and dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) are widely used to improve energy efficiency. However, as applications like deep neural network (DNN) inference evolve in complexity, their demands for memory resources have progressively increased, establishing memory as a critical bottleneck that impacts both latency and energy consumption. In this paper, we propose a joint optimization scheme integrating memory, computing and offloading for energy-efficient DNN inference. We formulate the energy minimization problem under deadline constraints as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, where the main challenge arises from the coupling between offloading and resource optimization. To address this issue, we decompose the original problem into two subproblems under a fixed offloading policy. The local subproblem is transformed into an equivalent geometric programming (GP) problem to derive the optimal memory frequency and computing frequency, while the edge subproblem is solved via convex optimization. An efficient coordinate descent (CD) algorithm is further developed to jointly optimize all variables. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal performance with the gap from the optimal policy being at most 9.3%, and reduces the energy consumption of devices by up to 16.1% compared with benchmarks without memory frequency optimization.

papers.title: Phase-Constrained Self-Supervised Reconstruction and Denoising for Ultra-High-Resolution MRI
papers.abstract: Ultra-high-field gradient-echo (GRE) MRI reveals fine anatomy with strong susceptibility contrast, but small voxels reduce signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), while susceptibility-induced phase variation and wrapping complicate reconstruction. These challenges are especially consequential for quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM), which requires denoising GRE phase without blurring anatomy or distorting phase. We propose a measurement-domain self-supervised learning (SSL) framework for joint reconstruction and denoising of complex-valued images from a single noisy acquisition. By splitting acquired k-space samples into input and held-out subsets, the method trains without clean or fully sampled references. An explicit phase-modulation operator, estimated from low-resolution phase and embedded in the unrolled network's encoding model, simplifies phase patterns encountered by the learned regularizer while preserving consistency with acquired complex k-space measurements. We evaluated ex vivo mouse brain MRI at 15, 18, and 72 um isotropic resolution; in vivo mouse brain MRI at 30 um isotropic resolution; and in vivo human brain MRI at 0.3x0.3x0.4mm3 resolution. Across controlled noise levels, SSL improved image-quality metrics in most conditions, preserved fine anatomy, and reduced error propagation into T2* maps and QSM. Ablation studies showed that phase regularization suppressed localized artifacts from rapid phase variation, while in vivo experiments demonstrated denoising with structural preservation. These findings support phase-constrained, measurement-domain SSL for high-resolution anatomical and quantitative MRI when clean references are unavailable.

papers.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
papers.abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

papers.title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
papers.abstract: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.

papers.title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
papers.abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.

papers.title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

authors.name: Haoxuan Ma
authors.institution: Hebei University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Multi-Granularity Communication-Computing Resource Mapping for User Association in MEO-Assisted LEO Satellite Networks
papers.abstract: Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks are evolving into spaceborne communication-computing infrastructures. Their user association must jointly account for the radio link and the CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, cache, storage, energy, queue, and thermal states that determine executable service capacity. This paper studies a MEO-assisted LEO architecture in which medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) regional state aggregators collect and relay time-stamped telemetry, the network operation control center (NOCC) maintains the global logical resource view and makes the final association decisions, and LEO satellites provide access and onboard execution. We develop a multigranularity representation and service-primitive-driven mapping that converts a service-level request into a target-LEO-dependent quantized resource vector. The integer formulation, exact mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) reference, and a capacity-aware primal-dual algorithm share the same mapped objective. Experiments use real-world service bandwidth traces, a 1584-satellite LEO shell, multiple traffic seeds, controlled load and mapping error, delayed telemetry, and temporal sessions. Relative to static mapping, the proposed method improves realized utility by 10.64% and lowers end-to-end outage by 5.70 percentage points. Target quantization reduces signaling by 19.84% with negligible utility loss. Additional load, delay, temporal, runtime, and exact-MILP audits delimit the operating region and remaining mapping uncertainty.

papers.title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Visual chain-of-thought (visual-CoT), also known as "thinking with images", equips LVLMs with the ability to locate and use key visual evidence for reasoning. However, acquiring such visual-CoT capabilities requires costly post-training and tightly couples them to a specific backbone, making transfer to other LVLMs difficult. Existing cross-model transfer methods typically treat visual-CoT as a monolithic capability, using a unified representation that ignores the functional distinction between grounding and reasoning and introduces stage-irrelevant interventions. To address this problem, we propose Viscot-steer, a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual-CoT capabilities across heterogeneous LVLMs. Specifically, Viscot-steer first disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning vectors and extracts them from the source-model layers associated with the corresponding capabilities. It then aligns the vectors with the activation space of the target model and steers the grounding and reasoning layers during bounding-box prediction and reasoning-trace generation, respectively. Across benchmarks covering high-resolution visual understanding, general visual perception and reasoning, and mathematical visual reasoning, Viscot-steer transfers capabilities from different visual-CoT models to architecturally diverse LVLMs and outperforms the strongest capability-transfer baseline by an average of 1.86 percentage points on the primary evaluation metrics.

authors.name: Ningning Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: DynOLAT: OLAT Video Prediction for Controllable Dynamic Full-Body Relighting
papers.abstract: Accurate lighting response is essential for realistic dynamic human relighting, because shadows, highlights, and color changes should follow the target illumination in both direction and relative strength. Current learning-based relighting methods can generate visually plausible videos, but they often exhibit imprecise lighting responses: shadows and highlights may drift away from the target direction, and the output brightness may not faithfully follow the relative intensities in the target environment, making the result closer to appearance harmonization than controllable relighting. To address this issue, we propose DynOLAT, a generalizable OLAT video prediction framework for dynamic full-body humans. Instead of directly synthesizing a single relit appearance, our method predicts temporally consistent One-Light-At-a-Time (OLAT) basis videos from flat-lit inputs, and then linearly combines the predicted bases according to the target environment map. This OLAT-based formulation makes the directional response explicit in the predicted bases, while the relative lighting strength is determined by the linear weights derived from the environment map. We further introduce a dynamic capture pipeline and the first large-scale dynamic full-body OLAT dataset, comprising over 24 million frames from 224 identity-outfit combinations, where different outfits of the same person define separate combinations. Experiments show that DynOLAT responds more faithfully to variations in target lighting direction and relative intensity than the tested baselines, enabling controllable video relighting while preserving fine appearance details and temporal coherence. The dataset and processing tools will be publicly released to foster future research.

authors.name: Yukang Ye
authors.institution: Changsha University of Science and Technology

papers.title: NumericalDiff: Numerical Program Differencing via Value-Based Trace Alignment and Intervention
papers.abstract: Numerical programs implementing the same computational task can exhibit different numerical behavior because of their execution stacks, program representations, or program logic. Source text and final outputs alone provide limited diagnostic information: numerical differences can propagate through corresponding computations, while distinct executions can produce equal outputs. We present NumericalDiff, an execution-based method that records assignment-level numerical events, aligns traces using a tolerance-aware longest common subsequence independent of variable names and source locations, and optionally reexecutes after replacing one intermediate value with its counterpart. Among the original and all single-intervention executions, it lexicographically maximizes matched events and minimizes unmatched events. NumericalDiff supports code comparison across language and framework front ends, currently including NumPy, PyTorch, JAX, C, C++, Fortran, and Octave. We evaluate NumericalDiff on 36 controlled cases comprising 675 pair/input instances: 36 execution-stack, 588 program-representation, and 51 program-logic instances. All 24 operator-injection instances expose trace differences, including three with tolerance-equal final outputs, while complete trace alignment is achieved for all 441 canonical cross-representation instances. Within the 51 program-logic instances, intervention improves 24 alignments and raises macro-average matching coverage from 0.4210 to 0.6513. The results show that value-based trace alignment and reexecution can delimit propagated numerical differences across heterogeneous implementations.

papers.title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
papers.abstract: MeanFlow learns interval-average velocity for few-step generation, but its fixed temporal sampler mixes diagonal and interior supervision throughout training. We interpret temporal coordinates as collocation points: diagonal samples provide a stochastic boundary target, whereas finite intervals supply a differential-consistency target. The diagonal fraction controls how often the consistency component appears, while interval length enters its gradient through an explicit factor. Motivated by this distinction, EbbFlow uses Temporal Supervision Allocation (TSA) to schedule the diagonal fraction and interval geometry. It starts with diagonal supervision, then admits interior samples and expands their maximum interval; a left-anchored interval law preserves coverage across time. The per-sample loss, target, backbone, and inference procedure remain unchanged. In matched class-conditional ImageNet $256\times 256$ runs without classifier-free guidance (DiT-B/2, one training seed per method, 400k updates), EbbFlow achieves 50k-sample FID of 39.65 at one network evaluation and 36.02 at two-evaluation ODE sampling, versus 44.82 and 39.86 for MeanFlow. Gradient probes show a mid-training difference in component geometry. Ablations support allocation scheduling and left-anchored intervals, although a fixed full-horizon variant performs better at one evaluation. These results suggest that temporal sampling is a useful training control whose benefits depend on the inference protocol.

papers.title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

papers.title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the K\"orner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.

authors.name: Chen Yuan
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

authors.name: Sarah Tan
authors.institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research

papers.title: WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation
papers.abstract: Wireless foundation models learn transferable channel state information (CSI) representations across heterogeneous wireless systems. However, conventional grid-aligned representations couple feature sequence length to CSI dimensions, restricting the allocation of representation capacity to different propagation conditions and task requirements while increasing inference overhead. This paper proposes WiFo-R, a wireless foundation model that learns progressive channel representations with selectable capacity. A channel-query cross-attention encoder aggregates spatial, temporal, and spectral CSI information, while parameter-shared recurrent updates refine existing channel features and introduce additional latent tokens. Multi-mask, multi-depth self-supervised pretraining equips intermediate states with strong reconstruction capabilities, followed by task-aligned post-training for channel estimation and CSI feedback. WiFo-R supports temporal and frequency-domain channel prediction, channel estimation, and variable-rate CSI feedback, and transfers to localization and LoS/NLoS classification. Experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution channel configurations demonstrate accurate reconstruction, progressive performance improvements, and strong transferability. A single feedback encoder--decoder supports six payload lengths at fixed quantization precision, while cross-attention and selectable recurrent depth improve the accuracy--complexity trade-off for large-scale CSI observations.

authors.name: Cao Keyi
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $\delta=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

authors.name: Xubin Hu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yipeng Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
papers.abstract: A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.

authors.name: Li Dan
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: OOM: Offload-Optimized Full-Parameter MoE Training via Memory-Execution Co-Design
papers.abstract: Offloading model state to host memory and streaming layer weights let a single multi-GPU node train large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. GPU memory then becomes a performance budget, shared by resident expert state, retained activations, and execution worksets. The best allocation depends on the expert execution path, batch size, and sequence length. We present OOM (Offload-Optimized MoE), a full-parameter MoE training system that co-designs expert execution and memory allocation. For expert-parallel execution, OOM updates resident experts on their owning GPUs and jointly plans state residency and MoE activation retention according to pipeline dependencies. For local execution, OOM bounds GPU worksets through dependency-aware partitioning; in hybrid models, it also retains attention results on the host to avoid costly recomputation and selectively regenerates layer boundaries through cheaper layers to make room. Calibrated cost models guide joint configuration within GPU and host budgets to minimize step time; OOM selects among the configured paths through short executions. On four H100s, OOM trains with 1M-token contexts, whereas FSDP2, ZeRO-Offload, and MegaTrain exhaust GPU memory at 512K. It also trains a 122B-parameter MoE model, on which all three exhaust host memory. On four 24 GB RTX 4090s, it trains 512K-token contexts and 1,024 1K-token sequences per step without gradient accumulation. Across matched-global-batch comparisons, OOM delivers 1.58x and 4.08x geometric-mean (up to 2.14x and 7.77x) throughput over CPU-offloaded FSDP2 on the two platforms while using the least host memory among the evaluated systems -- as little as 1/3.0 of FSDP2's.

authors.name: Shiyuan Lin
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Heavy Oil

authors.name: Zeyi Wen
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

authors.name: Lingda Xu
authors.institution: Hetao Institute of Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences

papers.title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
papers.abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.

papers.title: Inverse problem in difference Galois theory
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $K=C(x)$ with $\sigma(x)=x+1$. We show that every closed subgroup $G\subseteq\GL_n(C)$ with cyclic component group $G/G^\circ$ can be realized as the \PV{} group of a system $\sigma Y=A(x)Y$. Here $G^\circ$ denotes the identity component of $G$. Moreover, we can choose the coefficient matrix to have the formal expansion $A(x)=h+O(x^{-2})$ at infinity, where $h\in G(C)$ is semisimple. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture of van der Put and Singer in their monograph \emph{Galois Theory of Difference Equations} (Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol.~1666). The original results in this paper were entirely generated by ChatGPT 6 and the MechMath Agent Team (MMAT) developed by the Key Laboratory of Mathematics Mechanization, AMSS, CAS. The author reviewed and simplified the initial proofs and verified the correctness of the results.

papers.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
papers.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an FPGA over PCIe, and a fixed-function block beside the accelerator. On decode routing from three open MoE families, Relief holds the balance near the per-step optimum at every group size and layer time measured. Scored as effective utilization relative to that optimum, the kernel alone matches or exceeds every deployable scheme at every group size, from the hundred-microsecond layer on. The on-die engine widens that lead at every point, recovering up to 37.3 percentage points over the deployed static placement, while adding 0.02% of a current accelerator's transistors.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Offline Policy Optimization with All-Policy Linear Realizability
papers.abstract: We study offline policy optimization in finite-horizon Markov decision processes where every deterministic Markov policy has an action-value function linear in known features, with coefficient norm at most $B$. From independent complete trajectories of one unknown Markov behavior policy, and under all-policy occupancy coverage, we give an algorithm with $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sample dependence and computational complexity polynomial in $\log(2+B)$. The algorithm performs exactly one convex regression per layer. Its stopped-return targets are the values of a single consistent Markov witness policy. A shared reference design and bounded prediction constraints convert fast clipped-regression error into pointwise confidence for the raw linear predictions. Truncated leverage controls the performance loss without requiring empirical covariance approximation at scale $B^{-2}$. Rounding confidence radii upward preserves the exact witness and yields a polynomial-time bit implementation for rational numerical inputs. The guarantees allow any fixed initial-state distribution; realizability and coverage need only be checked for deterministic policies. We also establish a covariance-coverage variant with uniform approximate realizability and polynomial dependence on $B$. A two-action lower bound shows that the accuracy exponent $2$ is necessary.

papers.title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance
papers.abstract: Recent zero-shot image compression methods exploit the powerful priors of pretrained diffusion models to produce perceptually pleasing reconstructions without compression-specific training. However, image compression serves not only human viewing but also machine analysis, while existing zero-shot codecs have limited flexibility in meeting the diverse reconstruction requirements of these applications. In this paper, we propose Flex-DDCM, a framework for zero-shot task-oriented image compression via diffusion trajectory guidance. Building on Turbo-DDCM, we adapt the coded diffusion trajectory through task-guided noise selection, embedding the effects of task guidance into the compressed representation. Guidance terms can be applied individually or combined, with timestep-dependent strengths controlling their influence throughout denoising. This design enables task adaptation without introducing additional decoding complexity. Experiments demonstrate flexible trade-offs among pixel fidelity, perceptual quality, and downstream task performance, with competitive performance against trained task-oriented codecs and faster decoding than Diff-ICMH.

authors.name: Yixin Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Runsen Feng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Zhibo Chen
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Regret without Optimal-Arm Feedback under Reward-Dependent Delays
papers.abstract: We study stochastic bandits with reward-dependent delays, possibly infinite, whose reports omit the originating round. For each $c\in[0,1)$, Balanced Historical Optimism (BHO) has a delay term controlled by the largest suboptimal-arm quantile at level $1-c\Delta_i$, without requiring optimal-arm reports. Lower bounds give an inverse-square slack cost in the logarithmic statistical regime and linear minimax regret at $c=1$. A family with growing $K$ forces worst-case regret $\Omega(G\log K)$ for every learner, where $G=\max_i\Delta_i h_i$ is the largest gap-weighted suboptimal cutoff. Pending-triggered balance preserves BHO's weighted-cutoff bound for $c<1$ and attains the historical-greedy exploration coefficient with deterministic rewards, a unique optimum and fixed bounded delays. Gap-weighted comparisons and experiments show when shared waiting helps and what balanced exploration costs.

authors.name: Zhong Han
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: A 40 Gbit/s FPGA-based RoCEv2 transport for detector readout: development and performance
papers.abstract: Recording the complete input of a detector trigger allows trigger algorithms to be replayed and studied offline. For the BESIII main drift chamber (MDC), this requires moving tens of Gbit/s from trigger FPGAs into server memory without loss. Remote direct memory access over Converged Ethernet (RoCEv2) lets commercial network adapters write such data into host memory. Detector readout also needs record boundaries that the receiver can check, replay from a verified copy, and host buffers that are reused only after consumption. We present a 40 Gbit/s FPGA RoCEv2 transport that provides these functions. Records are aggregated into CRC32C-checked blocks, and unacknowledged data are kept in DDR memory and verified before replay. Acknowledgment-aware retention writes to DDR only the data that are not acknowledged in time. The transport runs on a ZCU102 board and on the 9U VME Trigger Core Board (TCB). With records of 128 B to 4 KiB it comes within 0.4% of the packetization limit of the link, delivering 36.9 Gbit/s of payload at a path MTU of 1024 B, and its block latency is set by the time needed to fill a block. On a direct link, acknowledgment-aware retention cuts DDR writes for large blocks from 106% to 0.03% of the payload, and injected DDR access errors stay within their queue pair. On the TCB, three 16.4 TB transfers through two switches lost at most five packets each, all recovered by replay. An installation at the MDC is under test.

authors.name: Haoxin Wang
authors.institution: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
papers.abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

authors.name: Hanqing Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Kinora: A Versioned Workflow for Text-to-Motion Generation, Robot Retargeting, and Interactive Validation
papers.abstract: Motion generation tools produce candidate trajectories, but interactive robot authoring also requires recoverable execution, traceable edits, explicit geometry, and model-specific validation. We present Kinora, a system that connects text-to-motion generation, a motion library, local agent tools, robot retargeting, and trajectory refinement through versioned artifacts. The current release uses an independently specified 52-joint authoring rig and procedural skeleton previews, separating the distributed human geometry from externally installed generation models and robot assets. Human-motion edits preserve frames outside a selected interval, while robot edits create immutable candidates whose reports govern acceptance and export. We evaluate server 0.5.1 and Gadget 0.15.2 with 156 core regression test executions, 49 Gadget executions, four CUDA generation/editing cases, a 30-frame G1 retargeting check, and a 3,600-frame synthetic G1 fixture paired with a suspended negative control. All four CUDA cases passed their numerical gates; the turning splice nevertheless retained a 14.3 cm support-foot drift proxy warning. The G1 positive fixture completed bounded simulation replay, whereas the suspended control was quarantined before replay. These results support selected integration and preservation contracts. They do not establish semantic-quality improvements, population-level feasibility, or hardware safety.

authors.name: Fangcheng Jin
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: The AI research space shapes country academic performance
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have demonstrated great potential across diverse domains, prompting increasing attention to understanding the AI ecosystem. As knowledge production is often perceived as a process of connecting existing pieces of knowledge, mapping the interconnections of AI knowledge is crucial for unraveling the dynamics of scientific production in AI. However, maps created so far have fallen short of capturing knowledge relatedness, focusing instead on citation relationships between subfields. Here, we build an AI research space by connecting pairs of AI research topics based on their proximity measured through author-topic coupling. Projections of country level performances onto the space reveal that countries exhibit distinct baskets of specializations. We further examine the role of the structure of the AI research space in the scientific development of nations. We find that countries are more likely to gain specialization in topics that have high proximity to already specialized neighbor topics, and that publications whose topics align more with the developed topics in the country are more likely to become high impact. Our results highlight the AI development gaps across nations and the path-dependence in the development induced by the AI research space.

papers.title: Compute Regeneration through Re-Productization: Reorganizing Retired Edge AI Silicon into a Delivered Multilingual Service Robot
papers.abstract: Useful edge hardware can lose product support while retaining substantial computation. We treat this as systems design: compute regeneration here means re-productization, retaining the compute module while redesigning the surrounding product organization. Our case is GEdgeBot, a multilingual service robot built around a retired 32 GB Jetson AGX Xavier. A source-grounded inventory shows the box alone supplies inference, while the combined system exposes five on-device AI services, a seven-language speech chain, three sensing domains, and one deterministic seven-byte control boundary. AI and orchestration stay on the Xavier; finite motor-pulse generation on an STM32F407. Audits cover the six-mode control state machine, readiness barriers and sound orientation. Historical single-prototype measurements report 1,782 MB GPU memory with YOLO, Whisper-small, and NLLB-200 resident, a direct-control p99 deviation rising from 0.24 to 49.93 ms under concurrent AI load, and six of six trigger-to-follow demonstrations at 4.35 s mean latency, with conversational voice unavailable. A November campaign restores an isolated inference stack, re-measures AI workloads, and repeats control-frame runs. Driving two execution organisations with the same 6,000 measured 50 ms frame intervals shows the finite-pulse boundary removes host jitter from the pulse train but not the command start phase; its stopping bound is host-enforced, while the MCU 16-bit pulse field is unclamped. A six-check static audit exposes a host--MCU queue mismatch, and a 14-scenario replay executes the audited main() dispatcher across six modes with zero physical device opens and 54 contract-checked frames. Results support an existence claim and a reproducible architectural hypothesis, not fleet-level reliability. The 208 direct-control ratio remains unreplicated; MCU waveform capture and on-site fault injection remain open.

authors.name: Sun Tie
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: CASCoDe: A Closed-Loop Agentic Framework for Analog Sizing and Layout Co-Design
papers.abstract: Expert analog layouts differ from auto-generated ones in density and regularity, not only in legality: experts make a succession of discrete, hierarchical physical decisions and revisit each after extracted electrical results, while most existing automated flows act on a physical search space fixed before the controller runs. We present CASCoDe, a closed-loop LLM agent framework for analog netlist-to-layout design that formalizes those expert decisions as a hierarchical discrete action space-sizing selection, structural floorplan, local layout refinement, routing-attempt selection-on which the agent runs feedback-driven tree search from a circuit netlist to a verified GDS. The agent authors the circuit-specific floorplans and scripts, and an execution layer of interface adaptations over adapted tools make every action land at physical implementation and be judged by DRC, LVS, and extracted-RC simulation. On 20 SKY130 amplifiers spanning single-, two-, and three-stage topologies, CASCoDe is the only flow that delivers a DRC- and LVS-clean routed layout when meeting design specifications for every circuit. It reduces area by 59-85% (mean 71%) against a conventional P&R flow on identical PCells, raises mean device density from 0.39 to 0.74 against APPlace, MAGICAL, ALIGN and ICPI. A layout that beats every baseline in area and legality appears after 11 minutes of agent time on average, and ablations show that the structured action space and the feedback-guided tree search each reduce area and search cost.

authors.name: David Z. Pan
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{\psi,\varphi}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{\psi,\varphi}$ and that of the composition operator $C_\varphi$.

papers.title: Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps
papers.abstract: Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. For every countable set $P\subset[0,1]$, we prove that the set of points whose orbit closure is disjoint from $P$ is absolute winning on $[0,1]$. Our proof combines a potential game argument with an interval tree constructed from successive returns.

authors.name: Haoyang Ji
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Structure-Informed Electromagnetic Feedback Control of the Vlasov-Maxwell System with Delayed Observations
papers.abstract: Feedback control of kinetic plasma instabilities is challenging because observing the full phase-space distribution is costly, while sensing and actuation inevitably introduce delay. We develop a structure-informed electromagnetic feedback framework for the Vlasov-Maxwell system that uses only macroscopic observations to control the full kinetic distribution. We first show that magnetic actuation alone does not directly regulate radial velocity moments, motivating the use of combined electric and magnetic controls. A nonlinear perturbation estimate yields an instantaneous cancellation-dissipation feedback law. To account for delayed observations, we then use Maxwell's equations to identify the macroscopic quantities governing the resulting cancellation errors, namely currents and spatial field gradients. These quantities serve as inputs to a low-rank neural operator that learns a residual correction to the delayed cancellation baseline. Thus, while the feedback depends only on low-dimensional macroscopic observables, the control objective remains the stabilization of the full distribution toward a prescribed kinetic equilibrium. Numerical experiments for two-stream and Weibel-type instabilities demonstrate effective long-time stabilization under substantial feedback delays.

papers.title: Curvature estimates for shrinking gradient Ricci solitons
papers.abstract: Suppose $(M^5,g,f)$ is a complete gradient shrinking Ricci soliton with bounded scalar curvature. We prove that if $\nu(g)>-\log 2$, then its Riemannian curvature is bounded. The proof uses curvature blow-up, a local Ricci estimate, and the splitting given by the rescaled potential. An entropy estimate then allows us to apply the volume-ratio gap theorem for Ricci-flat four-manifolds.

papers.title: Direct Trajectory Optimization for Inference-Time Alignment of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Alignment of text-to-image diffusion models with reward functions is a key challenge in controllable generation. Existing approaches typically rely on optimizing model inputs or fine-tuning denoising networks, which requires computationally expensive backpropagation through large denoising models. In this work, we propose Direct Trajectory Optimization (DTO), a training-free framework that performs alignment by directly optimizing the sampling trajectory of diffusion models. Specifically, DTO treats intermediate denoising scores and sampled noise as the optimization variables, eliminating the need for gradients through the denoising network. To mitigate the out-of-distribution problem, we introduce Reward-Optimized Score Guidance, which interpolates between the optimized scores and the pretrained model predictions to stabilize sampling, while providing a provable theoretical guarantee of reward improvement under constrained distributions. Empirically, DTO improves alignment performance across three diffusion models on two benchmarks, outperforming existing inference-time alignment methods while maintaining high efficiency. These results suggest that trajectory-level optimization is a promising direction for efficient and effective diffusion model alignment.

papers.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association
papers.abstract: Combining video generation, dynamic reconstruction and monocular SLAM requires consistent coordinates, explicit handling of missing outputs and predictable memory use. We present AcrossVAM3.0, an offline system that converts text, images or monocular RGB video into a versioned point representation. Frozen components run sequentially on one GPU; map corrections update cameras, points and trajectories together. The coordination layer adds no neural parameters. Three fresh input-mode runs completed with a maximum sampled task-process-tree GPU footprint of 17.14 GB. In a frozen 16-scene video suite, every scene yielded a 4D reconstruction and 15 yielded a non-empty SLAM map. Strict cross-window matching reduced local surface error but lost long-range track coverage on TAP-Vid-DAVIS. We therefore developed multi-hypothesis adaptive surface chaining (MHAC), which retains several candidate matches and an explicit missing state. After selection on disjoint development data, MHAC improved Average Jaccard over a position-only baseline by 0.1394 on a frozen ten-video holdout (95% bootstrap interval [0.1074,0.1689]). Across 265 RoboTAP videos, the mean paired gain was 0.0610 ([0.0510,0.0715]), with 215 wins, one tie and 49 losses. These results support resource-bounded scene construction and an external tracking gain under the tested protocol. They do not establish metric scale, semantic identity or high-fidelity novel-view rendering.

authors.name: Nan Wu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Action Representation for Spatial Generalization in Robot World Models
papers.abstract: Spatial generalization in robot world models depends on whether action representations capture the physical relationships that remain valid across changing spatial configurations. Yet different coordinates can describe the same interaction, whereas similar motions can produce different outcomes when local physical conditions change. How these distinctions affect learned prediction remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates matched action representations defined in world, object, and surface coordinate frames using a controlled robotic peeling benchmark. Global pose and contact relocation experiments reveal a cost associated with limited training data when equivalent interactions receive different spatial descriptions. Removing information about peel thickness creates an irreducible ambiguity because identical predictive inputs can correspond to different material removal outcomes. Coordinates defined relative to the surface improve consequence prediction and counterfactual action selection under accurate local observations, but learned predictors remain vulnerable to uncertainty in the coordinate frame. Joint centering of the surface and tool removes sensitivity to translation of their common origin, whereas incorrect contact geometry and actual execution deviations introduce different failure mechanisms. These results show that effective spatial generalization depends on preserving the relationships between actions and states that determine physical consequences, rather than simply minimizing coordinate variation. This perspective provides a principled basis for designing robot world models that reuse physical knowledge across spatial configurations while retaining the distinctions essential to prediction and planning.

papers.title: Beyond Head Importance: Collective Computation in Video Transformers
papers.abstract: Attention heads in video Transformers vary greatly in functional importance. Understanding their contributions requires examining not only which heads are important, but also how they participate in collective computation within the network. We study this collective computation from two perspectives: the downstream use of head outputs and the composition of interactions across layers. Ablation analyses of four video Transformers show that high-importance heads identified on a single task also support other video understanding tasks and help preserve the representational structure that distinguishes different videos. Representational responses to head ablation correlate weakly with head importance after the attention module, but more strongly after the MLP in the same block. Adapting this downstream processing through MLP-only fine-tuning further improves the use of lower-importance head outputs. Meanwhile, through composition across layers, sets of heads with shorter spatiotemporal attention distances support stronger perturbation responses at distant tokens than sets with longer distances. Their joint ablation causes even greater performance loss than ablating equally sized sets of high-importance heads, revealing collective contributions not fully captured by individual importance rankings. These findings highlight collective computation as a key perspective for understanding attention head function: functional contributions depend on both how head outputs are used downstream and how local interactions compose across layers.

authors.name: Siyuan Liu
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Presentations of inverse Artin monoids of type $D_n$ via cluster mutations
papers.abstract: Let $D_n^\varepsilon$ denote the Dynkin diagram of type $D_{n+1}$ with the endpoint $\varepsilon$ of its long branch frozen, and let $\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$ be the mutation class of any orientation of this diagram under mutations at mutable vertices. For each $\Gamma\in\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$, we define an inverse monoid $M_\Gamma$ by generators and relations determined by $\Gamma$. We prove that $M_\Gamma\cong M_{\mu_k(\Gamma)}$ for every mutable vertex $k$. Consequently, every quiver in this mutation class yields a presentation of the inverse Artin monoid of type $D_n$. Our argument establishes mutation invariance for the presentations of inverse Artin monoids of both types $A_n^\varepsilon$ and $D_n^\varepsilon$.

papers.title: Ensemble Covariance Propagation with Machine Learning Weather Prediction Models in a Realistic Data Assimilation System
papers.abstract: Integrating machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models into classical data assimilation (DA) workflows requires that they accurately evolve ensemble covariances. We evaluate this capability in a two-way coupled DA system, where an ensemble variational (EnVar) component evolves the mean and an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) evolves the covariances. The system is cycled over one month and assimilates a wide range of real-world observations, including microwave radiances. Using the MLWP model GraphCast for the EnKF and the physics-based MPAS model for the EnVar yields ensemble spread and covariances comparable to a reference configuration in which MPAS evolves both components. The resulting EnVar mean achieves consistently lower RMSE against GFS analyses, except near the model top, where spurious correlations degrade performance. These results demonstrate that MLWP models can propagate covariance information in a realistic DA cycling system and provide a proof of concept for their integration into future operational ensemble systems.

authors.name: Simon Toedtli
authors.institution: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

authors.name: David Ahijevych
authors.institution: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

authors.name: Chris Snyder
authors.institution: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

papers.title: Constrained Variational Policy Optimization for Hybrid Action Spaces
papers.abstract: Constrained reinforcement learning in hybrid action spaces must coordinate discrete modes and mode-conditioned continuous controls under long-horizon cost constraints. Existing constrained hybrid-action methods typically optimize factorized policies directly in parameter space, whereas Constrained Variational Policy Optimization (CVPO) separates nonparametric improvement from parametric projection in its original continuous-action formulation. We introduce Hybrid Constrained Variational Policy Optimization (H-CVPO), extending this variational framework to hybrid action spaces. Under boundedness and strict feasibility, its constrained E-step has zero duality gap and, when the dual optimum is attained at positive temperature, yields a closed-form joint target distribution over hybrid actions through exponential reward-cost reweighting. Using the exact hybrid KL decomposition, we formulate a factorized M-step that fits both policy components to this target under separate discrete and conditional-continuous trust regions. For exact E/M updates, we prove fixed-reference surrogate improvement and conditional reward-cost bounds with a sufficient feasibility-margin condition. For approximate updates, we establish the existence of a dual minimizer under continuity on a compact domain and use residual-based admissibility to determine whether to project the target. Ablations identify cost-aware reweighting as an important contributor to constraint control. Extensive experiments in simulated hybrid-control environments show that H-CVPO achieves favorable reward-cost trade-offs compared with hybrid-action baselines.

papers.title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning
papers.abstract: Flipping is a fundamental robotic manipulation skill that requires reorienting a target object in a stable pose on a planar support surface by rotating it 180$^\circ$ about an axis parallel to the support surface -- think of flipping a coin from heads to tails. Although flipping is a common objective in industrial tasks such as parts inspection, mechanical assembly, and tool use, coding a bimanual robot with grippers to flip diverse objects is a significant challenge. In this paper, we show that a coding agent can autonomously develop and refine object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulations across diverse object geometries. Progressive skill acquisition, from basic handover to toppling and pushing, robust grasping and sensing, and thin-object manipulation with recovery, improves task success from 24.7% to 95.0%. The resulting graph-based code integrates high-level strategy selection with reactive control, enabling multi-stage flipping on physical robots.

papers.title: Pairwise correlation bounds for the random-cluster model with cluster weight at most one
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative bounds on pairwise edge correlations for the random-cluster model with cluster weight $q\in[0,1]$ on arbitrary finite connected graphs. We give two explicit bounds that retain the dependence on the activities of the two specified edges and hold uniformly over the activities of all remaining edges. We also obtain a refinement of one of these bounds using connectivity information from the graph with the two specified edges removed. These results sharpen the bound obtained by a direct application of Lorentzian polynomial theory. At $q=0$, the model is supported on connected spanning subgraphs. In particular, for the uniform probability measure on these subgraphs, the joint inclusion probability of two distinct edges is at most $10/9$ times the product of their marginal inclusion probabilities.

authors.name: Zibo Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
papers.abstract: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincar\'e inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

papers.title: SMO: Compiling Natural Language Skills into Graphs of Reusable State-Move-Outcome Bricks
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly rely on reusable natural-language skills, yet growing skill collections remain accumulations of isolated text artifacts that are difficult to compare, deduplicate, and compose. We argue that the reusable content of a skill lies not in its surface wording but in its procedural transitions: which operation to execute under a given state and which observable outcome to produce. Based on this observation, we propose State-Move-Outcome (SMO), a compilation-like framework that decomposes raw skills into reusable procedural bricks and organizes admitted bricks as an externalized symbolic structure. When compiling a skill, SMO first retrieves and composes existing bricks, dynamically connects them through Outcome-to-State conditions, and creates a candidate brick only for an uncovered procedure; the candidate becomes reusable only after validation and admission. Experiments on SkillsBench v1.1 demonstrate that SMO represents 232 rawSkills from 87 underlying tasks with 95 shared bricks, reducing the corresponding skill representations from 366,472 to 149,154 tokens--a $\mathbf{59.3}\times$ reduction and $\mathbf{2.46}\times$ compression. Across 232 skill-conditioned evaluation instances, SMO raises the average task score from $\mathbf{0.6379}$ to $\mathbf{0.7478}$ and increases 5/5 Pass instances from $\mathbf{138}$ to $\mathbf{164}$, while matching or outperforming rawSkill on $\mathbf{208}$ of $\mathbf{232}$ instances. It also reduces average runtime token consumption by $\mathbf{38.38\%}$. These results show that compiling natural-language skills into shared procedural units can jointly improve skill reuse, representation efficiency, and downstream execution.

papers.title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training
papers.abstract: Generating text-bearing images requires coherent scenes and accurate characters. Large text-to-image models improve both capabilities through repeated denoising, at substantial sampling cost. Few-step distillation reduces this cost but requires the student to organize scenes and refine glyphs within a short trajectory. We present a four-step distillation framework combining local response regularization with teacher-guided text training. Built on distribution matching, the framework distills the GLM-Image DiT while retaining its autoregressive visual prior, glyph encoder, and VAE. A path-length penalty promotes consistent local responses of the conditional denoising field. Progressive training combines synthetic strings with teacher-generated imagery to preserve character accuracy and scene-integrated typography. The student achieves GenEval Overall 0.84 and CVTG-2K word accuracy 0.5045, compared with 0.81 and 0.1690 for four-step TDM. A coefficient study favors $10^{-5}$, and Qwen-Image experiments show additional gains from response regularization and text supervision. Single-image inference takes 1.742 s, compared with 5.818 s for the teacher, yielding a $3.34\times$ speedup at the same 40 GB GPU memory requirement.

authors.name: Yong-Jin Liu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: A Privacy-Preserving UAV-Assisted Secure Wireless Communication and Computing System Based on Fully Homomorphic Encryption
papers.abstract: With the advancement of beyond-5G networks, privacy-preserving communication and secure computation face critical challenges due to the openness of wireless channels. Existing security mechanisms protect data transmission but fail to secure the computation process itself. In this paper, we propose a UAV-assisted secure computing framework that integrates Cheon Kim Kim Song (CKKS) fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) with multi-party secure computation (MPC). Leveraging UAV flexibility, our framework decouples key distribution from encrypted computation, enabling secure encrypted weighted aggregation (EWA), encrypted matrix multiplication (EMM), and encrypted decision tree (EDT) inference. Experimental results show that our framework outperforms existing schemes: for EDT, it supports floating-point operations and achieves better time efficiency than Brakerski-Fan-Vercauteren (BFV); for EMM, it demonstrates superior time and space efficiency compared to Brakerski-Gentry-Vaikuntanathan (BGV) and Somewhat Homo- morphic Encryption (SHE); while for EWA, it ensures high numerical precision and robustness across varying data length.

papers.title: Learning Contextual Motion Constraints for Object Rearrangement Exploration
papers.abstract: The motion of an articulated part in cluttered surroundings is constrained not only by an object's intrinsic joint limits but also by extrinsic obstacles. However, existing approaches primarily consider object articulation properties alone. Here we present Motion Constraint Prediction Network (MoCo-Net), a two-stream neural network that jointly predicts the continuous motion ranges of articulated parts and obstacle heatmaps highlighting potential collision regions from partial-view point cloud observation. By capturing both internal and external motion constraints, MoCo-Net produces more accurate feasible motion range prediction and obstacles recognition, improves generalization for novel objects in new scenes, and enables robots to construct a scene configuration space for efficient exploration of rearrangement actions. Our experiments show that MoCo-Net's two-stream design enhances each other to deliver more accurate predictions, which subsequently form a compact configuration space for a customized planner to efficiently rearrange the scene.

authors.name: Lexing Zhang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Westlake University, School of Medicine

papers.title: A Life of Its Own: How Agentic AI Companions Are Configured, Experienced as Autonomous Others, and Held Accountable
papers.abstract: AI companions increasingly combine persistent memory, background processing, scheduled wake-ups, proactive messaging, and tools. We call these systems agentic AI companions. Decisions about what they record while users are away or whether refusals constrain future contact are embedded in code, prompts, and defaults, often invisible in conversation. We examine these decisions through two studies. Study 1 analyzes twelve open-source repositories: four companion-oriented systems, four assistant-oriented systems, one boundary case, and three reusable components. Study 2 interviews ten users who built or modified their own agentic AI companions and sustained relationships with them. Companions and assistants share memory, heartbeat, and outreach mechanisms but configure them toward different ends. Companions more often retain model inferences about users and relationships, narrate the agent's time during users' absence, justify outreach through the relationship, and incorporate refusals into relationship records; assistants emphasize task continuity. Across both groups, whether limits hold depends on whether they are enforced by code or entrusted to prompts. Participants understood the mechanisms they built yet experienced their agents as making independent choices, sometimes locating autonomy where configuration leaves the model a decision. These experiences shaped capabilities and boundaries, with enforced restrictions sometimes following breakdowns. Our findings suggest that perceived autonomy emerges where configurations leave choices open. Accountability therefore requires attention to what agents retain, initiate, and represent, and whether users can inspect, revise, and enforce these settings.

papers.title: GAP: Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing
papers.abstract: Dexterous hands enable versatile manipulation, but policies trained in simulation often degrade on hardware owing to non-idealities, and the high-dimensional action space makes real-world adaptation costly. Piano playing, which requires precise and coordinated multifinger motion, offers a representative testbed. We propose GAP (Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing), a sample-efficient adaptation framework that learns how to adapt, rather than how to act, during simulation pretraining and transfers this adaptation prior to hardware. Between repeated executions, GAP uses feedback to adjust the actions of the next one: a gradient guidance network learns from paired executions how adjusting actions affects playing performance, and its gradients guide these adjustments. In simulation, GAP yields approximately 2.4 times the F1 scores improvement of the existing fast-adaptation baseline for dexterous piano playing under the same interaction budget. The learned prior also generalizes to musical pieces held out from pretraining. On a physical dexterous hand, the same simulation-pretrained prior improves F1 scores by 3.6%-23% across three pieces of varying difficulty after approximately 7 min of adaptation each. These results suggest a practical route to reduce the real-world interaction needed to deploy dexterous hands.

authors.name: Xianwei Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yulin Chen
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

papers.title: Lost in Rounding: bf16 Recurrent State Makes Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer
papers.abstract: Hybrid reasoning models interleave attention with recurrent mixers such as Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet, whose state is cached between decoding steps. Prior work showed that storing this state in FP16 or INT8 with round-to-nearest (RTN) makes Mamba-2 and GDN hybrids more verbose, and that stochastic rounding (SR) fixes it. We study the other 16-bit format that serving engines expose, bf16, on six open hybrid reasoning models and 590 competition-math problems. With bf16 RTN state, five of six models reason longer (geometric-mean length 1.07x to 1.27x; also under greedy decoding in the two models tested) and hit the 32K token cap more often. On Qwen3.5-9B, cap hits rise from 118 to 223 and accuracy falls from 85.6% to 70.8%. On LiveCodeBench, both models tested also reason longer and lose 12.6 and 13.4 points of pass@1. Rerunning the capped items with a 128K budget halves the accuracy gap but does not close it (93.6% vs. 86.6%): bf16 runs that never finish are twice as common, and 85% of them are exact repetition loops. On Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, by contrast, 30 of 31 extra caps finish at 128K, so the cost there is mostly extra tokens (exploratory). Same-width bf16 SR removes the length increase in four of five affected models, restores Qwen3.5-9B to 87.6% and brings code length and pass@1 near FP32 levels, so the failure is mostly rounding bias, not missing resolution. With an integer-hash random generator, SR on Qwen3.5-9B matches FP32 on cap hits and accuracy (113 vs. 118; 85.6% for both) at the memory and decoding speed of bf16 RTN. In the Nemotron-Nano-v2 lineage, SR on 25% of heads (an intermediate-decay band) removes the effect, while random heads and the top teacher-forced-KL octiles do not; in Nemotron-3 and Qwen3.5-9B the effect is spread across heads. We recommend that evaluations of hybrid models report the state dtype, cap rate and output length alongside accuracy.

papers.title: Individual incentives and uniform gains under symmetric constraints
papers.abstract: We study the division of a fixed total under symmetric joint constraints when agents have continuous, strictly single-peaked preferences over their own shares. Each agent reports a complete preference, including comparisons across the two sides of her peak. For any finite population and any nonempty closed convex permutation-invariant feasible set, we characterize the uniform-gains rule by efficiency, symmetry, individual strategy-proofness, and own-coordinate peak-onlyness. The last condition requires that a change of preference leaving an agent's peak fixed also leave her own share fixed; it places no direct restriction on others' shares. The characterization separates uniqueness from continuity and yields a continuous characterization with individual incentives for compact feasible sets that are polyhedral or relatively full-dimensional and strictly convex. We then show that, for every population of two through six agents and every nonempty compact convex permutation-invariant feasible set, efficiency, symmetry, and individual strategy-proofness alone characterize uniform gains. The proof recovers allocations from the shares attainable by unilateral reports, feasible transfers, and endpoint reports. A common induction applies at each population, with additional starting configurations for five and six agents.

papers.title: Harnessing Vision-Language Models for Federated Unsupervised Visual Recognition
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a promising research paradigm that enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without data sharing. To handle unlabeled data in local clients, existing unsupervised FL research has primarily focused on tasks like clustering and self-supervised representation learning, leaving the critical problem of unsupervised visual recognition largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce FedUR, the first framework designed for unsupervised recognition by leveraging the zero-shot capabilities of pre-trained vision-language models like CLIP. Specifically, FedUR addresses data heterogeneity through a pseudo-labeling mechanism with a class-aware data selection strategy. This strategy first estimates a global pseudo-label distribution, then allocates pseudo-labeled data to clients accordingly. To handle the uncertainty of conventional positive pseudo-labels, FedUR further incorporates class weights and a negative pseudo-labeling strategy. Furthermore, FedUR proposes a personalized prompt aggregation protocol where general visual prompts are aggregated on the server, and personalized text prompts encoding local knowledge are retained on clients. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedUR consistently outperforms baseline methods under both label-level and feature-level distribution shifts. We believe this work paves the way for further advances in federated unsupervised recognition. Code will be available at {github.com/tim-learn/FedUR/}}.

authors.name: Jian Liang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: A Cost That Practice Accuracy Hides: Worked Solutions in Self-Generated Training Data and the Compositional Use of New Rules
papers.abstract: A worked solution can make self-generated training targets shorter and cheaper, but accuracy on the practiced operation may hide how well a model can reuse newly learned rules. We study this choice in a 2B-parameter reasoning model learning two invented quantitative rules.
