papers.title: Validating AI-Discovered Cloud Threats on Live Infrastructure: A Multi-Model, Multi-Cloud Study
papers.abstract: Cloud infrastructure threat modeling lacks empirical validation of AI-discovered threats. We present a three-phase methodology of multi-agent threat discovery, automated exploit synthesis, and non-destructive live validation, and apply it to three commercial foundation models on two cloud architectures, validating each threat natively on the cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure) it was discovered against. Of 233 AI-discovered threats, 103 were confirmed and 34 refuted (75.2\% precision, 95\% CI [67.3, 81.7]); 44 were conditional (the named mechanism refuted but an equivalent impact shown through another path) and 52 indeterminate. Multi-model discovery helped through breadth, not agreement: the three models together found 2.2$\times$ the confirmed threats of the best single model at comparable precision, while threats reported by several models were confirmed no more often than single-model ones. False positives were not architecture-specific: they asserted access or system state the deployment did not have. Threats coded in advance as observable configuration resolved cleanly more often than multi-step behavioral threats (72.5\% vs.\ 51.6\%), which were more often conditional, suggesting that models more often misidentify the exploitation mechanism than the underlying weakness. AI-assisted discovery is a practical input to security workflows when paired with empirical validation.

papers.title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
papers.abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

authors.name: Guangying Lv
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
papers.abstract:
We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(\psi,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form
  \begin{align}
  \psi(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}},
  n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)
  \end{align}
  in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system.
  The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(\psi,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$.
  We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

papers.title: Prospective Importance-based Cognitive Pilot Design for Semantic Sensing in ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Semantic sensing enables integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to acquire environmental information relevant to downstream tasks. However, existing pilot design methods either rely on static pilot configurations or learn end-to-end pilot selection policies, without explicitly evaluating the semantic contribution of candidate pilot locations. In this work, we propose a cognitive semantic sensing framework for human activity recognition in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. Rather than directly learning a high-dimensional mapping from observations to pilot locations, we introduce a semantic importance weight (SIW) to measure the semantic contribution of each candidate pilot location. Leveraging the information bottleneck (IB) principle and the mutual information-minimum mean-square error (I-MMSE) relationship, SIW assigns high values to future time-frequency (TF) channel coefficients that are both difficult to infer from the preceding observations and valuable for downstream inference. To efficiently obtain the SIW, we further develop a conditional diffusion model that predicts the corresponding uncertainty through denoising covariance estimation. Experiments on a real-world Wi-Fi sensing dataset show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baselines across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and pilot budgets.

authors.name: Zeyan Zhuang
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Luminescent Materials and Devices

papers.title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
papers.abstract: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

papers.title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.abstract: Iodine-vacancy migration and association are important factors in the structural stability of halide perovskites. Although neighboring vacancies have been suggested to form energetically favorable pairs, their stability and reconfiguration under finite-temperature lattice deformation remain unclear. Here, we combine machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain. The MLMD trajectories reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of short-time hopping fractions on strain, with strong isotropic compression favoring point-like separation and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping. Notably, biaxial compression produces distinct orientation-dependent responses: vacancy pairs initially aligned with the compressed plane preferentially undergo separation, whereas those perpendicular to the plane predominantly exhibit relay hopping. Complementary static calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential yield repulsive interactions for all configurations examined. These findings highlight the importance of finite-temperature dynamics and strain-dependent local geometry in understanding vacancy-pair stability and reconfiguration in halide perovskites.

papers.title: Coverage and shape of conformal highest-density sets: A minimax theory
papers.abstract: We study conditional coverage and geometric efficiency of conformal highest-density sets. The excess volume of such a set over the conditional highest-density set, the smallest set with the required conditional coverage, splits into a coverage error and an excess mass. We show that, among procedures whose volume is accurate up to a constant, the coverage error has the minimax rate of nonparametric regression on the covariate, and that the excess mass has the squared minimax rate of conditional density estimation. The usual split conformal construction calibrates these sets with a single threshold, which corrects the bias of the density estimate only on average over the covariate. We prove that its coverage error can then be of the order of the slower density rate. We therefore propose two-stage calibration, which estimates the coverage of the super-level sets of a density estimate by a regression on the covariate and uses this estimated coverage as the conformity score. Since these sets are fixed at each covariate value, their coverage is as smooth as the conditional density, and, under mild regularity conditions, the coverage error attains the regression rate even when the density estimate is inconsistent. The shape of the set still depends on the accuracy of the density estimate: sup-norm accuracy controls it at the minimax excess-mass rate, whereas accuracy in an integrated norm, even of minimax order, does not. With a local polynomial density estimate, two-stage calibration attains both minimax rates up to logarithmic factors. Simulations and an application to bike-sharing demand illustrate the results.

papers.title: Graph-Based RL for Sequential Rendezvous Planning with Multiple Patrolling USVs
papers.abstract: In patrol missions involving multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), a designated command USV can support fleet management by sequentially rendezvousing with each patrolling USV. These operations require motion-feasible route planning and priority-aware rendezvous sequencing, with the objective of minimizing mission completion time and total tardiness relative to priority-dependent due dates. We propose a framework combining grid-based path planning, surrogate travel-time prediction, and graph-based reinforcement learning. The path planner accounts for ocean currents and approximates turn-rate constraints through multi-stage maneuvers, with path feasibility empirically validated through trajectory-tracking simulations. For rendezvous sequencing, a Feasible Transition Graph (FTG) represents candidate rendezvous events and temporally feasible transitions, enabling a graph neural network to exploit spatiotemporal rendezvous relationships for policy learning. A surrogate predicts travel times from compact current and motion features to avoid repeated path searches during FTG construction and policy training. Evaluation using grid-based path planning shows statistically significant average objective reductions of 10.5%, 3.5%, and 1.5% compared with greedy, MLP-RL, and 2-step lookahead greedy, respectively. The policy achieves these improvements while requiring approximately 1/35 of the latter's computation time. It maintains its advantage over MLP-RL under unseen priority-tier settings, with larger gains as fleet size increases.

papers.title: Rescene-ESM: an Earth system model built around a frozen AI weather model
papers.abstract: Earth system models underpin climate projections, but their cost limits how many scenarios, ensemble members and impact pathways can be explored. Machine-learning weather models forecast as skillfully as physics-based models at a fraction of the cost, yet coupled to an ocean they have produced weak El Nino variability or have learned it from climate-model output, and none carries the climate through rivers to the people exposed to it. Here we present Rescene-ESM, an Earth system model whose coupler, YAHO, yokes a frozen 20.8-million-parameter AI weather model to physically formulated ocean, sea-ice, land, river, carbon and energy components constrained by observations. Adding the couplings one at a time shows what each contributes: over a climatological ocean the AI atmosphere varies from year to year by a third of the observed amount over the oceans, and an interactive mixed layer, an equatorial wave ocean, the residual of the observed sea surface temperature (SST) equation as stochastic forcing and the land's moisture flux raise this step by step and bring El Nino and its teleconnections, leaving the mean climate almost unchanged. The full model simulates about 1,000 years per day on one graphics processing unit, holds the observed climate for a thousand years without drift, reproduces the observed 1979-2022 global warming, carries forced change with a physically based structure around the frozen network (transient climate response 1.60 K), routes runoff to 212 river gauges with a median seasonal-cycle correlation of 0.79 and, driven by emissions, separates the heatwave exposure of an SSP1 and an SSP3 world by a factor of 4.7 in 2081-2100, three-quarters of it through the warmer climate.

authors.name: Kaoru Kakinuma
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Feasibility-Aware Learning for Network-Constrained Unit Commitment
papers.abstract: Learning-based approaches to network-constrained unit commitment (NCUC) usually still rely on an optimization solver to repair or complete their predictions, which limits the speedup they can deliver. This paper proposes FALCON-UC, a feasibility-aware graph learning framework that predicts commitment and dispatch jointly and produces final schedules without solving a mixed-integer program at inference time. It combines an LSTM--GraphSAGE predictor over a fully connected generator graph, a differentiable correction that embeds commitment-dependent dispatch bounds, power balance, and PTDF-based branch flows in training, and deterministic commitment, dispatch, and ramp-coupled reserve repairs at inference. On the 2383-bus system, FALCON-UC achieves $99.09\%$ commitment accuracy and a $0.4350\%$ mean absolute cost gap with all evaluated constraints within tolerance at $0.0562$ s per instance, a $2.27\times10^{3}$ speedup over the solver. MTLR R-SCUC-FL is slightly more accurate but still needs an optimization solver to complete each schedule, which takes $262.2$ s per instance, $4.67\times10^{3}$ times the FALCON-UC runtime. A label-only baseline without repair violates the balance and branch limits on every 2383-bus test instance, and FALCON-UC also meets all evaluated constraint tolerances on a 1354-bus system.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

papers.title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
papers.abstract: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|\chi_u+\chi_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.

papers.title: ClearForm: Shared-Surface Gaussian Splatting for Transparent and Opaque Scenes
papers.abstract: Transparent-interface reconstruction must recover glass surfaces even when most observed color comes from the scene behind them. We present ClearForm, a shared-planar-Gaussian method for jointly reconstructing transparent interfaces and the appearance seen through them. We identify and analyze the Geometry-Appearance Compositing Dilemma (GACD): when the same transparency-dependent alpha controls both color and geometry, revealing the background can weaken a transparent surface's contribution to geometric reconstruction. We derive its effect on plane-based depth estimation, identify a mechanism that can weaken geometric learning, and quantify the loss of interface support through controlled comparisons. To address this conflict, we develop geometry-preserving dual-opacity surface reconstruction. Shared planar Gaussians retain interface contributions in geometry compositing while modeling transmission and sparse reflection in RGB, supported by transparency-aware geometric constraints. To manage the different primitive-visibility requirements of these compositors, we introduce Dual-Evidence Lifecycle (DEL), which retains Gaussians supported by multi-view geometry or RGB reconstruction evidence. On 3D-FRONT-T, ClearForm achieves 27.05 mm Chamfer distance (CD) and 0.928 F1, compared with 59.18 mm CD for our PGSR reproduction and the reported 34 mm CD and 0.836 F1 for GLINT. On TransLab, it achieves 1.65 mm CD, 0.963 F1, and 40.14 dB PSNR. In matched ablations, dual-opacity compositing reduces CD from 59.25 to 27.09 mm, while DEL improves PSNR by 2.06 dB. Our project page is available at https://hajeongx.github.io/clearform/.

papers.title: Coexistence of LEO Satellite Communication Systems under Regulatory Protection Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the coexistence of two low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems sharing the same frequency band: a primary system with regulatory precedence over the spectrum and a secondary system that must not cause excessive interference to the primary system's ground users. This spectrum sharing paradigm was recently formalized by the United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC) through short-term and long-term protection criteria that limit primary-link unavailability and throughput degradation due to interference inflicted by the secondary system. To facilitate coexistence, we propose a satellite selection mechanism that associates the secondary system's satellites with clusters of ground cells at each handover to maximize secondary-user throughput while abiding by these regulatory constraints. Our mechanism enforces both constraints through a cumulative assessment that combines past primary-link performance with predicted performance over the upcoming handover interval. Simulation results show that our proposed method achieves up to 31% higher secondary-user throughput than prior work that imposes interference-to-noise ratio (INR) constraints, even when its constraints are tuned to satisfy the FCC's throughput-based protection criteria.

authors.name: Sunwoo Min
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Who Benefits, and When? Trajectories of Academic Achievement and Interest in AI-Supported Learning
papers.abstract: AI-supported learning environments are increasingly used, yet relatively little is known about how students' achievement and interest develop over time or whether these trajectories vary across learners. This study examined longitudinal trajectories of mathematics achievement and interest in a semester-long AI-supported mathematics learning. Using a mixed-methods longitudinal design, repeated measures of mathematics achievement were collected at four time points and mathematics interest at three time points. Linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to examine overall changes over time, while linear quantile mixed models (LQMMs) were used to examine differences in trajectories across the lower, median, and upper portions of the outcome distributions. Mathematics achievement increased substantially during the intervention, with the largest gains emerging between the second and third measurement occasions. However, the trajectory differed across the achievement distribution. Mathematics interest increased significantly after the first month, but this increase was not sustained through the end of the semester. Qualitative findings further indicated that students experienced the AI platform differently. The study highlights the importance of examining both cognitive and motivational trajectories.

papers.title: Disentangling Channel Semantics in Vision Transformers via Token Decorrelation and Composition-Aware Modulation
papers.abstract: Multi-channel images encode heterogeneous channel semantics aligned over a shared spatial structure, which requires models to jointly capture globally shared structure and channel-specific variations. Recent multi-channel Vision Transformers attempt to address this challenge by augmenting the [CLS] token with memory tokens to organize multi-channel representations under varying channel compositions. However, we find that these context tokens collapse onto a few dominant channels under high inter-channel redundancy, producing redundant representations and a biased global summary that fails to reliably support composition-aware channel interpretation. We propose MuCa-ViT (Multi-Channel Composition-Aware Vision Transformer), a unified framework that addresses these limitations through two coupled mechanisms. Factorial Token Learning (FTL) enforces token-level decorrelation among context tokens, encouraging the [CLS] token to capture globally shared semantics while memory tokens preserve complementary channel-specific cues. Channel Composition-Aware Modulation (CAM) uses the FTL-refined [CLS] as a semantic anchor to generate sample-wise modulation signals, which enable composition-aware interpretation of channels within a unified backbone rather than relying on static channel embeddings. Experiments on JUMP-CP, CHAMMI, and So2Sat show that MuCa-ViT outperforms prior multi-channel ViTs across all three benchmarks, and the magnitude of improvement aligns with the inter-channel redundancy of each dataset ($\rho \in [0.19, 0.77]$), validating the diagnostic analysis that motivates our design. Our code is available at https://github.com/kimdanni/MuCa-ViT .

papers.title: EmbodiedIntentBench: Benchmarking Intent-Driven Runtime Adaptation for Mobile Robotic Missions
papers.abstract: Mobile robotic sensing systems must adapt to operator requirements, limited resources, changing connectivity, and observation opportunities shaped by physical motion. Evaluating runtime strategies therefore requires assessing whether their decisions fulfill mission objectives, beyond isolated perception accuracy or execution efficiency. We present EmbodiedIntentBench, a benchmark for intent-driven runtime adaptation in mobile robotic missions. It represents mission intent through structured contracts for coverage, temporal evidence, reporting, urgency, and resources, and couples simulated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) workloads with causal, resource-accounted execution. Computation decisions affect mission time, resource use, and which observations can contribute evidence. We evaluate fixed and adaptive perception strategies in multi-phase missions and under changing urgency, connectivity, and battery conditions. In the multi-phase Depot study, a configuration with 87.5% full-bank target recall across visible target observations completes only 1 of 16 missions, whereas a lower-recall configuration completes 14. In an ablation, ignoring execution-induced observation loss increases aggregate mission success and reverses the ordering of two runtime strategies. Replays using Jetson AGX Orin CPU and GPU profiles change the relative success of local and remote strategies. In selected Jetson GPU-profile replays, intent-driven adaptation reduces modeled task energy by up to 28% with unchanged mission success. EmbodiedIntentBench provides an extensible framework for evaluating runtime decisions against mission fulfillment under physical and resource constraints.

papers.title: SRA: Spatial Reasoning Adapter via Evolving Social Interaction Graphs for Trajectory Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting where multiple agents will move next is fundamental to autonomous driving, robotics, and any system that must share space with people safely. Modern stochastic predictors read off inter-agent interactions once from the observed past and keep that view fixed throughout the generative rollout, so the reciprocal geometric constraints that emerge as the joint future sharpens are not re-examined. We address this gap with SRA (Spatial Reasoning Adapter), a modular graph denoiser that is integrated into existing diffusion and flow-matching predictors without redesigning their generative cores. At every reverse step, SRA reads the host's current future estimate, builds a sparse Euclidean interaction graph on the predicted trajectories, and returns a residual correction to the host's decoding path. Our adapter consists of three core components: a sparse neighborhood retrieved with a learned query-key score and a geometric bias, a future-conditioned relational feature recomputed on the evolving prediction, and uncertainty-weighted message passing where confident agents act as anchors for uncertain ones. We instantiate SRA on three structurally different hosts (LED, MID, and MoFlow) across four multi-agent benchmarks: SDD, NBA, Soccer, and Football. SRA improves ADE for every host on every dataset, with average gains of 5.8% in ADE and 7.0% in FDE. A cumulative ablation shows that the three components act as one mechanism: only together do they improve every host on every sports dataset, indicating that spatial reasoning over the model's own evolving future, weighted by how far that future can be trusted, is broadly useful across denoising architectures. Code is available at https://github.com/Jaewoo97/SRA.

papers.title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
papers.abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

authors.name: Kyungchun Lee
authors.institution: Seoul National University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global Context Guidance for Diffusion Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive LLMs, enabling parallel generation through iterative denoising. Recent guidance methods improve diffusion LLMs by introducing a weak model to guide the prediction of the base model during denoising. However, the influence of the weak model during denoising remains less clear, and computing its prediction requires an additional forward pass at each denoising step. We present in this paper an in-depth analysis of how diffusion LLMs use contextual information during denoising. Our analysis reveals that diffusion LLMs rely more heavily on local context while often underutilizing global context. Based on this observation, we introduce Global Context Guidance (GCG), a feature-space guidance method that enhances global-context utilization without constructing an explicit weak model. Extensive experiments on LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B, and LLaDA-1.5 across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that GCG consistently outperforms existing guidance methods, while incurring much lower inference overhead.

papers.title: SHIN: Scalable Hierarchy for INcremental 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides high-quality real-time novel-view synthesis, but deployment budgets vary across devices and network conditions. Most compact methods target one operating point, so another budget requires a separate representation. SHIN is a scalable 3DGS hierarchy with a reusable Base and additive enhancement layers, so each higher-quality operating point extends rather than replaces the decoded representation. Constructing this hierarchy requires deciding which Gaussians each stage adds and how much spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance each retains, because these choices remain fixed in later prefixes. SHIN derives one shared Gaussian order from multi-scale position-scale sensitivity and divides each stage budget between adding Gaussians and retaining SH bands using calibrated gradient-based scores per byte. Lightweight opacity updates adjust compositing while transmitted geometry and SH coefficients remain unchanged. Across three benchmarks, SHIN progressively improves one cumulative representation and achieves the best PSNR-size efficiency in every overlapping comparison with the multi-rate and progressive baselines.

papers.title: Formalizing Patient-Set Semantics for OMOP CDM-Based Clinical Trial Feasibility Assessment:A Neuro-Symbolic Methodology for Traceable Site-Feasibility Patient Counts
papers.abstract:
This study examines the interpretation and execution of natural-language eligibility criteria for clinical trial site-feasibility patient-count estimation using the OMOP Common Data Model (CDM). It treats each count as the size of a patient set produced under explicitly declared choices about clinical concepts, temporal conditions, exclusions, proxies, and available data.
  The study presents NS-CoT, a neuro-symbolic pipeline that uses an LLM to interpret and structure criteria, followed by symbolic processing and deterministic SQL compilation. Intermediate representations and execution records document how criteria are translated into patient sets and counts.
  Evaluation uses synthetic OMOP CDM data, controlled benchmarks, and a multi-site simulation. Comparisons with a direct-SQL baseline examine execution success, count agreement, patient-set agreement, and preservation of reference-defined site-feasibility labels and rankings. Performance varies across evaluation settings. Layer-wise inspection also supports the identification of implementation and policy errors, followed by correction and re-evaluation.
  The work investigates the reviewability and fidelity of cohort computation relative to declared reference definitions. It does not establish that these definitions capture a unique clinical ground truth or demonstrate improved recruitment, site selection, or trial outcomes in practice.

papers.title: AmodalBox: Automated 3D Bounding Box Annotation under Partial Visibility
papers.abstract: Recent progress in vision foundation models (VFMs) has made automated open-vocabulary 3D bounding box annotation increasingly feasible by jointly leveraging LiDAR point clouds and images. However, partial observations remain a major challenge in sparse driving scenes, where visible LiDAR points often cover only a small fraction of the object's surface and provide insufficient cues for estimating its full spatial extent. As a result, existing methods often produce mislocalized boxes or leave objects unlabeled. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{\Ours{}}, an automated annotation framework that leverages image-generated 3D assets as amodal geometric priors for partially observed objects. By establishing correspondences between input images and rendered views of 3D assets, \Ours{} robustly aligns canonical amodal geometry with partially observed world-space LiDAR point clouds. To improve temporal consistency and reduce computational cost, \Ours{} generates a single asset per instance, estimates its metric scale once at a single frame and propagates it across frames for dynamic instances, and aggregates multi-frame observations for static instances. 3D object detectors trained on annotations from \Ours{} improve performance over strong baselines by 14.1 mAP on the nuScenes dataset and by 12.45 AP at IoU 0.5 for the vehicle class on the Waymo Open Dataset (WOD). Our project page is available at: \href{https://oliver0922.github.io/AmodalBox/}{https://oliver0922.github.io/AmodalBox/}

authors.name: Kwonyoung Ryu
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MoE-DAgger: Transition-Aware Router-Entropy Gating for Selective Human Correction in Phase-Structured Manipulation
papers.abstract: Selective data acquisition in Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) on robots requires deciding which learner rollouts to correct and when to intervene. In manipulation with ordered phases, router entropy from a phase-supervised soft mixture-of-experts (MoE) is insufficient: the same value can reflect either a normal adjacent-phase handoff or support for nonadjacent or earlier phases. We propose MoE-DAgger, which uses causal router history to distinguish these cases without providing the policy with a phase label, progress variable, or hard phase command during execution. The acquisition rule allows an adjacent transition to settle, but requests correction when high entropy persists outside such a transition, the transition times out, or routing persistently favors an earlier phase. Under matched active human-control budgets, MoE-DAgger achieves 84.0% task success on Green and 78.0% on Red, exceeding phase-unaware filtered entropy by 22 percentage points on Green and 26 points on Red, with no observed collisions in 50 rollouts per task. On 50 shared intervention-free traces per task, 83.3% and 80.0% of its first proposals fall on failed rollouts within predefined failure windows when 15 and 25 traces are selected, compared with 70.0% and 72.0% for temporal action-chunk disagreement and 63.3% and 60.0% for ensemble disagreement. Shadow replay and an active no-veto ablation indicate that suppressing queries at normal adjacent handoffs is a key contributor to the improved allocation.

authors.name: Sungjun Heo
authors.institution: Korea University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Sungjun Yang
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Heedon Jeong
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Robust and Efficient Continual Model Merging via Global Singular Subspace Separation and Restoration
papers.abstract: Continual model merging incrementally integrates task-specific models without revisiting past models or data. However, repeated merging entangles past task components and distorts their singular geometry, making balanced task-wise allocation increasingly difficult. We propose Global Singular Subspace Separation and Restoration (GS3R), which augments the merged update with a compact restoration state. At each merge, GS3R restores the retained singular geometry, separates task-wise subspaces, and globally reallocates the available rank across tasks fairly. To reduce merging-time memory overhead, we further introduce Pre-merge Restoration and Flushing (PRF). Experiments on vision, NLP, and multimodal benchmarks show that GS3R provides a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

authors.name: Juncheol Shin
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Byeongho Yu
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Eunhyeok Park
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
papers.abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.

papers.title: Room to Reconsider: Reply Length Decides Whether Pushback Makes Language Models Sycophantic or Self-Correcting
papers.abstract: Language models often abandon a correct answer when a user pushes back without giving a reason, and this behavior is usually studied as sycophancy to be suppressed. The same pushback, however, also leads models to revisit and sometimes repair a wrong answer. We measure both effects on multiple-choice questions from MMLU and ARC-Challenge with four open models from two families (Qwen3 1.7B, 4B and 8B, and OLMo-2 7B), reading the final answer exactly from option logits after a free-form reply. The reply budget changes the verdict. When Qwen3-4B may answer the challenge in at most 96 tokens, pushback leaves accuracy unchanged or slightly lower; with 1,024 tokens, it corrects 43% of its wrong answers and pushback raises accuracy by 5.7 points. Whether pushback helps overall follows a simple break-even rule in the cave and correction rates. Inside the model, caving can be partly predicted before the challenge: hidden states add about 0.04-0.06 AUROC over turn-1 confidence in three of our four probing runs. A probe trained only on self-correction cases predicts caving beyond confidence when replies are truncated, but not when the model can finish its reasoning. Activation steering never reduced caving selectively: where it worked, it suppressed self-correction as well. We conclude that sycophancy evaluations should allow full replies and report self-correction alongside caving.

papers.title: The Race Is Decided Early! A Kernel Law Predicts Lock-In in Majority-Vote Test-Time RL
papers.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning with majority-vote rewards trains a language model on unlabeled questions by rewarding the samples that agree with its most frequent answer. During training, each question locks into one answer, on hard questions often a wrong one, but which answer it locks into is known only after training. In this paper, we show that this outcome is decided early, in a short race driven by sampling noise between the answers that are close at the start, and we derive the probability of each outcome. With a separate logit for each answer, the runner-up wins with a normal tail probability of the initial gap, scaled by an explicit noise constant. In a network, however, the answer logits depend on shared parameters, and through the kernel of these parameters the updates of the trailing answers also change the gap of the two leaders. This spillover shifts the boundary between the starts won by each leader, and a closed form computes the shifted probability from a kernel probe and the start logits. In LoRA experiments with three models from two families, predictions made before training with the kernel frozen at its start value forecast which answer each question locks into better than a logistic model refitted on the outcomes, although they use no fitted constants. The closed form matches these predictions on the runs in which a check before training finds that the two leaders stay above the other answers, and it explains why a law that ignores the spillover needs a strongly inflated step.

papers.title: Guidance at Pure Noise Erodes Speaker Similarity in Few-Step Token-Conditioned Flow-Matching TTS
papers.abstract: Text-to-speech systems built from a language model and a flow-matching mel decoder now run the decoder with two to four Euler steps instead of the official ten or more. At two steps the word error rate (WER) is unchanged, but speaker similarity (SIM) drops by one to six points. This paper shows that most of this loss comes from classifier-free guidance on the first step. At pure noise the network can only return the conditional mean, so guidance shifts every trajectory by nearly the same vector. Later steps do not remove this shift, and its size grows with the length of the first step, so it is negligible with ten or more steps and accounts for most of the loss with two. Two training-free samplers are derived from this analysis. First-step unguided sampling (FSU) leaves the first step unguided and recovers $84$--$91\%$ of the two-step SIM loss on CosyVoice~2/3 with no significant WER increase. FSU-Mid replaces the two Euler steps by one midpoint step with an unguided first evaluation, recovers $77$--$85\%$ on IndexTTS-2 and matches the ten-step teacher on CosyVoice~2 and GLM-TTS. Both use three network function evaluations, one fewer than the official two-step sampler, and FSU-Mid gives the highest mean recovery among eight published guidance rules re-run at two steps on four decoders.

authors.name: Han-Lim Choi
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: FRESCO: A Novel Consistency Control for Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training
papers.abstract: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism can accelerate distributed model training, but suffers from instability caused by inconsistent gradient computations. We identify a fundamental source of this inconsistency: error signals are coupled to forward-time features, not just parameter states. This means that parameters may evolve as long as they preserve forward-equivalence. Leveraging this insight, we introduce FRESCO, which frames asynchronous updates as a constrained optimization problem: it finds the minimal update modification that acts trivially on the activation subspace. We demonstrate that FRESCO consistently outperforms representative asynchronous baselines in LLM pre-training, with the gains most pronounced under deep pipelines and high inconsistency levels: at pipeline depth 32, it reaches the same loss as the strongest baseline with 43% fewer iterations and 30% less wall-clock time, while requiring 8~921$\times$ less memory overhead. Moving beyond the current limitations, FRESCO establishes a new foundation for high-utilization pipeline parallel training, providing a scalable path for large-model development on diverse, resource-constrained systems.

papers.title: Zero Replacement and Latent Profiles in Short Media Diaries: Checking Recording Status Before User Segmentation
papers.abstract: Short media diaries contain many zeros because many activities go unrecorded during the observation period. Log-ratio analysis of time allocation requires these zeros to be replaced with small positive values; as a result, all respondents who did not record an activity receive nearly the same value. We examined how such zero replacement affects classification in latent profile analysis and propose checks to perform before profiles are interpreted. Three-day diaries of 8,089 adults from the 2025 Korea Media Panel Survey were converted into nine-part time-use compositions. Gaming was not recorded by 88.9% of the respondents, and in every model with two to eight profiles and a covariance matrix held equal across profiles, respondents who recorded gaming and those who did not were classified into different profiles. Even when the replacement value equaled the minimum recording unit (5 min/day), the two-profile classification largely matched gaming recording status, and the two groups separated more sharply as the replacement value decreased, until the separation was complete. Before naming profiles, researchers should therefore check the proportion of respondents who did not record each activity and its replacement value, the same proportion within each profile, and the distribution of usage time among those who recorded the activity.

papers.title: CVaR Deep Optimal Stopping
papers.abstract: Risk-sensitive optimal stopping is useful when poor stopping outcomes carry substantial costs, as in option exercise, sequential medical treatment, and safety-critical control. A natural objective is Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the stopped reward. We develop a theoretical framework and algorithm for CVaR deep optimal stopping. The framework and algorithm address four difficulties in applying risk-sensitive reinforcement learning to optimal stopping: state augmentation, score-function pathology, blindness to success, and dependence on auxiliary networks. We isolate three structural properties of optimal stopping: single-point reward, action-independent dynamics, and sum-zero gradient. We exploit these properties to establish Markov optimality without state augmentation and derive a pathwise gradient estimator. Under bounded policy derivatives, the pathwise estimator has bounded second moments near deterministic policies, avoiding the divergence that can occur with score-function estimators. Building on this framework, we propose DIOS (Distribution-Informed Optimal Stopping) to address the remaining two difficulties. A per-time-step soft penalty combined with tail-level annealing mitigates blindness to success. Estimating the reward quantile directly from each batch removes the need for an auxiliary critic. For a fixed tail level, we establish a finite-time stationarity guarantee under regularity assumptions along the training iterates. Across the 24 main Bermudan max-call configurations, DIOS achieves the highest mean CVaR and the shortest recorded training time among the tested CVaR baselines.

papers.title: Directional asymmetry of atmospheric pole-to-pole teleconnection
papers.abstract: Paleoclimate proxies show that abrupt Greenland changes were followed by Antarctic responses within decades, suggesting a fast atmospheric pole-to-pole teleconnection involving shifts in the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and reorganization of extratropical jets. Here, we examine how the mean ITCZ position modulates this interhemispheric teleconnection. Using an aquaplanet slab-ocean model, we apply northern high-latitude forcing in climatologies with different mean ITCZ positions. The southern high-latitude response is about twice as large when the mean ITCZ is in the Southern Hemisphere. The teleconnection is therefore directionally asymmetric. The asymmetry arises in the subtropical jet response per degree of ITCZ shift, because, even with a comparable Hadley cell response, the angular momentum carried into the upper branch depends on the distance of the ITCZ from the equator, so that an ITCZ shift toward or away from the equator reinforces or offsets the jet response. Our results suggest that the southward-displaced glacial ITCZ made Arctic-to-Antarctic transmission more efficient than today, whereas the present-day ITCZ favors the reverse.

papers.title: A Distributed Observer with Random Agent Activations over Random Communication Networks
papers.abstract: This paper develops a distributed observer for the forward-Euler discretization of a continuous-time linear time-invariant system under random local operations and random communications. Under uniform stochastic strong connectivity, we establish almost sure exponential convergence of all local state estimates for sufficiently small discretization step sizes. We further examine how the underlying parameters and components affect the admissible range of the discretization step size and the guaranteed convergence rate bound. Unlike related approaches, the proposed method does not require each local unobservable subspace to admit an $A$-invariant complement.

papers.title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.

authors.name: Xu Gan
authors.institution: Zhejiang University of Water Resource and Electric Power

papers.title: Planners Exploit Deterministic Error: Dithered Low-Bit World Models
papers.abstract: Sampling-based planners such as MPPI and CEM query a learned world model thousands of times per control step, so low-bit world models are an obvious way to make model-based control cheaper on a robot. With round-to-nearest activation quantization and no calibration, we find that planning can collapse, by up to 100 points of success, while the world model's latent one-step prediction error stays no larger than that of a stochastic rounding scheme that plans well. At the same bit width, what decides the outcome is not the size of the rounding error but whether it persists across planner iterations and is shared across candidates. Round-to-nearest leaves an error that persists, and an iterating planner drifts toward the candidates that this error favors; in TD-MPC2, holding the same dither fixed within a step or an episode brings the drift back. Dither shared by all candidates and redrawn at every iteration removes most of the damage at the same bit width and without training: at least half of it in all 19 affected Meta-World cells (task $\times$ bit width) of TD-MPC2 (median 95%), in 4 of 5 DINO-WM cells, and in all 8 affected tasks of a 317M-parameter multi-task TD-MPC2. Captured as CUDA graphs on an Ampere GPU, a W8A4 integer TD-MPC2 world model runs its planning rollouts 1.9-3.3$\times$ and the whole planning step 1.3-1.5$\times$ faster than FP32, though not faster than BF16 with pre-converted weights; shared dither adds at most 2.3% latency. In TD-MPC2, block-scaled NVFP4 removes most of the damage and MXFP4 part of it, which ties the failure to coarse grids with a shared scale. Hypotheses, thresholds and analysis code were fixed before the data that test them, and the hypotheses that failed are reported.

papers.title: How Many Candidates Does a One-Step World Model Need? A Random-Codebook Account of Nearest-of-m Training on Frozen DINO Tokens
papers.abstract: One-step stochastic world models avoid the mode averaging of deterministic feature predictors without the tens of network evaluations per step that diffusion and flow matching require. The simplest such objective is nearest-of-m matching (conditional implicit maximum likelihood estimation, IMLE): draw m candidate futures and pull only the one closest to the observed outcome. Recent work conjectures that a small m suffices for feature-space world models and that a strictly proper energy score should replace the hard minimum. We test both claims with one-step world models on frozen DINOv2/v3 patch tokens, using benchmarks whose futures can be enumerated. Under mode-like uncertainty, nearest-of-m with m=16 covers the enumerated futures better than 50-step flow matching (at about 1/30 of its latency), one-step flow generators and an energy-score generator at matched parameter counts, and its rollouts stay on the token manifold where flow rollouts drift. One quantity governs the choice of m: the nearest-of-m objective is the expected distortion of a random codebook of m draws from the generator. This view yields three predictions, recorded before the corresponding runs: (i) memorization of the realized outcome in contexts that never repeat, whose strength is governed by the codebook's miss distortion I(m) rather than its miss probability, and which an energy-score generator does not escape by raising m; (ii) a flattening of mode probabilities with m, matching a known optimum within 0.01; and (iii) under-dispersion on continuous high-dimensional outcomes, which bounds the method on real robot video. Per-step matching on self-rollouts cuts long-horizon error by a third on a stochastic Push-T variant; an ablation separates its manifold and coverage benefits. Planning success does not improve despite accurate risk estimates, a negative result we report with its diagnosis.

papers.title: When Audio and Video Mislead: Evaluating Multimodal AI for Conversational Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation (MERC) combines lexical, acoustic, visual and conversational cues, but accepting audio and video does not establish their effective or robust use. We audit off-the-shelf Omni models while holding the target transcript and prior textual context fixed and adding, removing or replacing target audio and video. In the primary evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Baichuan-Omni-1.5 and MiniCPM-o 2.6 on MELD and the full five-session six-class IEMOCAP set, T+A improves Accuracy in all six model-dataset pairs, with four gains significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Across three source mappings, unrelated A/V (RandA/V) lowers Accuracy relative to Full in all 18 comparisons; all 18 remain significant under dialogue-cluster inference and BH-FDR correction, both on common-valid pairs and when invalid/OOM outcomes are treated as incorrect. Comparisons with modality-omission baselines further distinguish replacement penalties from mismatch-specific harm. A Qwen/MELD case study finds significantly greater gold-vs-best-candidate margin recovery in Late than Early or Middle under decision-query audio knockout, relative to an edge-count-matched Video-Sham control, using Holm-corrected tests. These results distinguish genuine-modality benefit from sensitivity and vulnerability to misleading input.

papers.title: TIRAD: Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Recent anomaly detection studies have shown that residual features, which model the discrepancy between normal and abnormal patterns, provide strong generalization to anomalies unseen during training. However, existing residual-based approaches mainly rely on visual discrepancies derived from image representations, while semantic discrepancies that can be explicitly expressed through language remain largely underexplored. To address this problem, we propose TIRAD, Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection, a multimodal residual learning framework that defines the discrepancy between textual representations of normal and abnormal states as a Text Residual Feature and uses it to guide the Image Residual Feature. Specifically, a Text Fusion Module converts patch-level text residuals into a gate that modulates the image residual of each patch. The gate retains the visual discrepancies that the text residual identifies as defect-related and attenuates the others, leading to more discriminative anomaly representations. Extensive experiments on industrial benchmarks and industrial-to-medical transfer demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing image-centric residual learning methods.

authors.name: Seongsu Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
papers.abstract: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.

authors.name: Enyan Koh
authors.institution: Singapore University of Technology and Design

papers.title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration
papers.abstract: Camera-LiDAR calibration is essential for reliable perception in robotic and autonomous systems. Most target-based calibration methods rely on checkerboard observations, but accurate checkerboard feature extraction from LiDAR point clouds remains challenging due to measurement sparsity. Existing approaches either require manual annotation of 3D corners or depend on geometric feature extraction methods, both of which can become unreliable when checkerboard features are insufficiently observed. In this paper, we formulate checkerboard localization as a 2D detection problem using cylindrical LiDAR reflectivity images. To overcome the limited availability of labeled training data, we propose ray-aware physics augmentation (RAPA), which generates diverse synthetic samples from a single checkerboard observation. The generated data are used to improve detector robustness and generalization under varying sensing conditions. Across four independently captured indoor and outdoor locations, the proposed synthetic augmentation exceeds the strongest evaluated image-space augmentation baseline by 16.1-43.1 percentage points in mAP@0.5. Compared with training-free target-based methods on 242 observations, RAPA yields the largest number of valid target localizations, with 96.4% of its returned detections yielding valid target poses. These reliable localizations support downstream camera-LiDAR calibration across all four evaluated locations. Overall, RAPA addresses a key bottleneck in target-based calibration by enabling automated LiDAR-side target localization with only a single annotated target observation.

papers.title: Computational Structure of Pairwise Housing Connectedness Networks
papers.abstract: Directed housing-submarket networks combine common market movement with heterogeneous bilateral relations, and different node-level measures need not yield distinct empirical rankings. We construct a positive pairwise net-connectedness network from the generalized forecast error variance decomposition (GFEVD) of a vector autoregression (VAR) and use it to compare complementary node positions. Net directional connectedness (NET), PageRank, and Viral Centrality summarize net directional balance, recursively weighted incoming position, and normalized multistep reach. When bilateral net differences are nonzero, the network is a weighted tournament. A least-squares edge-flow decomposition separates the pairwise-net matrix into a NET-equivalent gradient component and a NET-orthogonal residual, while a monotone-allocation condition establishes exact PageRank-indegree correspondence in a transitive tournament. In Seoul's 25-district network, the gradient component accounts for 70.9% of the squared Frobenius norm, leaving 29.1% in the residual component. PageRank is strongly aligned with indegree (Spearman $\rho=0.987$), and Viral Centrality with outdegree ($\rho=0.935$); the PageRank alignment exceeds the range of independently weighted simulations with comparable tournament consistency and edge-weight variation. Three common-component treatments reduce total connectedness from 81.98% to 50.60-52.00%, a 36.6-38.3% reduction relative to the raw system, and reverse 97-98 of 300 pairwise net directions. Thus, both the magnitude and the apparent direction of connectedness depend materially on the treatment of citywide common movement. Songpa's positive NET position remains prominent across common-component treatments and dynamic specifications and ranks first in both chronological subsamples.

papers.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
papers.abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Occupancy Modelling of Biased Landslide Inventories: When Does Separating Occurrence from Recording Improve on Neutralisation?
papers.abstract: Landslide susceptibility models are trained on inventories that record where landslides were seen, not where they occurred. The established remedy fits bias-describing variables and neutralises them when mapping. We adapt occupancy-detection modelling from ecology, treating several inventories as imperfect observers of one event and separating occurrence from recording, and ask when this improves on neutralisation. We use near-complete inventories of the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi, 2015 Gorkha and 2010 Haiti earthquakes with simulated reporting bias, and three real Gorkha inventories. Compared with standard practice, the occupancy model reduces road bias in 24 of 25 paired draws and raises AUC by 0.08-0.14 on Gorkha and 0.03 on Haiti, but only 0.01-0.02 on Iburi. Its median predicted-to-true landslide rate is 0.99 (range 0.44-1.89), against 0.24-0.30 for the baselines. Rescaling the baselines with the same anchor area corrects their median but leaves larger errors (range 0.20-4.34). Cell-level probabilities remain too extreme (calibration slope 0.59). Compared with the best neutralised model, AUC is higher on Iburi (by 0.03-0.07) and lower on Gorkha and Haiti (by 0.01-0.05). Transplant experiments tie the Iburi advantage to the structure of its true landslide pattern, not to its terrain or road network. In all eight settings with a low interaction gap, computable from biased records, neutralisation was at least as accurate, including a prespecified test on Haiti; a high gap did not guarantee an advantage. The real Gorkha inventories are slope-biased, not road-biased, and there the model brings no meaningful gain. Report-based catalogues remain the main untested case.

papers.title: Perturb, Aggregate then Reconstruct: Consensus Aggregation and Fourier-Attended Multi-Decoders for Reconstruction-based Multi-View Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Multi-view anomaly detection is crucial for industrial inspection to identify defects hidden from single viewpoints. Yet, despite their strong success in single-view applications, reconstruction-based methods remain largely underexplored in multi-view settings. A key challenge in extending these methods lies in generating view-consistent pseudo-anomalies. To address this, we propose PAR, a reconstruction-based framework for enhanced multi-view anomaly detection. First, we introduce a feature perturbation strategy coupled with a consensus aggregation module that integrates these perturbed features across viewpoints to mitigate view-inconsistent anomalies and construct highly aligned pseudo-anomaly representations. Second, we employ a view-specialized multi-decoder architecture; by assigning a dedicated decoder to each view, we increase the model's representational complexity, enabling the generation of highly feasible, localized anomaly maps rather than less precise, view-agnostic reconstructions. Last, we incorporate Fourier attention into the decoders to emphasize global frequency-domain structures over local token evidence, effectively preventing identity mapping. Extensive experiments on the Real-IAD dataset demonstrate that PAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in sample-level, image-level, and pixel-level anomaly detection. Our code is available at https://github.com/SpatialAILab/PAR_mvad.

papers.title: RankShift: Evaluating Ranking Instability Across Benchmark Dimensions in Document Parsing
papers.abstract: Document parsing benchmarks are often treated as stable measures of model quality, yet rankings may depend substantially on benchmark design choices. In this work, we present RankShift, a systematic study comparing OCR and vision-language models (VLMs) under controlled variation in dataset composition, matching strategy, and scoring methodology. Using OmniDocBench as a case study, we evaluate the ranking stability of 16 models across 3 dataset configurations, 6 matching strategies, and 3 scoring metrics. We quantify rank stability using pairwise rank correlation, top-k churn, and pairwise reversal rate. Our results show that the interaction between matching strategy and ground truth format is a substantial but understudied driver of instability: scoring against OmniDocBench's JSON annotations versus its Markdown rendering yields a mean Kendall's tau of approximately 0.33 under region-level matching strategies, with individual pairs as low as tau = 0.23, compared with tau = 0.77 when each page is scored as a single concatenated string. Dataset composition produces comparable instability across page-type strata (mean tau = 0.48) and layout-type strata (mean tau = 0.49), while the cross-dataset shift from OmniDocBench to Real5's Scanning reconstruction of the same pages is more stable (tau = 0.80). Metric choice is the most stable dimension, with mean tau of approximately 0.78 across NED, BLEU, and METEOR. These findings indicate that leaderboard position is not solely a property of model capability, motivating leaderboards that report not only headline scores but also the robustness of rankings across reasonable design choices.

papers.title: TimeTraveler: Temporal Strategy Planning with Time Dictionary for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Streaming video understanding (SVU) requires models to answer user queries over continuously evolving video streams. Unlike offline video QA, SVU must handle queries whose evidence may lie in the past, appear in the current scene, or emerge only after future observations. Existing streaming video systems often rely on compact visual memories or fixed evidence-access schemes, which can lose fine-grained details and fail to adapt the answering process to the temporal intent of each query. In this paper, we propose TimeTraveler, a streaming VQA framework that performs temporal strategy planning with a Time Dictionary. Inspired by the need to search across different temporal regions of a stream, TimeTraveler stores each observed moment as a timestamp-indexed structured caption and uses this dictionary as an explicit source of queryable evidence. Given a query, TimeTraveler determines whether to recall past evidence, read the present context, or wait for future observations, and then applies a strategy-specific evidence acquisition process. Comparative experiments on streaming video QA benchmarks show that TimeTraveler improves streaming question answering by preserving fine-grained temporal evidence and selecting the appropriate temporal strategy for each query. The project page is available at https://geppa.github.io/TimeTraveler.

authors.name: Junho Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
papers.abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral $v$-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen

papers.title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{\lambda,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+\lambda(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $\lambda\in\F_q^*$, $-\lambda\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.

papers.title: End-to-End Joint Training of Super-Resolution and Compression Artifact Removal for Industrial Machine Vision
papers.abstract: In industrial machine vision, images captured by edge devices are often downsampled and compressed to reduce bandwidth, introducing resolution loss and compression artifacts that severely degrade the performance of downstream tasks, such as defect detection. Existing quality enhancement methods typically apply super-resolution (SR) or compression artifact removal (CAR) independently or in a sequential manner and are largely optimized for human visual fidelity rather than machine perception. This paper proposes an end-to-end quality enhancement framework that integrates SR and CAR with a unified training strategy that optimizes both human-perception and machine-perception objectives. We investigate fixed-weight and uncertainty-based dynamic-weight loss functions to balance reconstruction quality and machine vision task performance. Extensive experiments on PCB Defect, DeepPCB, and NEU-DET datasets show that the proposed jointly trained model generally outperforms standalone and separately trained SR-CAR pipelines. In particular, under severe JPEG compression, our method improves defect detection performance from 0.461 to 0.887 mAP@50 on PCB Defect over sequential SR-CAR baselines, with only a slight reduction in PSNR. These results demonstrate that joint optimization is critical for compression-aware industrial machine vision systems.

papers.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
papers.abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

papers.title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets
papers.abstract: Constrained preference-conditioned MORL typically assumes full task observability, treating preferences and safety budgets as stationary task signals. In real-world deployment, however, these signals are often unreliable proxies: intent may drift, safety tolerances may shift with context, and exposed descriptors may be noisy, delayed, or incomplete. We therefore formulate constrained preference-conditioned MORL as a partially observed task-specification problem, where the agent must navigate a fundamental conflict between unreliable external signals and latent interaction dynamics. We propose \textbf{BECON}, a belief-conditioned framework for constrained MORL with drifting preferences and budgets, which infers latent task context from recent histories to estimate preferences and safety budgets. These estimates are fused with the exposed task signal via uncertainty-dependent gates, enabling the policy to defer to observations under high epistemic uncertainty while correcting them when history is informative. The fused context jointly conditions preference optimization and context-adaptive constraint enforcement. Experiments on diverse multi-objective control tasks demonstrate that BECON consistently improves over state-of-the-art MORL baselines, achieving stronger robustness and constraint satisfaction under task drift.

papers.title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
papers.abstract: Large language models offer a promising technique for translating natural-language optimization problems into solver code, but their reliability remains constrained by the quality of template retrieval. While recent structured methods improve over flat prompting through hierarchical taxonomy search, their traversal rules remain fixed or LLM-driven at inference time, leaving retrieval unable to improve from past successes and failures. This motivates treating template retrieval as a policy that can be learned from modeling experience, rather than as a static inference-time rule. We propose COMPASS, a policy-amortized framework for retrieving optimization templates in LLM-based solver modeling, which represents the template library as a directed acyclic graph and formulates retrieval as a sequential decision process over template nodes. A deep Q-network learns a reusable traversal policy from template-level judgments and execution feedback, reducing reliance on fixed heuristic traversal through feedback-driven graph navigation. To support extensible retrieval, COMPASS embeds problem descriptions and template nodes in a shared semantic space, allowing newly inserted templates to be scored from their text descriptions without redefining the action space. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and optimization-modeling benchmarks demonstrate that COMPASS consistently improves over heuristic structured retrieval, with the largest gains on complex and mixed-category problems.
