papers.title: Text Grouping Changes Completion-Time Comparisons in Long-Form Simultaneous Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Does grouping translation updates before speech synthesis change the measured completion gap between two translators? We compare StreamAtt with its fixed-audio-history baseline on ten English-German talks. For each translation, we keep the intended text and its availability times fixed and vary how updates are grouped for synthesis. Four-second grouping increases StreamAtt's mean completion lead from 106.6 to 229.1 seconds with XTTS-v2, but reduces it from 169.5 to 146.5 seconds with Piper. Both produce shorter audio; different changes in playback idle account for the opposite effects. These directions recur on a separately selected twenty-talk panel. In continuing CosyVoice 3 sessions, grouping instead leaves paired audio unchanged and delays completion on nineteen of twenty blocks. A speech-timing comparison therefore needs to specify how text enters synthesis, not just which synthesizer is used. Recognition and automatic word timing describe the outputs, but do not establish translation accuracy or intelligibility.

papers.title: Multi-objective drift-aware MLOps agent for model retraining
papers.abstract: Deployed ML models face non-stationary data and delayed labels, yet most retraining strategies rely on fixed schedules or brittle drift thresholds that ignore operational cost. In this setting, retraining is a sequential decision problem rather than a one-time threshold choice. We present DARE (Drift-Aware Retraining Engine), an offline, event-driven retraining framework that separates ingestion, monitoring, policy decisions, training, and logging through explicit schemas and deterministic replay. We compare DARE against practical heuristic retraining baselines, including fixed-interval, threshold-persistence, and action-rate-matched fixed scheduling policies. On Airline, the locked LinUCB policy achieves a higher mean F1 while substantially reducing intervention frequency relative to heuristic and action-rate-matched baselines. Additional runtime-calibrated evaluation shows that these gains persist when measured using the cumulative update wall-clock time. These results suggest that conservative sequential retraining policies can improve performance while reducing unnecessary operational overhead under delayed feedback.

papers.title: Burden, Bounty, or Bliss? Muscle-Aware Retargeting and Null-Space Exploration for Whole-Body Musculoskeletal Control
papers.abstract: Learning whole-body musculoskeletal control from human motion is important for developing human-like robots, assistive devices, and rehabilitation systems. This task presents two main challenges, namely reference trajectories that are kinematically plausible but difficult to reproduce through muscle-driven dynamics, and a highly redundant 700-dimensional action space in which unstructured exploration can easily disrupt the target motion. In this paper, we propose a motion-to-policy pipeline that exploits muscle redundancy in two complementary stages. First, muscle-aware retargeting (MAR) performs bounded adaptation of kinematic trajectories subject to hard semantic, anatomical, and contact constraints. We motivate the constraint bounds by analyzing how reference-trajectory artifacts affect muscle-driven tracking. Second, null-space exploration (NSE) estimates a one-control-frame mapping from muscle excitations to generalized forces and injects bounded, anatomically structured perturbations along its null space into the actions of a value-guided flow policy. On a 24-clip motion-capture benchmark, MAR and NSE together solve every reference, reach the full horizon with half the samples of the baseline pipeline, and lower joint-center error by 44% without late collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end pipeline that transforms monocular video into a trained whole-body imitation policy controlling 700 muscles.

papers.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models have emerged as promising paradigms for decoding brain activity through large-scale self-supervised pretraining. Notably, most existing approaches employ masked patch reconstruction, in which randomly selected EEG patches are masked and recovered by the network. However, purely random masking may limit representation learning as informative patches from highly correlated channels often remain unmasked, causing the network to underutilize weakly correlated channels or serial dependencies. Furthermore, because these models are typically based on transformer architectures, their performance is influenced by the choice of positional encoding. Although positional encoding has been extensively explored in natural language processing and computer vision, few studies have adapted it to the unique characteristics of EEG signals. To address these limitations, this study introduces a conditional positional encoding method based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to explicitly model inter-channel correlations, along with an adaptive masking strategy that enhances representation learning by modulating the difficulty of masked patch reconstruction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to integrate graph-based representations into conditional positional encoding and introduce adaptive masking within EEG foundation model pretraining. Experimental results on ten benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCN-based positional encoding and adaptive masking strategies, both individually and in combination, achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance, highlighting their effectiveness in EEG foundation modeling.

papers.title: The Dusty Circumstellar Structure of the Yellow Hypergiant IRC +10420: Constraints from the SED and Near-Infrared Imaging Polarimetry
papers.abstract: The yellow hypergiant IRC +10420 is a post-red supergiant evolving toward higher temperatures. We model its circumstellar dust with the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D, including polarized scattering, constrained by the spectral energy distribution (SED) from 0.4 $\mu$m to 1.3 mm and by the K' (2.2 $\mu$m) imaging polarimetry of Shenoy et al. (2015), assuming a pole-on view. The model consists of an equatorial structure (a flared inner disk of 0.3 $\mu$m grains at 300-3000 au, a ring at 3000-16,000 au whose surface density peaks at $\approx 10^4$ au, and a thin mid-plane disk of 300 $\mu$m grains) embedded in a spherical envelope of 0.15 $\mu$m grains with $\rho \propto r^{-2.3}$. It reproduces the SED within 0.07 dex and the total- and polarized-intensity profiles; the fractional polarization peaks at 15% at 1.7 arcsec (observed: 14%). The rising surface density of the ring produces the polarized-intensity plateau, and 0.5 $\mu$m grains at its outer edge the decline beyond 2 arcsec; grains of $\gtrsim 0.7$ $\mu$m are excluded. A thin disk of large grains suggests a settled mid-plane. Stellar temperatures of 7000-8500 K fit equally well. Of the total extinction ($A_V \approx 6.9$ mag), 5 mag is interstellar. Most of the $7.4 \times 10^{-2}$ $M_\odot$ of dust is equatorial; the envelope implies a mass-loss rate of $\approx 10^{-5}$-$10^{-4}$ ($\psi$/100) $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$. Because equatorial dust redirects starlight poleward, the pole-on SED overestimates the luminosity by $\approx 1.5$; at the Gaia distance, $L_\star \approx 3.3 \times 10^5$ $L_\odot$. Subtracting a scaled stellar PSF removes most of the nebular light within $\approx 1$ arcsec.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: A Bussgang-based Latent Lifting Method: Discrete RIS Channel Estimation and Beamforming
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of discrete phase-shift optimization in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multiuser communication systems. Practical RIS hardware often utilizes low-resolution phase shifters, leading to challenging combinatorial optimization problems. To address this challenge, we propose a Bussgang-based latent lifting (BuLL) method that represents discrete phase shifts as quantized outputs of continuous latent variables. Our BuLL method calibrates the Bussgang gain and distortion covariance under a reference distribution and keeps these moments fixed during deterministic latent optimization. These fixed moments are then used to construct a distortion-aware continuous surrogate that incorporates reference-averaged discretization effects without penalty terms. For uplink channel estimation, we develop a matrix quadratic transform-based algorithm to optimize a mean-square-error surrogate. For downlink beamforming, we develop a generalized power iteration-based RIS phase-shift optimization algorithm for a spectral efficiency (SE) surrogate. Numerical results demonstrate improvements in channel estimation accuracy and sum SE over conventional benchmarks in the evaluated low-resolution RIS settings.

papers.title: HiddenPathQA: A Benchmark for Knowledge Graph Question Answering When Questions Hide Their Paths
papers.abstract:
Knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) systems are typically evaluated on questions whose surface tokens lexically expose the gold KG path. Users, however, may ask questions without knowing the underlying schema: "Which condition could Andrew have due to family history?" compresses a 4-hop chain "Andrew --[father]--> parent --[father]--> grandparent --[medical condition]--> disease --[subclass of]--> hereditary disorder" into a single phrase (family history) that names none of those relations. We identify this collapse of path-question alignment as a blind spot in existing KGQA evaluation. Three major LLM-KG paradigms, hop-by-hop exploration, plan-then-retrieve, and similarity-based retrieval, implicitly rely on such lexical cues, an assumption rarely tested in practice.
  We make three contributions. (i) We introduce HiddenPathQA, a manually verified benchmark of 1,055 questions spanning 2-6 hops and multiple domains, constructed so that question wording does not reveal the gold path's relations. (ii) We propose Holistic Path Selection, which compares questions against candidate relation chains in the local subgraph as complete units, replacing irreversible per-hop relation scoring with globally informed chain-level reasoning. We develop two implementations, TieredHolistic and FlatHolistic. (iii) We conduct a pseudoword stress test that replaces entity names with meaningless placeholders to distinguish KG-grounded reasoning from entity-level memorization. Holistic Path Selection outperforms six strong KGQA baselines (ToG, PoG, FiDeLiS, R2-KG, KAPING, and KARPA) by 8.8-17.9 accuracy points across two LLM backbones and both original and pseudoword settings. Its advantage under pseudoword replacement shows that the gains cannot be explained by entity-level memorization alone.

papers.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication
papers.abstract: Remote face authentication requires protection against both presentation attacks and biometric data injection attacks prior to face matching. Methods based on active screen illumination appear promising for both by introducing randomized visual stimuli through the user's device screen and evaluating the corresponding facial responses. Although such methods have been more studied for presentation attack detection (PAD), their systematic evaluation for injection attack detection (IAD) remains limited. To address this gap, we first classify injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes based on their expected responses to the challenge. We then adapt an active screen-illumination approach into an implementation we term color wave and develop a systematic, injection-specific evaluation protocol. The protocol examines detection effectiveness, generalization across operating conditions, robustness to signal degradation, and susceptibility to selected evasion strategies. The findings demonstrate a strong discriminative signal under controlled conditions but also reveal performance limitations under overexposure, low screen brightness, and subject motion, as well as vulnerabilities to selected evasion strategies. By relating detection outcomes to attack types and operating conditions, this study provides an interpretable assessment of when and why active screen illumination succeeds or fails as an IAD mechanism.

authors.name: Vyacheslav Shen

papers.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic, real-time rendering on commodity GPUs and is increasingly adopted in generative world models and autonomous driving simulators. However, existing optimizations rely on algorithmic changes that often require retraining, or on specialized accelerators that lack flexibility across evolving 3DGS variants. In this paper, we identify a fundamental inefficiency in GPU-based 3DGS rendering: severe SM-level load imbalance caused by uneven workloads across screen tiles. This imbalance creates a long execution tail, leaving most SMs idle while a few process computationally intensive tiles, particularly in large-scale urban scenes. To address this, we present a software-defined GPU scheduling approach that mitigates the execution tail. Our approach uses a persistent kernel to schedule heavy tiles first and selectively chunks outlier tiles across multiple CTAs. A lightweight per-frame policy determines when and how much to chunk using tile statistics already available in the rendering pipeline. Our approach requires neither retraining nor specialized hardware and can be applied orthogonally to existing optimizations across diverse 3DGS variants. Averaged per scene, it accelerates alpha blending by up to 2.93x on a large-scale urban scene, and by up to 5.6x on its most imbalanced frames, while retaining the original alpha blending formulation.

papers.title: Repeating Work Can Lower Energy per Successful Goal in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: When a temporary call failure interrupts a tool-using LLM agent, the framework must choose how much completed work to repeat. Repeating less completed work intuitively saves computation, but recovery mechanisms also change subsequent execution and the chance of success. We compare recovery mechanisms by energy per successful goal (EpG), which divides the energy of all task runs (including failed runs) by the number that finish correctly. In controlled vLLM experiments on one node, we measure board energy above idle for eight recovery options on reliably solved multi-turn tasks, with selected comparisons across three model families. For the model tested across all eight options, with the prefix cache retained, starting over has 22 percent lower EpG than continuing after early failures. Under the same cache condition, continuing has 24 percent lower EpG than starting over after late failures. Among all eight recovery options, repeating only the interrupted turn has the lowest observed EpG after early and late tool failures on this model. Holding recovery fixed, retaining the prefix cache reduces prompt tokens needing fresh computation by 86 percent but reduces recovery energy by only 8 percent at contexts up to 7,333 tokens. These measurements and a condition relating recovery energy and success show when repeating work lowers EpG, helping framework developers choose how their agents recover on their intended models and tasks.

papers.title: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can write the weights of small neural networks directly, without gradient descent. This weight-space programming creates policies for sequential decision-making from a task description alone, but nothing guarantees that a written policy behaves as intended. We combine weight-space programming with probabilistic model checking. Given an environment modeled as a Markov decision process and a requirement in probabilistic computation tree logic (PCTL), an LLM writes all weights of a policy network, optionally repairs them on a dataset of optimal actions, and receives model-checking feedback until the requirement holds or a round limit is reached. The model checker Storm computes, rather than estimates from simulations, the probability that the policy satisfies the requirement, so every returned policy is verified. With two LLMs on three environments, the created policy of each of the 18 runs attains the optimal probability, before any dataset or model-checking feedback. Four of six policies programmed for two transporter jobs also complete three jobs with probability 1, so they generalize to a task that the LLM never saw. The pipeline also programs a policy that satisfies a complex safety requirement expressed with the PCTL until operator in all six runs. In one of them, dataset repair raised the accuracy to 98.4\% but broke the requirement, and one round of model-checking feedback restored it.

papers.title: Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments
papers.abstract: We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.

papers.title: The Delta Gap: Cellular World Models for Perturbation Response Prediction Are Far Harder Than Global Correlation Implies
papers.abstract: Cellular world models aim to predict how cells respond to genetic perturbations, analogous to world models in reinforcement learning. Perturbation response models are evaluated almost exclusively by global Pearson correlation between predicted and observed transcriptomes. We show this metric is dominated by thousands of non-responsive genes and severely inflates apparent performance. On the Replogle K562 screen (509 unseen perturbations, 5000 genes), GEARS achieves global Pearson 0.977, but its delta Pearson is only 0.076. A trivial baseline predicting mean training delta achieves 0.267, which is 3.5x better than GEARS. Our primary contribution is methodological: we identify and quantify this delta gap as a systematic evaluation artifact, and propose delta-space evaluation as the primary benchmark. We provide two post-hoc corrections (RWR on co-expression graphs and kNN matching) and show that 2.8x of the remaining gap lies in perturbation representation geometry, not decoder capacity. We further show the gap is partially addressable end-to-end: delta-aligned training (lambda = 3.0) raises delta Pearson to 0.179 on Replogle (2.35x over GEARS) and surpasses the trivial baseline on direction accuracy (0.680 vs 0.567) and gene recovery (1.52 vs 1.19); combined with kNN it reaches 0.217. An amplitude-calibration variant (eta = 0.3) further raises gene recovery to 2.16 while reaching 0.218. Critically, these representations transfer zero-shot across cell lines: from Replogle K562 to unseen Norman A549, the delta-aligned model reaches 0.328 on 741 shared genes, 4.7x a trivial baseline and 2.1x standard GEARS. This is the first systematic quantification of the delta gap, and the first diagnostic framework localizing the residual gap to perturbation representation geometry via an oracle upper bound.

papers.title: MOMENT-DP: Momentum Aware Evaluation of Correlated Noise for Differentially Private Training
papers.abstract:
Temporally correlated noise can substantially improve the utility of differentially private optimization, yet candidate mechanisms are commonly designed or evaluated using only partial information about the optimization process, such as workload structure, learning-rate schedules, or local curvature. We study whether persistent optimizer state provides additional information that can change the relative utility of privacy-valid correlated-noise mechanisms.
  We introduce MOMENT-DP, an optimizer-state-aware framework that models how temporally correlated privacy noise propagates through momentum-based optimization. For locally quadratic objectives, MOMENT-DP expresses privacy-induced final loss through an optimizer transfer operator that jointly captures curvature, learning-rate scheduling, momentum, and temporal noise covariance. NoiseCurve's curvature-aware quadratic criterion is recovered exactly as the zero-momentum, constant-learning-rate special case.
  Changing only momentum while holding curvature, schedule, privacy calibration, and candidate mechanisms fixed induces genuine mechanism-ranking reversals. The effect persists outside exact quadratic dynamics in per-example-clipped private logistic regression, while remaining unresolved in the neural regime we study. These results establish optimizer state as an under-modeled, decision-relevant axis in evaluating temporally correlated privacy noise.

papers.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
papers.abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.

authors.name: John R. Klein
authors.institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

papers.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
papers.abstract: One hundred known errors were planted into 10 open-access psychology papers, and the modified papers were then run through frontier models and two commercial AI review tools. The best single system caught 71 of the 100 errors, while the worst caught 30. Pooling every system's output caught 93. Models are only partly correlated in the errors they find, which makes ensembling a big lever for finding issues in papers. Seven errors could not be caught by any system, and all seven were omissions: information deleted from a paper rather than mistakes inserted into it. Refine.ink contributes more unique catches than any other single system, though it is expensive on a per-error basis. False positives were not measured, and how this error distribution compares to the distribution of errors in real papers remains unknown. The papers, errors, model outputs, and full experiment log are public, so that others can build on this toward a comprehensive evaluation benchmark across disciplines.

papers.title: RadAI: Gaze-Intention Fusion Pipeline for Attention-Guided Educational Videos in Chest X-Ray Interpretation
papers.abstract: Chest radiograph interpretation errors often arise from failures in visual search: although trainees may correctly identify an abnormality once pointed out, they frequently fail to fixate on the relevant region, while expert search strategies (where radiologists look, in what sequence, and for how long) remain largely implicit. Eye movement modeling examples (EMME), which replay a recorded expert's gaze over the image, have been shown to improve novice detection of findings on chest radiographs, but producing one requires an eye-tracking session on that specific case, so teaching sets are limited to recorded sessions by experts. In this work, RadAI is presented, the first end-to-end framework for transforming predicted radiologist gaze into narrated instructional videos, enabling scalable gaze-guided training without collecting new eye-tracking data. Given only a chest X-ray and its report, RadAI predicts an expert fixation sequence, associates each interval of that sequence with the diagnostic finding it pursues, extracts the corresponding image region, and renders the result as an EMME-style video in which each highlighted finding is narrated with synthesized speech. RadAI is evaluated on 97 cases from the EGD-CXR dataset, assessing whether the highlighted regions correspond to annotated abnormality locations. We position this work as a framework for scalable generation of educational content for residents and medical students in the field of radiology.

papers.title: Weighted Matroid Intersection under Minimum Rank Oracle
papers.abstract:
We consider matroid intersection under the minimum rank oracle model, in which two matroids are accessible only through an oracle that returns the minimum of the ranks of a given set in the two matroids. By Edmonds' theorem, this oracle determines the matroid intersection polytope, although it does not reveal the exchangeability graphs on which classical algorithms rely. Recent work by B\'ar\'asz, B\'erczi, Kir\'aly, Oki, Yamaguchi, and Yokoi (2025) showed that unweighted matroid intersection is polynomially solvable in this model.
  In this paper, we present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for weighted matroid intersection in this model. The key to our algorithm is a polynomial-size extended formulation of tangent cones of common base polytopes that can be constructed using the minimum rank oracle. We also give min-max theorems in terms of the minimum rank function via 1/3-submodularity, and present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm to compute an optimal dual solution.

papers.title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
papers.abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.

papers.title: Curve theory in $S^2\times S^2$ with applications to ruled surfaces in $S^3$
papers.abstract: The Riemannian product $S^2\times S^2$ of two unit spheres admits several important geometric interpretations. It can be identified both with the complex quadric $Q^2$ and with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$. In this paper, we first develop a unified framework for the geometry of curves in $S^2\times S^2$. We introduce projection-regular curves in $S^2\times S^2$ and their curvature data, and prove a congruence theorem for these curves. As an application of this framework, regarding $S^2\times S^2$ as the complex quadric $Q^2$, we classify K\"ahler magnetic geodesics associated with the product K\"ahler--Einstein structure. For closed generic projection-regular curves, we establish a sharp Fenchel-type inequality. We then identify $S^2\times S^2$ with the space $\mathcal{L}(S^3)$ of oriented geodesics in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$ and apply our curve theory to ruled surfaces in $S^3$. In particular, we prove that every nonsingular closed generic projection-regular ruled surface attaining equality in the Fenchel-type inequality is an embedded torus.

papers.title: SurvAD: How Anomalies Survive Diffusion Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based anomaly detectors reconstruct a test image towards normality, yet how much of an anomaly survives, its leak, remains uncharacterized. We show that a first-order deterministic sampler obeys an exact recursion along the anomaly, whose continuous limit is a survival law. The anomaly decays exponentially as the noise falls, at a rate set by the retention $r$, the share the model keeps on the states it visits. Because $r$ depends on the noise level and not on the step count, one measured path predicts the leak of other step counts, samplers and schedules from a nearby start to within a few hundredths, on four diffusion models and real defects. The law also shows that the leak's growth over steps is exposure bias and that normal details obey the same law, so changing the path or the training trades leak for detail error. We introduce SurvAD, which fine-tunes the reconstructor on inference-like starts and fits a comparator that adds evidence to the residual map without suppressing its ranking elsewhere. For under $2\%$ more inference time, SurvAD raises the multi-class pixel average precision (P-AP) of DeCo-Diff from $76.8$ to $80.7$ on MVTec AD and from $57.5$ to $60.0$ on VisA. It matches CostFilter-AD on the same reconstructor with $9\times$ fewer trainable parameters and, under Dinomaly's protocol, exceeds its reported P-AP on Dinomaly on both benchmarks.

authors.name: Lexing Zhang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hangzhou First People's Hospital, Westlake University, School of Medicine

papers.title: Panel Local Projections with Missing Data
papers.abstract: A panel local projection can remain identified even when missing data leave no complete regression case. We recover the projection over specified dates by combining factor-based conditional means with idiosyncratic covariances from observed pairs. Under strong factors in the auxiliary panel, sufficient factor variation at observed dates and enough observations of the required pairs, a second-order expansion yields bias-corrected moments and a joint score for inference. The localized multiplier bootstrap provides pointwise confidence intervals and simultaneous bands under additional dependence restrictions. We revisit the investment response to geopolitical risk studied by Caldara and Iacoviello (2022) with a larger quarterly firm sample and extend the analysis to monthly projections of trailing-three-month investment intensity. In the monthly analysis, the six-month response difference between high- and low-exposure firms becomes more negative as firms with incomplete histories enter the sample.

papers.title: Dipolar Exchange and Emergent Electric-Dipole-Carrying Quasiparticles in Electronic Ferroelectrics
papers.abstract: Electronic correlations underpin diverse spontaneously ordered states in matter, whose collective excitations emerge as quasiparticles that encode the underlying order. While spin exchange interactions give rise to magnetic order and its quasiparticle excitations known as magnons, their counterparts in electronic ferroelectrics remain poorly understood. Here, we derive an analogous quantum dipolar-pseudospin exchange model for electronic ferroelectricity and identify the associated bosonic quasiparticles that carry intrinsic electric dipole moments. Unlike ferrons in conventional lattice-based ferroelectrics, these dipolar quasiparticles arise entirely from collective electronic dynamics without involving lattice vibrations. Their excitation spectrum exhibits a linear Stark shift under a static electric field, while coupling to an oscillating electric field enables their coherent excitation, leading to colossal, resonantly enhanced second-harmonic generation and optical rectification in the terahertz regime. These dipolar quasiparticles offer promising opportunities for electrically tunable nonlinear optics and open a route toward extending the paradigm of transport in electronic systems beyond conventional charge currents to electric dipole currents.

papers.title: MySign: A High-Fidelity Motion-Capture Dataset for 3D Sign Generation in Bahasa Isyarat Malaysia
papers.abstract: Progress in 3D sign generation is constrained by the scarcity of high-fidelity 3D sign language datasets, a limitation that is particularly severe for under-resourced languages. We introduce MySign, the first motion-capture dataset for isolated signs in Bahasa Isyarat Malaysia (BIM). Its 5,000 samples cover 1,000 lexical items (glosses) and were produced by five Deaf native signers. Prior datasets that rely on SMPL-X parameters regressed from video provide pseudo-labels, which are often affected by depth ambiguity, inaccurate finger poses, and temporal jitter. MySign instead provides ground-truth SMPL-X sequences retargeted from recordings made with a motion-capture setup tailored for sign language; these sequences offer higher-fidelity motion, particularly in fine-grained hand and finger articulation. A controlled comparison on the same glosses and signers indicates that training on these sequences improves generation over training on such pseudo-labels. We establish MySign as a challenging benchmark for gloss-conditioned 3D sign generation: state-of-the-art models produce visually plausible outputs but fall short of the ground truth, most notably in fine-grained articulation, revealing persistent gaps in modeling articulated sign motion. In contrast, recognition baselines consistently achieve high lexical accuracy, indicating that the dataset reliably supports supervised learning. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/mysigner/MySign

papers.title: Robust Implicit Neural Representation for Multiparameter Elastic Full-Waveform Inversion
papers.abstract: Multiparameter elastic full-waveform inversion (EFWI) provides a powerful means of reconstructing subsurface elastic properties, but its practical application remains challenging because of strong nonlinearity, parameter crosstalk, and the different sensitivities of seismic data to individual elastic parameters. We develop a robust implicit neural representation (INR) framework for multiparameter EFWI, using continuous neural representations to parameterize the subsurface model and provide an effective model-space constraint during inversion. Within this framework, we systematically investigate different elastic parameterizations and demonstrate that parameterization plays a critical role in controlling parameter coupling and inversion stability. Among the tested formulations, combining P-wave velocity (Vp), P-wave impedance (Ip), and the Vs/Vp ratio provides the most robust overall performance, yielding improved parameter separation and more reliable reconstruction of elastic properties. We evaluate the proposed approach on the Marmousi and Overthrust models under increasingly challenging inversion conditions and further apply it to the field Volve ocean-bottom-node dataset. Both synthetic and field-data results demonstrate that the INR-based formulation, together with the Vp-Ip-Vs/Vp parameterization, improves inversion stability, suppresses parameter cross-talk and inversion artifacts, and produces geologically coherent multiparameter models. These results highlight the importance of jointly considering model representation and physical parameterization in multiparameter EFWI and demonstrate the potential of robust INR-based inversion for complex synthetic and field seismic applications.

papers.title: Trajectory Density Ratios under Weak Support: A Survey across the Sciences
papers.abstract: Many problems across the sciences compare two stochastic processes through the sequences they generate. Reinforcement learning asks what a new policy would return from the trajectories of an old one; molecular simulation asks how much more a ligand binds from samples of the unbound state; climate attribution asks how a heat wave shifted under warming; and language-model post-training asks what a deployed agent will do from logged interactions. In every case, one quantity would answer all these questions at once: the ratio of the two probability laws over their generated sequences, the trajectory density ratio. This ratio exists only under strong conditions. When one process reaches states the other cannot, the ratio does not exist; when their overlap is thin, its variance grows without control with the sequence length; and when they concentrate on different lower-dimensional sets, the ratio is undefined altogether. Weak support of this kind is the norm for sequence data, not a sampling accident, and its price is paid in identifiability rather than in noise alone. This survey organizes the field around a three-level diagnosis of weak support and a map of the nine retreats that methods take when the full ratio is out of reach, from direct estimation and reweighting through staged decomposition, stationarization, and partial-identification bounds to smoothing, transport couplings, operator spectra, and direct estimation of a single functional. Each retreat keeps part of what the ratio offers and pays for the rest, and each application domain has standardized the retreat its data force. The survey closes with open problems: testable diagnostics at every level, partial identification at the trajectory level, a rate theory of time-amplified error, and benchmarks with ground truth.

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

papers.title: QCVS: Question-Contrastive Visual Steering for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Inference-time steering in vision-language models often entangles query-relevant reasoning dynamics with low-level perceptual noise, causing collateral degradation on correct predictions. We propose Question-Contrastive Visual Steering (QCVS) to isolate task-specific intervention directions via double-differential activation probing. By contrasting spatial layout perturbations under the target query against a generic description reference, QCVS cancels task-agnostic visual artifacts without ground-truth supervision. A dual-threshold gating mechanism then evaluates relative interaction strength and signal amplitude, selectively applying a single bounded hidden-state update only when necessary. Empirical evaluations across multiple scales of Qwen3.5 (2B to 9B) and DeepSeek-VL2 on DynaMath and We-Math demonstrate that QCVS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy gains under sparse coverage (approximately 22%-30%). Crucially, QCVS yields repair rates up to 13.98% while suppressing collateral damage down to 0.41%, proving high intervention precision and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
papers.abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erd\H{o}s-P\'osa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

papers.title: ODSA: Orchestrated Discovery and Self-Aggregation
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling improves the accuracy of a language model's answers by spending more computation at inference time. Established methods do so either sequentially, revising a single solution over several passes, or in parallel, generating several independent solutions and selecting among them. We present ODSA (Orchestrated Discovery and Self-Aggregation), an LLM-directed scaling framework in which an orchestrator LLM is given existing test-time scaling methods as actions --- discovery of a new independent solution, comparison of existing solutions to build a better one, and acceptance of a proposed answer, which triggers its verification --- and directs stateless workers to carry them out. The orchestrator does not solve the problem itself: it allocates computation, feeds the results of earlier actions into later ones, and takes every action from a single context, so that each decision is informed by everything tried before. On Humanity's Last Exam, ODSA improves accuracy by 4.7 to 18.0 points across three models over a single direct call to the model with no test-time scaling. On LiveCodeBench, where a single direct call already solves most problems, it improves accuracy by 0.6 to 14.0 points.

papers.title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
papers.abstract:
The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$.
  In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $\gamma_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$.
  Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on all smooth 13-spheres
papers.abstract: Every smooth homotopy $13$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive sectional curvature. We construct a special $S^3$--$S^3$ bundle over $S^{13}$ whose star quotient represents the nonzero class $\pm\alpha_1\beta_1\in\Theta_{13}\cong\mathbb Z/3$. The defining equivariant map factors through the Blakers--Massey map by a smooth Hopf construction representing an unstable $J$-generator. This factorisation retains the prescribed base representation and makes Schultz's plumbing composition formula applicable; a normal-invariant computation in smoothing theory then identifies the smooth structure. On the quotient we implement the compatible-disk strategy with complete curvature estimates on arbitrary two-planes, matching boundary metrics, and a strictly positive sum of outward second fundamental forms. A direct smoothing argument completes the metric construction. Orientation reversal gives the remaining nonzero class in $\Theta_{13}$.

papers.title: Gravitational Production of Non-minimally Coupled Vector Dark Matter in Warm Inflation
papers.abstract: We study the purely gravitational production of a massive vector dark matter with a non-minimal coupling to the Einstein tensor, $\xi G_{\mu\nu}X^\mu X^\nu$, in warm inflation. The background, $V=\lambda\phi^4$ with a dissipation coefficient linear in temperature, is constrained by CMB observations and parametrized by the dissipation ratio $10^{-4}\le Q_0\le1$. We consider both unavoidable production channels: freeze-in from the Standard Model bath through graviton exchange, and cosmological gravitational particle production (CGPP). For freeze-in, we compute the scattering amplitudes including the contact interaction induced by $\xi$, which enhances the production of light dark matter through the longitudinal mode and suppresses that of heavy dark matter through destructive interference. For CGPP, the slow-roll parameter is not small during warm inflation, which enhances the production of light dark matter by up to three orders of magnitude relative to cold inflation. Combining both channels, CGPP excludes most of the light freeze-in branch, leaving $m_X\lesssim2.4\times10^{-5}$ GeV, a narrow window around $10^{10}$ GeV for strong dissipation, and $m_X\gtrsim10^{14}$--$10^{15}$ GeV. Only the heavy branch remains viable for all $|\xi|\lesssim1$.

papers.title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
papers.abstract: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

papers.title: Stochastic Port-Hamiltonian Gaussian Processes for Learning from Noisy Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.abstract: Learning predictive models for dynamics is difficult because observations are often sparse and noisy, while the underlying dynamics evolve on nonlinear configuration manifolds and are affected by environmental dissipation and stochastic disturbances. Standard neural dynamics models can fit short-term trajectories but often violate physical structure, accumulate error over long horizons, or rely on parameterizations that introduce singularities such as gimbal lock. We introduce LieSPHGP, a stochastic Gaussian-process framework for learning rigid body dynamics with port-Hamiltonian structure and stability-aware robustness. LieSPHGP represents motion on Lie groups and Lie algebras, enabling coordinate-consistent optimization without singular parameterizations. Learned mass, potential energy, dissipation, and control components retain physical roles and a separate diffusion term represents stochastic forcing. Each component is modeled by Mat\'ern kernel Gaussian processes which capture uncertainty induced by noisy observations. To improve physical validity, Lie group exponential map updates preserve rotational constraints, while positive-definite damping ensures nonnegative deterministic energy dissipation. The implicit-explicit integrator additionally provides unconditional stability for the frozen linear damping subsystem. The resulting model learns predictive dynamics that are robust to noise, respect rigid body geometry, and capture both intrinsic motion and environmental dissipation. Experiments on various noisy rigid body benchmarks show improved prediction accuracy, stronger long-horizon stability, and better satisfaction of manifold constraints compared with neural dynamics baselines. Code, data and interactive results are available on the project website: https://thribhuvanrapolu.github.io/liesphgp/

papers.title: Watching Itself Watch: Self-Auditing Visual Reliance for Video Reasoning
papers.abstract: Video reasoning hinges on a small number of visually decisive tokens embedded in otherwise largely language-driven chains of thought. Yet prevailing post-training methods such as GRPO overlook this structure, assigning coarse trajectory-level rewards while requiring multiple rollouts and often costly external judges. We introduce Visually-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation (VIOS), a post-training framework that identifies where a model under-utilizes visual evidence and concentrates learning at those positions. Our key insight is that a model can audit its own visual reliance: the divergence between its next-token distributions with and without the video reveals how strongly each prediction depends on the visual input. Measuring this reliance for both a student and an answer-privileged teacher exposes a per-token reliance gap, identifying positions where the teacher exploits visual evidence that the student overlooks. VIOS translates this signal into dense, targeted supervision through three complementary components: an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher that co-evolves with the student, a contrastive objective that encourages predictions to depend on the video, and a reliance-gap gate that focuses learning on visually under-utilized tokens. Crucially, VIOS requires only a single on-policy rollout from a single model, without external rewards, judges, or larger teachers. Across 12 benchmarks spanning general, temporal, spatial, knowledge-intensive, and long-video understanding, VIOS consistently improves three model backbones and outperforms contemporary video-reasoning systems, while training in over 9x fewer steps, 60x fewer FLOPs, and 111x fewer generated tokens. Project page: https://vision.cs.utexas.edu/projects/VIOS/

authors.name: Mi Luo
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Kristen Grauman
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Telling coordination from coincidence: a no-interaction twin for collective systems
papers.abstract: Measures of emergence based on information theory or causal closure ask whether a group variable has a predictable law of its own, but not whether that law was produced by the members' interactions: the centre of mass of non-interacting random walkers passes the standard criterion $\Psi$. We introduce the interaction share S, the fraction of the forecast error of a system's no-interaction twin (the same members with every interaction removed) that the real group law eliminates, and a projected estimator with expectation zero without interaction. For Gaussian forecasts, $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1-S)$ is the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence of the real group law from the twin's. S is exactly zero for the centre of mass of linearly coupled walkers, and a machine-checked proof extends this to any pairwise force obeying Newton's third law. Across magnets, oscillators and flocking models it rises from 0 to about 1 where collective order appears. With time-shifted virtual groups and positive controls, it separates real fish schools (0.54-0.91, 17 recordings, two species) from groups that never interacted (-0.10 to 0.07), and it falls to zero when zebrafish are placed in the dark. In 221 mouse brain areas and in US stock markets the shares are small (about 1-3%) and were confirmed in pre-registered tests on unseen data. For linear forecasts the share is a memory gap, computable from two autocorrelation curves without fitting a twin; it matches measured shares (Spearman 0.97) and predicted fresh markets within 0.004. All code, data pipelines and hashed pre-registrations are public.

papers.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
papers.abstract: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.

papers.title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
papers.abstract:
We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[
  |\{N>\lambda\}|\le C\left(|\{A>\lambda\}|+\lambda^{-2}\int_{\{A\le\lambda\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.

papers.title: Lifting mechanical zero modes without dispersion
papers.abstract: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

authors.name: Joohan Nam
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.

papers.title: From MNH to the Friedman--Komogortsev Method---which changes improve eye-movement classification?
papers.abstract: The Friedman-Komogortsev Method (FKM) is a rule-based classifier of fixations, saccades, and post-saccadic oscillations in 1000-Hz recordings, developed from the modified Nystr\"om-Holmqvist algorithm (MNH) and used in several recent studies. FKM changes MNH in many ways at once: it centres MNH's Savitzky-Golay filter, adds a position-based test for whether an apparent post-saccadic oscillation continues the saccade, adds rejection tests, and changes several thresholds. We asked which of these changes alter agreement with human classification. Both algorithms were scored against twenty 26-s GazeBase reading recordings hand-classified by three trained raters, and each change was reverted in turn. FKM agreed better than MNH as MNH was used: saccade Cohen's kappa rose on all 20 recordings (median +0.034), and saccade boundaries moved from 2-3 ms late to the raters' sample. One change produced this: centring the filter, which removes a three-sample delay. Reinstating the delay returned FKM's saccade kappa to MNH's value, and centring MNH's filter alone made MNH match FKM on saccades and exceed it on post-saccadic events. The position-based test changed how saccades with several velocity peaks were divided, splitting 8% of rater-labelled "wavy" saccades into a saccade and a spurious oscillation against 39% for delay-corrected MNH. FKM's higher post-saccadic velocity floor traded recall for precision. The remaining changes had no measurable effect on these recordings. FKM's improvement over MNH is therefore a filter-alignment correction that MNH users can apply directly, plus a segmentation rule for multi-peak saccades.

papers.title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the map $\Theta$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$, including the optimal H\"older exponent of $\Theta^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $\Theta$ and $\Theta^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $\Theta$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $\Theta$ has an infinite derivative.

papers.title: Laplace approximation of the parameter posterior with embedded error for efficient uncertainty quantification of expensive model calibrations
papers.abstract: In practical engineering, there is a clear need for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of models used in design because forward UQ puts probabilities on performance predictions. However, without surrogate building, most forward engineering models are too expensive for traditional UQ methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our goal is to provide inexpensive, approxi- mate UQ that can be applied after an expensive traditional least squares fit, where the UQ handles both uncorrelated noise and parameter variance as in the embedded-error treatment developed by Sargsyan, Najm, and Ghanem (2015). After developing the basic theory to connect a Laplace-like approximation to Bayesian calibration, we compare the proposed method to black-box variational inference in terms of cost and fidelity. Then we demonstrate the method on real-world calibration of solid material models.

papers.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
papers.abstract:
It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ ( $0<\delta<\pi$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been
  $$
  O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(\pi-\delta)n)\biggr).
  $$
  We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}$ satisfying
  $$
  c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}\le \rho_{n,\delta}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2},
  \quad 0<\delta\leq\pi,\quad n\geq1,
  $$
  where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $\delta$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words,
  $$
  \rho_{n,\delta} \asymp \frac{\tan\frac\delta 4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_\delta(\pi-\delta)n\bigr),
  $$
  where $c_\delta$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi]$ and
  $$
  \lim_{\delta\to\pi^-}c_\delta=1,\ \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}c_\delta=+\infty.
  $$
  We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}'$ of the optimal algorithm is
  $$
  \rho_{n,\delta}' \asymp \sqrt{\delta/\pi}\sin^n(\delta/2).
  $$

papers.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
papers.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<\gamma<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

papers.title: Exploiting Native Hardware Heterogeneity: Custom GPSIMD Operators for Accelerating Emerging LLM Memory on AWS Trainium
papers.abstract: Emerging memory modules of large language models, such as Engram in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, mix irregular integer work (a 64-bit n-gram hash and a sparse table lookup) with dense computation (a GEMM and a gate). When deploying on a GPU-FPGA system, we can disaggregate operations to different devices for Engram to speed up by 5.9$\times$. AWS Trainium provides a similar heterogeneity natively: each Trainium NeuronCore pairs dense engines with a customizable GPSIMD Engine, and all engines share the on-chip SBUF. However, the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) exposes the GPSIMD cores only through fixed built-in instructions, and the official GPSIMD custom-operator toolchain does not support Trainium 2 or 3 and cannot be used with NKI. In this work, we build a toolchain that compiles C++ custom operators for the GPSIMD cores and injects them into the compiled NEFF from the NKI kernel on Trainium 3, expanding the customizability of GPSIMD with the current software stack. Over a hand-optimized NKI baseline of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, two GPSIMD operators speed up the n-gram hashing by 1.79$\times$ at decode, the table retrieval by up to 4.95$\times$, and the whole Engram computation by up to 1.14$\times$.

papers.title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
papers.abstract:
We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\in\Omega \subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(\Omega; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality
  \[
  |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } \Omega
  \]
  with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(\Omega)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $\Omega$.

papers.title: Separable social welfare evaluation without completeness
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study incomplete social evaluation of utility vectors to capture situations in which there is disagreement in society about the degree of inequality aversion. We characterize multi-prioritarian criteria using efficiency, equity, impartiality, separability, and a condition called continuous divisible completion condition. We also provide uniqueness results and investigate comparative inequality aversion.

papers.title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
papers.abstract: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters. A matching-parameter specialization factors into the enumerators of a Motzkin excursion and a Motzkin bridge and proves the conjectured product of type~A and type~B Narayana polynomials for a two-row grid with its maximum removed. The general identity also records the two row supports separately. For combs, maximum ideal excess leads to a scalar recursion and a cubic generating function with independent spine and tooth weights. This proves a compositional-inverse conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton and gives explicit $\gamma$-coefficients by Lagrange inversion. We prove $\gamma$-positivity for all two-row Ferrers cell posets and for the combs. The truncated-grid enumerators have simple negative zeros.

papers.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

papers.title: A proof of the Erd\H{o}s-Herzog-Piranian lemniscate conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\geq 1$. In 1958, Erd\H{o}s, Herzog, and Piranian conjectured that the length of the lemniscate $\{z\in\mathbb C:|p(z)|=1\}$ is maximized by $p(z)=z^n-1$. We prove this conjecture in every degree and show that equality holds precisely for $p(z)=(z-z_0)^n-e^{i\theta}$, where $z_0\in\mathbb C$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$. The proof uses M\"obius variations of the critical values and estimates for the inverse branches of $p$, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted estimates in a finite range of degrees.

authors.name: Teng Zhang
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Objective Diversification of Dynamic Hedging
papers.abstract: A hedging objective reflects the risk preference of the hedger, so the conventional approach is to estimate the hedge ratio directly under the chosen objective. This paper asks whether that estimate should be used alone. We construct five objective-specific rolling hedge-ratio estimators---minimum variance, least absolute deviation (LAD), downside semivariance, lower-tail quantile, and Expected Shortfall (ES)---from the same historical stock--market returns, and combine the resulting estimates under a fixed final evaluation objective. Separate multi-output ExtraTrees models predict the within-stock-date ranks of the five candidates under MSE, LAD, downside semivariance, and 10\% quantile loss. The design uses pre-specified 60-, 90-, 120-, and 180-day windows with objective-matched rolling estimators as benchmarks. Adaptive weighting improves the corresponding loss in all sixteen objective--window comparisons. Equal weighting, which uses the same objective-specific hedge ratios without state variables or learned reweighting, already improves downside and quantile hedging. The results therefore suggest that estimates generated under other objectives can be useful even when the final hedging preference and evaluation objective are fixed, while adaptive weighting can provide a further improvement.

authors.name: Carlin Chun Fai Chu
authors.institution: Hang Seng University of Hong Kong

papers.title: The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
papers.abstract: A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge. The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue probability density functions. The new results relate to the large $N$ expansion of correlation functions and conditioned gap probability generating functions with hard edge scaling for the Jacobi ensemble. For all even $\beta$ we are able to show that these quantities admit expansions in inverse even powers of the variable $N_{\rm hJ}':= N - 1/2 + (a + b + 1)/\beta$. For the $\beta =2$ Jacobi unitary ensemble, we can relate the leading (next leading) correction to the limit law to a particular second order (fourth order) differential operator applied to the latter. The analogous second order differential operator is found for $\beta=1,4$, leading then to its conjectured form for all $\beta>0$.

authors.name: Peter J. Forrester
authors.institution: ARC Centre of Excellence for Mathematical and Statistical Frontiers

papers.title: Irreducible Representations as Local Maxima of a Matrix-Coefficient Functional
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite group $G$ and, for unit vectors $v$, let $\Phi(v)$ be the mean of $|\langle v,gv\rangle|^2$ over $g\in G$. We show that $v$ is a local maximum of $\Phi$ if and only if the subrepresentation generated by $v$ is irreducible. Thus local maximization of $\Phi$ extracts irreducible subrepresentations of $V$ directly, with no character or isotypic projection specified in advance. The proof is elementary: Schur averaging reduces it to a singular-value calculation. The values and dimensions of the connected components of the local-maximum set determine the degrees and multiplicities of the irreducible constituents, and for $H\leq G$ the intersections of the $G$- and $H$-local-maximal loci encode branching multiplicities. We also determine the critical landscape and give a normalized gradient iteration whose generic limit generates an irreducible subrepresentation.

papers.title: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
papers.abstract:
Frontier agentic LLMs are trained on verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning (RL) environments built from real software repositories. A passing test suite is treated as the reward for solving the task. We show that, on hard problems, frontier models often satisfy these rewards by obtaining the answer instead of deriving it, known as reward hacking. Prior reports document this behavior on public benchmarks. We test its persistence on unseen problems.
  In a hardened environment where the answer cannot leak, nearly every model we tested attempted to recover the answer, escalating through tiers of increasingly specialized exploitation: mining the repository history for the upstream fix, inspecting the git object store directly, and sweeping the filesystem for a possible newer copy of the source or hidden tests. These attempts were concentrated on the hardest problems, and the models differed in whether, how often, and how deeply they escalated. Our position is that this behavior is a learned shortcut, acquired in RL environments that leak the answer, not a sign of intelligence. We release agent traces for these models to support further study at https://huggingface.co/datasets/logitly-ai/reward-hacking-raw-v1.

papers.title: Identifying Contributions to the Superconducting Diode Effect through Nonreciprocal Superconducting Properties
papers.abstract: Nonreciprocal superconducting responses provide a sensitive probe of superconducting states in systems where inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken. However, in the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where the critical current differs for opposite current directions, nonreciprocity can also arise from vortex-induced contributions caused by minute magnetic field misalignment, complicating its interpretation. Here, we investigate a noncentrosymmetric $[Nb/V/Ta]_{40}$ superlattice and demonstrate nonreciprocity in all three fundamental superconducting properties: the critical current, critical field, and superconducting transition temperature. By measuring the angular dependence of the nonreciprocal critical field $\Delta B_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, we separate the contribution of misalignment-induced out-of-plane vortices from the in-plane response. We identify a sharply enhanced SDE emerging near $B_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, accompanied by nonreciprocal responses in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. These observations exhibit phenomenology similar to that reported in layered superconductors, where an orbital-FFLO state with finite-momentum Cooper pairing has been reported. Our results establish a protocol for assessing out-of-plane vortex contributions to the superconducting diode effect and demonstrate that nonreciprocal responses provide complementary probes of unconventional superconducting states.

papers.title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
papers.abstract: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Supercurrent-controlled magnon transport via suppression of the superconducting gap
papers.abstract: Understanding interactions between different low-energy excitations is a central theme in condensed-matter physics. Magnons and superconducting condensates represent two distinct macroscopic quantum states, yet their mutual interaction remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate supercurrent-controlled magnon transport in a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure. We observe that the magnon transport signal decreases as the supercurrent increases. This suppression originates from a supercurrent-induced reduction of the superconducting gap, which enhances magnon dissipation into the superconductor via Bogoliubov quasiparticles. Our results provide direct experimental evidence of a supercurrent-controlled interaction between magnons and quasiparticles in the superconductor. The approach used in this study relies on supercurrents, enabling magnon modulation without Joule heating. These findings establish a new route to control magnons via superconductivity and pave the way for energy-efficient magnonic devices.
