papers.title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
papers.abstract:
We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $\phi^\star(\alpha)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula.
  Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre $z$ equals $\barW(z)\,\Up$, where $\barW$ is the degree function of the graphon and $\Up=-(\Id-P)^{-1}[P(H_\rho\rho)]'$ is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with $m$ edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of $z$. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.

papers.title: Weak $\lambda$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mr\'owka spaces
papers.abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $\lambda$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $\lambda$-space is a $\lambda$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $\lambda$-set that is not a $\lambda$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $\omega_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $\lambda$-set is a $\lambda$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>\omega_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.

papers.title: Deriving Tsallis Entropy from First Principles
papers.abstract: The kinetic approach for q-distribution is extended through a "bottom-up" procedure to the corresponding entropic formula. In this way, the validity of Tsallis' formula, S_q(W) = k_B ln_q(W), is established from first principles. The resulting q-entropy is additive and the zeroth law of thermodynamics is automatically satisfied because the conventional identification beta = 1/(k_B T) remains valid. Entropy, energy, and all relevant quantities for both discrete and continuous cases are evaluated using standard (linear) averages. The "bottom-up" and "top-down" approaches yield the same q-distribution for velocities. The standard results are naturally recovered in the limit q -> 1.

papers.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
papers.abstract: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. This work presents a study of the interaction of the protoplanetary disk with the protoplanet and the following types of orbital migration that can occur, and to verify this interaction, numerical simulations were performed using the magneto-hydrodynamics code FARGO3D. The researchers made five simulations with a 2-Jupiter-mass planet in the protoplanetary disk. The only parameter varied was the initial radial position with the aim of verifying the influence of this parameter on the behavior of planetary migration. As a result of these simulations, we find that the initial radial coordinate is a very significant parameter in how the planet interacts with the gas in the disk and the formation of gas gaps.

papers.title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
papers.abstract: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $\Sigma(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $\Sigma(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $\Sigma(p_c)$ completely: $\Sigma(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $\Sigma(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.

papers.title: The Truth Beneath the Tokens: Prompt-Space Recovery of Knowledge Edits in Language Models
papers.abstract: Model editing provides an efficient way to update factual knowledge in transformer models. Recent approaches reverse edits by modifying, masking, or decomposing model weights, but make recovery dependent on weight-space interventions. We instead show that pre-edit knowledge can be recovered through input-space interventions alone, without modifying the edited model's weights. We introduce Memento, a prompt-space mechanism for auditing residual knowledge that learns a reusable recovery signal to steer an edited model toward its pre-edit response. Memento supports both continuous recovery prefixes and discrete textual prompts for standard text interfaces. Across three LLMs and five editing techniques, Memento recovers 80.07% of held-out edited facts, achieving a 9.58% relative improvement over baselines, suggesting that editing may suppress the facts without fully eliminating their recoverability. We further investigate whether prompt-space recovery extends beyond model editing. On pristine, unedited LLMs, Memento improves average factual recall by 53.9% relative to standard inference. These results demonstrate the potential of prompt-space recovery for auditing residual knowledge in edited models and investigating the gap between factual knowledge and its accessibility during inference. We will release our source code.

papers.title: Seeing Isn't Enough: Unlocking Visual Reasoning by Bridging the Reasoning-Access Gap with TIGER
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) inherit strong textual reasoning capabilities from their language backbones and text pretraining, but often fail to apply the same level of competency to visual inputs. We show that this degradation cannot be attributed to only perception failures, by evaluating models on semantically-equivalent text and rendered-text image inputs: models can accurately read text in the images and recover near-text performance when provided their own transcriptions, but just cannot reason well on the images directly. We characterize this discrepancy as a modality reasoning-access gap, where models fail to route perceived visual content into existing reasoning machinery accessible with text. To bridge this, we propose TIGER (Text-to-Image Gap-targeted training for Enhanced Reasoning), which first mines synthetic modality counterfactuals where a model succeeds on a text problem but fails when provided the corresponding rendered image, and post-trains the model on the image input via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), along with SFT and DPO variants. Importantly, although trained exclusively on synthetic rendered-text images with no multimodal annotations, TIGER results in model performance improvements across diverse real-world visual benchmarks including geometric diagrams (MathVerse), multi-disciplinary sciences (EMMA, MMMU), complex charts (ChartQAPro), and embodied spatial reasoning (RoboSpatial-Home). TIGER also complements existing state-of-the-art RLVR visual reasoning methods, yielding further performance gains. Analysis involving reasoning-subspace activation and activation patching provide support indicating that TIGER helps to align visual-to-reasoning pathways toward text reasoning states. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/minhngh/Tiger.

papers.title: Bisect-Index-Choose: A Fast and Exact Algorithm for EV Charging under Minimum Charging Rates
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations are increasingly operated with an aggregate power limit below the sum of their port ratings, and require scheduling algorithms to divide the available power among the connected EVs. Charging standards permit a current that is either zero or at least a minimum rate, typically 6 A, which makes this allocation problem non-convex. Existing methods either solve a mixed-integer program with a commercial solver, which can be computationally expensive, adds software dependencies, and incurs licensing costs, or apply heuristics without optimality guarantees. This paper proposes Bisect-Index-Choose (BIC), a fast and solver-free scheduling algorithm that computes a globally optimal allocation among EVs under mild assumptions on their utilities. For $n$ EVs, BIC runs in $O(n \log n)$ time when all EVs share one maximum rate and in $O(n^2)$ time for two, times a logarithmic factor in the numerical precision. In tests with up to 1000 EVs, BIC attains global optimality and is up to three orders of magnitude faster than the solver. On real-world charging data, it needs less capacity and delivers more energy than existing heuristics. We implement BIC on a low-cost microcontroller and show that it solves instances with 1000 EVs in less than 90 ms.

papers.title: Algorithms for Soft Tree Containment on Tree-Child Networks
papers.abstract:
Phylogenetic networks generalize evolutionary trees by allowing lineages to merge. The Tree Containment problem asks whether a network $N$ displays a tree $T$ on the same taxa. When the polytomies of $T$ reflect uncertainty rather than simultaneous divergence, the relevant notion is soft display, in which $N$ may refine the polytomies of $T$. We take it in its asymmetric reading. Soft Tree Containment is NP-hard on reticulation-visible networks even at reticulation indegree three, and it was open for a non-binary tree and a tree-child network with multifurcating tree nodes or reticulations of indegree above two.
  We solve this case. A cluster characterization reduces soft display to realizing all clusters of $T$ by one switching, and in a tree-child network the vertices that can realize a cluster lie on a single chain. The per-cluster requirements then form a constraint network of width one, which arc consistency decides without search, and a $2$-SAT instance when $N$ is binary. This yields, to our knowledge, the first polynomial-time algorithm for soft Tree Containment on single-labelled tree-child networks of arbitrary reticulation indegree, and a linear-time algorithm when $T$ is binary. The same method decides the symmetric variant of the problem, in which the polytomies of $N$ may be resolved as well.

papers.title: The Photonic Bath at Infinity: Foundations, Derivations, and Consistency Checks
papers.abstract: The photonic bath at infinity represents the unbounded electromagnetic environment as an effective reservoir in the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. It accounts for outgoing radiation and incoming electromagnetic fluctuations, allowing radiative transport to be described consistently. We clarify how environmental fluctuations are incorporated without double-counting the outgoing radiation response already contained in the free retarded Green's function. We develop four complementary approaches to deriving the bath self-energy: infinitesimal environmental absorption, semi-infinite leads, inversion of the free Green's function, and sesquilinear forms with outgoing radiation boundary conditions. In particular, we present an explicit three-site matrix inversion for a planar geometry and introduce a sesquilinear form that relates the bath self-energy to the Silver--M\"uller radiation condition. We establish the connections among these approaches and obtain explicit bath self-energies for one-dimensional, planar, and spherical geometries. The resulting bath self-energies reproduce the Planck spectrum, the Stefan--Boltzmann law, and radiation pressure, and provide the radiative contribution required for energy conservation in photon NEGF.

papers.title: Beyond Falsehoods 2026: Global Trends in the Regulation of Misinformation and Disinformation
papers.abstract:
This report examines global legislative and regulatory responses to misinformation, disinformation, and mal-information (MDM) between 1995 and 2025. Drawing on an expanded and updated dataset of 409 coded regulatory and policy entries, including hard and soft law, policy measures, and proposed or draft instruments, it analyses their growth, geographic distribution, substantive focuses, and regulatory designs, which represent the various approaches taken against MDM, as well as early evidence of their implementation.
  The central finding is sustained and accelerating regulatory growth. Annual activity increased from 11 instruments in 2016 to 46 in 2023, 67 in 2024, and 71 in 2025. The number of instruments currently in force has reached 282, despite 34 measures having been repealed, withdrawn, or judicially invalidated. This growth has also been accompanied by a shift in regulatory focus. Earlier measures relied heavily on broad prohibitions of "false information," whereas more recent measures increasingly target specific harms, including deepfakes, election interference, non-consensual intimate imagery, and child safety. Regulatory responsibility is also increasingly being placed on platforms rather than solely on individual creators and users.

papers.title: Pointed Hopf Algebras from Pale Braidings in Characteristic 2
papers.abstract: We determine Nichols algebras associated with several families of pale braidings over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. For the rank-$4$ families under consideration, we obtain presentations by generators and relations, explicit monomial bases and dimension formulas. We also study families of arbitrary rank consisting of a two-dimensional pale block and several points, including cases with both vanishing and nonvanishing interaction parameters. Realizations as Yetter--Drinfeld modules over suitable finite abelian groups yield finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebras by bosonization.

papers.title: Performance Benchmarking of Federated Learning Frameworks for Medical Image Classification
papers.abstract: Selecting a Federated Learning (FL) framework requires understanding the resource demands of its training and evaluation workflow. This work compares Flower, NVIDIA FLARE, and FedBioMed using two-dimensional MedNIST classification with ResNet-10 in a containerized, single-host environment. Following a dated review of repository activity and documented medical applications, we evaluated nine configurations per framework, with three random seeds, for a total of 81 executions. The configurations varied federation size, communication rounds, and batch size. We monitored execution time, CPU and RAM consumption, host-level GPU utilization, server network traffic rates, and model accuracy at the end of each execution. The implementations shared nominal learning settings while retaining differences in data splitting and federated evaluation. Configuration-blocked non-parametric analysis identified differences in execution time, client and server memory, GPU utilization, and network traffic rates. NVIDIA FLARE exhibited the lowest server-memory consumption and the highest host-level GPU utilization, Flower exhibited the highest average server network traffic rate, and FedBioMed required more client memory and longer execution time. No statistically significant difference in final accuracy was detected within the evaluated short training schedules; this does not establish convergence or equivalent predictive performance. The results characterize the configured workflows under shared hardware resources. They provide a concrete case study of system behavior, with conclusions bounded by workflow asymmetries, local networking, and the lightweight MedNIST workload.

papers.title: Learning of Tree Automata applied to Neural Language Acceptors
papers.abstract:
We extract visibly pushdown grammars (VPGs) from neural language models in a fully black-box setting. Our work builds on the VPL* framework, which learns VPGs from recurrent networks by exploiting access to the target's internal state.
  First, we replace the white-box equivalence oracle with PAC sampling over trees. The resulting algorithm applies unchanged to transformer language models and, more generally, to any acceptor exposing only binary decisions.
  Second, we further observe that the original framework only ever queries the target on well-formed sequences that can be accepted by the most permissive VPG (called BParse) with the target's ranked alphabet. That is, VPL* is blind to the target's behavior outside BParse. Thus, we propose to sample trees directly instead of sequences and call the target with all the resulting sequences in order to provide an error estimate of how far the target deviates from being a VPG.
  Last but not least, we develop a learner that captures a tree automaton describing discovered behaviors of the target outside BParse, which results in a larger learnable space.
  We evaluate the approach on several cases, including transformers trained with Dyck grammars and synthetic targets designed to be outside BParse.

papers.title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
papers.abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

papers.title: Think or Remember: The Exchange Rate of Agentic Inference
papers.abstract: Agents built on reasoning models resend their growing transcript at every call. Two transacting parties, not the model, decide what that costs: the client keeps or edits messages; the server decides whether earlier reasoning returns in the prompt and what its cache reuses. We define a cost model whose counts match an instrumented engine exactly; the architecture charges $c$ per token processed and $\beta$ per pair attended. Their ratio $P^*=c/\beta$ is an exchange rate between thinking and remembering: per token, processing dominates below this context length, a thinking regime, and attention above it, a memory regime. A policy change has a mechanical cost, incurred even if the agent writes the same tokens, and a behavioral one: it writes different tokens, changing cost and outcome. Serving alone can flip which policy is cheaper: on recorded Qwen3-8B ScienceWorld runs, dropping earlier reasoning costs 1.74 times keeping it when the server reuses generated states and 0.34 times when it reuses nothing. In live reruns, dropping it cuts correct HotpotQA answers by 9-23 percentage points on four models, at lower point-estimate cost. Comparing context policies means comparing systems: architecture and serving set the cost of the history kept and the work it induces.

papers.title: Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
papers.abstract: Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.

papers.title: On the $\Delta$-primitive squares conjecture
papers.abstract: A natural number $n$ has the $\Delta$ property if some difference of complementary divisors of $n$ is the sum of two such differences; equivalently, if some split graph has a factor graph containing an $n$-simple triangle. In additive terms, $n$ has the $\Delta$ property exactly when the positive part of the factor-difference set of $n$, introduced by Erd\H{o}s and Rosenfeld, is not sum-free. The set $\mathbb{N}(\Delta)$ of such numbers is closed under multiplication by squares, and it was conjectured that it contains infinitely many $\Delta$-primitive perfect squares. We prove this conjecture, and show that these squares can be chosen to avoid any prescribed finite set of primes but $3$.

papers.title: Competing Influence in LLM Populations: Budget Timing and Baseline Drift
papers.abstract: When competing campaigns target a population of large language model (LLM) agents, observed opinion changes may reflect both campaign influence and changes that would occur without intervention. We study how the timing of campaign expenditure and the population's own evolution shape outcomes in a network of persona-conditioned LLM agents that exchange and revise opinions in natural language. A proponent and a challenger are tasked with generating opposing messages under equal delivery budgets, while a separate stance probe measures opinions without influencing the simulation. Across eight claims, we compare single-campaign and competitive conditions against matched no-campaign runs, and evaluate all nine combinations of early, sustained, and late spending on a reference topic. Baseline stance drift varies substantially across claims and, on some, accounts for a sizeable fraction of apparent campaign effects. After accounting for this drift, the direction of observed campaign-associated changes aligns more closely with the claim's epistemic standing than with the campaigner's assigned role. Uninfluenced populations also consistently lose stance diversity, demonstrating that directional opinion change and convergence are distinct phenomena. In networks with two opinion-segregated communities, campaigns primarily reduce differences between communities rather than diversity within them. LLM campaign agents do not always argue for their assigned positions, particularly when these conflict with established evidence. Finally, campaign outcomes depend on the opponent's expenditure schedule: unlike a matched numerical bounded-confidence population receiving interventions at the same times and locations, the LLM population exhibits a payoff structure with no pure-strategy equilibrium.

papers.title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
papers.abstract: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.

papers.title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models
papers.abstract: Unified whole-body pose estimators jointly predict body, face, and hand landmarks, but often degrade on small, blurred, or occluded hands. Attaching a standalone hand specialist introduces extra detection overhead, coordinate alignment, and wrist-stitching artifacts. We introduce S2HAND, a hand-specialized Sapiens2-5B framework that preserves the native 308-keypoint output interface. Specifically, S2HAND-MT adapts a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch to route 40 finger heatmaps while strictly preserving the shared Transformer, auxiliary task heads, and the other 268 body, foot, and face heatmaps. S2HAND-Pose further fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters), trading exact preservation for stronger hand recovery: it lifts macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL, and FreiHAND EVAL, and surpasses HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 systems on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks. On COCO, S2HAND-Pose improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points. Across a 512-image multi-task audit, it maintains 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint, with quantified normal and pointmap drift. Its 2D coordinates also lower 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer, while our optional TailGuard re-cropping module cuts S2HAND-MT's severe failure rate on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%. S2HAND thus resolves the whole-body hand bottleneck with either exact non-hand preservation (MT) or empirically audited trade-offs (Pose).

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

In our earlier work, see [FR26], we adopted a topological approach to the geometrisation problem where branched projective structures are realised by gluing a finite collection of simplexes modelled on the real projective plane. In the present work we adopt a complex-differential approach based on the theory of Higgs bundles. Upon fixing a Riemann surface XX of genus g≥2g\geq 2, the now classical non-abelian Hodge correspondence identifies the moduli space of poly-stable GG-Higgs bundles with the character variety of reductive representations of the surface group into a complex or real semi-simple Lie group GG. In a different and more recent direction, the holomorphic theory of Higgs bundles has been used to construct geometric (G,𝕏)(G,\mathbb{X})-structures directly on the underlying surface. In his doctoral dissertation [Bar09], Baraglia provided a pioneering contribution by showing, among other results, how a properly convex ℝ​ℙ2\mathbb{RP}^{2}-structure can be recovered from a stable SL⁡(3,ℝ){\mathrm{SL}(3,{\mathbb{R}})}-Higgs bundle lying in the image of the Hitchin section. Baraglia also developed an analogous construction for PSp⁡(4,ℝ)\mathrm{PSp}(4,\mathbb{R}), leading to the convex foliated projective structures studied by Guichard–Wienhard; see [GW08]. Related questions have subsequently been investigated for several other real Lie groups, including SO⁡(2,n)\mathrm{SO}(2,n) [CTT19], SL⁡(3,ℝ)\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R}) [RT25], in connection with other geometric structures as in [NR25], G2′\mathrm{G}_{2}^{\prime} [Eva25, DE25a], and SO⁡(p,p+1)\mathrm{SO}(p,p+1) [DE25b].

papers.title: But It Was True When I Checked: Compiling SHOP-Style Method Preconditions into Partially-Ordered HTN Planning
papers.abstract: Method preconditions specify when a method may be applied in hierarchical task network (HTN) planning, but their meaning differs under two established semantics. The SHOP planners, like the classical HTN formalism of Erol, Hendler and Nau, require the precondition to hold immediately before the method's first action. HDDL, the input language of the International Planning Competition's HTN track, instead introduces an auxiliary action to check it; under partial order, unrelated actions may invalidate the precondition before the method starts. HDDL's designers adopted this weaker semantics because the first-action reading could not easily be compiled. Subsequent work has repeatedly identified its compilation under partial order as an open question, with existing transformations limited to total order. We give a compilation of the first-action semantics into standard partially ordered HTN planning without method preconditions using only two additional facts, thereby resolving a longstanding question in the HTN planning community.

papers.title: Imperfectly Imperfect: Evaluating Graded Cognitive Diversity in LLM Persona Simulations
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as synthetic participants in social, behavioural, and decision-making research, yet it remains unclear whether they can express graded cognitive diversity as assigned when engaging in simulated behaviour. We introduce a cognition-suite evaluation that tests whether simulated populations reproduce human variation in reasoning, self-reported traits, their associations, and downstream behaviour. Agents conditioned on synthetic or human-derived profiles of cognitive reflection, Need for Cognition, and Big Five personality answer the same suite as a cohort of 473 adults: two newly assembled tests, a Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) and a Behavioural Reflection Test (BRT) whose decision scenarios measure reflection in behaviour, alongside an established CRT and the two trait questionnaires. Across seven full-battery simulation runs of four models, agents recover Need for Cognition and Big Five trait distributions on self-report questionnaires, but fall short on simulating diversity of cognitive task performance and downstream behaviours. In the four Claude Sonnet 4.6 runs, every agent scores full marks on both CRTs, whatever reflection level its persona was assigned. In the other three runs agents make intuitive-lure errors (the tempting wrong answers CRT items invite), but 49 to 85% score full marks, against under 10% in the human sample. Claude Sonnet 5 comes closest to people's item-by-item pattern of lures; the other two runs give fewer lures and vary less between items. In the BRT scenarios, every run over-produces 8 to 11 of 15 coded behaviours by at least 20 percentage points, and people's links between reflection and behaviour carry over only in part. Useful synthetic populations must preserve not only trait descriptors but the structured variation in reasoning, error type, and behaviour those descriptors are meant to organise.

papers.title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

papers.title: PENSA: A Spatial Accelerator for BitNet b1.58 Inference on an HBM-equipped AMD Alveo FPGA
papers.abstract: Ternary large language models (tLLMs) replace general multiplication in dominant linear layers with sign-controlled accumulation, shifting hardware bottlenecks toward packed-weight delivery, reduction, and operator occupancy. PENSA is an end-to-end FPGA accelerator for the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model on an AMD Alveo U50. Two row-partitioned ternary matrix engines consume packed TQ1_0 weights from eight independent high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pseudo-channels, each processing 1,280 ternary weights per cycle through sign selection and integer reduction. The sequencer, attention, and vocabulary-projection units remain resident on the FPGA, while two-stream interleaved scheduling overlaps sequences across the persistent pipeline to form the Penta-Unit. At 104.1~MHz, PENSA achieves 58.09 tok/s at context 128 and 24.60 tok/s at context 2048, corresponding to 2.14-3.14$\times$ the throughput of a same-model Xeon E-2356G baseline. The resulting system demonstrates end-to-end FPGA execution of 2B-scale BitNet topology without modifying its model structure.

papers.title: Hyperelasticity as an efficient regularizer for 2D-3D thoracic motion models
papers.abstract: Patient-specific motion models enable real-time volumetric imaging of the thorax from a single x-ray projection, but most existing approaches require hours of training. The VM-DS framework trains in minutes, yet its image-space self-consistency regularizer accounts for 40% of the motion-model fitting time and does not prevent the fitted fields from folding. In this paper, we explore a range of regularization approaches including scaling-and-squaring, bending energy, diffusion, first-order inverse consistency, isotropic total variation, a negative-Jacobian hinge, |log det J|, a control-point injectivity bound and hyperelastic regularization. Hyperparameters were selected on two development cases from the public DIR-Lab 4D dataset under rules fixed in advance, and the regularizers were tested on eight held-out cases. At a fixed number of training steps, the hyperelastic term trained in 5.6 against 8.4 min and gave a lower held-out TRE (2.5 mm). With a quarter of the motion-model budget it matched the baseline (2.7 mm), and at every budget from 2 to 17 min its mean TRE was lower by 0.3-0.5 mm. Hyperelastic fields had no folded voxel in any held-out view, whereas baseline fields folded in 83 % of views, with image similarity unchanged. A hyperelastic volume penalty can therefore replace image-space self-consistency, matching accuracy with 3-5 minutes of training and removing folding, bringing on-the-day motion models closer to routine use in image-guided interventions. Code will be available at https://github.com/Image-X-Institute/Voxelmap/tree/hyper

papers.title: Short-term associations between wild-bird and mammalian high pathogenic avian influenza detection in the United States
papers.abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. Monthly state-level mammalian counts were analysed using negative-binomial mixed models adjusted for seasonality, preceding mammalian detections and state-level heterogeneity. The selected model contained contemporaneous and one-month-lagged same-state wild-bird counts. A doubling of one plus the contemporaneous wild-bird count was associated with a 57.9% increase in the expected mammalian count (95% CI 43.5-73.8%), and a doubling of the preceding-month count with a 15.9% increase (5.2-27.8%). Bordering-state exposure did not improve fit. In a six-month temporal holdout, adding same-state wild-bird exposure reduced mean absolute error by 23.8% and root mean squared error by 27.9%, although total detections remained overpredicted. After exact-row deduplication, the corresponding effects were 59.7% and 13.3%. Wild-bird surveillance records contained short-term, geographically local information about mammalian HPAI detection activity, but the associations do not establish direct transmission and require further calibration before operational forecasting.

papers.title: KR A1: Design and Preliminary Evaluation of a Humanoid-Robot Interaction Prototype Integrating Personalized Voice Synthesis, Contextual Dialogue, and Emotion-Aware Response Generation
papers.abstract: This paper presents the design and preliminary evaluation of KR A1, a humanoid-robot interaction prototype that integrates personalized voice synthesis, contextual dialogue processing, and emotion-aware response generation for potential mental-healthcare applications. The system architecture combines a locally hosted large language model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, served via Ollama) for natural-language understanding and response generation, OpenVoice v2 for zero-shot speaker-adaptive speech synthesis, and a two-tier emotion-processing pipeline comprising a keyword heuristic and LLM-based inference. Face recognition (InsightFace) and vector memory retrieval (FAISS with sentence-transformer embeddings) enable user-personalized interaction. The experimental evaluation reported here is limited to the voice-cloning component: cloned voices were evaluated against reference recordings using eight acoustic similarity measures - mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, pitch, spectral centroid, spectral contrast, spectral rolloff, zero-crossing rate, formants, and speaker-embedding cosine similarity - supplemented by a same-speaker versus cross-speaker baseline comparison. All tests were conducted on a small, informal development sample; no statistical significance testing against a held-out baseline was performed. The emotion-recognition accuracy, end-to-end response latency, and therapeutic or clinical impact of the integrated system have not yet been formally evaluated and are identified as directions for future work. All testing was informal and self-conducted by the development team; no patients or external human participants were involved, and the system has not been evaluated or deployed in a clinical setting.
papers.intro:
The integration of artificial intelligence and robotics into mental healthcare has garnered significant research attention, with studies demonstrating potential benefits in patient engagement, social companionship, and therapeutic support [1]–[8]. Humanoid robots, equipped with natural-language understanding and affective computing capabilities, have emerged as promising platforms for delivering personalized, empathetic interactions in therapeutic settings [9]–[13]. Concurrently, advances in voice cloning and speech emotion recognition have enabled the synthesis of familiar voices and the detection of emotional states from acoustic and linguistic cues [14]–[18].

papers.title: Specific, cumulative and reversible odour learning in a whole-brain connectome model of Drosophila
papers.abstract: Whole-brain models of the fruit fly built from the FlyWire connectome can predict how neurons respond to a stimulus, but they keep every synapse fixed and so cannot learn, while models that do learn simulate only the mushroom body. I made the synapses from Kenyon cells (KCs) to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) plastic in a whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model of the FlyWire connectome, under a rule in which dopamine weakens each synapse in proportion to how strongly its KC fired. Odours reached the KCs through the connectome's mapped olfactory wiring, and punishment was delivered by driving the 12 PPL1 dopamine neurons at 100 Hz. Pairing an odour with punishment lowered the response of approach MBONs to that odour from 11.3 to 0.3 Hz in all five noise replicates of one simulated brain, while unpaired and never-paired odours and controls with the rule switched off or scrambled changed little. A second odour paired on the already trained brain was learned at 85.5% of the strength reached by a naive brain, and approach MBONs ended with weak responses to both odours. With a timing rule in which dopamine arriving before the odour strengthens a synapse, a simulated fly body driven by the model unlearned and relearned in four of four cycles, whereas the first rule got stuck after one; backward pairing alone was too weak to reach behaviour. All results are for aversive learning; reward learning could not be tested because, at the synaptic weight and synapse floor used here, sugar input does not recruit the reward dopamine neurons. Learning depended on an authored plasticity rule, an injected punishment signal and other authored choices detailed in Methods; given these choices, the odour-specificity of learning followed from the structure of the connectome.

papers.title: Counting Events, Not Seeing Them: Diagnosing and Repairing the Readout Failure in Video LLMs
papers.abstract: Video LLMs fail conspicuously at counting how many times an object crosses the screen, a failure attributed to missing object permanence. Using construction-grounded synthetic testbeds with independently validated labels, we show this attribution is incomplete: the count signal is present but unread - linear probes decode per-window presence at 93% while global count decoding collapses to a duration confound. Concurrent work reports the same representation-output dissociation for repetition counting; we show that in exit-and-reappear event counting it is repairable: two readout-directed repairs (episode-localization supervision and a discrete event-symbol side channel) raise same-object counting from 46.7% to 65.0% (oracle 66.7%) on a chance-33% benchmark across 7B-30B systems. Transfer to an independent factory costs nothing, and an audit of the measurement apparatus exposes four data-integrity failures that had obscured the boundary. A real-video audit (REALCOUNT, n=18, blind-audited) shows the boundary persists - best 55.6% at chance 33.3% - and symbol transfer fails zero-shot. A 1-epoch in-domain adaptation bench is negative (six levers at 28-50%), but a 3-epoch schedule shows this is budget-limited for the symbol channel: with a 3-epoch schedule and sequence-disjoint oracle timelines the reader reaches 94.4% on REALCOUNT, and with the deployed detector's timelines a 2-epoch run reaches 72.2%. The residual gap is detector evidence and the reader's match to detector noise, not reader capacity: a frozen-feature boundary probe finds the signal weak (AUC 0.62 over a 0.51 permutation control) and non-transferring across clips (0.77 within-clip vs. 0.62 across windows).
papers.intro:
Ask a video LLM how many times the red square crossed the screen, and it will fail—not occasionally but systematically, across model scales and training regimes. This “same-object counting” failure has survived every axis it has been tested on: 7B and 30B models, zero-shot and fine-tuned, dense and mixture-of-experts, attention-LoRA and expert-LoRA (Sec. 4). Because heterogeneous-object counting is near-perfect for the same models, the deficit has been characterized as missing object permanence—a representational gap in how identity is maintained across time (Baillargeon, 1987).

Ask a video LLM how many times the red square crossed the screen, and it will fail—not occasionally but systematically, across model scales and training regimes. This “same-object counting” failure has survived every axis it has been tested on: 7B and 30B models, zero-shot and fine-tuned, dense and mixture-of-experts, attention-LoRA and expert-LoRA (Sec. 4). Because heterogeneous-object counting is near-perfect for the same models, the deficit has been characterized as missing object permanence—a representational gap in how identity is maintained across time (Baillargeon, 1987).

This paper argues the deficit is elsewhere, and that it is repairable. Our diagnosis pipeline—error-structure analysis against trivial-baseline controls, linear probing of the model’s own token stream, and temporal-granularity measurements—locates the failure in the readout: the information needed to count is present in the model’s visual token stream (a linear probe recovers per-window object presence at 93%), but the language model cannot aggregate it into a count. Counting, for a video LLM, is not perception; it is symbol manipulation over evidence it can already see.

The model learns to articulate the event structure it is asked to count (episode recall 84% at IoU≥\geq0.5). 2. papers.title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $\mu^3_3$, where $\mu_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

papers.title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
papers.abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.
papers.intro:
This is the first of three papers on the compatibility of Atiyah–Floer isomorphisms with cobordism maps. The present paper proves the comparison over 𝔽2\mathbb{F}_{2} and establishes the mixed-equation analysis used throughout the series. Paper II [Wue26b] develops the integral theory: orientations are transported from the almost-complex gauge convention, and the comparison holds up to chain homotopy and one overall sign for each cobordism. Paper III [Wue26c] identifies this integral comparison with the usual singular Hopf-link instanton maps and, at common regular data, with the Daemi–Fukaya–Lipyanskiy mixed count in a specified coherent orientation system. It also constructs, for every closed connected oriented three-manifold, a comparison with the normalization in which attachment of a generating sphere preserves orientation. That construction uses finite integer combinations of products of geometric counts and retains the stated surgery and oriented gluing inputs. Thus the series proceeds from the comparison modulo two, through integral naturality, to identification and normalization of the integral maps.

papers.title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
papers.abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.
papers.intro:
The perfect cuboid problem asks for a rectangular box with positive integer edges for which all three face diagonals and the space diagonal are integers. Sharipov’s polynomial approach leads to three irreducibility conjectures [1]. The third concerns a degree-1212 even polynomial depending on three positive integer parameters; its exceptional parameter relations and its connection with a Diophantine equation are described in [2].

The third concerns a degree-1212 even polynomial depending on three positive integer parameters; its exceptional parameter relations and its connection with a Diophantine equation are described in [2].

Goal. We establish a common structural obstruction to complete factorizations of the third polynomial. Instead of excluding degree patterns individually, we obtain a normal form governed by the involution t↦−tt\mapsto-t, square classes of constant terms, and one uniform local factor. The resulting conditions exclude 5454 of the 7676 reducible degree partitions of twelve.

Evenness alone excludes 3737 of these partitions, since every odd degree must occur an even number of times. The arithmetic restrictions proved here reduce the remaining 3939 patterns to 2222. Sharipov’s structural theorem [2, Theorem 6.1] characterizes integer roots through 4848 positive integer variables. Our result instead constrains the complete irreducible factorization; it does not exclude rational roots.

papers.title: From Video to Digital Twin: An Exploratory Study of World Models and Gaussian Splatting on In-the-Wild Video
papers.abstract: Generative world models and 3D Gaussian Splatting promise to turn ordinary video into explorable 3D scenes, but little is reported on how they behave on uncurated, in-the-wild footage. We study what these models recover when the only input is a publicly available news walkthrough of a food bank warehouse, with presenters walking through every shot and no drawings, scans or site visit, and we use the result as the geometry of a digital twin. A commercial world model given 20 frames recovered camera poses and metric depth for three areas, which we fused into about 747,000 Gaussian splats for 200 credits (20 US cents). Splat models optimized locally on a CPU, at no credit cost, were photorealistic near the filmed path but degraded quickly away from it. On held-out frames, scored in pixels not covered by people, they reached 21.2 and 23.1 dB PSNR from 64 and 43 training frames, and lost 3.8 and 5.4 dB when given only the 8 frames a world model accepts. Removing the trainer's background fill and person-hull carving raised held-out PSNR, showing that cleaning the space behind moving people costs fidelity in observed pixels while its gain lies where no ground truth exists. Asking the world model to generate views of areas the video never showed failed on the provider's side twice, so extrapolation could not be evaluated and unseen space was filled by a scripted model instead. We also describe the corrections needed to turn world-model output into a valid, metric Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD) asset with its native splat schema, which serves as the only interface to a data layer, a browser viewer, Blender and NVIDIA Omniverse. The findings suggest that today's models recover the observed parts of a real scene cheaply and at metric scale, while few-view fidelity and extrapolating unobserved space remain open. The work is an exploration of these methods, not a deployed product.
papers.intro:
A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical asset that stays synchronized with it through data [22, 27]. In industry, twins are used to plan layouts, monitor equipment and rehearse changes before they are made on the floor [46, 19]. The geometry of a facility twin is usually the expensive part. It comes from terrestrial laser scanning, photogrammetry campaigns or hand-built computer-aided design (CAD) models, and specialists then import it into a simulation tool. That cost is tolerable for an automotive plant. It is prohibitive for a regional food bank, which runs warehouse-scale cold-chain logistics on a non-profit budget.

Two developments change that cost structure. Neural scene representations, and 3D Gaussian Splatting in particular [26], produce photorealistic scenes that render in real time from ordinary images. Classical reconstruction recovers camera poses with structure-from-motion [43]; neural radiance fields [31] improved view synthesis but render slowly; learned multi-view geometry such as DUSt3R [49] reduces the number of views needed. All of these reconstruct only what was observed. Generative world models [23, 8] go further: from a few views they produce a coherent, explorable 3D world and fill in regions the input never covered. World Labs’ Marble [53] exposes this capability through an API that returns Gaussian-splat worlds. For a twin, generation has a double edge. It makes a sparse walkthrough usable, but it also invents geometry.

Three lines of recent work bear directly on footage like ours. First, feed-forward geometry models predict poses and dense geometry from a handful of unposed images: DUSt3R [49], MASt3R [29] and VGGT [48]. Sparse-view splatting methods such as FSGS [55] and InstantSplat [17] build on such priors to train Gaussian splats from a few views. Second, in-the-wild reconstruction handles transient content, from appearance embeddings and transient masks for radiance fields (NeRF in the Wild [30]) to distractor-robust splatting (WildGaussians [28], SpotLessSplats [42]); the presenters who walk with the camera in our video are exactly such transients. Third, generative models synthesize unobserved views: multi-view diffusion (CAT3D [20]), video diffusion conditioned on a point cloud (ViewCrafter [54]) and interactive world models trained on video (Genie [9]). Faster and anti-aliased radiance fields [33, 6] set the evaluation conventions we follow: novel-view metrics on held-out frames. We do not benchmark these methods; we use a commercial world model and a standard 3DGS objective as representatives and measure what they recover from one uncurated video.

In parallel, Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD), originally from Pixar and now developed under the Alliance for OpenUSD, has become an open, vendor-neutral scene description with layered composition and typed schemas [40, 2]. Its 26.03 release added the ParticleField3DGaussianSplat schema family [3, 38], so a splat reconstruction is no longer a viewer-specific file. It can sit in the same stage as sensors, equipment and annotations. NVIDIA Omniverse [35] is a set of libraries that bring OpenUSD data interoperability, RTX rendering and physics simulation into applications. Its licensing is mixed: some components are open source, while the Kit SDK is distributed under NVIDIA’s own license terms: the Kit App Template states that its software and materials are governed by the NVIDIA Software License Agreement and the Product-Specific Terms for NVIDIA Omniverse [36], not an open-source license.

Surveys of digital twins identify geometry acquisition, data integration and interoperability as the recurring barriers [46, 19]. This work addresses the first and third barriers directly and keeps the second deliberately thin. This paper is an exploratory study of the learning methods behind the first barrier. We ask three questions: what a world model and locally optimized Gaussian splats recover from uncurated, publicly available video with no CAD drawings, laser scans or site visit; whether the generative step can fill in space the camera never saw; and what it takes to carry the result into an open scene format that other tools can use. To answer them we compose existing models into a three-step pipeline (Figure 1) and apply it to one realistic input, a news walkthrough of a food bank. The steps are: 1. Video to digital twin with world models. Blur-aware frame extraction feeds a world model that returns a Gaussian-splat world, which is converted to an OpenUSD stage in metric, Y-up coordinates. Where the camera saw too little, a facility model scripted in Blender fills in the building, published in the same format. 2. Connecting existing data systems on Amazon Web Services (AWS). A serverless API exposes operational data in the twin’s coordinate frame through a small, versioned JSON contract. The reference implementation simulates cold-chain telemetry; the contract is designed so that a real sensor feed or warehouse management system can replace the simulator without changing any renderer. 3. NVIDIA Omniverse as the visualization layer. Omniverse renders the USD twin with RTX on a rented GPU; binding live data to scene objects is the planned next step. A browser viewer and Blender read the same USD and the same JSON, so the renderer is a deployment choice rather than an architectural one.

papers.title: Ninada: Sub-Clause Split-Graph VITS Streaming and Capability-Routed 24 kHz Speech Synthesis Across Twelve Scripts
papers.abstract:
End-to-end VITS text-to-speech models synthesize natural speech in a single forward pass, yet standard ONNX exports execute monolithically over an entire clause, delaying Time-To-First-Audio (TTFA) to several seconds and spiking activation memory. Client-side deployment across Indic scripts faces four further bottlenecks: 138.8 MB float32 checkpoints per language strain browser caches, mobile WebGPU stalls for 6-14 s compiling convolution shaders while still running slower than real time ($1.44\times$ RTF), small WebAssembly pthread pools stall at barriers on big.LITTLE mobile CPUs, and mobile Web Audio pipelines drop frames or mute output under AudioWorklet contention and iOS WKWebView rules.
  We present Ninada, an open-source 24 kHz TTS system covering English, Classical Sanskrit, and ten Indian languages (sa, en, hi, kn, mr, bn, ta, te, ml, gu, pa, or) across a capability-routed 48-checkpoint fleet: 24 studio HiFi-GAN v1 specialists (27.9 MB W8A32+FP16 ONNX) for desktop/WebGPU and 24 distilled c8c8_384 iSTFTNet specialists (21.7 MB ONNX, $2.64\times$ fewer vocoder MACs via an exact NOLA dual-window ConvTranspose1d inverse STFT with zero complex ops) for mobile WASM, plus a 0.0 MB zero-dependency Klatt fallback. At runtime, Ninada splits a single ONNX file in memory in $< 15$ ms into prior, flow, and windowed vocoder sub-sessions streaming 12-frame halos with raised-cosine crossfades. On $N = 480$ held-out 24 kHz studio utterances, Ninada achieves 3.22 dB 0-8 kHz MCD (3.09 dB mobile iSTFTNet; 1.33 dB 24-voice distillation MCD, vs. 5.17 dB for the 1,526.8 MB 16 kHz Meta MMS fleet) and 6.07 dB 8-12 kHz error, delivering 89-155 ms audible startup on desktop WebGPU and 538-649 ms zero-underrun streaming at 0.75-0.76x RTF on a physical Google Pixel 10 Pro XL.
papers.intro:
Running speech synthesis directly inside a client browser or local edge process eliminates server inference costs, network tail latency, and transcript transmission to external APIs. Screen readers, language-learning tools, bilingual voice interfaces, and offline educational readers across South Asian languages require full-band 24 kHz audio, native script fidelity across Brahmic and Latin orthographies, sub-second audible startup, and uninterrupted playback on everyday phones.

Variational Inference with adversarial learning for end-to-end Text-to-Speech (VITS) [4] suits client deployment because it avoids autoregressive mel decoding. However, standard VITS exports hit four systems bottlenecks in web browsers: 1. Utterance-Blocking Graph Execution: Standard VITS ONNX exports chain the text encoder, stochastic duration predictor, normalizing flow, and HiFi-GAN generator [6] into one static graph. No audio sample is emitted until the entire clause latent z∈ℝ192×Tz\in\mathbb{R}^{192\times T} is upsampled by 256×256\times, pushing TTFA past 2–4 s on long clauses and allocating peak activations proportional to 256​T256T. 2. Footprint vs. Orthographic Fidelity: Open checkpoints such as Meta MMS-TTS [9] generate 16 kHz audio (rolling off above 8 kHz) at 138.8 MB per language (1,526.8 MB across 11 Indic models). Conversely, pooling scripts into a shared Romanized model introduces cross-language accent bleed and erases script-specific contrasts such as Sanskrit vocalic sonorants, Vedic pitch marks, Malayalam atomic chillus, and Tamil/Kannada retroflex sonorants. 3. Mobile GPU Stalls and Compute Limits: While desktop WebGPU runs HiFi-GAN v1 at ∼\sim0.09×\times Real-Time Factor (RTF), profiling pure-FP16 NHWC WebGPU on a physical Google Pixel 10 Pro XL shows 5.9–14.0 s cold shader compilation followed by 1.44–1.53×1.44\text{--}1.53\times warm effective RTF (1.90–2.11×1.90\text{--}2.11\times NCHW), slower than real time. Meanwhile, full 28.82 GMAC/s HiFi-GAN v1 also exceeds real time on mobile ARM WebAssembly (1.30×1.30\times RTF at 6 threads). 4. Asymmetric CPU Barriers and Mobile Audio Quirks: On physical 8-core big.LITTLE phones, small WebAssembly pthread pools stall at per-operator barriers when threads land on efficiency cores (2T=3.60×2\text{T}=3.60\times and 3T=2.40×3\text{T}=2.40\times RTF vs. 1T=1.55×1\text{T}=1.55\times and 6T=1.30×6\text{T}=1.30\times). Simultaneously, 2.67 ms JavaScript AudioWorklet callbacks contend with WASM threads on Android, while iOS WKWebView browsers (CriOS/Safari) enforce pthread memory ceilings and hardware mute-switch silencing.

papers.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
papers.abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horv\'ath and L\'angi, it remains to exclude the other simplicial types, which we do by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic.
papers.intro:
Which convex polytope with nn vertices, inscribed in the unit sphere 𝕊d−1\mathbb{S}^{d-1} of ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}, has the largest volume? Fejes Tóth raised this question in three dimensions [4], and it is listed among the open problems of discrete geometry [3]. papers.title: Autonomous Code Review: Hidden-Test Results on GitHub Issues
papers.abstract: Can an autonomous cross-provider review step change whether code written for a real issue passes hidden tests? We report a retrospective benchmark of 12 historical GitHub issues (five C#, five JavaScript, and two Python) from five repositories. Two directed author--reviewer pairs, OpenAI GPT-6.1-Sol and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5, each ran twice per issue, yielding 48 planned workflows. A bounded terminal agent produced an initial patch; a cross-provider model reviewed it; the author model adjudicated findings and could revise the patch. The same hidden evaluator assessed initial and final patches. Forty workflows completed, while eight terminated before a complete evaluator outcome. Four completed workflows passed, and all four already passed before review. No initial-to-final pass/fail transitions occurred among completed workflows.

papers.title: Full fillings at the accumulation point and triangular limits of almost toric diagrams
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a closed symplectic four-manifold admitting an almost toric fibration over a disk. The ellipsoid embedding function of $M$ has an infinite staircase if it has infinitely many nonsmooth points. Cristofaro-Gardiner, Holm, Mandini, and Pires showed that these points must then accumulate at a solution of an explicit quadratic equation, and that at this accumulation point the ellipsoid embedding function agrees with the volume obstruction. We call this a full filling at the accumulation point, and study it in terms of almost toric fibrations. We show that if $M$ admits a sequence of almost toric base diagrams, each with a Delzant corner, converging nontrivially to a triangle, then $M$ has a full filling at its accumulation point. For the one-point blowups $H_b$ of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we also prove the converse. As a consequence, $H_b$ has an infinite staircase if and only if it admits such a sequence converging to a triangle whose hypotenuse has irrational slope.

papers.title: Calculation and Recurrence Relations of the Determinants of the Hessenberg - Toeplitz Matrices
papers.abstract: The determinant D(n) of a n x n Hessenberg - Toeplitz matrix is given as product of certain functions of its elements. A compact expression of D(n) is presented and recurrence relations involving determinants and matrix elements of the Hessenberg -Toeplitz matrices are found.

papers.title: Caleta: An Evidence-Oriented Trust Layer for Reproducible Local Large Language Model Inference
papers.abstract: Local large language model (LLM) inference is often described as private, verified, or reproducible without separating the technical claims behind those terms. This paper presents Caleta, an Apache-2.0 process supervisor and evidence layer around llama.cpp rather than a new inference engine. Caleta combines versioned manifests, exact-size and SHA-256 verification, controlled backend construction, a restricted OpenAI-compatible proxy, prompt-free execution records, benchmark reports, and a small conformance suite. Its contribution is the composition of these mechanisms into explicit contracts that distinguish integrity from authenticated provenance and privacy controls from operating-system isolation. We evaluate the implementation through static checks, 22 unit tests, deterministic end-to-end tests on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows, and a pinned real-model experiment on Windows CPU using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M and llama.cpp b11981. The real experiment validates artifact verification, startup, model listing, non-streaming and server-sent-event chat, and conformance. Three independent benchmark invocations produced fifteen successful warm requests with no failures. In this single configuration, median time to first token was 18.066 ms and median decode throughput was 54.394 tokens/s. These descriptive measurements do not establish cross-engine superiority, output quality, energy efficiency, or hardware-general performance. Raw JSON, commands, and environment metadata are published. Remaining challenges include signed manifests, time-of-check/time-of-use replacement, operating-system containment, proxy-overhead measurement, and broader experimental matrices.
papers.intro:
The deployment of LLMs on local machines is motivated by latency, cost, data-control, availability, and operational-sovereignty requirements. Open-source runtimes such as llama.cpp, MLX-based systems, Ollama, Uzu, and BaseRT address important parts of this problem, including hardware coverage, model packaging, ease of use, and optimized execution [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. However, the ability to execute a model locally does not by itself answer several operational questions: Which bytes were executed? Which backend and runtime options were active? Which interfaces were exposed? What was measured, and which runs failed? What evidence remains after execution?

These questions are often conflated under broad claims of privacy or verification. A cryptographic digest can establish correspondence between an artifact and an expected value, but not the identity of the publisher who supplied that value. An offline backend flag can request network inactivity, but it is not equivalent to an operating-system firewall. A local HTTP listener can avoid wide-area exposure while remaining reachable by other local processes. Similarly, a throughput number without artifact identity, generation parameters, cold/warm separation, and failed-run accounting is insufficient to reproduce an experiment.

papers.title: Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive K\"ahler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.

The appearance of Ricci solitons as singularity models naturally leads to the question of their stability: heuristically, whether flows starting near a soliton remain close or converge to it. Stability is a classical topic in the variational theory of Ricci solitons (and Einstein metrics), and plays an essential role in determining which solitons might occur in ‘generic’ solutions to Ricci flow. In mean curvature flow, Colding and Minicozzi’s classification of stable self-shrinkers [8], and numerous subsequent developments (see for instance [6, 7, 2]), have led to a deep understanding of generic mean curvature flows of embedded surfaces in ℝ3\mathbb{R}^{3}. Developing a corresponding theory of generic Ricci flow remains an important goal, particularly in dimension four where the next frontier of Ricci flow stands.

papers.title: A Zero-Free Sum of Cauchy Kernels with Positive Coefficients
papers.abstract:
We construct a zero-free meromorphic function \[
  f(z)=\sum_n\frac{c_n}{z-a_n},\qquad
  c_n>0,\qquad |a_n|\to\infty,\qquad
  \sum_{a_n\ne0}\frac{c_n}{|a_n|}<\infty, \] thereby disproving the Clunie--Eremenko--Rossi conjecture. The construction starts from a product of two rotated Airy functions. The zeros of this product are shifted simultaneously so that all residues of $f$ are positive. The poles lie on the rays $e^{\pm i\pi/3}[0,\infty)$. The resulting function has order and lower order $3/2$, and the sum of its residues in the disc $|z|\le r$ is asymptotic to $\frac{4}{3\pi}r^{3/4}$.

papers.title: What extraction cannot slim, and whether function injection can: a pre-registered study of 580 Java repositories
papers.abstract: A method of 26 code lines or more reads as a Long Method, and Extract Method is the usual fix. Some long methods have no single-exit fix: a return cannot leave an extracted piece, a piece hands back one value, and some methods are knotted so that every cut is blocked. Function injection, as the OfficeFloor framework does it, cuts differently: each piece becomes a function the framework injects and sequences, an early return ends a function, and a function hands on several values. The framework's author pre-registered a test of whether it takes apart what extraction cannot. A stratified random sample of 580 open-source Java repositories, each pinned before AI coding assistants were in general use, was scanned by released tools whose cost models were fixed before the sample was drawn: 3,026,902 methods, 168,466 of them long. Single-exit extraction cannot slim 22.8% of the long methods. The registered hypothesis, that at least a quarter of those stuck methods are ones only function injection takes apart, is refuted: 22.2% (95% CI 20.3 to 24.3). Nearly half of the stuck methods are early-return methods the plan counts as conventionally fixable, and the split takes three in four of those apart as they stand. Where extraction would do, the split chooses injection and costs less for 29.0% against extraction wrapped as one function and 17.2% against plain extraction, almost always as a straight sequence of functions. An exploratory reading of the quarter of the stuck methods that neither takes apart finds a third of it tables and literals, long for their data rather than their logic, and most of the rest blocked by a jump inside a loop, by a nested statement too large to cut, or by values too many for any cut. Three registered studies are proposed: the classes as rules in the tools, a refinement per class, and the same measures on code written with AI assistants.
papers.intro:
Fowler catalogued the Long Method and named its fix, Extract Method [6, 8]. An earlier study of this author’s found that the length at which reviewers call a method a Long Method is 26 code lines, lines that hold code with blank and comment lines not counted [16]. A tool, SinewSlim, followed: for every method of 26 lines or more it searches for a set of extractions that brings the method, and every extracted piece, to 25 lines or fewer, pricing each cut by what crosses it and taking the segmentation whose widest cut is narrowest. Tools that find Extract Method opportunities are not new [19, 9]; SinewSlim’s difference is that it prices every cut and says when no cut is feasible, and that is where this paper starts. Some long methods cannot be slimmed by extraction into single-exit pieces at all. A return cannot leave such a piece, so a method of guard clauses blocks every cut that contains one. An extracted piece hands back one value, so a run of statements that produces two needs a record to carry them, at a cost of its own. Some methods are knotted so tightly that every cut needs more parameters than a reader should follow. These methods are called stuck here, and stuck means stuck under extraction as SinewSlim models it: one exit, one output and at most five parameters a piece. The first finding of this paper is the count of them: on 580 repositories, 22.8% of the long methods are stuck, between a fifth and a quarter.

Function injection cuts a method differently. In OfficeFloor, a framework the author created, a function is an ordinary Java method whose arguments the framework supplies, as dependency injection does [7], and whose next function the framework chooses: the developer writes the pieces and the wiring between them, and the framework sequences them. An early return becomes a flow from its function to the method’s end; an if can become a decision with a flow per branch; a function hands on several values, because the next function asks the framework for them; the instrument used here lets a function take up to five such values as parameters. So a method extraction cannot slim might still come apart as functions. The author expected it would, often. papers.title: ROLECUE: Diagnosing Cross-Lingual Role-Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can recognize events in images and parse sentences, but it remains unclear when they bind visual Agent-Patient structure to linguistic semantic roles across languages whose role cues depend on morphology, word order or construction. We introduce ROLECUE, a controlled diagnostic that pairs 192 validated two-person action images with German, Turkish, Japanese, English, Korean and Bangla sentences in canonical and patient-first orders. The evaluation separates image-only role recognition, text-only role parsing, direct image-sentence matching, response-compliance behavior and an external modular composition of the model's own component predictions. Across eight recent open-weight VLMs, ROLECUE reveals a structured spectrum: some models fail visual or linguistic component tests, some largely solve the diagnostic, some collapse to constant semantic assent and several show component-joint gaps in which reliable image-only and text-only role predictions do not survive direct joint inference. The largest non-degenerate gaps reach 44.9 percentage points, with final bootstrap intervals confirming that the effect is not a point-estimate artifact. These results reveal multilingual component-joint performance gaps and acceptance biases hidden by aggregate VLM benchmarks and show why component diagnostics are necessary before interpreting joint multimodal errors.
papers.intro:
Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly evaluated as general-purpose systems that can answer questions about images, read text, and judge whether a caption matches a scene. Yet many such evaluations do not isolate a basic semantic requirement: determining who did what to whom across modalities. This matters especially outside English. Languages such as German, Turkish, Japanese, Korean, and Bangla can place the patient before the agent while grammatical marking or constructional cues still indicate the event roles. For example, a Japanese sentence may begin with “the blue-shirted man” while still meaning that the red-shirted man pushes the blue-shirted man. A model that treats the first mentioned participant as the agent can appear fluent while failing the semantic role binding needed for grounded understanding.
